bodyHtml:
Chandler, AZ, part of the Metropolitan Phoenix area, is uniquely positioned to provide visitors easy access to various activities and fulfilling experiences. The city sees over 300 days of sunshine annually, setting the stage for invigorating outdoor recreation such as hiking, world-class golfing, horseback riding, and hot air ballooning over the majestic Sonoran desert. There are so many things to do in Chandler!

 

Sign up for our newsletter and check out our visitor’s guide to get started on planning your next vacation today!

Among the seemingly endless list of things to do is exploring vibrant downtown Chandler, a hub for arts and culture, shopping, gallery hopping, nightlife, and a thriving restaurant scene. Whether your taste buds cry out for Italian, Asian, pub grub, or a premium steakhouse, you’ll find it and everything in between at these tasty restaurants in Chandler, AZ. 

Explore the region's rich history through captivating museums like the Chandler Museum or Arizona Railway Museum. At the Huhugam Heritage Center, learn about and celebrate the area's Native American heritage and modern-day culture.

Combine all this with welcoming, smiling locals, comfortable hotels with elevated hospitality, Arizona resorts, and plenty of family-friendly fun, and it's easy to see why Chandler is the ideal choice for your next getaway.

When you visit Chandler—where the city meets the desert—there's always something new to discover.

bodyHtml:
Welcome to Chandler, Arizona! 

We're thrilled to have the AANLCP Nurse Life Care Planning Conference 2025 select Chandler as their home base for their spring meeting.

Located about 20 minutes from Sky Harbor International Airport, along I-10, Chandler, AZ is a vibrant city with a diverse community and thriving tech industry. The city of Chandler embodies an active lifestyle with easy access to outdoor recreation, a lively dining scene, a wide variety of shopping destinations, award-winning events, world-class golf facilities, and a vibrant downtown.

April 4 - 6, 2025

Your host hotel for the weekend is the Crowne Plaza Phoenix Chandler Golf Resort.

Experience a Ride in an Autonomous Vehicle

Have you wondered how autonomous vehicles are changing the world? While visiting Chandler, see and feel the future by experiencing a ride in a Waymo One autonomous vehicle. Waymo rides offer convenience like no other by operating 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. Unlike other ride-sharing services, take your Waymo to popular spots like Chandler Fashion Center and make stops along the way, all in one booking.

By booking and routing a Waymo One, the autonomous vehicle service works much like Uber or Lyft. Download the Waymo One app, link your Google account and payment method, and enter your destination within the service area to request a ride. Shortly afterward, a sleek white Jaguar I-PACE will arrive, with your initials displayed on a rotating screen atop the vehicle. Alternatively, you can also book a Waymo One ride directly through the Uber app.

WHILE YOU ARE HERE...

We hope you will enjoy our diverse community and savor a meal or two at one of Chandler's fabulous restaurants featuring a variety of cuisines. Fun fact, there are 40 local restaurants and bars within walking distance of your host hotel, a collection of boutique shops, and plenty of entertainment options. Although we know the sunshine and pool may be calling your name.

About VisitChandler.com

The Economic Development Division is the designated Destination Marketing Organization (DMO) and a part of the City of Chandler. The Visit Chandler tourism office manages a multi-layered tourism marketing campaign promoting Chandler as a preferred travel destination for leisure and business travel.  The Visit Chandler team provides information to visitors, meeting and event professionals and the media about Chandler hotels, restaurants, attractions and businesses. 

The City of Chandler Economic Development Division's overall mission is to attract and preserve quality retail, industrial, office, downtown redevelopment and tourism development that will enhance employment opportunities, improve Chandler's tax base and quality of life for its citizens. 

Visit Chandler stocks an unstaffed, self-service visitor center inside Chandler City Hall.  The Chandler Visitor Center is open Monday - Friday, 8 a.m. - 5 p.m., closed on holidays.

bodyHtml:
CHD Amenities

Chandler Municipal Airport is a designated reliever airport for the Greater Phoenix area. It is designed to meet the needs of the general aviation community, be they small - medium sized corporate jets, single or multi-engine aircraft or helicopters.

Several businesses operate at CHD offering a variety of aviation related services including an FBO, flight schools, aircraft maintenance, avionics, insurance, and charter operations. Other amenities include:

  • Ramp space/tie-downs available
  • No Landing Fees
  • Terminal building (Airport Administration Building)
    • Pilot's Lounge​
    • Passenger lobby
    • Free Wifi
  • FBO and line services
  • Jet A, Self-serve 100 LL Avgas
  • Meeting rooms available in the terminal
  • Air Traffic Control Tower 6 a.m. to 9 p.m. daily
  • Free automobile parking
  • Hangar Cafe serving breakfast and lunch seven days a week

metaDescription: Enjoy delicious barbeque in Chandler, Arizona at one of our fine BBQ restaurants. View detailed listings and maps to find the perfect barbeque restaurant.
ogTitle: Chandler BBQ Restaurants | Restaurants in Chandler AZ
bodyHtml:
BBQ and Western

If your idea of a perfect day includes smoky brisket, ribs that practically fall apart when you look at them, or a plate piled high with slow-cooked magic, Chandler’s calling your name. From classic smokehouses to backyard-style joints with live music and picnic vibes, the city is a true haven for American BBQ in Chandler. So grab some napkins and your appetite, and make your way to these local favorites for the best BBQ restaurants Chandler, AZ has to offer.

American Way Smokehouse

Best for: Vintage vibes and deli-meets-BBQ comfort

Tucked inside Merchant Square Antique Marketplace, this spot feels like stepping into an old-school general store…if that store also had insanely good brisket. American Way’s brisket sandwich is top-tier, and don’t skip the homemade cookies from Tattered Apron. It’s cozy, quirky and perfect if you’re already treasure-hunting through the antique market inside.

Back Alley BBQ

Best for: Live music and award-winning meats

Back Alley BBQ is exactly what it sounds like: off the beaten path, totally unassuming and absolutely worth finding. Their chefs? Award-winning. Their pulled pork? Chef’s kiss. And when live music fills the relaxed, backyard-style space, it becomes one of the best BBQ restaurants in Chandler, AZ. This Downtown Chandler spot is great for hanging with friends who love food and good vibes.

Can’t Stop Smokin’ BBQ

Best for: Hungry families and serious meat cravings

This place is for people who don’t mess around with portions. Whether you go solo with a plate or tackle one of their massive family meals, you’re guaranteed to leave full (and probably with leftovers). The sliced brisket, sausage links, and fruit cobbler are favorites. But honestly? Everything hits the spot at Can’t Stop Smokin’ BBQ.

Famous Dave’s Bar-B-Que

Best for: Variety and convenience

Located near Chandler Fashion Center, Famous Dave’s is a solid pick when you’re craving BBQ, but also need something quick and crowd-pleasing. The St. Louis ribs are a classic, and there’s enough on the menu to keep picky eaters happy. Think “BBQ pit stop” after a day of errands.

Rudy’s Country Store and Bar-B-Q

Best for: Classic Texas BBQ and casual vibes

Paper towels on the table. Big trays of brisket. Creamed corn that somehow turns into the star of your plate. Rudy’s is everything you want in a Texas-style BBQ joint, without the fuss. It’s cafeteria-style ordering, super chill and perfect for families or anyone who just wants good food, fast.

Craving something beyond smoked Texas brisket or juicy St. Louis ribs? Chandler also boasts a stellar Korean BBQ scene—think sizzling tabletop grills, marinated meats bursting with flavor, and all the banchan (Korean side dishes) your heart could want!

Whether you’re team brisket, team ribs, or just here for the sides, Chandler’s BBQ scene is packed with flavor and charm, making it a true destination for American BBQ. And if you’re truly about that ‘cue life, don’t miss the annual Downtown Chandler BBQ Festival. It’s the quintessential meat-lover’s dream, with local pitmasters, bands, and more saucy samples than you can count.

bodyHtml:
Bear Creek Golf Complex

Chandler's Bear Creek Golf Complex hosts a variety of Arizona Golf Association events each year on its rolling fairways. The Nicklaus Design Group and architect Bill O'Leary complex features an 18-hole championship length, Par-71 "Bear Course" that spans 6,825 yards and the fun and sporty,  "Cub Course" with a Par-59 and 3,552 -yard executive course that is well suited for beginners, seniors and family play.  

The facility is well equipped to accommodate golf players of all ages and abilities and golf instruction from PGA Professionals is available for groups and individuals when booked in advance.  

The complex also features on-site dining at the Bear's Den Bar & Grill with plenty of indoor and covered patio seating with sweeping views of the course.  Diners may select from a variety of breakfast and lunch dishes.

Whether you are planning for an enjoyable day on the course, or a corporate outing, Bear Creek Golf Complex is able to accommodate a variety of events at its 36-hole Chandler, Arizona golf facility.

headings.text: 10 Places Not to Miss While Visiting Chandler

bodyHtml:
Chandler offers visitors a well-rounded home base, combining a lively local scene with easy access to some of Greater Phoenix’s most established cultural and outdoor destinations. Whether your plans focus on walkable dining districts, regional museums, desert landscapes, or day trips, our city supports a flexible, balanced itinerary.

Downtown Chandler

Located just south of Chandler Blvd 
Along Arizona Avenue, Chandler, AZ 85225 
(480) 855-3539, Downtown Chandler Community Partnership

Downtown Chandler serves as the city’s social and cultural core, bringing together restaurants, breweries, shops, and gathering spaces in a compact, walkable area. You can spend an afternoon browsing boutiques, then transition easily into dinner, live music, or evening events, as well as the historic Crowne Plaza San Marcos Golf Resort and the Chandler Center for the Arts. While strolling in the trellis-covered walkways and colonnades, be sure to stop by Vision Gallery to view the art collection there.  

If you’re hungry, grab a table at SanTan Brewing Company, home to some of Arizona’s finest craft beers as well as gourmet burgers and pizza. Or satisfy your sweet tooth at The Screamery, where handcrafted ice cream is made on‑site with grass‑fed milk and natural ingredients. Seasonal festivals, farmers’ markets, and community celebrations regularly add activity and character to the district as well.

 

Huhugam Heritage Center 

21359 S. Maricopa Road 
Chandler, AZ 85226 
(520) 796‑3500 

The Huhugam Heritage Center highlights the ancestral, historic, and contemporary cultures of the Gila River Indian Community, including the Akimel O’otham and the Pee Posh tribes. Built in 2003 to preserve Him dak (“our way of life”) the center features desert‑inspired architecture and state‑of‑the‑art collections that include Huhugam (Hohokam) archaeological holdings, O’odham baskets, Pee Posh pottery, and memorabilia from Akimel O’otham jazz musician Russell Moore. Visitors can also explore exhibitions that celebrate master artists, traditional crafts, and cultural histories that have shaped the community for generations.

 

South Mountain Park and Preserve

10919 S. Central Avenue 
Phoenix, AZ 85042 
(602) 262-7393 

South Mountain Park and Preserve stretches across rugged desert terrain, with miles of trails and panoramic views of the Valley. As one of the largest municipal parks in the country, it supports hiking, mountain biking, horseback riding, and scenic drives across varied elevations. Locals often set aside time early or late in the day to take advantage of cooler temperatures and softer desert light. Leashed dogs are also welcome on the trails, making it easy to bring them along.

 

Queen Creek Olive Mill

25062 S. Meridian Road 
Queen Creek, AZ 85142 
(480) 888-9290 

A visit to Queen Creek Olive Mill centers on food, agriculture, and locally produced olive oil. The working olive farm and mill invites you to explore its marketplace, sample products, and dine on-site. Guests frequently include this spot as part of a culinary outing, pairing tastings with relaxed meals and events. This one allows well-behaved, leashed dogs outside.

Phoenix Zoo 

455 N. Galvin Parkway 
Phoenix, AZ 85008 
(602) 286-3800 

Covering a large footprint near Papago Park, the Phoenix Zoo offers a full day of discovery focused on animal care, conservation, and education. Exhibits span multiple habitats across a walkable campus designed for extended visits by families and groups. The zoo also hosts a range of captivating events throughout the year.

OdySea Aquarium  

9500 E. Via de Ventura 
Scottsdale, AZ 85256 
(480) 291-8000 

OdySea Aquarium is an immersive environment where you’ll encounter marine life through large-scale exhibits and interactive displays. The climate-controlled setting makes it a popular option during warmer months, and its educational focus attracts guests of all ages. With rotating presentations, unique viewing experiences, and opportunities to learn about conservation, it’s a standout stop for anyone looking to dive deeper into the underwater world.

Desert Botanical Garden 

1201 N. Galvin Parkway 
Phoenix, AZ 85008 
(480) 941-1225 

Winding trails and curated landscapes define an outing to the Desert Botanical Garden, where Sonoran Desert plant life takes center stage. Visitors can explore themed garden trails highlighting everything from towering saguaros and desert wildflowers to global desert species showcased in thoughtfully designed habitats. Interpretive exhibits, sculpture installations, and seasonal displays add layers of interest throughout the year.

 

Musical Instrument Museum 

4725 E. Mayo Boulevard 
Phoenix, AZ 85050 
(480) 478-6000 

Global music traditions converge at the Musical Instrument Museum, where its Geographic Galleries present instruments and music from distinct world regions through audio and video performances, alongside additional galleries that explore artists, mechanical music, hands-on experiences, STEM connections, and rotating exhibitions. Live performances and changing installations keep the museum dynamic year-round.

 

Taliesin West 

12621 N. Frank Lloyd Wright Boulevard 
Scottsdale, AZ 85259 
(480) 860-2700 

Taliesin West stands as a National Historic Landmark and the former winter home of architect Frank Lloyd Wright. Guided tours interpret the site’s design, materials, and relationship to the surrounding desert landscape. You can also choose an interactive self‑guided tour for more flexibility. Because tour slots fill quickly, advance reservations are recommended.

 

Heard Museum  

2301 N. Central Avenue 
Phoenix, AZ 85004 
(602) 252-8840 

The Heard Museum provides an in-depth look at American Indian art, both historic and contemporary. Exhibitions feature works from numerous Indigenous cultures, presented alongside interpretive context and educational programming. Visitors often visit the museum to gain a deeper understanding of the region’s cultural foundations.

 

Events, Dining, & Local Flavor 

Check out our annual events calendar to explore festivals, performances, and seasonal celebrations to plan your stay around what’s happening. Downtown remains the city’s most walkable dining destination, while shopping hubs such as Chandler Fashion Center add variety for retail and dining outings during your stay.

 

Tips for a Great Visit 

Many of the destinations listed sit within a short drive of Chandler, making it easy to combine city experiences with regional attractions. If you’re traveling with pets, check out each spot’s policy in advance, as guidelines vary by location. Outdoor plans benefit from seasonal awareness: cooler mornings and evenings are often the most comfortable times to explore. Some places also recommend advance reservations during busy periods, so it helps to plan ahead. For accessibility considerations, consult our accessibility guide. 

 

Start Planning Your Chandler Adventure 

With so many exciting things to do, Chandler offers a flexible and rewarding place to visit. Start planning your visit and discover how easily you can shape a trip that fits your style.

bodyHtml:
Champagne may be the drink of choice on New Year’s Eve, but January 1st is all about the Bloody Mary, especially for those who may have had too much bubbly the night before. The tomato juice and vodka-based cocktail is a great addition to breakfast out, but the drink has been so popular on January 1st that the day was designated National Bloody Mary Day. 

 

While visiting Chandler, you can kick off your New Year with the morning-friendly cocktail (and maybe even a hearty brunch) at one of these Chandler restaurants, each known for its outstanding Bloody Marys. Some of the Chandler, Arizona restaurants listed below offer their Bloody Mary with weekend brunch, perfect for weekend toast with family and friends.

Craft & Cork - a  craveable weekend brunch

This South Chandler eatery is a fantastic choice for a leisurely morning, with a top-notch weekend brunch menu that hits all your cravings. On Saturdays and Sundays, brunch begins at 10 a.m. at Cork & Craft, and the breakfast menu features loaded Bloody Mary cocktails with zingy pickles, spicy, creamy pepper jack cheese, and smoky bacon. 

 

Location: 4920 S. Gilbert Road #3, Chandler AZ 85249 or (480) 637-4278

Hash Kitchen - features the ultimate DIY Bloody Mary bar

Located in north Chandler, Hash Kitchen is famous for its highly customized Bloody Mary bar, offering guests more than 50 craft toppings to create their ultimate Bloody Mary. The lively restaurant offers more than eight Bloody Mary options, including a non-traditional green Bloody Mary that combines jalapeño vodka and tomatillo.  Complement your Hash Kitchen beverage with one of their over–the–top brunch items, including Cannoli Doughnuts, Pineapple Upside Down Pancakes, or the Chicken Tinga Frittata, for a memorable meal.

 

Location: 2855 W. Ray Road, Chandler AZ 85224 or (480) 909-4270

 

Helluva Brewing Company - sample and taste more with a flight of four Bloody Marys

If you are hungry and craving a Bloody Mary, look no further than Helluva Brewing Company, where you can get a Breakfast Tostada, Brunch tacos, a Highwayman Breakfast Burger, and more to pair with your Bloody Mary Flight. Helluva's flights include four Bloody Marys of your choice, either Smoked BBQ Bacon, Whiskey Twist, Pickle, Olive, Spicy Horseradish, or the Helluva 'Goody Ole Boy' Michelada. This West Chandler restaurant serves brunch on Saturdays and Sundays from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. 

 

Location: 3950 W. Ray Rd. Suite 5, Chandler, AZ 85226 or (480) 664-6488

Over Easy in Chandler - a popular brunch spot with two Chandler locations

With two locations in Chandler - in Downtown Chandler and West Chandler, this Arizona brunch hot spot is known not only for its great food, which has been featured on the Food Network’s shows Diners, Drive-ins & Dives, and The Best Thing I Ever Ate, but the Chandler restaurant also offers a divine menu of daytime cocktails.

Options at Over Easy include three signature Bloody Marys: the Bloody Good, more of a traditional option featuring vodka, pickle spear, fresh lemon, and lime; the Bacon Bloody with applewood smoked bacon-infused vodka, a chili salt rim, and a slice of bacon; and the Viva Maria featuring Blanco tequila, avocado, jalapeño, and hot sauce.  These are the perfect complement to their brunch-forward dishes.

 

Downtown Chandler Location: 140 N. Arizona Ave., Chandler AZ 85225 or (480) 257-3449

West Chandler Location: 7131 W Ray Rd Suite #7, Chandler AZ 85226 or (480) 306-6681

 

The Parlay Kitchen + Cocktails - an excellent option for large groups

This modern kitchen offers a unique mix of cuisine and cocktails, all served in its expansive dining room and large patio, both ideal for large groups. You can't go wrong with the Parlay's Charcuterie House Bloody, which features their housemade bloody mary mix, bacon, pickle, and charcuterie skewer.

 

Location: 1245 S Price Road #1, Chandler AZ 85286 or (480) 500-5247

 

Pedal Haus Brewery in Downtown Chandler

The locally owned and award-winning craft brewery offers not only a fantastic selection of local Arizona beers and gastropub eats, but it has also recently unveiled a Bloody Mary lineup that hits all the right notes.  The zesty and zingy beverages feature garnishes such as shrimp, bacon, shishitos, cheese, cured meats, olives, and more. A great option for al fresco dining on the Pedal Haus Brewery patio, with one of their dishes. We think the Haus Mac N' Cheese, made with a blend of their house-made beer cheese, white cheddar, and cavatappi pasta, is an excellent pairing.

 

Location: 95 W Boston St, Chandler, AZ 85225 or (480) 656-1639

 

SanTan Brewing Company - a local brewery featuring a solid Bloody Mary

The Bloody Mary at SanTan Brewing Company isn’t your typical Bloody Mary, but it’s considered by many to be one of the best in Arizona. SanTan’s version features chipotle bacon-infused vodka topped with a float of its own Gordo Stout, a nitrogenated Irish stout. Garnished with a smoked chipotle salted rim, green onion, and lime, the drink is an excellent addition to the weekend brunch.

 

Location: 8 S. San Marcos Pl., Chandler 85225 or (480) 917-8700

 

St. Amand Kitchen + Cocktails - a South Chandler favorite

Make your way to St. Amand Kitchen + Cocktails for their Sunday brunch from 10 a.m. - 2 p.m. for live music, sports at the bar, and one of their delicious dishes made even better with its traditional Bloody Mary. St. Amand's version is perfectly balanced with just the right amount of zip and garnished with olives, lemon, lime, and a slice of bacon.

 

Location: 3990 S Alma School Rd, Chandler, AZ 85248 or (480) 782-5550

 

 

Tryst Cafe - a well-regarded brunch spot with top-notch cocktails

A dining destination for organic and natural cuisine, Tryst Cafe serves made-from-scratch meals using locally sourced ingredients and features a fantastic selection of cocktails - and yes, you guessed it - a fabulous Bloody Mary that can be enjoyed in the dining room, on the patio, or in their semi-private dining room.

 

Location: 4205 S Gilbert Road, Chandler AZ 85249 or (480) 656-1011

 

U.S. Egg Breakfast & Lunch Restaurant

For nearly 30 years, U.S. Egg Breakfast & Lunch Restaurant has been serving breakfast, lunch, and great Bloody Marys from 6:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. daily. Choose from four varieties: the Traditional, garnished with olives and pickles, the Eye Opener, served with jalapenos and Cholula Hot Sauce, the Tailgate, served with two slices of bacon, and the Bacon N' Egg, with two slices of bacon and a hard-boiled egg. Or get the Bloody Mary Flight and try all four options! 

 

Location: 5840 W. Chandler Blvd., Chandler AZ 85226 or (480) 705-0868

headings.text: 15 Things to See and Do in Downtown Chandler

bodyHtml:
Where culture meets charm, Downtown Chandler offers a plethora of must-see-and-do attractions and activities. From vibrant art galleries showcasing works by exciting artists, to a vast variety of eateries offering the most scrumptious dishes, the city’s core has something for everyone. Whether you’re a visitor or a local, here are 15 of some of our favorite things to experience in Downtown Chandler. Enjoy!

Show-stopping performances

If your ideal of the perfect evening involves an exciting theatrical show or a world-class concert by a global entertainer, prepare for an unforgettable experience at the Chandler Center for the Arts. Having hosted top-tier performances, this Downtown Chandler landmark is the place to go for a memorable night out.

Laugh out loud

Prepare to have your funny bone tickled at Downtown Chandler’s latest entertainment spot. Mic Drop Comedy Chandler brings side-splitting comedians to Arizona, from exciting newcomers to some of the biggest names in the comedy game. Whether you’re looking to share a few laughs with your friend squad, or want a cool way to break the ice on date night, this hot spot is the perfect place to enjoy side-splitting comedy in Downtown Chandler.

Chandler after dark

Forget the notion that once the sun sets, Downtown Chandler settles in for a casual, laid-back evening. In actuality, the city comes alive with a vibrant nightlife scene filled with trendy bars, chic lounges and lively places to dance the night away. Whether you’re into craft cocktails, local beers, delicious eats or live entertainment, the city’s hidden gems will let you experience the energy of Chandler’s nightlife like never before.

Explore artistic treasures

To truly experience Chandler’s vibrant art scene, visit the Vision Gallery. Located at Chandler City Hall, the fine arts gallery allows visitors to interact with works by local and regional artists in a contemporary setting filled with natural light. Continue your art journey with a visit to the Gallery at the Chandler Center for the Arts, where you’ll be immersed in a world of exciting art in a variety of media, including ceramics, photography, painting and sculpture, among many others.

Unwind in style

Take your visit to Downtown Chandler to the next level by checking into one of downtown’s beautiful hotels. From the historic Crowne Plaza Resort to the modern Hilton Garden Inn, these accommodations not only offer comfort and convenience, they’ll also immerse you in the nonstop attractions and activities happening in the heart of the city.

Groove to the rhythm

A true haven for music lovers, Downtown Chandler is home to bars, restaurants and venues that offer the best in live entertainment. Chandler meets Nashville at The Stillery, where you’ll be treated to performances by top country music singers and entertainers. For a wide variety of music styles and performers, check out Murphy’s Law, where you can groove to the sounds of local and national musicians and dance to your favorite beats.

Unleash your inner artist

At Downtown Chandler’s Burst of Butterflies, creativity knows no bounds. Designed for artists of all ages and skill levels, this family-owned art studio encourages guests to channel their creative side to create their next masterpiece. From pottery and canvas painting to glass fusing and clay making, you’ll participate in hands-on projects that will allow your imagination to soar.

Artistry on every corner

Take a leisurely stroll through Downtown Chandler and you’re guaranteed to encounter true works of art. Known for its robust public art program, Chandler is filled with brilliant murals created by local and national artists that reflect the city’s commitment to art and creativity. Plus, with their vibrant colors, the murals make for the perfect backdrop to your memorable moment visiting Chandler’s downtown district.

Elevate your evening

Any viewpoint of an Arizona sunset is a good one, but the views atop one of Downtown Chandler’s rooftop bars will leave you breathless. At The Perch Brewery, enjoy stunning panoramic views of the city as you nibble and sip on an array of American-style pub food and drink. For a truly laidback sunset experience, head to the rooftop lounge at Puro Cigar Bar, where you can relax with a cigar, beer or spirit.

Sip, savor and cheers

Downtown Chandler has emerged as a craft beer haven, boasting an impressive roundup of bars and breweries that cater to beer enthusiasts. Helping put downtown on the craft beer map is SanTan Brewing Company, whose award-winning brews are made right here in Chandler. Also serving great beers are Quart Haus, The Perch, and Buqui Bichi, known for its authentic Sonoran craft beer.

Bask in the open air

With more than 300 days of sunshine, dining al fresco is a way of life in Arizona. Luckily, Downtown Chandler offers an abundance of restaurants that embrace the delight of outdoor dining. Whether you’re having a leisurely brunch on a sunny morning or a romantic dinner under the stars, you’ll find the perfect spot at such places like SanTan Brewing Company, Craft 64, The Hidden House, and DC Steakhouse.

Farm fresh finds

Every Saturday from October to May, Downtown Chandler transforms into a playground for foodies and shoppers in search of local goods and products. As you stroll through the market, you’ll revel in the vast array of fresh produce from local family farms; gourmet foods, sauces and breads; and handmade artisanal goods—many made right here in Arizona.

Indulge in dessert delights

If you’ve got a sweet tooth, Downtown Chandler is calling your name. Whether you’re craving classic treats or in search of innovative confections, you’ll find a delectable array of bakeries, pastry shops and ice cream parlors that will have exactly what you’re looking for. Stop by Crispy Cones for a grilled dough cone filled with soft serve ice cream or The Screamery, known for its handcrafted ice cream.

Swing into paradise

From innovative art galleries to renowned restaurants, Downtown Chandler has got it all. But did you know it also has an 18-hole, USGA championship golf course? The historic San Marcos Golf Course offers some of the best golfing in town thanks to its tree-lined fairways, manicured greens and sparkling water features. Just steps away from the Crowne Plaza Resort, it’s the perfect place to hit the links then enjoy all downtown has to offer.

Play a game of padel

Have fun and unwind under one roof at Padeland, where padel and pickleball courts, craft beers, and authentic Mexican dishes come together.

bodyHtml:
You have 24 hours to spend in Chandler. What should you do? The options are endless, so we’ve created an itinerary to help point you in the right direction, from sunup to sundown, breakfast to dinner, and everything in between. Extend your stay and experience a fun-filled 24 hours in Chandler, AZ!

Rise and Shine in Nature: 6 a.m.

Set your clock for a picturesque sunrise and explore the exquisite flora and fauna of the Sonoran Desert via a hot air balloon ride, a horseback ride or a trail hike as the day breaks. Regardless of your view, our stunning natural surroundings make it easy to be an early riser with a fresh perspective.

Visualize the Arts: 9 a.m.

After enjoying the most important meal of the day at a Chandler breakfast spot, hit the streets with a cup of local Joe to explore the artistic street murals that dot the landscape and showcase the city’s expressive, cultural diversity and heritage. You also can visit Chandler Center for the Arts to view rotating art exhibitions and the Chandler Museum, which features educational programming, historical archival materials and traveling exhibits.

Grab a Nourishing Bite: Noon

You have numerous options for lunch in Chandler, with a lineup of eateries, cafes and regional chains that focus on sourcing ingredients from local purveyors—sometimes with a twist. Your choices include sandwich joints, pizzerias, elevated gastro pubs, European bistros and authentic global cuisines including Mexican and Southwestern flavors for your midday meal needs.

Schedule Time for Retail Therapy: 2 p.m.

After lunch, clock some retail therapy (and steps) at the many local boutiques and independent shops found throughout Downtown Chandler, where you’ll also find a weekend farmers market filled with handcrafted produce and gifts crafted by local growers and artisans. You also can head to the Chandler Fashion Center, the second largest mall in the Phoenix metro area, or the Premium Outlets, with savings of up to 65 percent off luxury brands.

Make the Rounds: 4 p.m.

Check in for happy hour and sample some of Chandler’s specialty pours, particularly its local beer culture with multiple taprooms that feature one-of-a-kind brews. If you want to learn the science behind the craft, book a tour with SanTan Garden, which includes stops along each stage of the brewing and fermenting process at Arizona’s largest combined brewery and distillery.

Refuel at Dinner: 7 p.m.

Round out your meal plan with a mouth-watering dinner in Chandler, a foodie destination where you can dress up or down and savor a range of cuisines and award-winning dining atmospheres, from casual hangouts to chef-driven restaurants, craft breweries and fine dining. Plus, you can take in one of our world-class sunsets from the patio-friendly spaces that are popular among the eclectic dining scene here.

Check In After Hours: 9 p.m.

Live music, dancing and a dose of humor are the perfect way to wrap up a fun-filled day in Chandler. Depending on what entertainment box you want to tick, the city’s late-night venues cover the after-hours gamut. From speakeasys to honky-tonks, and folk and jazz clubs, you won’t miss a late-night beat. You can even tickle your funny bone at Mic Drop Comedy Chandler in Downtown Chandler, where you might just become part of the act!

bodyHtml:
Whether you’re craving fluffy pancakes, savory omelets, bloody marys or Arizona-inspired comfort food, Chandler has a breakfast spot to satisfy every palate. From trendy cafés to cozy diners, here are some of the city’s top morning eateries where you can fuel up for the day ahead.

U.S. Egg

Family owned and operated since 1986, U.S. Egg serves hearty traditional breakfasts. Dig into biscuits and gravy, omelets, Benedicts or their signature protein pancakes made with blueberries, homemade granola, almonds and cinnamon. You’ll find plenty of healthy options on the menu, too, including vegan waffles and avocado toast, and the coffee is so good, the restaurant sells it by the bag. Breakfast is served daily from 6:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. and can be enjoyed on the patio, as well as inside or ordered to go.

Hash Kitchen

Despite its name, Hash Kitchen dishes up more than skillets filled with tasty corned beef and crispy potatoes. It offers classic breakfast entrées like eggs over easy and pancakes, as well as creative offerings like s’mores French toast and cannoli donuts, sugar-dusted fried dough with a sweet cannoli cream. Gluten-free options and a kids menu are available, too.

The restaurant also boasts Arizona’s largest Bloody Mary bar with more than 40 toppings and a full bar crafting morning cocktails and fruity mimosas. If you’re feeling adventurous, sample a Cereal Flight Shooter, four shots of cereal-infused, spiked coconut milk, as you listen to the DJ spin tunes. Hash Kitchen opens daily at 7 a.m.

Downtown Chandler Café and Bakery

Local favorite Downtown Chandler Café and Bakery makes everything from scratch daily, using only the freshest ingredients. That includes the ciabatta bread served as toast, the fresh-baked pastries in the case, and the homemade granola you can order for breakfast. Get there at 7 a.m. when the restaurant opens for the best selection.

For breakfast, choose from traditional dishes like the two-egg American breakfast, waffles, or cheese omelet. Or chow down on a Southwestern breakfast like chilaquiles, featuring tortilla chips smothered in red chili sauce and topped with two eggs. Can’t decide? You can’t go wrong with the Ranchero skillet: home fries, chorizo, scrambled eggs, and fresh toppings served with two corn tortillas.

First Watch

Focused on all things fresh, dishes at First Watch are made in-house with seasonal ingredients, from cage-free eggs to their made-from-scratch pancake batter. With two Chandler locations, on in south Chandler and the other on the west side, this popular spot offers a refreshing take on morning classics.

In the mood for something sweet? Try the seasonal Hawaiian French toast made with thick-cut challah bread topped with caramelized pineapple, coconut whipped cream, caramel toffee sauce and spiced gingerbread cookie crumbles. If you’re leaning towards something on the healthy side, order up a serving of steel-cut oatmeal or a superfoods bowl filled with coconut chia seed pudding, fresh fruit, and house made granola. Breakfast is served daily from 7 a.m. to 2:30 p.m.

Eggstasy

As the name implies, eggs reign supreme at this southeast Chandler eatery, where every dish is a celebration of farm fresh flavors. Dive into their menu filled with creative twists on breakfast classics, like the fried truffle egg brioche made with fried eggs, fontina cheese and truffle butter, or the Greek huevos rancheros featuring Hatch chiles, peppers, feta, fried eggs and oregano.

The vibrant and inviting atmosphere makes this the perfect spot for a leisurely brunch with friends and family. And speaking of brunch, choose a drink from the “fun bar” offering such favorites as a blood orange mimosa, chocolate-covered bacon Bloody Mary, sparkling pomegranate punch, boozy salted caramel iced coffee, and spiked sweet tea. Breakfast service begins at 7 a.m. every day.

Over Easy

Experience breakfast done right at Over Easy, where an innovative menu features unique creations. If you light up at the thought of golden-fried goodness, try the Golden Waffle Dogs, a fun take on a corn dog featuring sausage links dipped in a vanilla waffle batter and deep fried to perfection. Or try the aptly-named Crying Pig omelet filled with bacon, sausage, onion and Swiss cheese. 

Featured on the Food Network’s “Diners, Drive-Ins & Dives,” this retro-inspired eatery is a Chandler favorite go-to spot for a hearty and satisfying breakfast, from mouth-watering pancakes—cheekily referred to “breakfast cakes”—and crispy bacon. For good measure, enjoy your breakfast with a mimosa flight, featuring your choice of classic orange, peach, prickly pear, mango, strawberry and raspberry. The both the Downtown Chandler location and west Chandler location open at 6:30 a.m. daily.

Bisbee Breakfast Club

Get a taste of Arizona history at this charming spot that made its way from Bisbee to locations throughout the state, including right here in Chandler. Unique to this location, it is the only one offering a full bar with delicious cocktails. Indulge in their mouthwatering house favorites such as the chicken fried steak, filet and eggs, and Bandit’s Brisket Scramble made with eggs, smoked brisket, green onions and cheddar jack cheese. Here, every meal feels like a comforting home-cooked feast.

For the ultimate Arizona experience on a plate, order the Copper Queen Skillet featuring home fries topped with scrambled eggs, ground bacon, ham, sausage, red onion, spicy sausage gravy and cheddar jack cheese. Enjoy your meal in a cozy and inviting ambiance that creates the perfect setting for a leisurely breakfast or brunch, with friendly staff ready to make you feel right at home. Breakfast is served seven days a week from 6 a.m. to 2:05 p.m.

Broken Yolk

If hearty portions of classic breakfast dishes are your idea of the perfect morning, make your way to the Broken Yolk. Get lost in their extensive menu featuring everything from fluffy omelets to stacked pancakes to hefty breakfast burritos.

Standout items include the crunchy French toast made with extra-thick slices of bread rolled in crunchy frosted flakes and sprinkled with almonds, raspberries and powdered sugar. There’s also the Sope Benedict, a unique take on traditional eggs Benedict that features sopes (fried corn tortilla) filled with shredded beef and topped with poached eggs, ranchero sauces, avocado, salsa, cotija cheese and sour cream. Restaurant hours are 7 a.m. to 2 p.m. Monday to Friday, 6 a.m. to 3 p.m. Saturday and Sunday.

 

From established favorites to new trendy eateries, explore more delicious options for breakfast and brunch in Chandler.

headings.text: Best Spots for Happy Hour in Chandler AZ

bodyHtml:
Whether you’re looking to unwind with coworkers or grab a few drinks with friends after exploring the city, Chandler has you covered. From the vibrant streets of Downtown Chandler to hidden gems throughout the area, this city boasts an impressive array of restaurants and bars featuring happy-hour food and drink specials. 

Note: Happy hour deals are typically for dine-in only and are subject to change.

Downtown Chandler

Featured Spots: Bourbon Jacks American Tavern and The Sleepy Whale

Downtown Chandler is home to Bourbon Jacks American Tavern, an All-American hotspot known for live music, dancing, and a menu packed with delicious food and drinks. Enjoy deals on well drinks and domestic drafts, paired with appetizer specials like fully loaded brisket tater tots or crispy fried pickles.

Happy Hour: Monday through Friday, 2 to 7 p.m.

Head to The Sleepy Whale, a laid-back beer bar and bottle shop offering discounts on select draft beers (50 cents to $2 off) and $2 off wine pours. With indoor and outdoor seating, it’s perfect for casual get-togethers after work. Don’t miss their exciting events!

Happy Hour: Monday through Friday, 11 a.m. to 5 p.m.

East Chandler

Featured Spots: Tryst Cafe and Modern Margarita

Known for its fresh, organic ingredients, Tryst Cafe offers $8 bites like creamy hummus with pita and beer-battered green beans. Pair them with $8 cocktails such as the Rock Candy Martini or a Mojito. House wine is $6, red sangria is $7, and drafts are $1 off. 

Happy Hour: Daily, 3 to 6 p.m.

Modern Margarita is a vibrant Mexican restaurant that combines quality spirits, flavorful small plates, and a laid-back atmosphere. Indulge in $7 dishes like loaded nachos and veggie tostadas. Choose from $5 select beers, $7 house wines, $7 well drinks, or featured tequila for $7. Signature cocktails include the OG Rustic, OG Rita, and the Frozen Margarita at this Chandler happy hour.Happy Hour: Monday through Saturday, 3 to 7 p.m.; Sunday, 10 a.m. to close.

Near Chandler Fashion Center 

Featured Spots: The Sicilian Butcher and Thirsty Lion

After shopping at Chandler Fashion Center, head to The Sicilian Butcher for happy hour, available every day. Enjoy deals on wine, craft beer, well spirits, and select cocktails, as well as a special offer on a bottle of wine paired with a charcuterie board. On Wine Wednesdays, savor 50% off select bottles, and don’t miss the Sicilian tapas available for just $8 any day of the week for one of the best happy hours in Chandler.

Happy Hour: All day, every day

Thirsty Lion is a vibrant gastropub and scratch kitchen celebrated for its extensive selection of craft cocktails, beer, and wine. Patrons can enjoy discounted premium well drinks, $2 off all draft pints, select wines, and cocktails like the Thirsty Lion Margarita and Moscow Mule. You’ll also find Chandler happy hour specials on shareable plates such as creamy queso dip, spicy fried cauliflower, and sushi rolls.

Happy Hour: Daily, 3 to 6 p.m.; Thursday through Saturday, 9 p.m. to close (extended hours).

South Chandler

Featured Spot: St. Amand Kitchen & Cocktails

St. Amand Kitchen & Cocktails is a cocktail-themed restaurant in South Chandler that combines chef-inspired dishes with a stylish and inviting atmosphere. Happy hour specials include deals on signature wines, cocktails, draft beer, and dishes like fried chicken sliders and short rib tacos. Don’t miss Wine Down Wednesdays, where you can enjoy 50% off bottles of wine.

Happy Hour: Monday through Friday, 3 to 6 p.m.

Uptown Chandler

Featured Spot: The Sugar Bar

The Sugar Bar in Uptown Chandler is a craft beer and wine taproom and bottle shop featuring $1 off all drafts and wine pours. Additional weekly deals include Thirsty Thursday, with discounts on wine bottles and growler fills.  

Happy Hour: Monday through Friday, starting at 6:30 p.m.

West Chandler

Featured Spot: Z'Tejas

Check out Z'Tejas, a favorite in West Chandler, for bold flavors and unbeatable happy hour deals. Enjoy drink specials like $6 house margaritas, $2 off all margaritas, $2 off wine, and $5 draft beers. Pair your drinks with mouthwatering food specials, including $5 yuca fries, $7 gringo Tacos a la carte, and catfish beignets for $9 making it one of the best options for enjoying happy hour in Chandler, AZ .

Happy Hour: Tuesday through Friday, 3 to 6 p.m.

Downtown Ocotillo

Featured Spot: The Trophy Bar

Happy hour at The Trophy Bar in Downtown Ocotillo offers great deals on drinks and bites in a lively atmosphere. This sleek, modern bar is a haven for fans of sports, cars, and spirits, featuring a massive video wall perfect for catching the game. Whether you're there for the specials or the vibe, The Trophy Bar is an ideal spot to relax and enjoy good company.

Happy Hour: Monday through Friday, 3 to 6 p.m.

bodyHtml:
Live music makes a great day even better and in Chandler, you’ll have no problem finding it at local restaurants, coffeehouses and bars. Whether you’re into acoustic sets, classic rock or Elvis tributes, these spots bring the sound and the vibes.

Looking for what’s happening this weekend? Be sure to check out Downtown Chandler Live, an excellent resource for live music in Chandler this weekend, plus details on upcoming shows, venues and more.

Here are some of the best Chandler restaurants for live music, with a mix of styles, bites and beverages.

The Stillery

Located in the heart of Downtown Chandler, The Stillery is where Southern-style comfort food meets a Nashville-style honky-tonk vibe. It’s one of the prime music spots in Chandler, especially when the place comes alive with high-energy sets from artists like Bobby Joe Bell, the Southbound Band, and touring Nashville acts such as Mitch Clarke and Matt Marinchick. Whether you’re craving hot chicken or just looking to dance the night away, this is one of the best Downtown Chandler restaurants with live music, especially if you’re into country, rock or pop with a side of bourbon.

What to order: The Hot Chicken sandwich and a Kentucky Mule.

Cork & Craft

Perfect for wine lovers who appreciate an elevated menu and smooth live music, Cork & Craft feels like an intimate hideaway tucked into Chandler’s bustling dining scene. Live music takes center stage here Tuesday through Saturday nights, with an impressive lineup that complements the refined, relaxed atmosphere. Recent acts include Danny Austin, whose modern country sound sets a feel-good tone; Chad Wilson Bailey, known for a genre-blending set that spans classic rock, blues, Motown, alt-rock and pop; and Painted Soul, who bring the energy with their vibrant mix of R&B, funk and pop.

What to order: The pesto margherita flatbread and a red wine flight.

Legends Showcase Music Hall

A rising star in the Chandler music scene, Legends Showcase brings a sophisticated twist to live entertainment. Founded by acclaimed performer Mike Russell, whose Elvis tribute act was named one of the top 20 in the nation, the venue celebrates the golden age of music with a mix of local talent and tribute artists that know how to captivate a crowd.

What to order: Try the Legends Steak with a classic Old Fashioned.

Good Time Charli’s Neighborhood Craft Pub

Gastro food pub Good Time Charli’s has something for everyone, including live music. Most performers play classic rock or country with the occasional DJ, jam session or karaoke to round things out. In addition to daily music, Good Time Charli’s has daily deals on food. Come on Tuesday for a tasty taco platter special, Wednesday for whiskey and wings, or Friday for a fabulous fish fry. You can also enjoy specials on brunch cocktails on the weekends.

What to order: Their pepperoni and cheese garlic knots pair perfectly with an ice-cold local beer.

Singing Pandas Asian Restaurant & Bar

Dinner and a show? Absolutely. At Singing Pandas Asian Restaurant & Bar, you’ll find delicious Chinese classics paired with nightly entertainment that goes well beyond your typical dinner music. The venue features live performances most nights of the week (they’re closed Mondays), including Talent Tuesdays, a showcase of up-and-coming singers and performers; Bingo Singo Wednesdays, which mixes music trivia, bingo and a whole lot of laughs; and Las Vegas-style variety shows throughout the week that channel the glitz and glam of The Strip right here in Chandler.

What to order: The green curry chicken is flavorful and just the right amount of spicy.

SoZo Coffeehouse

There are many reasons to visit SoZo Coffeehouse. Not only does it serve great coffee drinks, herbal teas and lattes, but it donates a portion of every purchase to local or international causes such as the Arizona Humane Society, The Water Project, and Feed My Starving Children. Live acoustic sets and jazz performances fill the air most Thursday through Saturday nights. And if you’ve got talent, sign up for an open mic night.

What to order: The Moroccan mint green tea hits just right for a low-key night.

headings.text: 5 Things to Know About the Chandler International Film Festival

bodyHtml:
Each January, the Chandler International Film Festival (CIFF) brings filmmakers, artists, and audiences together to celebrate award-winning films from around the world.  The festival will screen more than 120 films from 35 countries showcasing a diverse range of genres. Held from January 19 to 28 at LOOK Dine-In Cinema in Downtown Chandler, the 2024 festival is in its eighth year and has expanded into a week-long event with free downtown parking.

Highlights include an opening night ceremony, red carpet events, interactive workshops, film screenings, and special celebrity appearances by such actors as Cuba Gooding Jr., Eric Roberts, and Dean Norris, among many others. The 10-day event culminates in an Oscar-inspired gala complete with red carpet entrance, gourmet dinner and awards presentations.

This year’s event is also being held in partnership with the City of Chandler’s 29th annual Multicultural Festival, designed to honor the city’s heritage and diversity. Here’s what else you can expect at the 2024 Chandler International Film Festival.

Films Galore

With more than 120 films being screened, movie buffs won’t have any trouble finding the perfect flick to sit back, relax and enjoy. Genres include thriller, horror, comedy, documentary, and animation. Buzz-worthy films include the world premieres of “Third Wheel,” a millennial coming-of-age breakup story; and “Guardians,” which tells the story of a charismatic minister who works with guardian angels to save people from modern-day, life-threatening situations.

Opening Night

The festival kicks off with red carpet festivities at LOOK on January 19. Don your best formal wear and mingle with the likes of filmmakers and actors, including Mallory Everton, Colin Mochrie and Jason Gray, stars of “Villains Inc.,” a film three co-workers left destitute and living in an abandoned grocery store after the death of their boss.

Party into the Night

Each night of the film festival concludes with an after-party where you can meet filmmakers and enjoy local sips and bites at spots like Recreo Cantina, La Ristra New Mexican Kitchen, The Uncommon, The Stillery, DTC Sports Grille, West Alley BBQ, Craft 64, and The Perch.

Workshop It

Festival-goers can register for a variety of workshops taught by professionals, including Jon Fitzgerald, who will teach the ins and outs of entering your film in a festival; Sean Dillingham, who will cover the finer points of improv and scene study; and Spero Stamboulis, who will lead a film distribution workshop. You’re also invited to participate in “Coffee Connections” events featuring conversations with representatives from the Arizona Film Commission, Chandler mayor Kevin Hartke, and actor Patrick Kilpatrick.

And the Award Goes To…

The festival wraps up with a glamorous awards ceremony at SoHo63, where winners from multiple categories will be announced, including best new filmmaker, best feature film, and best international film.

bodyHtml:
Chandler’s newest full-service hotel, Marriott Phoenix Chandler, offers a new option for business travelers and for Chandler meetings. Here are five things you should know about it.

1. It’s the tallest occupied building in Chandler

The Marriott Phoenix Chandler stands eight stories, making it the tallest occupied building in Chandler. Of its 264 rooms, 74 have mountain views while a majority of the remaining rooms overlook the manicured landscapes of neighboring corporations. The hotel backs to Gila River Indian Community lands.

Not surprisingly, rooms on the seventh and eighth floors offer the best views and are reserved for Bonvoy Elite members (although you can upgrade to these floors). Guests on these floors also have access to M Club, the hotel’s exclusive lounge where they can enjoy complimentary breakfast, hors d’oeuvres, sodas, and Starbucks coffee.

2. It’s one of Chandler’s most environmentally friendly hotels

The Marriott Phoenix Chandler boasts several environmentally friendly practices. Like many hotels, it gives you the option to reuse your linens and towels, but it also has a Green Choice program that awards you 500 Bonvoy points for each day of declined housekeeping service (excluding your checkout date). Save your points or donate them to Marriott’s Plant-a-Tree program.

Additionally, Marriott has implemented a new in-room dining service, Fresh Bites, that uses only environmentally-friendly packaging, eliminating the need to wash dishes and utensils. Thirsty? Bring your water bottle, and refill it at the hotel’s water stations located on every floor.

3. It celebrates local flavors and ingredients

You don’t have to leave Marriott Phoenix Chandler to sample local flavors. At Proof 19, bartenders craft cocktails featuring local ingredients like the prickly pear syrup combined with Tanteo Habanero Tequila and pineapple juice to create the bar’s signature drink, the Javelina.

For a “true taste of Arizona,” try Café MeSo. The restaurant serves American cuisine with Southwest and Mediterranean twists for breakfast, lunch and dinner. If you want to taste local flavors, Chef Juan Vasquez-Santos recommends the fried avocado sandwich, featuring a crispy avocado seasoned with the spices of his childhood, greens, heirloom tomato, chipotle aioli and roasted red pepper on a brioche bun.

4. It’s great for business

Located along the Price Corridor across the street from Northrop Grumman, the Marriott Phoenix Chandler was designed for the business traveler. All rooms feature Wi-Fi twice the standard hotel room speed, larger-than-usual mini-fridges, plenty of convenient outlets and keyless entry. You can even check in and out using the Marriott app.

The hotel also boasts the largest conference room in the area. At 10,100 square feet, it can accommodate 720 people at tables and up to 1,000 without tables. There’s an additional 4,000 square feet of pre-function space, as well as five breakout rooms, each with wall-mounted TVs. Additional areas are available for classes, meetings and events.

5. It has a state-of-the-art fitness center

The fitness center at the Marriott Phoenix Chandler isn’t your typical windowless room with a few treadmills and a set of free weights. Bright and open, it features treadmills, a stair stepper, and a Peloton bike, which gives you access to more than 10,000 pre-recorded spin classes with 15 high-energy instructors. Choose from 20-, 30-, 45-, 60- or 90-minute rides.

Or take a virtual fitness class. Content ranges from yoga to strength training and more. Available equipment for classes or personal use in the fitness center includes kettle ball, yoga mats, exercise balls and dumbbells. If you prefer to exercise outside, the hotel has a swimming pool, too.

ld.articleBody: An early flight, a meeting-packed schedule and a client dinner can push exercise off your calendar while traveling for business. Chandler makes it easy to stay active on these trips with city paths, single-class studio passes, hotel gyms, shorter golf options and appointment-based recovery.

headings.text: Ways to Stay Active While Traveling for Business in Chandler, AZ
Start Your Day with a Walk
Turn Networking into an Active Experience
Fit in a Workout Without a Membership
Take Your Business Trip to the Fairway
Build an Active Chandler Business Trip Itinerary

bodyHtml:
An early flight, a meeting-packed schedule and a client dinner can push exercise off your calendar while traveling for business. Chandler makes it easy to stay active on these trips with city paths, single-class studio passes, hotel gyms, shorter golf options and appointment-based recovery. Conference attendees, remote workers and bleisure travelers can choose the activities that work best around their commitments. 

 

Start Your Day with a Walk

Treat morning movement like any item on your pre-work day agenda. Set the duration, choose the location for the evening before, and place your walking shoes by the door. 

Veterans Oasis Park opens at 6 a.m. and offers several choices for a morning walk in southeast Chandler. Among them, a 0.4-mile paved path circles a 5-acre lake, while 4.5 miles of groomed dirt trails cross the 113-acre park. That layout lets you take one lap or cover more ground without committing to the full trail network. 

In the heart of the city, Downtown Chandler is a walkable district with shops, restaurants and public gathering spaces. This compact downtown core puts City Hall, the Historic Square and key landmarks within close reach.  

History buffs can take the self-guided downtown walking tour featuring 11 historic buildings and sites, including the original City Hall, First National Bank Building and the San Marcos Hotel. 

For a canal walk, look to the Paseo Trail. It follows the eastern side of the Consolidated Canal along a 6.5-mile, 10-foot-wide concrete path. Walk as far as your morning allows, including retracing your steps to get back in time. 

 

Turn Networking into an Active Experience

Move beyond traditional networking environments and invite a colleague to a walking meeting, putting the topic plus turnaround time in the calendar invitation. A 30-minute or 1-hour block suits introductions, project updates or a conversation that goes beyond the screen.  

Take the discussion to Desert Breeze Park, where the waterfront scenery and uninterrupted path encourage conversation, or choose Tumbleweed Park for its wide-open green spaces and quieter atmosphere that feels far removed from the office. 

Another idea: meet in Downtown Chandler at Peixoto Coffee. Its crop-to-cup story begins at the Peixoto family farm in Brazil, where many of the beans served in Chandler are grown. Pick up your drinks and check out downtown murals that reflect the city’s history, growth and diverse community, while continuing the conversation in a setting that feels more creative and engaging than a conference room. 

 

Fit in a Workout Without a Membership 

When your schedule is tight, the details matter more than the gym or studio size. Compare class length and cancellation policies as you explore fitness options and book the one that works best for you. 

FLO Yoga & Cycle sells drop-ins across all formats. Its class menu covers 45- to 60-minute yoga flows, mat Pilates, cycling, FLEX and Fusion Restore. This final offering combines a 30-minute high-energy ride and 30 minutes of deep stretching. Book online beforehand and check availability for current reservation windows for non-members. 

Sumits Yoga Chandler provides hot, gently heated and nonheated classes. Buy one class or select the Just Visiting three-class pack, which includes a mat, towel and water at each session.  

Your lodging may remove the extra drive for a workout altogether, as many options include fitness centers. For instance, hotel guests at Marriott Phoenix Chandler can use treadmills, ellipticals, exercise bikes, stair climbers, free weights and strength equipment. Guests staying at the Element Chandler Fashion Center can also check out a loaner bike, including helmet and bike lock, for a fun way to explore and unwind on their travels.

Take Your Business Trip to the Fairway 

Golfing in Chandler fits into a few free hours or a smaller gap in the day, whether you play a quick round or head straight to the practice range. Golf also works for meetings when you want to talk business outside the meeting room. 

Bear Creek Golf Complex gives you a realistic shot at playing 18 holes without giving up half the day. Its Cub Course is executive length with an expected pace of about 2 hours 40 minutes, playing 3,552 yards at par 59. Short on time? Use the practice range, short-game area or one of two putting greens. 

In South Chandler, Springfield Golf Resort provides a relaxed, player-friendly par‑61 course. Wide fairways and a shorter layout make it perfect for beginners, younger players, and those looking to finish a round in under three and a half hours.

Another option, Ocotillo Golf Club, has a double-ended driving range with 24 stations that use grass or simulated-turf tees, plus a putting green and a chipping green. The club sells daily range access separately from a round. Check seasonal hours and maintenance closures before your visit. 

 

Prioritize Recovery & Wellness 

Recovery deserves a protected time slot after flights, long meetings or exercise. Chandler offers several recovery options, including focused assisted stretching and spa visits. Many lodging properties also offer swimming pools, a hot tub and other amenities that make it easy to fit relaxation into a busy schedule.  

StretchLab Chandler books personalized, one-on-one assisted stretching in 25- or 50-minute sessions. A Flexologist reviews your personal movement assessment, identifies key focus areas and imbalances and guides an assisted stretch tailored to your needs. That fixed duration may work well between your final meeting and dinner. 

The NOW Massage Chandler offers 25-, 50- and 80-minute massage appointments. Choose a Swedish-inspired, energy-balancing or sports-inspired massage, with enhancements such as deep tissue, gliding cupping and crystal hot stones also available. Walk-ins are welcome, but scheduling ahead is recommended due to high demand. 

Set aside enough room around your appointment so you don’t have to rush. The NOW asks guests to arrive 15 minutes early for check-in, so a 50-minute massage needs at least a 65-minute opening on your work calendar, not including travel time.  

 

Build an Active Chandler Business Trip Itinerary  

Use this sample itinerary as a framework, adjusting each block to fit your meeting location(s), the forecast, and your transportation plans. 

Morning: Grab coffee at Downtown Chandler Café and Bakery and take a walk through Downtown Chandler. If you want more time outdoors, drive to Veterans Oasis Park for a stroll around the lake or along its trail system. Carry water and leave enough time to cool down, eat breakfast and get ready for conference sessions or meetings. 

Lunch: Take a short walk before or after lunch downtown at George & Gather, a full-scratch, seed-oil-free kitchen. Its Harvest Bowl combines roasted sweet potato, bell pepper, zucchini, quinoa, tomatoes, avocado, pine nuts, house-made pesto and arugula, with chicken or pan-seared salmon available if you want to add protein.  

Afternoon: Return to meetings or remote work. When the location and time permit, take a brief walk between appointments. 

Evening: If there’s still daylight after meetings, stop by Springfield Golf Resort and hit a bucket of balls at the public practice range, which typically stays open until sunset. If you’d rather wind down after a long day, book an assisted stretch or massage, or spend some time relaxing by the pool at your hotel. 

Healthy business travel doesn’t require a flawless routine. One planned walk and one well-timed workout, golf session or recovery appointment can add movement to a work trip while keeping your agenda on track. Chandler delivers enough variety to scale that plan up or down if your work schedule changes. 

Ready to put together the rest of your trip? Plan your visit with more ideas for getting around, where to stay and things to do between meetings.

headings.text: A Bird's Eye View of The Perch in Chandler, AZ

bodyHtml:
The Perch is the type of brewery you tell friends about—the beer is outstanding, live music plays five nights a week, and the misted patio is home to more than 70 rescue birds. It also boasts one of the best rooftops in the Valley following a $1.5 million renovation that tripled its size.

“We hear that it’s like being in Las Vegas when you’re on the roof,” says owner Rebecca Lavenue. “There are high-end, stainless steel designer panels and an upgraded lighting system. We used a crane to get a 1957 Grumman bread truck up there.”

The truck serves shareable foods available only on the roof, including three types of tacos, two bruschetta options, house made chicharrons, and meatball sliders. Munch on these as you sip a cold beer from one of the rooftop’s 60 taps, some of which are exclusive to the upstairs bar.

Adding to that Vegas atmosphere, the roof has 11 new TVs, and music plays most nights and twice on Saturday and Sunday.

However, one of the most appreciated upgrades is the addition of four bathrooms on the roof. “People are glad they don’t have to go downstairs anymore,” Lavenue says.

You don’t need a reservation to enjoy the rooftop. The 6,000-square-foot area can accommodate more than 400 people and is perfect for a group outing. During the summer, it’s open Wednesday and Thursday from 6 to 11 p.m., Friday from 6 p.m. to 1 a.m., Saturday from noon to 1 a.m., and Sunday from noon to 10 p.m.

The rooftop wasn’t the only part of the Chandler brewery that got a makeover; the patio expanded from 600 to 1,200 seats. By removing a building on the property, Lavenue says she was not only able to increase the number of tables, but to also spread them out, allowing guests to better maintain their social distance from one another.

What hasn’t changed is the great beer and food. The Perch Brewery taps an eclectic mix of beers brewed onsite, ranging from the popular All Saints Hefe, a refreshing hefeweizen, to the Sweet Potato Fi, a sour. Not in the mood for beer? Try an Adult Capri Sun, a spiked pouch drink concocted by the brewery’s creative mixologists, or a glass of wine.

In addition to burgers, tots, and other pub fares, The Perch serves seared salmon, pork shank, braised beef short rib, and woodfired pizza for dinner and salad, wraps, and sandwiches for lunch. On the weekends, come for brunch to sample egg-topped tamales, chicken and waffles, or buttermilk pancakes.

Located in Downtown Chandler, The Perch is open Tuesday through Thursday from 4 to 11 p.m., Friday 11 a.m. to 1 a.m., Saturday from 9 a.m. to 1 a.m., and Sunday from 9 a.m. to 10 p.m. Happy hour runs Tuesday through Thursday from 4 to 6 p.m. with drink specials that include $2 off The Perch beers, $1 off well liquor, and $1 off house wines, as well as $6 appetizer specials.

Map: 232 S. Wall St., Chandler AZ 85225 or (480) 773-7688

Step into the Outdoors and Explore Nature
Hit Your Steps Inside the Mall

bodyHtml:
Walking 10,000 steps a day doesn’t just boost your health — it’s a fun way to explore Chandler’s best spots. In addition to great local hiking trails, discover scenic parks and colorful murals, local eats, and unique attractions for walking in Chandler. Here’s how to hit your step goal while experiencing all the city has to offer on foot.

 

 

Ready, Set, Eat

Start your day off right with a pedometer and a delicious breakfast in Chandler. Eggstasy, a popular breakfast spot, takes pride in its commitment to quality and is known for its mostly made-from-scratch menu featuring a great selection of healthy and indulgent breakfast dishes.

 

Fuel up with a variety of options, including eggs, omelets, crepes, Benedicts, French toast, skillets, as well as soups, salads, and burgers. Don't forget to try their fresh-squeezed juices, and for a lighter option, consider the Skinny Elvis Protein Cakes to help you stay light on your feet.

Location: 2430 S. Gilbert Road, Chandler AZ 85286 or (480) 361-9275

Step into the Outdoors and Explore Nature

Experience the beauty of Veterans Oasis Park, a 113-acre mixed-use urban park and wetlands habitat featuring 4.5 miles of trails for walking, running, horseback riding, and biking, all centered on a picturesque lake. If you're visiting with children, you can enrich your outing with an educational adventure on the Solar System Walk, where you can explore the journey to the moon and back. Don’t forget to share your discovery photos on social media by tagging @VisitChandler!

Note: Wear comfortable shoes and carry water — the desert climate can heat up quickly.

Location:  4050 E. Chandler Heights Road, Chandler AZ 85249

Refuel in Downtown Chandler

 

Lunch & Food in Downtown Chandler

After charting some distance in the park, recharge with a lunch in Downtown Chandler, offering free parking and more than 40 diverse restaurants and bars with cuisine that suits everyone’s taste buds. Cuisine options in Downtown Chandler include prized pizza at Craft 64, Championship barbeque at Back Alley BBQ, or bold and flavor-filled dishes at one of Arizona’s award-winning breweries, SanTan Brewing Co. You’ll also find great cafes for sandwiches, street-style tacos, conveyor belt sushi, and more.

 

Street Art & Shopping Walk

Once you’ve refueled, hit the trellis-covered walkways on the square for a post-lunch calorie burn while you shop the local boutiques and stores. Or view vibrant street murals and public art installations (see this interactive map of displays showcasing the creative talents of local artists and helping tell the story of Chandler’s unique culture and history).Location: Along Arizona Avenue, just south of Chandler Blvd.

Discover Local Culture

Enhance your stroll by stopping at the Chandler Museum, where you can immerse yourself in the vibrant culture, rich history, and inspiring art of Chandler! You'll discover captivating public art, community-driven programs, and world-class traveling exhibits. Don’t forget to check out the Chandler Museum Store for delightful mementos that showcase our unique community. The charming campus also features inviting outdoor spaces and the historic McCullough-Price House for its historic architecture and local stories. The house is listed on the National Register of Historic Places and serves as a cutting-edge research and archive hub. It’s the perfect destination for both learning and enjoying Chandler's spirit!

Location: 300 S. Chandler Village Dr., Chandler AZ 85226 or (480) 782-2717

Hit Your Steps Inside the Mall

The Chandler Fashion Center is a great way to round out your step goal — with open walkways and plenty of reasons to keep moving between stores and outdoor spaces. This vibrant shopping hub boasts more than 180 upscale retailers, including favorites like Apple, Coach, and Kendra Scott, alongside beloved anchor stores such as Macy’s, Dillard's, and SCHEELS. After your shopping adventure, unwind in the adjacent outdoor entertainment village or treat yourself to a delicious meal. Check out The Mexicano, a trendy eatery near the mall entrance on the outer ring road, offering a Mexico City-inspired dining experience with a lively atmosphere.

Location: 3111 W. Chandler Blvd., Chandler AZ 85226 or (480) 812-8488

 

Whether you’re walking for health, adventure, or fun, this Chandler itinerary helps you reach 10,000 steps while discovering local favorites. Tag your steps with #VisitChandler for a chance to be featured!

bodyHtml:
Summer in Chandler brings not only great things to do with the kids, but it often brings our famous monsoon season and its unique weather hazards: short, intense storms full of cold rain and great walls of dust that can engulf the community. These short, desert storms also bring welcome cloud cover and cooler temperatures to hot summer days, and the rain brings a burst of life to the desert plants and local Chandlerites who love the rain. Of course, locals and photographers alike enjoy the dramatic skies during the Arizona monsoon system, which creates stunning sunsets, fierce lightning storms, and towering cloud systems that really showcase the desert landscape.

Monsoon storms can be dangerous, but by following a few safety tips, you can stay safe and enjoy the show from indoors. Discover more about monsoon storms and how to protect yourself here.

Right in the heart of Chandler and just a short walk from lots of dining and entertainment options, this resort is perfect whether you’re traveling for work, hitting the course, or just looking for a family getaway.

Relaxation with a modern touch

The resort has 249 recently renovated roomy guest accommodations, each designed to make you feel at home. Whether you’re sipping coffee on your private balcony or catching some sun on the patio, the Arizona vibes are unbeatable.

Inside, you’ll find little touches that make a big difference—like a spacious work desk with easy-access outlets, a mini fridge for your snacks, and a Keurig to get your mornings started right. After a long day, kick back with a 43-inch HDTV and enjoy the full bath amenities to unwind.

 

Food and drinks you’ll love

Start your day at AJ’s Café with a breakfast that’s both fresh and flavorful, whether you’re into hearty plates or lighter bites. When evening rolls around, the 1912 Lounge Bar and Grill is the go-to spot for a laid-back drink or catching up with friends. Don’t miss their monthly drink specials! If you’re in a rush, the 24-hour Marketplace has you covered with snacks and quick bites.

Feeling adventurous? The resort is located just steps from Downtown Chandler's 40+ vibrant restaurants and bars to enjoy all day long.

 

Golf, pools and the great outdoors

One of the highlights here? The 18-hole championship golf course. It’s a par-72, 6,500-yard course and holds the title of being “The Original Grass Golf Course” in Arizona. Whether you’re a pro or a newbie, the resort’s PGA pros offer both private and group lessons. Planning a corporate retreat or special event? They can set up custom golf tournaments and team-building activities that your group will love.

After hitting the greens, cool off by the outdoor resort pool or stroll through the garden courtyards, complete with cozy fire pits perfect for desert evenings. If you’re someone who likes to stay active, the 24-hour fitness center has everything you need. And if work calls, the fully equipped 24-hour business center will keep you connected.

 

Perfect for events big and small

Looking for a venue for your next meeting, wedding or special event? The Crowne Plaza Phoenix-Chandler Golf Resort has you covered with 32,000 square feet of flexible event space. They offer 16 meeting rooms, including a stylish hospitality suite and beautiful outdoor spaces. With full-service catering and customizable event planning, it’s a great pick for everything from corporate conferences to dream weddings.

Fun fact: The resort just celebrated its 111th anniversary in November 2024 (yep, it’s been a Chandler staple for over a century!). They’ve even participated in events like the Phoenix Bridal Show and the Downtown Chandler Wedding Walk, showing off their knack for creating unforgettable wedding experiences.

Historic charm with a modern touch

Along with its rich history, the resort has kept up with the times. They’ve added Tesla charging stations for eco-friendly travelers and offer free Wi-Fi in public areas and meeting rooms, so you’ll stay connected without a hitch.

 

Whether you’re in Chandler for business, a vacation, or a special event, the Crowne Plaza Phoenix-Chandler Golf Resort has the perfect mix of comfort, convenience, and that laid-back Southwestern charm. Book your stay and see why this resort has been a beloved part of Chandler’s story for over 100 years.
