bodyHtml:
When you’re in Chandler for work or a quick getaway, the evening offers several ways to unwind near local hotels. Downtown Chandler brings together great restaurants, breweries, live entertainment, and public art in a compact district. After meetings wrap up, you can step out for dinner, catch a performance, take a short stroll for dessert, or settle into a patio with a drink. If you prefer something quieter, cafés or hotel lounges provide a comfortable way to decompress.

 

Where to Eat Tonight (Near Hotels & Downtown)

When deciding where to eat in Chandler, The Stillery offers an easy starting point. Located near the heart of downtown, it combines comfort‑driven fare with an energetic atmosphere, featuring live music almost nightly, making it a natural place to start or end an evening out before exploring nearby restaurants and bars.

 

SanTan Brewing Company pairs Arizona craft beer with pub-style plates, making it a natural first stop after work. Just down the block, The Brickyard Downtown serves tapas-style plates and craft cocktails in a relaxed dining room with patio seating. If fine dining is more your speed, head to DC Steak House for steaks, seafood, and other dinner entrees.

 

Several restaurants feature patios, making outdoor dining highly appealing for much of the year. Many include heaters during the cooler months and misters in warmer weather, so guests can remain comfortable.

 

Catch Live Music or a Local Event

After dinner, music venues often provide the next stop. As one of the city’s primary entertainment spaces, the Chandler Center for the Arts hosts concerts, theater productions, and other performances throughout the year. For smaller shows, Murphy’s Law Irish Pub features live music and other activities in a casual pub setting, giving visitors a relaxed place to hear performers while enjoying food and drinks.

 

Looking to remain close to where you’re staying? Some hotel lounges schedule live entertainment or social events during the evening. Checking venue calendars or hotel events can help you find something happening. Because many of the most popular venues are located in the downtown district, reaching them from nearby hotels typically requires only a short ride.

 

If you’re up for a higher‑energy end to the evening, several casinos are located a short drive from Chandler’s hotel corridor, offering gaming, dining, and late‑night entertainment.

 

Walk & Browse Downtown Chandler

If you seek a slower pace after eating, the area offers a pedestrian-friendly setting for a walk. Streets throughout the district feature murals and sculptures that create an open-air gallery experience. A stroll might start near Dr. A. J. Chandler Park, which anchors the district and often hosts community events. From there, you can wander through streets that pass through local shops.

 

Many visitors turn this outing into a simple loop: dinner first, followed by a relaxed walk-through downtown before stopping for dessert or ice cream. One great option, The Screamery serves delicious small-batch ice cream pasteurized on-site at their locally owned facility. Hours vary by business, night, and season, but some shops, restaurants, and dessert spots stay open later on certain nights.

Nightcaps & Quiet Corners

To extend the evening, downtown includes several places suited for a drink. QuartHaus offers a beer garden setting with craft beer, wine, and lawn games. Hidden House serves classic cocktails, wine, and beer in a restored historic cottage, with indoor seating, a front courtyard, and a back patio. Guests who prefer a quieter atmosphere often settle into a table here for conversation.

 

Travelers seeking a calmer end to the evening sometimes return to their hotel for a drink in the lounge or order takeout from a restaurant. Maple House can also provide a relaxed place for conversation or a late coffee or cocktail before heading back. These options let you decide whether the night continues downtown or winds down close to your hotel.

 

Plan Your Visit & Enjoy Chandler at Night

A rewarding evening in the city can come together naturally. Start with dinner downtown. Next, take a short stroll or stop for dessert. After that, catch live music or visit a brewery or return to your hotel for a low-key night in. Downtown’s compact layout and mix of dining, arts, and nightlife options make it easy to build a plan without complicated logistics. Explore more ideas and plan your stay in Chandler.

bodyHtml:
From archery to ziplining, Chandler offers fun, unique experiences for every kind of adventurer. Whether you’re visiting for the first time or rediscovering your own backyard, here’s your ultimate A to Z guide to all the excitement Chandler, AZ has to offer.

A – Archery at Paseo Vista Recreation Area

Take aim in Chandler’s desert landscape at Paseo Vista Recreation Area’s scenic archery range. You’ll know you’re in the right place when you spot the massive arrow and bullseye at the entrance, perfect for a selfie before testing your skills with each shot.

B – Brewery Tour at SanTan Gardens

Go behind the scenes at SanTan Brewing Company’s brewing facility and learn how award-winning craft beer is made. After the tour, head to their Downtown Chandler pub for great food and a refreshing pint (or two).

C – Comedy Show at Mic Drop Comedy Chandler

Laugh the night away at Mic Drop Comedy, Chandler’s home for stand-up comedy. Catch nationally touring comedians or join the crowd for open mic night, where local talent takes the stage with quick, four-minute sets that’ll keep you entertained.

D – Discover Vintage Trains at the Arizona Railway Museum

Step back in time at the Arizona Railway Museum, where you can explore restored trains, cabooses and engines. With guided tours available for a fee and lots of exhibits, it’s a hit for history lovers and curious kids alike.

E – Escape Room at Escape Chandler

Put your puzzle-solving skills to the test at Escape Chandler. Choose from four themed rooms and race the clock to solve clues and break free. Each room gives your group 90 minutes to escape (and claim bragging rights).

F – Fishing at Veterans Oasis Park

Relax by the lake and try your luck at Veterans Oasis Park, where a 5-acre lake is stocked with catfish, trout and bass. Just make sure to grab a fishing license from the Arizona Game & Fish before you cast off.

G – Golfing at Ocotillo Golf Club

Challenge yourself at Ocotillo Golf Club, known for its 27 holes of water-lined fairways and stunning desert views. After your round, kick back at Tillo’s Kitchen & Patio with a cold drink and casual bite.

H – Historic Downtown Chandler

Stroll through historic Downtown Chandler, where century-old charm meets modern vibes. Browse quirky shops, grab a coffee, and enjoy live music or happy hour along its brick-lined streets.

I – Ice Skating at the Ice Den Chandler

Cool off and hit the rink at the Ice Den Chandler, where all ages can enjoy public skating. Need gear? The pro shop has you covered. Need a snack? Grab coffee, Dippin’ Dots, or a cold Icee from the Chilly Bean Café.

J – Japanese Cuisine at Shimogamo

Craving top-tier sushi? Head to Shimogamo, cone of the Valley’s best spots for Japanese cuisine. From signature rolls to traditional sashimi, every dish is artfully prepared. For something extra special, opt for the chef’s omakase experience.

K – KOLI Equestrian Center

Saddle up at KOLI Equestrian Center and take in the Sonoran Desert on horseback. No experience? No problem. Their wranglers will guide you on a scenic ride, whether you’re a seasoned rider or a first-timer.

L – Live Performance at Chandler Center for the Arts

Catch a show at the Chandler Center for the Arts, where concerts, plays and dance performances light up the stage. While you’re there, don’t miss the Gallery at CCA, featuring rotating exhibitions by local and national artists.

M – Mural Hunting in Downtown Chandler

Take a self-guided mural tour and discover Chandler’s street art scene. From bold, colorful walls to hidden alley gems, there’s something to spot around every corner. Check out our Chandler Mural Quest pass to find all the murals and win a souvenir to take home!

N – Nightlife at The Perch

Make your way to the rooftop bar at The Perch, where great drinks and skyline views make for a memorable night out. Enjoy craft cocktails, live music and a rooftop vibe that’s perfect for weekend hangs.

O – Open a Bottle at The Sleepy Whale

Part bar, part bottle shop, The Sleepy Whale is a cozy local hangout with a killer selection of craft beer and wine. The dog-friendly patio, chill vibe and take-home bottles make it ideal for a casual night with friends.

P – Public Art Tour

Chandler’s streets double as an open-air art gallery. From sculptures to large-scale installations, the city’s public art scene tells stories of local history and culture. For locations and a full list from the Chandler Arts Commission, check the Vision Gallery's public art information.

Q – Quizzes & Games at Game Show Battle Rooms

Feel like you’re on TV at Game Show Battle Rooms, where you and your crew compete in real-life versions of classic game shows. Think flashing lights, live hosts and fast-paced fun—perfect for team-building or just a good laugh.

R – Retail Therapy at Chandler Fashion Center

Shop till you drop at Chandler Fashion Center, with over 180 stores, tons of dining options, and fun extras like movie theaters and play areas. It’s more than a mall; it’s a one-stop destination for a full day of fun.

S – Street Tacos at Taqueria Factory

No visit to Chandler is complete without tacos, and Taqueria Factory delivers the goods. With two locations serving up street-style tacos, bold flavors and house-made salsas, it’s perfect for taco Tuesday (or really any day).

T – Trail Hiking at San Tan Mountain Regional Park

Whether you’re up for a tough climb or a casual stroll, San Tan Mountain Regional Park offers hiking trails for every level. Enjoy wide-open views, desert flora and a peaceful escape just outside the city.

U – Uptown Jungle Fun Park

Bounce, climb, zip and explore at Uptown Jungle Fun Park, Chandler’s ultimate indoor playground. Perfect for kids (and adventurous adults), this place is packed with obstacle courses, climbing walls and action-packed fun.

V – View the Vision Gallery

Located in Downtown Chandler, the Vision Gallery showcases thought-provoking works by both Arizona and regional artists in a variety of media, from sculpture to textiles to photography. It’s a small but mighty space that packs an artistic punch.

W – Wine Tasting at BlackSheep Wine Bar

Head to BlackSheep Wine Bar for a curated lineup of wines from around the world, all served in a relaxed, cozy setting. Located in a charming historic building, it’s a great place to unwind or explore something new from their reserve list.

X – Xtreme Play at Rush Fun Park Xtreme

Rush Fun Park Xtreme is made for thrill-seekers. Tackle an 18-foot skywalk, take flight on the bungee course, or drop 30 feet on the epic Drop Slide. It’s the perfect place to let loose…no matter your age.

Y – Yoga at FLO Yoga & Cycle

Stretch, strengthen, and unwind at FLO Yoga & Cycle, where experienced instructors lead classes for all levels in a calming, energizing studio space. Whether you’re new to yoga or a seasoned yogi, you’ll leave feeling refreshed.

Z – Zipline at Playtopia!

Located inside Tumbleweed Park, Playtopia! is a kid-friendly wonderland with themed play zones and, yes, a zipline! Little adventurers can fly through the air before exploring Farm Land, City Land, and Critter Land, complete with dino bones and giant tortoises.

bodyHtml:
It doesn’t matter whether you’re planning a bachelor, bachelorette, or co-ed party, Chandler can help you celebrate the upcoming nuptials with dinner, dancing, and more.  

SanTan Brewing Company

8 S. San Marcos Place
Chandler, AZ 85225
(480) 917-8700

One of the most popular breweries in the state, SanTan Brewing Company is a great option for a laid-back bachelor or bachelorette party or the perfect way to kick off an evening of festivities. Start with dinner. Entrées range from pizzas, salads, and burgers to fish and chips, pork enchiladas, and smoked beef briskets. Wash your meal down with a SanTan favorite brew like Mr. Pineapple or HopShock IPA, or try one of their seasonal offerings. Guest brews, cider, and wine are also available. 

Rooftop brews: The Perch, a nearby brewery in downtown Chandler, has a rooftop that can be rented for special events and parties.

Bourbon Jack’s 

11 W. Boston St.
Chandler, AZ 85225
(480) 664-1738

You don’t have to be a country music fan to kick up your heels on the dance floor or a bourbon aficionado to toast the groom (or bride) at Bourbon Jack’s, but if you are either, you won’t find a better place to party in the Valley. This “urban country bar” features live music Wednesday through Saturday and a full drink menu, including flavored vodkas, in addition to more than 200 bourbons and whiskies. Come hungry for ½-pound hamburgers, ribs, steaks, BBQ chicken, and nine different dinner salads. 

D'Vine Bistro & Wine Bar 

3990 S. Alma School Rd.
Chandler, AZ 85248
(480) 782-5550

Wine lovers will love an evening at D’Vine Bistro & Wine Bar, where they can sip selections from around the world while enjoying bruschetta, cheese platters, and hearty entrées like braised short ribs and then listen to live music Tuesday through Saturday nights. Even though D’Vine is known for its wine selection, it also has an extensive beer menu and one of Chandler’s best mixology programs. 

Another option: The Keg also has a great wine selection and upscale menu, minus the live music, making it a good choice if you want to be able to talk to the bride and/or groom. 

Wild Horse Pass Casino

5040 Wild Horse Pass Blvd.
Chandler, AZ 85226
(800) 946-4452

There’s no shortage of party options at Wild Horse Pass Casino. For starters, you can test your luck at the 956 slots and 65 gaming tables and then take in a show in the casino’s showroom. (Past shows have ranged from country music artists Clint Black to comedian Sinbad and mixed martial arts contest.) Or, dance the evening away at Chrome Nightclub on Friday and Saturday nights. The casino is also a short drive from Wild Horse Pass Motorsports Park, which holds Friday Night Drags and racing events on its multiple road courses. 

Bob Bondurant School of High Performance Driving

20000 S. Maricopa Road, Gate #3
Chandler, AZ 85226
(800) 842-7223

Founded by race car driver Bob Bondurant, this school teaches advanced driving skills in high performance cars such as the Camero SS, Challenger Hellcat, and open cockpit Fomula Mazda racecar. Your party can sign up for an existing course or work with the staff to create a custom event. The school also has kart racing classes. (You must be at least 16 years old and have a valid driver’s license to participate in the high performance driving classes and 18 years old to participate in the racing classes. Kart classes are available for those 8 years old and up.)

Mic Drop Mania

250 S. Arizona Ave.
Chandler, AZ 85225
(480) 699-4598

Fill your Friday or Saturday night with laughter at Mic Drop Mania. The one-hour, interactive comedy show is fueled by audience suggestions, so what you see on stage is new every time. Attend the 7 p.m. show multi-generational appropriate content and the 9 p.m. show for an “unfiltered” experience. 

Tip: Begin your party with dinner at one of the downtown Chandler restaurants such as Crust or DC Steak House.

Uptown Art

1900 W. Germann Rd.
Chandler, AZ 85286
(480) 813-8059

Create your own masterpiece at an Uptown Art bachelorette (or co-ed) party. You pick a painting for the group to paint, and they provide instruction, paint supplies, and canvases. Daytime parties start at $25 per person with a 12 person minimum ($35 per person with a 35 person minimum for evening). Chandler-based Painting with Canvas also provides instruction and supplies to complete a painting but will come to your home ($35 per person with a 10 person minimum). 

Pottery: If you’d rather paint on pottery than on canvas, you can hold a party at Burst of Butterflies Create and Paint Studio (from $12 per person, 10 person minimum). The studio allows you to bring your own beer or wine. 

Alamo Drafthouse

4955 S. Arizona Ave.
Chandler, AZ 85248
(520) 213-8129

Alamo Drafthouse isn’t your typical movie theater. Sure, it has nine screens for new releases, family movies, and independent films, but it also serves entrées made with locally-sourced ingredients, local craft beers, and adult milkshakes to enjoy while you watch the show. Visit the website before you go to reserve your seats and arrive early for the pre-show of cartoons and shorts (instead of the typical advertisements). The best part? Alamo has a strict no calls, no text, and no talking rule and won’t seat latecomers.   

The Brickyard Downtown

85 W. Boston St.
Chandler, AZ 85225
(480) 963-1373

If your group is into craft cocktails, head to The Brickyard Downtown. The cocktail “ledger” is divided into three categories: classic cocktails, seasonal creations, and the Brickyard Hall of Fame. Plus, you’ll find 15 pages of liquors and house-made scrubs and syrups you can challenge the mixology staff to combine into a one-of-a-kind cocktail. The Brickyard specializes in small plates for sharing. 

More cocktails: The Ostrich, located directly below Crust, crafts classic and historic cocktails. In fact, the mixologists here take cocktails so seriously they handcraft their own ice and make their own soda water from a jerk.

bodyHtml:
They say it’s the journey, not the destination. But if you decide to explore Chandler by bike, it can be both and you can rent the perfect cruiser for your excursion at a Chandler bike shop. With more than 100 mostly flat cycling routes in the city, it’s easy to ditch the car for a chance to see the city’s mix of urban and desert landscapes up close. 

Biking Safety

Whether you’re riding through the city or on a desert trail, be sure to stay safe and respectful of other trail users. Before heading out, pack plenty of water and consult the Arizona Department of Transportation’s Active Transportation Program for tips on Arizona law and safety guidelines for our riding in our cities.

Consolidated Canal Path

The Consolidated Canal Path is a good place the start your exploration of the East Valley. What started as a dirt path connecting Chandler with neighboring cities Gilbert and Mesa is now an 18-mile network of developed multi-use trails. Along the path, there are several city parks, like Tibshraeny Family Park, that provide parking, bathrooms and easy entry.

Paseo Trail

The portion of the Canal Path that runs through Chandler is known as the Paseo Trail. This 6.5-mile section of the waterway is lined with a wide, concrete path on one side and a dirt surface on the other. The popular and gentle path is open to walkers, joggers and horseback riders, as well as cyclists.

The Paseo Vista Recreation Area sits near one end of the trail and is a highlight of the ride. The 64-acre park includes an archery facility, disc golf and dog park. Enter the Paseo Trail at Tibshraeny Family Park or Tumbleweed Park.

Western Canal Trail

For those interested in riding alongside a piece of Southwest history, check out the 20-mile stretch of the Western Canal Trail. This part of the canal network borders one of the Valley’s original eight canals that pre-date Arizona’s statehood.

These canals once connected the Salt River to our burgeoning agricultural areas. Today, the recently renovated trail connects Phoenix to most East Valley neighborhoods. Pick it up from the Paseo Trail near Freestone District Park.

San Tan Mountain Regional Park

If an off-road challenge is your cycling style, head to the San Tan Mountain Regional Park to test out your desert mountain biking skills. This 10,000-acre preserve includes a portion of the San Tan Mountains that border Chandler’s southern horizon. The park includes 29 miles of mostly easy to intermediate mountain bike trails. A main 11.6-mile loop climbs to just over 1,000 feet and winds through lush Sonoran desert landscape. Locals advise parking at the northern trailhead (Wagon Wheel and Skyline) and to be sure to pay the $2 park entry fee.

Plan ahead

There are plenty of great resources online to plan your bike day. The Maricopa County Association of Governments has an interactive bike map at geo.azmag.com/maps/bikemap and the Mountain Bike Project (mtbproject.com) is a user-generated guide of off-road trails that offers reviews, approach details and insider tips.

bodyHtml:
It’s easy to find a Mexican restaurant in Chandler, AZ. What’s difficult is deciding where to eat because of all the amazing options ranging from tacos to burritos to margaritas and more. If you’re in the mood for some of the best Mexican food found in the Valley, we can help. Here are some of the best choices for Mexican food in Chandler that are guaranteed to satisfy your every craving.

Serrano’s Mexican Food Restaurant

Come get your combination plates and margaritas at the locally owned chain, Serrano's, a family business that started out as a clothing store in downtown Chandler in 1919. Today, you can expect all the fixins’ for a great Sonoran-style Mexican meal, from enchiladas, fajitas and flautas to tacos, tostados and tamales, plus house specialties including machaca, pollo fundido, and chile relleno. And don’t forget Serrano’s famous bean dip.

Map: 141 S. Arizona Ave., Chandler AZ 85225 or (480) 899-3318

Elmer’s Tacos

Since the ’70s, Elmer's Tacos, the multi-generational family business has been serving freshly made tacos, burros and a whole lineup of recipes influenced by the original owner’s Sonora, Mexico, and Los Angeles roots—right in the heart of Chandler. Guests also can order flautas, taquitos, tostados and fry bread at the legendary Arizona Avenue eatery that has been a Chandler mainstay for decades.

Map: 355 N. Arizona Ave., Chandler AZ 85225 or (480) 963-6763

Espo’s Mexican Food

Known for its traditional Mexican dishes passed down from generations, Espo’s is a landmark in Chandler. Its green chili is the dining star but the family-run restaurant, which opened in 1974, offers burritos, breakfast burritos served all day, flautas, tostados, quesadillas, combinations plates, chimichangas, tacos and taco salads as part of its wide lineup of Mexican cuisine.

Map: 3867 W. Chandler Blvd, Chandler AZ 85226 or (480) 588-7377

Valle Luna Mexican Restaurant

The family-owned and operated business, Valle Luna, launched its first establishment in the West Valley, but brings founder Tia Rita’s Arizona-Sonoran food traditions to the Chandler location. The extensive menu includes appetizers, burritos, American plates, soups and salads, homemade dips, Tia Rita’s favorites such as the Chimichanga Dinner, as well as Luna specialties, sizzling fajitas, and fundido.

Map: 1949 W. Ray Road, Chandler AZ 85224 or (480) 786-3100

Nando’s Mexican Café

If you’re looking for a Sonoran-style dining experience with a family-friendly neighborhood vibe, set your dining GPS to Nando’s Mexican Café. The casual, restaurant/bar with a weekday happy hour from 3 to 6 p.m. offers apps, soups/salads, combo plates, fajitas, tacos, platos de huevos, and specialties such as enchiladas stuffed with crab, baby shrimp and cheese. Plus, the American fare includes burgers and sandwiches and a kid’s menu.

Map: 1890 W. Germann Road, Chandler AZ 85286 or (480) 855-4344

Rosa’s Mexican Grill

Savor the taste of the Baja at Rosa's Mexican Grill that’s been focused on the regional cuisine of the sea for 25 years. The restaurant’s trophy wall is filled with accolades for its selection of stuffed chimichangas, burros, quesadillas, fajitas, carne asada, tacos and tamales with shrimp, salmon as well as red/green pork and beef choices. Of course, all can be served with a side of chips, chunky guacamole and queso cheese dip.

Map: 3002 N. Arizona Ave,#18 Chandler AZ 85225 or (480) 830-6263

La Ristra New Mexican Kitchen

Look for authentic New Mexican dishes with red and green chiles as the essential ingredient, and a healthy selection of tequila, margaritas and beer at this casual, Southwestern eatery. La Ristra serves up tapas, soups and salads, tacos, burritos, grilled items such as carne asada and fajitas, and hosts a weekend brunch that includes biscuits and green chile gravy, and huevos rancheros.

Map: 140 N. Arizona Ave, Chandler AZ 85225 (480) 590-0002

El Sol Mexican Café

Don’t let the tiny surroundings of El Sol’s café and bakery fool you. The counter spot delivers big flavor, from all-day breakfast to lunch and an array of pan dulce. (sweet breads). The lineup includes house-made tortillas, breakfast burritos, burros, fish and shrimp tacos, pico de gallo made daily, and pastries and baked goods such as empanadas and cuernitos—all in one convenient, charming stop.

Map: 760 N. Arizona Ave, Chandler AZ 85225 or (480) 786-0811

 

Abuelo's Mexican Restaurant

At Abuelo’s, made-from-scratch food and dishes crated from chef Luis E. Sanchez’s family recipes shape the authentic Mexican menu. With an open-air courtyard and a mix of both modern and traditional Mexican décor, the restaurant uses the freshest ingredients for its handmade salsas, sauces, tortillas, sides, hand-rolled enchiladas, Tex-Mex items and house specialties including Pechuga con Calabaza and Port Tenderloin Abrigada.

Map: 3440 W. Chandler Blvd, Chandler AZ 85226 or (480) 855-0960

Someburro’s

This popular Arizona-based, Mexican restaurant chain, Someburro's has several locations where guests can dine-in or drive-through. The common denominator, however, is a scratch menu made from time-honored recipes handed down by the Vasquez family. Burros are the signature at Someburro’s, while crispy tacos ($2.50 each on Tuesdays, naturally), enchiladas, tamales, hand-made tortillas, slow-cooked meats and the hot sauce are equally guest favorites.

Map: 3461 W. Frye Road, Chandler AZ 85226 or (480) 726-8226

Map: 5095 S. Gilbert Road, Chandler AZ 85249 or (480) 597-6043

bodyHtml:
Chandler’s dog-friendly restaurants make it easy to enjoy a meal with your pup, thanks to spacious patios and relaxed, welcoming settings. Plan a fun day around breweries, cafes, and casual dining spots that invite your furry companion to join you outdoors, then round out your day together by adding nearby attractions and lodging that fit your travel style. When you build your itinerary around pooch-welcoming establishments, you keep the day flexible and enjoyable from the first coffee to the last bite.

Pedal Haus Brewery sets an approachable tone through award-winning craft brews and a wraparound patio designed for kicking back and enjoying time with friends (and Fido). The layout gives groups room to spread out, even during busy happy hours, and the vibe provides the style of welcome one seeks when they want to hunker down and enjoy a lovely Arizona afternoon. Misters, attentive staff, and steady foot traffic create an easygoing social pulse that keeps the patio active while still relaxed and unhurried.

Pedal Haus Brewery Address: 95 W. Boston St., Chandler, AZ 85225

QuartHaus takes a more playful approach. Its enclosed, off-leash dog park is a grassy area where energetic pups can move freely while their humans stay nearby with a drink in hand. Lawn games like cornhole keep the mood social and laid-back, making it especially appealing for travelers whose dogs benefit from activity rather than long stretches of sitting.

QuartHaus Address: 201 S. Washington St., Chandler, AZ 85225

SanTan Brewing Company combines on-site brewing with a classic brewpub vibe rooted in craft beer and comfort-driven fare in a setting that stays lively without being overwhelming. The sidewalk-facing patio welcomes well-behaved canine companions and offers first-rate people-watching. Thoughtful touches, like fresh water and treats, make it a solid choice for your pup to decompress as you enjoy a longer meal and keep the experience outdoors.

SanTan Brewing Company Address: 8 S. San Marcos Pl., Chandler, AZ 85225

Hash Kitchen brings the magic to the brunch hour, pairing bold flavors with a pooch-friendly patio designed for warm-weather dining through a misting system and oversized umbrellas. The social atmosphere suits dogs that are comfortable around crowds and movement. This stop works best for travelers who want brunch to serve as a memorable event rather than a quick bite.

Hash Kitchen Address: 2855 W. Ray Road, #4 Chandler, AZ 85224

Maple House offers a nice outdoor seating area for you and your four-legged pal. Espresso drinks and pastries anchor the morning, and fire pits and outdoor games give the patio an inviting feel as the day unfolds. The space transitions easily from coffee to cocktails, allowing you to stay put longer without the environment becoming static.

Maple House Address: 198 W. Boston St., Chandler, AZ 85225

Crust Simply Italian adds tasty Italian to the lineup and features a generously sized patio for you, your party, and of course, your beloved tail-wagger. Familiar Italian dishes make it an ideal dinner choice after a full day out, and the outdoor layout gives dogs space to settle in as meals unfold at an unhurried pace. It suits evenings that call for an easy, dependable place to unwind without overthinking the plan.

Crust Simply Italian Address: 10 N. San Marcos Pl., Chandler, AZ 85225 

The Stillery leans into atmosphere, pairing comfort food with live music and outdoor tables that add to its lively Downtown Chandler backdrop. The outdoor seating lets your fur‑covered plus‑ones stay part of the crew as music, food, and good conversation shape the night. This stop feels less like a meal out and more like a destination in its own right.

The Stillery Address: 130 S. Arizona Ave., Chandler, AZ 85225

Tryst Cafe focuses on health-conscious menus without sacrificing variety. Vegan, vegetarian, and gluten-free options make it a practical choice for mixed groups, while outdoor seating welcomes doggos to join their humans in an easygoing setting. Cocktails sit alongside salads, bowls, and other menu options, allowing Tryst to work for everything from casual lunches to evening dining.

Tryst Cafe Address: 4205 S. Gilbert Road, Chandler, AZ 85249 

Timing plays a key role in a smooth, dog-friendly dining experience. Mid-morning and early evening patio hours often feel calmer, providing more space and fewer distractions for tail-wagging sidekicks. Simple preparations, like bringing a leash, a collapsible water bowl, or a familiar mat, can also make longer meals more relaxed.

Chandler also has clear leash rules worth keeping in mind: in public parks and open spaces, pets must be on a leash no longer than six feet and under the owner’s control at all times. Staying leashed keeps your adventure buddy safe and makes dining smoother for everyone.

To extend a day trip into a dog-friendly vacation, you’ll need suitable lodging. Chandler’s pet-friendly hotels keep travelers close to walkable districts, outdoor seating, and open-air attractions. Between meals, visitors can branch out to local attractions, explore nearby recreation areas, or plan around festivals and live music that add texture to the experience. A thoughtful balance of food, pacing, and place makes traveling with dogs in Chandler feel natural rather than restrictive. Start mapping out your Chandler getaway with your furry best friend today.

bodyHtml:
Valentine’s Day is one of the most popular days to pop the big question. And the location of the life-changing inquiry is almost as important as the answer. If your February 14th plans include a “Will you marry me?,” here are some romantic spots in Chandler to help set the tone for a favorable offer of marriage.

KOLI Equestrian Center

Since you’re about ready to blaze new trails with a wedding proposal, why not saddle up at KOLI Equestrian Center? Located in the Gila River Indian Reservation Community, with scenic views of the Sierra Estrella Mountains as a backdrop, the equine facility offers horseback riding for all levels and ages amid surroundings rich in native flora and fauna.

For the big ask, schedule a private ride on one of the many desert trails where you can wrangle a “yes” and perhaps get a glimpse of wild horses as a proposal bonus.

6940 W. Broken Ear Road, Chandler AZ 85226

Veterans Oasis Park

Take your intentions outdoors at Veterans Oasis Park, which offers an abundance of recreational choices covering 113 acres. The park has a community fishing lake, scenic hiking and horseback riding trails, tranquil pavilions, monthly bird walks and an outdoor amphitheater, plus unique wildlife and plants.

Let nature do most of the talking with a peaceful declaration of love by popping the question waterside or tuck away on one of the park’s many trails to declare your commitment.

4050 E. Chandler Heights Road, Chandler AZ 85249

Chandler Museum

Combine your love of history and art at the Chandler Museum to ask for your intended’s hand in marriage. The museum offers world-class rotating art exhibitions, public forums and events, and is a learning destination to explore the community’s cultural heritage.

Wait for dark and illuminate your heart under the Infinite Wave, the museum’s outdoor courtyard techno installation with a metal wave-shaped canopy and a multi-colored light show.

300 S. Chandler Village Drive, Chandler AZ 85226

An upscale dinner

Don’t underestimate a well-developed palate—and a reservation—to spark a romantic marriage request. Chandler offers plenty of fine dining options to mark the occasion, from regional and American fare to global culinary experiences.

Set the mood by checking out Chandler’s upscale restaurant choices to create a first-class moment for your proposal over incredible food, ambience and impeccable service.

Paseo Vista Recreation Area

The 80-acre regional recreation facility sits on top of a hill and is a playground for all ages—and a whimsical proposal venue. It includes a tournament archery range with covered shooting areas, an 18-hole disc golf course, dog park, interpretive play areas and art features, multipurpose pathways, parking, native landscaping and significant erosion protection.

Put an exclamation on your proposal play date with a picture-perfect setting by watching one of Arizona’s famous sunsets while you enjoy the beautiful views of the East Valley.

3850 S. McQueen Road, Chandler AZ 85286

Commonwealth Canal Mural

Get to the heart of the matter in Downtown Chandler by staging your request alongside the Commonwealth Canal mural, located by the Crown Plaza Hotel at 1 N. San Marcos Place, Chandler AZ 85225. The mural is one of several public art murals scattered throughout Chandler that depict local pride and iconic imagery.

If you need help spelling it out, take your pick of letters to stand (or kneel) next to on the expansive canal mural that reads Chandler as you make your heartfelt, hometown case.

Forest-inspired “I do”

Set a lifetime of roots as you propose to your forever love in an enchanting grove of pistachio trees. Away from the hustle and bustle, this secluded haven offers a serene and dreamy setting filled with dappled sunlight and a lush canopy of leaves.

Give your marriage proposal a higher, earthy power of connection at this small, wooded grove located behind Grove Coffee at 2777 S. Gilbert Road, Chandler AZ 85286. Your proposal will become a chapter in your love story, woven into the tapestry of Chandler’s natural beauty.

Kind Bean

Tucked into a cozy little corner, Kind Bean is part coffee shop, part bakery, and all gluten-free-friendly. Pastries and sweets rotate daily, but they’re all rich, moist, and clearly made with care. With the shop’s philosophy centering on kindness—toward others, the planet, and the local community—every visit feels like a little act of good.

Map to Kind Bean: 1020 E. Pecos Road, Chandler, AZ 85225

Over Easy

A modern twist on the classic diner, this retro-inspired restaurant keeps things fun by offering comfort food classics—with a twist. Take the Loko Moko, a Hawaiian-inspired dish with sticky rice, beef patty, sunny-side-up egg, mushroom gravy, and crispy onions. It’s savory, satisfying, and totally Over Easy.

Map to Over Easy in Downtown Chandler: 140 N. Arizona Ave., Chandler, AZ 85225

Map to Over Easy in West Chandler: 7131 W. Ray Road, Chandler, AZ 85226

 

Tryst Café

Bright, casual and full of fresh flavor, Tryst Café is the kind of place that works for brunch with friends or a low-key dinner date. Most of the menu items are gluten-free, giving you a wide range of delicious options to choose from. Case in point, the strawberry custard French toast. Stuffed with strawberry cream cheese and topped with fresh strawberries, raspberry drizzle, and powdered sugar, it’s your strawberry dream come true.

Map to Tryst Café: 4205 S. Gilbert Road, Chandler, AZ 85249

Gluten-Free Lunch and Dinner Restaurants in Chandler, AZ

 

Cooper’s Hawk Winery & Restaurant

Date night, anyone? Cooper’s Hawk Winery & Restaurant is an upscale restaurant by Chandler Fashion Center that blends fine dining with a robust wine selection. With clear gluten-free designations (no second-guessing needed), the menu includes decadent gluten-free dishes, such as the gnocchi with roasted butternut squash and the braised short rib risotto. Pair either with a wine flight for a culinary experience to remember.

Map to Cooper’s Hawk Winery & Restaurant: 3325 W. Chandler Blvd., Chandler, AZ 85226

 

Flower Child

With cheerful vibes, colorful bowls and a menu that’s super easy to navigate, Flower Child makes it simple to eat clean. To brighten your day, try the Glow Bowl. Brimming with sweet potato noodles, shiitake mushrooms and snap peas, and topped with cilantro, mint and sunflower sauce, it’s both light and comforting. Gluten-free never felt so zen.

Map to Flower Child: 7131 W. Ray Road, Chandler, AZ 85226

 

George & Gather

With its bright, modern vibe and creative menu, George & Gather makes gluten-free dining feel easy. They offer a variety of GF-friendly dishes, but the real win? Nearly every pizza on the menu can be made with a gluten-free crust. From veggie-packed to meaty and cheesy, there’s something for every kind of pizza fan…minus the gluten.

Map to George & Gather: 336 S. Washington St., Chandler, AZ 85225

 

Original ChopShop

Quick, healthy and endlessly customizable. Original ChopShop has some of the best gluten-free options in Chandler thanks to its mix-and-match bowls, protein plates and smoothies. The spicy Korean steak bowl is a fan fave. Available with steak (of course), chicken, shrimp or tofu, it’s served with a side of bok choy tossed with green onions and sesame seeds.

Map to Original ChopShop: 35 W. Boston St., Chandler, AZ 85225

 

Pita Jungle

With a Mediterranean-inspired menu, Pita Jungle makes healthy eating taste indulgent. Their signature wood-fired Norwegian salmon is a crowd favorite, as is their version of the popular chicken tikka masala. End your meal on a sweet note with a gluten-free brownie ice cream sandwich. This is one of the best spots for celiac-friendly Chandler dining if you’re looking for a tasty pick-me-up.

Map to Pita Jungle at Anderson Springs: 1949 W. Ray Rd., Ste. 29Chandler, AZ 85224

Map to Pita Jungle at The Steelyard: 5025 S Gilbert Rd Suite 8, Chandler, AZ 85249

 

Stone & Vine Urban Italian

This popular South Chandler eatery serves up classic Italian flavors with some great gluten-free twists. Stone & Vine's popular bruschetta? You can get it with gluten-free bread, guaranteeing you won’t miss out on all the tasty options. And if pizza’s calling your name, just ask for a cauliflower crust. It’s crispy, light, and holds up beautifully under all that melty, savory goodness.

Map to Stone & Vine: 1035 W. Queen Creek Road, Chandler 85248

 

Wildflower Café

Part bakery, part bistro, all comfort. Located inside Chandler Fashion Center, Wildflower Café offers a menu with clearly marked gluten-free options. The banana walnut pancakes are a standout: warm, fluffy and just sweet enough. It’s a perfect stop for a relaxed breakfast before a day of shopping, strolling or just good old-fashioned people-watching.

Map to Wildflower Cafe: 3111 W. Chandler Blvd., Chandler AZ 85226

GLUTEN-FREE DESSERTS IN CHANDLER, AZ

 

Spooky's Swirls

Because no gluten-free roundup is complete without something sweet, head to Spooky’s Swirls, Chandler’s 100% dedicated, gluten-free bakery. Expect wild décor and seriously delicious cupcakes, brownies, cookies, cakes and more. They even have a selection of vegan treats that are spooky and sweet. Hands down, this is one of the top Chandler restaurants with gluten-free menus.

Map to Spooky’s Swirls: 3029 N. Alma School Road, Chandler 85224

Whether you’re grabbing a quick bite or planning a night out, there are plenty of gluten-free restaurants in Chandler, AZ, that make you feel like you’re not missing out. From nourishing bowls to creative desserts, you’ll find that the best gluten-free options in Chandler are ready to serve up memorable meals for everyone at the table.

bodyHtml:
Sometimes what you’re really craving is a great sandwich. Nothing fancy, just something stacked with flavor and tucked into fresh bread.
 

Luckily, Chandler has plenty of options. From classic deli subs and hearty cheesesteaks to global favorites like bánh mì and tortas ahogadas, the city’s sandwich scene has something for just about every appetite. Whether you’re grabbing a quick lunch between meetings or refueling after a day out, these local spots are a great place to start.

Classic Sandwiches & Subs

Retro’s Subs & Brews

Retro’s brings together two things that always pair well: creative sandwiches and craft beer. The menu mixes classic subs with some more inventive options, but the Paisley Park Pesto is a standout. It’s stacked with roast turkey, bacon, Swiss, avocado and pesto mayo—big flavor without feeling over-the-top. With its relaxed atmosphere and rotating beer list, Retro’s works just as well for a laid-back lunch as it does for a casual evening hangout.

Address: 275 W Warner Rd, Chandler, AZ 85225

Wildflower

A longtime Valley favorite, Wildflower has built its reputation on fresh soups, salads, and sandwiches that feel simple but thoughtfully made. One of the highlights is the Chipotle Chicken Melt, layered with all-natural chicken breast, Swiss, poblano peppers, caramelized onions, pepper relish, avocado and chipotle sauce on grilled sourdough. It’s warm, balanced and consistently satisfying.

Address: 3111 W Chandler Blvd, Chandler, AZ 85226

Cheba Hut

If you’re looking for something with personality, Cheba Hut delivers. Known for its toasted subs and playful vibe, the shop leans into bold flavors. The Kali Mist roasted turkey, chipotle mayo, jalapeños, bacon, pepper jack and avocado—brings just the right amount of heat while still feeling hearty and comforting.

Address: 11 W Boston St, Chandler, AZ 85225

Hot Sandwiches & Cheesesteaks

Eddie’s Philly

When cheesesteak cravings hit, Eddie’s Philly keeps things classic. The traditional Philly Cheesesteak with their signature red sauce is a solid starting point, but the Loaded Cheesesteak takes things further with mushrooms, peppers, onions, lettuce, tomato and plenty of melted cheese.

Address: 3016 N Dobson Rd Suit 9, Chandler, AZ 85224

Forefather’s Cheesesteaks

Well known around the East Valley, Forefather’s  takes its cheesesteaks seriously. Build your sandwich with grilled steak or chicken, your choice of cheese (including the classic Cheese Whiz), plus veggies and sauces. Add a side of fries (regular, sweet potato or cheese) and you’ve got a meal that fully satisfies.

Address: 1075 W. Queen Creek Rd. #1, Chandler, AZ 85248

Outta Bronx

Bringing a bit of New York deli energy to Chandler, Outta Bronx is known for its generously stacked sandwiches. The Empire Steak is a standout, filled with thinly sliced beef, grilled peppers, mushrooms, onions and melted provolone and American cheese on a buttery French baguette.

Address: 1175 W Ray Rd #105, Chandler, AZ 85224

Philly’s Famous

As the name suggests, Philly’s Famous sticks close to the traditional cheesesteak playbook. The Bellyfiller lives up to its name, loaded with grilled onions, mushrooms, sweet bell peppers and melted white American cheese on a soft Italian roll.

Address: 1250 N. Alma School Rd. #31, Chandler, AZ 85224 

Global Sandwich Flavors

Tortas Ahogadas Guadalajara

For something completely different, try a torta ahogada. This Mexican specialty features a crusty roll stuffed with seasoned shredded pork and then, quite literally, drowned in a rich, spicy red sauce. It’s messy, bold and absolutely worth the napkins.

Address: 518 N. Arizona Ave., Chandler, AZ 85225 

Lee's Sandwiches

For Vietnamese bánh mì, Lee's Sandwiches is a reliable go-to. Their baguettes are baked fresh and filled with savory meats, pickled daikon and carrots, cilantro and jalapeños. The BBQ Pork Bánh Mì is especially popular, and it pairs perfectly with a Vietnamese iced coffee.

Address: 1901 W. Warner Rd. #8, Chandler, AZ 85224

DTC Sports Grille Chandler sports fans will feel right at home at

headings.text: Best Sports Bars in Chandler, AZ

bodyHtml:
Looking for a spot to cheer on your favorite team? Grab your jersey and head to one of Chandler’s diverse sports bars, where you can relax, order drinks and food, and catch the big game on a big screen with the best seat in the house.

DTC Sports Grille

Chandler sports fans will feel right at home at DTC Sports Grille, housed in the building that was the former location of The Local. Short for DownTown Chandler, the latest addition to the city’s winning sports bar scene promises elevated takes on favorite pub fare. The toque behind the menu is celebrated chef Anthony Keoni, who offers up such items as scratch-made smashburgers, carne asada fries, signature “trifecta” wings, and piled-high cheesesteaks. While you feast, take in a game or two playing on any of the bar’s multiple big-screen TVs. And, of course, don’t forget to celebrate the big win with a round of draft beers, well cocktails or signature drinks.

Map: 55 W. Chicago St., Chandler AZ 85225 or (480) 397-1380

The Trophy Bar

A self-described “car lover’s sports bar,” The Trophy Bar is South Chandler’s go-to spot for sports and spirits. Decked out in rich tones and automobile-inspired décor, the bar also features a 16-foot video wall with 30 high-definition TVs—perfect for watching your favorite team in action. And what’s a sports bar without bar food? Choose your favorites from a menu filled with appetizers, pizzas, street tacos, burgers, sandwiches, wings and desserts. Complement your meal with a margarita, mule or custom cocktail, or a drink from their selection of wines and beers.

Map: 2551 W. Queen Creek Road Unit 4, Chandler AZ 85248 or (480) 590-3595

Dirty Blonde Tavern

Known for its live entertainment and overall high-energy vibe, this neighborhood hangout is just the right spot to spend the day enjoying a game, sipping a cold drink, and feasting on good, old-fashioned bar fare. While the classic standbys—burgers, pizzas, nachos and wings—are on the menu, so, too, are some breakfast favorites. Available Saturdays and Sundays from 9 a.m. to noon during football season, the menu includes breakfast burritos, omelets, egg sandwiches, and French toast.

Map: 4929 W. Chandler Blvd. #12, Chandler AZ 85226 or (480) 753-7175

BKD’s Backyard Joint

Whatever team you’re cheering for, the vibe at BKD’s Backyard Joint is a high-five community of camaraderie and sportsmanship, regardless of who wins on the field. The casual sports bar and eatery serves it up with daily brunch, a pre-game menu of wings and loaded nachos, build-your-own pizza, fields of greens, burgers and sandwiches, crafted entrees such as the smoked meatloaf and Chianti short-ribs, and post-game desserts. BKD’s beverage selections are just as expansive—and hospitable—with dozens of draft and bottled beers, mimosas, specialty mules and martinis, rotating wine and a beer tower for two.

Map: 980 E. Pecos Road, Chandler, AZ 85225 or (480) 935-2537

Blue 32 Sports Grill

Blue 32 is a destination for prime sporting events such as championships, tournaments and playoff series with large TVs for easy viewing of your favorite athletic event. But the locally-owned sports bar is also a full-service restaurant with a competitive culinary lineup featuring fresh ground burgers, steaks and seafood cut in-house daily, salads and sandwiches with house-made dressings and sauces, and specialties such as flatbread and a signature “black and blue” coleslaw. The spot also offers a variety of local craft beers, wine, martinis and cocktails.

Map: 4845 S. Arizona Ave., Chandler, AZ 85249 or (480) 284-6496

Jolie’s Place

You can bet on a good time at Jolie’s, where trivia night, pop culture bingo and poker tournaments are part of the gaming ticket at this friendly neighborhood bar and grill in the East Valley Mall shopping center. It’s also a huddle spot for Buffalo Bills fans during football season. The 6 a.m. to 6 p.m. happy hour schedule, live music from Wednesday to Sunday, and a pub grub menu made with fresh ingredients and award-winning wings are also a draw for the sporting regulars who appreciate owner Jolie Boucher’s penchant for competitive, old-fashioned entertainment.

Map: 140 W. Warner Road, Chandler, AZ 85225 or (480) 786-0436

Cold Beers & Cheeseburgers

Known for its gourmet brews—150 to be exact, including draft, bottled and canned choices—and fresh, made-to-order burgers, house-made appetizers, hand-crafted pasta, salads and gluten-free dishes, Cold Beers & Cheeseburgers is your neighborhood grub and sports destination. The lineup also includes stadium-style hot dogs, sandwiches, and mac-n-cheese options with 30 HD flatscreen TVs, comfortable leather booths, high-top community patio tables that feature built-in beer coolers, and an ultra-definition sound system to make a game day outing a full-court press.

Map: 1980 W. Germann Road, Chandler, AZ 85286 or (480) 899-2007

Fat Willy’s Family Sports Grill

Located in the Chandler Heights Marketplace, the Arizona chain is a familiar place where everyone is an MVP—and maybe even knows your name. The family-owned, casually cool neighborhood bar welcomes the whole gang to enjoy their American-inspired comfort food including appetizers, pizza, burgers, wings and pasta, plus local craft beer, premium spirits and daily happy hour deals. The best part is there are plenty of large plasma screens and not a bad seat in the house to catch the game. And if you want exclusive access to events, special pricing and secret menus, become a VIP.

Map: 4850 S. Gilbert Road Suite 4, Chandler, AZ 85249 or (480) 883-1356

Sidelines Bar & Grill

After 20 years in the business, Sidelines is in it for the hometown win. Grilled wings and burgers are the house specialties, but the sports bar offers a deep roster of grub to make it to the finish line including pre-game sliders, soups and salads, sandwiches and wraps. The grill also features daily specials and a kid’s menu with mini corn dogs and grilled cheese. In addition, it prides itself on having the coldest beer in town—both domestic and international—with craft selections, as well as mixed drinks and top-shelf pours.

Map: 2980 S. Alma School Road, Chandler, AZ 85286 or (480) 792-6965

Hob Nob Sports Grill

Die-hard Chicago sports fans will feel right at home at Hob Nob, which proudly waves its allegiance to the Windy City. The family-owned spot caters to Midwest sporting sensibilities, but everyone is welcome to support their favorite team pennant. The bar also hosts a team trivia night on Thursdays and offers up hearty fare including salads, sandwiches, burgers and chops and daily specials that remind everyone of home. Plus, there’s the usual rotation of wines, spirits and domestic drafts including Miller Lite, Budweiser and a take-one-for-the-team nod to Chicago’s own brew, Lagunitas IPA.

Map: 7200 W. Chandler Blvd., Chandler, AZ 85226 or (480) 940-4745

headings.text: Best Spots for Family Photos in Chandler, AZ

bodyHtml:
Whether you’re planning holiday cards, celebrating a big milestone, or just capturing a sweet moment before the kids grow another inch, Chandler has no shortage of beautiful spots for family photos. From wide-open desert views to cozy corners in downtown spots, it’s all right here, no long drive required.

Downtown Chandler

If you’re into that mix of charm and city vibes, Downtown Chandler is tough to beat. Brick paths, string lights, colorful murals and tucked-away courtyards all come together for a setting that feels cool, but still personal. Bonus: Stop in one of downtown’s coffee or ice cream shops for pre- or post-shoot bribes (looking at you, toddlers).

 

Chandler City Hall

Chandler City Hall is an underrated gem for family photos, especially at sunset. The modern architecture (hello, glass walls and clean lines) pairs perfectly with the grassy courtyard and tall trees, giving you both sleek and natural vibes in one spot. Stick around a bit longer and the neon lights kick in, adding a cool, modern pop. Great for milestone moments with a little extra flair.

Chandler Murals & Public Art

Want something bright, bold and a little artsy? Chandler’s public murals are full of personality—and they’re a fun twist on the classic family photo. Whether you’re going playful, edgy or modern, there’s a mural to match the vibe. Tip: Check out the Chandler Mural Quest pass to find a full map and hit a few spots in one go.

Veterans Oasis Park

This is a go-to spot for a reason. Veterans Oasis Park has a little bit of everything: a scenic lake, winding trails, shady ramadas, and all the desert charm you could want. Want those golden-hour shots with dreamy light bouncing off the water? This is your place. And with paved walkways, it’s stroller- and kiddo-friendly—so you don’t have to sacrifice comfort for a great shot.

Tumbleweed Park

Tumbleweed Park offers a mix of rustic charm and playful energy, making it an easy win for family photos of all kinds. Historic buildings, open green space, and kid-friendly areas like Playtopia give you multiple looks in one location. Bonus: Train lovers can add a quick stop at the nearby Arizona Railway Museum. Just be sure to check hours before you go.

Paseo Vista Recreation Area

Looking for something a little more rugged? Paseo Vista has desert trails, wide-open views of the East Valley, and cool terrain that makes photos feel adventurous (without too much hiking involved). It’s a great pick if you want something outdoorsy, with a little drama in the background.

Desert Breeze Park

Desert Breeze Park is perfect if you’ve got little ones who aren’t exactly into standing still. There’s space to run, grassy lawns, a pretty little lake, and spots with desert blooms. The best part? You can get those sweet candid shots while your kids are just being, well, kids. For great candid images, capture the kids on the Desert Breeze Railroad. Be sure to check the hours of operation and entry fees before you go.

Downtown Ocotillo

If you’re going for something a little more polished, the Downtown Ocotillo area has major photo appeal. Think lakes lined with palm trees, elegant bridges, and waterfront walking paths that give off laid-back resort vibes. Sunset here? Pure magic. It’s a solid pick for anniversary pics or those rare full-family portraits with grandparents included.

 

Fulton Ranch

Fulton Ranch is all about timeless, polished beauty. With its lakes, palms, waterfalls, walking paths, and gorgeous stone bridges, it offers a serene, upscale backdrop that photographs beautifully, especially at golden hour. Since it’s an active neighborhood, it’s best for smaller sessions like couples, seniors, or quick family shoots where you can move easily and keep things low-key.

Quick Tips for Picture-Perfect Planning

  • Go early or late: Morning and evening light is soft, flattering—and not blazing hot.
  • Keep it comfy: Choose locations with easy access and some shade. Happy kids equal better photos.
  • Mix it up: Don’t be afraid to try two locations (like nature and murals) for more variety in your gallery.

headings.text: Best Summer Cocktails and Refreshing Drinks in Chandler
‘Pop’ Into The Best Chandler Boba Bars

bodyHtml:
Summer is the perfect time to enjoy a few seasonal drinks, whether it’s an order of frosty cold ones for the entire family or a round of adult cocktails or cold pints for the big kids. Check out these establishments for some cool beverage ideas.

Family-friendly drinks

Sodalicious

Use a little mixology magic to create a signature soda at Sodalicious. Choose a base soda—7-up, Dr. Pepper or Coke, to name a few—and then select from a list of inventive flavors and ingredients to make your specialty beverage. Dr. Pepper and horchata anyone? Customers also can blend energy drinks and flavored waters as part of the soda experiment.

80 W. Warner Road, Chandler, AZ 85225 or (480) 791-3002

Bahama Bucks

If you want to beat the heat, bite into a crunchy snow cone at Bahama Bucks, where you pick from 100 gourmet flavors and toppings for a light and airy shaved ice treat. The lineup at Bahama Bucks includes smoothies, specialty sodas and frozen coffees to offset the temps.

4040 S. Arizona Ave., Chandler, AZ 85248 or (480) 219-5899

American Way Smokehouse

Quench your thirst the old-fashion way at American Way Market, which features 150-plus vintage and specialty bottled sodas that harken back to simpler times. The fizzy flavors run the gamut from A&W root beer to Red Rock cola and Zuberfizz key lime with more choices being added to the menu.

1509 N. Arizona Ave., Chandler, AZ 85225 or (480) 772-1877

Fruit Daddy

Fresh fruit is the main ingredient for shaved ice and drinks at Fruit Daddy, where sweet and savory profiles provide the cooldown with such options as the Mango Loco, an Italian shaved ice with mango, chamoy, tajin, peanuts and tamarindo candy; or the Mazapan Rasapado with infused raspado and vanilla ice cream.

920 N. Arizona Ave., Chandler, AZ 85225 or (480) 465-8029

Mango Crazy

Take a mercury break with the mango-infused smoothies, sorbets, aguas frescas, and other chill drinks and summertime concoctions filled with fresh fruit and spices such as tajin, chamoy, lime juice and hot sauce that bring the heat, but not the temperature.

1005 S. Arizona Ave., Chandler, AZ 85225 or (480) 590-6082

Boba Cutea

How would you like your boba? At Boba Cutea, you can order the popular Taiwanese cold beverage many ways. The tea house serves an array of milk teas, fruit teas, bubble milk, brown sugar drinks, galaxy boba drinks and smoothies in a variety of combinations and flavors that provide a tasty cooldown.

3400 W. Chandler Blvd., Chandler, AZ 85226 or (480) 306-6847

Adult cocktails

The Hidden House

The 1939 repurposed cottage features classic cocktails with a refreshing twist such as its take on the mint julep, made the old-fashioned derby way with Old Forester, bourbon sugar, and mint over pebble ice. Or the pisco sour, the national drink of Peru, featuring La Caravedo Pisco, a Peruvian brandy, paired with lemon, sugar and an egg white for a frothy touch.

159 W. Commonwealth Ave., Chandler, AZ 85225 or (480) 275-5525

The Parlay Kitchen + Cocktails

The American gastropub might be a causal neighborhood hang, but it takes its adult beverage selections seriously, pouring classic and crafted cocktails, international wines and local draft, domestic and imported beers. Plus, the modern eatery offers happy hour seven days a week from 3 to 6 p.m.

1245 S. Price Road, Chandler, AZ 85286 or (480) 500-5247

St. Amand Kitchen & Cocktails

Upgrade your summer beverage itinerary at St. Amand with signature cocktails such as a raspberry mojito or Mexican mule. The elevated chill vibe also comes with a cooled patio, wine, craft beer and even a Bucket of Fun—five High Noon Hard Seltzers of your choice: grapefruit, black cherry, pineapple or watermelon.

3990 S. Alma School Road, Chandler, AZ 85248 or (480) 782-5550

The Ostrich

What better place to sip a cold drink than in a dark speakeasy? Located in a basement, the craft cocktail lounge is inspired by the illegal drinking establishments of the Prohibition Era. But don’t worry, you can legally order a whisky, gin, scotch and assortment of spirited drinks, as well as wine, draft and handheld beer while you escape the rising temps.

10 N. San Marcos Place, Chandler, AZ 85225 or (480) 917-4903

The Brickyard Downtown

It’s easy to cool down at the locally-owned stylish bar and restaurant in downtown Chandler, especially with is Library of Libations, a 15-page ledger of the innovative cocktails and spirits made with premium liquor, house-made scrubs and syrups and garnishes. Plus, there’s curated wine and draft beer to help take the edge off the elements.  

85 W. Boston St., Chandler AZ, 85225 or (480) 963-1373

headings.text: Must-Try Thai Restaurants in Chandler, AZ
What to Order at a Thai Restaurant
Unique Patio Dining Experiences in Chandler, AZ

bodyHtml:
Family ownership and direct ties to Thailand shape much of Chandler’s Thai dining scene. Many local restaurants are operated by chefs and families who bring recipes, cooking techniques and culinary traditions from Thailand, creating a dining culture rooted in authenticity rather than adaptation. 

That authenticity is reflected in the variety of dishes available across the city. Beyond classic favorites such as pad thai, diners can explore regional specialties, rich curries, fragrant noodle soups, Thai-style seafood dishes and fresh salads. Many restaurants also allow guests to customize spice levels, making it easy for both adventurous diners and newcomers to find something that suits their tastes. 

Together, these restaurants showcase the depth and diversity of Thai cuisine while contributing to Chandler’s growing reputation as a destination for international dining. 

Grace Thai Downtown Chandler 

Grace Thai Downtown Chandler offers popular curries, noodles and specialty entrees. Its menu includes Pad Thai, Pad See Ew, Drunken Noodles and various curries. You can also choose your preferred spice level, with options running from no spice to extra Thai hot. 

Grace Thai sits within Chandler’s walkable downtown district near coffee shops, bars and other gathering spots, so a Thai lunch or dinner can fit into a larger outing without requiring another drive. 

Chon Thai Food 

Over the years, North Chandler’s Chon Thai Food has built a loyal local following around traditional Thai dishes. Chon Thai’s menu covers curries such as yellow, red, green and massaman, along with Tom Yum Noodle Soup and specialties including Crispy Garlic Chicken tossed in garlic sauce and topped with crunchy basil leaves. 

The menu also accommodates different dining preferences, with vegan and vegetarian dishes plus a dedicated kids’ menu. 

Mama Thai Kitchen 

Mama Thai Kitchen brings a broad mix of Thai comfort food and house specialties to South Chandler. The restaurant emphasizes high-quality fresh ingredients across a menu of more than 70 dishes.  

Pad See Ew, Drunken Noodles and Pad Thai cover the noodle favorites, while dishes such as Crying Tiger, Goong Ob Woon Sen and Pumpkin Curry with Shrimp offer something less expected. The combination of comfort food, fresh ingredients and distinctive specialties provide plenty of reasons to return to this popular spot. 

Savor Thai 

Savor Thai now occupies the location that previously housed Phuket Thai Cuisine. The Thai husband-and-wife duo describes its menu as a modern fusion that combines Thai traditions and authentic Thai ingredients with contemporary and international influences. 

Current offerings include noodle dishes like Pad Thai, Pad Kee Mao, Pad See Ew, red, green and yellow curries, plus Thai Basil stir-fry and Spicy Fried Rice. Savor Thai serves lunch and dinner, giving South Chandler diners another Thai dining choice grounded in go-to dishes and modern interpretations. 

Thai Chili 2go 

Thai Chili 2go gives Chandler a fast-casual authentic Thai option for dine-in or takeout. The restaurant prepares Thai curries, noodles, fried rice, soups, appetizers and rice bowls. 

Several familiar Thai dishes anchor the menu. Pad Thai combines thin rice noodles, green onions, bean sprouts, egg and crushed peanuts with that irresistible Pad Thai sauce, while Drunken Noodles bring together wide rice noodles, vegetables, basil and chili garlic sauce. Curry choices include red, green, yellow, massaman and panang. 

Thai Rama  

The family-owned local favorite Thai Rama has been part of Chandler’s Thai dining scene for decades. Its selection features an impressive array of curries, soups, house specialties and fried rice and noodle dishes. Try the Japanese eggplant stir-fried with onions, mushrooms, carrots and basil or the Evil Jungle Noodles, a red curry-based noodle dish that one longtime customer describes as a classic staple after nearly 17 years of visits. 

What to Order at a Thai Restaurant 

A few core dishes make a useful roadmap when the menu feels unfamiliar. Recipes and ingredients vary by restaurant, but common versions often include: 

Pad Thai: Tangy, savory and slightly sweet, Pad Thai offers a balanced introduction to Thai noodles. It suits diners looking for plenty of flavor without much chile heat. 

Pad See Ew: This savory noodle dish leans subtly sweet, with soy sauce giving it a deeper, richer flavor. It’s a good choice if you prefer mild dishes over spicy ones. 

Drunken Noodles: Basil, a chili base and garlic lend Drunken Noodles a bold, spicy profile. Those who like heat and stronger savory flavors may prefer this dish. 

Panang Curry: Panang Curry combines a rich, creamy texture with lightly sweet, savory and aromatic flavors. It appeals to people who want a coconutty, thick curry with milder heat. 

Green Curry: Green curry brings together coconut richness, fresh herbal flavors and noticeable heat. It works well for those seeking a creamy curry with a spicier edge. 

Tom Kha Soup: Coconut milk, lemongrass and galangal create this soup’s creamy, aromatic and tangy character. It may appeal to those who want a creamy soup brightened by citrusy flavors. 

Mango Sticky Rice: Ripe mango, coconut and sticky rice create a sweet, creamy and chewy dessert. It’s a good choice for diners who want a fruit-forward finish to the meal. 

Thai restaurants offer enough variety to build a shortlist by dish, spice level or dining style. Beyond curries and noodles, the region’s international dining scene opens the door to Vietnamese, Indian, Korean, Japanese and other cuisines throughout the city. Come hungry and discover what makes Chandler one of Arizona’s most diverse dining destinations.

headings.text: Best Ways to Explore Chandler with Your Dog

bodyHtml:
Have to travel for work or maybe heading to Chandler for a mini vacay? Don’t leave your best friend at home. Bring your pup with you to experience Chandler, AZ. Chandler has dog friendly patios restaurants, outdoor recreation opportunities, and even pet-friendly hotels.

Dog-friendly restaurants

Thanks to the more than 300 days of sunshine Arizona enjoys every year, patio dining is a favorite pastime for Chandler locals and visitors…and their four-legged friends. Located in south Chandler, BLD is the perfect place to bring your pooch. Open for breakfast, lunch and dinner, the restaurant has a K-9 menu with bowls ranging in price from $4 to $8. Treat your dog to the Hound Bowl, a ground beef patty served with rice.

At SanTan Brewing Company, pets receive a free peanut butter pupachino, while Brews TapHouse satisfies both dogs and owners with its chill vibe. Tryst Café is another pet-friendly location. As guests enjoy a healthy breakfast, lunch or dinner, their furry companion gets his own treats and fresh water.

Hiking with your dog

Chandler has plenty of trails to give you and your pup a chance to stretch your legs and take in some fresh air. For an easy option, head to Desert Breeze Park, where you can walk on paved trails around a lake. In southeast Chandler, Veterans Oasis Park has 4.5 miles of groomed dirt trails, including nearly a half mile that goes around its 5-acre lake. Got a dog that gets excited by birds? The park boasts more than 150 different species of birds.

For a longer walk, try the 6.5-mile Paseo Trail along the east side of the Consolidated Canal. Parking is available at the Paseo Vista Recreation Area and Tumbleweed Park. Or hike nearly 50 miles of trails at South Mountain Park, roughly a half hour from Chandler in Phoenix.

Chandler dog parks

You’ll find some of the Valley’s best dog parks in Chandler. Located at Paseo Vista Recreation Area, Shawnee Park, Snedigar Sportsplex, and Nozomi Park, the dog parks feature 6-foot-high chain link fences to keep your dog safe. All four also have doggy drinking fountains, pooper-scoopers, benches for dog owners, and obstacles to entertain your pet. Snedigar Dog Park has a fake fire hydrant, as well.

To play at the park, your dog must be up-to-date on his vaccines. Additionally, dogs in season are not allowed, and you can’t bring food into the fenced area. Paseo Vista, Snedigar, and Nozomi Dog Park are all open 6 a.m. to 10:30 p.m. Shawnee Park is open 6 a.m. to 8 p.m. Monday through Saturday and 9 a.m. to 8 p.m. on Sunday.

Dog-friendly hotels

Several Chandler hotels invite you to book a room with your dog. If you’re staying downtown, Crowne Plaza Phoenix – Chandler Golf Resort provides easy access to grassy onsite spaces, including Dr. AJ Chandler Park. And if you need to go out, you can leave your pet unattended in your room.

Near Chandler Fashion Center, pets receive a care package that includes a water bowl, dog toys, and treats at Fairfield Inn & Suites Phoenix Chandler Fashion Center. Also in the area, Element Chandler Fashion Center has grassy areas for you to walk your dog and water bowls and treats in the lobby.

headings.text: Concerts & Live Music in Chandler, AZ
Chandler Concert Series & Major Music Events
Exploring Live Music in Downtown Chandler

bodyHtml:
Chandler is a dynamic region with a thriving music scene that offers something for every type of music lover. From high-energy festivals and free open-air concert series to intimate gigs and rotating local acts, live music in this Arizona destination occurs year-round. Whether you’re a visitor or a local, you’ll find everything from jazz and rock to mariachi and acoustic sets across stages and gathering spots citywide.

 

This go-to resource covers everything you need to know about concerts and other musical shows in the area, including seasonal happenings, top venues, and the city’s cultural heartbeat. 

 

Chandler Concert Series & Major Music Events 

From October through March, typically on the third Thursday of the month, the Sonoran Sunset Concert Series at Veterans Oasis Park provides an intimate, lakeside setting for outdoor exhibits. These free, open-air concerts invite attendees to relax under the stars with blankets or folding chairs. While a limited selection of snacks and beverages is available for purchase, guests are welcome to bring refreshments. This series features diverse genres and styles from local music acts.

 

Spring brings the Chandler Jazz Festival, which transforms the downtown area into a lively, multi-stage celebration of jazz. The event includes free outdoor concerts, late-night performances at restaurants and bars, and appearances by both rising and established jazz artists.


The Chandler Center for the Arts holds its Summer Concert Series, offering free, indoor concerts on various Friday evenings—typically late July through August—throughout the summer. Featuring genres like jazz and blues, it’s a family-friendly way to enjoy a night of great tunes in a cool setting. Seating is available on a first-come basis, and some presentations are also live-streamed for those tuning in from home.

 

Exploring Live Music in Downtown Chandler

Downtown Chandler buzzes with energy, inviting visitors to explore its lively, walkable venues night after night. With a range of intimate spots, cozy patios, historic buildings, and a rooftop bar, it’s easy to explore the area and discover something new.

 

Popular spots like The Stillery, The Perch Brewery, and QuartHaus offer a steady lineup of live acts. Depending on the night, you might catch a jazz trio, an acoustic act, or a DJ spinning late into the evening. Many bars and restaurants feature open mic nights and multiple-act lineups, perfect for casual entertainment or enjoying local talent. If you’re looking for live music in Chandler tonight, downtown is the place to start. Simply show up and follow the sweet sounds.

 

Year-Round Music Venues & Listening Spaces 

In addition to our walkable downtown, the region has a variety of places offering music performances in more formal or ticketed settings. The Chandler Center for the Arts stands out as the city’s flagship performing arts venue, with tribute acts, cultural displays, and national tours. For outdoor experiences, Tumbleweed Park and Dr. A.J. Chandler Park host seasonal events and concerts in family-friendly environments. These locations are especially popular for festivals and celebrations.

 

Seeking a more laid-back vibe? Local breweries and restaurants often serve as informal music stages. Places like Cork & Craft and Puro Cigar Bar regularly have local musicians in a relaxed atmosphere. For a cozier setting, head to SoZo Coffeehouse, where rotating local art decorates the walls—available for purchase—and an inviting lineup of live music completes the warm, welcoming atmosphere.

 

Experience a vibrant live music scene, Tuesdays through Sundays, at The Forum Lounge featuring an upscale lounge experience with Arizona's best local bands and musicians. This 21 and over venue features a chic upscale vibe, complete with a VIP lounge that can be reserved for a small group of friends or colleagues for an elevated experience complete with comfortable seats, great food & drinks and dedicated staff. 

 

Rebel & Rogue is your go-to spot for karaoke every Tuesday night. Housed in a historic 1918 building, this high-energy American tavern serves up bold flavors, strong drinks, and a rock-and-roll spirit, all set to the backdrop of live music and lively crowds—an ideal backdrop for a fun night out. No matter your preference, the music scene here has a space for you to sit back and enjoy the music. Be sure to check the event calendar for what’s coming up.

 

Music Festivals & Seasonal Highlights

The local events calendar bursts with music-centered activities taking place throughout the year. One of the biggest is the Chandler Chamber Ostrich Festival, held in the spring at Tumbleweed Park. This multi-day event combines carnival attractions with live entertainment, featuring everything from pop and rock to country and Latin acts on a main stage.

 

In October, the Mariachi and Folklórico Festival at the Chandler Center for the Arts brings together great music and traditional dance in a celebration of Mexican culture. It’s a standout event during Hispanic Heritage Month, offering colorful performances by acclaimed mariachi ensembles and folklórico dancers.

 

Other festivals, like the Chandler Multicultural Festival held in January, include live music in their programming. The events highlight the city’s cultural diversity and showcase music as a central part of the experience. Since lineups and event formats can evolve, checking the town or tourism websites is the best way to confirm current offerings and discover new festivals.

 

Whether you catch a sunset concert in the park, listen to an acoustic duo over dinner, or stumble upon a surprise set downtown, live music adds rhythm and energy to every corner of this vibrant community. Ready to join the fun? Start planning your visit today.
