Breakfast to Kick Off the Day
Where to Get The Best Pizza in Chandler, AZ
Raise a Glass: Breweries & Local Hangouts
Make It a Full Father’s Day Weekend

bodyHtml:
Father’s Day is the perfect excuse to treat Dad to something memorable, and in Chandler, Arizona, you’ll find no shortage of ways to celebrate. From sizzling steakhouses and laid-back brunch spots to craft breweries, golf, and family-friendly adventures, Chandler delivers a full weekend of experiences designed with Dad in mind.

 

Whether you're planning a relaxed Sunday or turning it into a weekend getaway, here’s how to make Father’s Day in Chandler one to remember.

 

Start with a Father’s Day Feast

 

No Father’s Day is complete without a great meal, and Chandler’s dining scene offers everything from hearty comfort food to elevated culinary experiences.

 

For the Steak-Loving Dad

Treat Dad to a classic steakhouse experience at CHoP Chandler, where premium cuts and an upscale atmosphere set the tone for a special celebration. It’s a go-to for a refined Father’s Day dinner—just be sure to reserve early.

 

Local Flavor & Elevated Dining

For something uniquely Chandler, The Hidden House offers seasonal New American dishes in a charming historic setting—perfect for a relaxed yet elevated meal.

 

Casual & Comfort Classics

If Dad prefers something laid-back, head to American Way Smokehouse for hearty BBQ, house-made sauces, and nostalgic vibes that make every bite feel like home.

 

Breakfast to Kick Off the Day

Start Father’s Day with a leisurely breakfast at Downtown Chandler Café and Bakery, where fresh pastries, coffee, and classic breakfast dishes set the tone for a relaxed morning.

Explore more Chandler restaurants to find the perfect fit for dad!

Raise a Glass: Breweries & Local Hangouts

 

Celebrate Dad with a well-earned toast at one of Chandler’s standout craft breweries.

 

 Local Favorites

  • SanTan Brewing Company - A longtime Chandler staple with bold Arizona-inspired brews and known for Father’s Day specials.
  • The Perch Brewery & Pub – A one-of-a-kind experience featuring rooftop seating and a lively atmosphere.
  • Craft 64 – Pair local beers with wood-fired pizza in a relaxed downtown setting.

 

For Something Different

  • QuartHaus – A beer garden-style wine bar with lawn games and a social vibe
  • Helluva Brewing Company – Great for smoked eats and a casual Father’s Day hangout

 

Discover more Chandler breweries to enjoy during your visit.

Get Out and Play

 

Turn Father’s Day into an experience with activities built around Dad’s favorite things.

 

Hit the Links

Chandler is a golfer’s paradise. Book a tee time at:

  • San Marcos Golf Course – Arizona’s first grass course with historic charm
  • Springfield Golf Resort – A hidden gem, this course suits both beginners and experienced golfers.
  • Lone Tree Golf Club - Scenic desert landscaping with views of the San Tan Mountains.
  • Ocotillo Golf Club – Lush fairways lined with water features

 

Explore more golf courses in Chandler

 

Family-Friendly Fun

 

  • Swingin’ Safari Mini Golf offers Glow-in-the-dark fun for all ages
  • Harkins Theatres Chandler Fashion 20 – Catch the latest blockbuster in comfort
  • Taroko Sports - High-tech indoor batting cages, arcade games, and more

 

Outdoor Moments

 

Enjoy Arizona sunshine with a desert trail walk or picnic at Veterans Oasis Park, a peaceful desert escape perfect for quality time together.

Browse more things to do in Chandler

Make It a Full Father’s Day Weekend

 

Why limit the celebration to just one day? Stay the weekend and explore even more of Chandler’s dining, shopping, and entertainment.

 

  • Book a hotel and enjoy some poolside fun
  • Explore local shops for last-minute, Made in Chandler items for Father’s Day gifts
  • Use the Choose Chandler Experience Pass to discover deals and hidden gems

 

Father’s Day is about creating meaningful moments—and Chandler offers the perfect setting to celebrate every kind of dad, from foodies and golf lovers to craft beer enthusiasts and adventure seekers.

bodyHtml:
There’s something unmistakably patriotic in the air when the 4th of July in Chandler rolls around. A little more red, white, and blue on every front porch. A little more laughter spilling from neighborhood parks and a little more reason to gather, celebrate, and connect under Arizona’s summer sky. 

 

While the All-American Bash may be the main event, it’s far from the only way to mark the occasion. From relaxed, small-town-style gatherings to energetic, music-filled dinner parties, the 4th of July in our city has something for everyone. Use this detailed guide to plan a holiday filled with flavor, fun, and flag-waving pride.

 

Star of the Show: Chandler’s All-American Bash

At the heart of our Independence Day festivities is Chandler’s All-American Bash, a high-energy evening that draws families, neighbors, and visitors alike. Held on July 4, 2026, from 7 p.m. to 9:30 p.m. at Dr. A.J. Chandler Park, Stage Plaza, this annual tradition brings the community together with a friendly energy and plenty of wow factor.

 

Enjoy live music, balloon art, yard games, and raffle baskets, with a dazzling 15-minute pyrotechnic show lighting up the stage as part of the concert. Food vendors serve everything from cool drinks to Arizona festival favorites like tacos and hot dogs. For 2026 in honor of America's 250th, there will be the "27 Flags: Our History Through the Stars and Stripes" exhibit on display to see all 27 versions of the U.S. flag together. Best of all, the party is free to attend and is designed with families in mind, providing a playful and safe environment. While the Bash is a must-do, it’s only one piece of the city’s patriotic puzzle.

More Ways to Celebrate America’s 250th Birthday in Chandler

Beyond the downtown excitement, the region offers an energetic mix of local happenings, gatherings, and surprises. These outings bring together community, summertime indulgence, and good vibes.

 

​​SanTan Brewing Company: July 4th Brunch + Specials
July 4, 2026, 9 a.m. to 2 p.m.

Start your holiday weekend at SanTan Brewing Company. Savor a tasty brunch featuring their signature EveryDay Beer Can Chicken, served with creamy mac and cheese, for $19.25. Pair your meal with a $6 Freedom Shooter, available all day long. No reservations are required—just come hungry and ready for a great time. This one is an excellent choice for adults looking to kick off the celebration with flavorful eats and spirited drinks. Combine this brunch with other local festivities to create your ideal patriotic day itinerary.

 

Country Roots & Cowboy Boots Hoedown
July 4, 2026, 4 p.m.

Head to a star-spangled hoedown at this Western-themed evening hosted by Grill on the Green at Ironwood - IronOaks Country Club. The night begins with a bold Ribeye Steak Dinner Special at 4 p.m. and a whiskey and moonshine tasting featuring American-born spirits from 4 p.m. to 6 p.m. Soon after, the Campbell Brothers take the stage for a country performance that sets the tone for a night of dance and stars-and-stripes spirit. This is a solid choice for adults looking to celebrate with a touch of Chandler charm—be sure to contact the venue directly for reservations.

 

Indoor Escapes: Racing, Sliding & All-Ages Fun

If you’re looking to beat the heat while keeping your energy high, Chandler has you covered. Andretti Indoor Karting & Games offers high-speed Superkarts, arcade games, laser tag, duckpin bowling, and more, plus a full-service restaurant and bar to keep you fueled. For something just as exhilarating—minus the water—head to Slick City Chandler, a waterless indoor action park packed with dry slides, trampolines, and playgrounds for all ages. Both spots offer a fun-filled, air-conditioned escape perfect for families and friends spending the Fourth indoors.

Pro Tips for a Smooth & Memorable 4th

Arrive early to avoid traffic congestion, and consider using ride-sharing or carpooling when possible. Parking spots fill up quickly, and rideshare drop-off zones are often closer to the destination than general parking lots. No matter what's on your itinerary for your July 4th weekend, Downtown Chandler has lots of free parking options. Don’t forget to pack sunscreen, water bottles, and lightweight blankets for comfort.

 

Respect park rules and local ordinances—Chandler has strict regulations regarding the sale, use, and safety of fireworks. Take time to review and follow these rules and other applicable laws. Check the events calendar for the most up-to-date information, then start planning your star-spangled trip for an unforgettable 4th of July adventure.

headings.text: Celebrate National French Toast Day in Chandler
The Living Room Wine Bar & Lounge

bodyHtml:
November 28th is National French Toast Day. Celebrate the warm goodness of fluffy bread dipped in eggs and cinnamon and cooked to perfection at one of these great Chandler, Arizona restaurants. 

Downtown Chandler Café and Bakery

40 S. San Marcos Pl., Chandler 85225
(480) 855-3212
One of Chandler’s best breakfast joints, Downtown Chandler Café and Bakery also serves some of the city’s tastiest French toast. Purists can order a plate a la carte with butter and syrup ($5.49) or a platter that includes two eggs any style and the choice of bacon, sausage, or ham ($8.99). 

Diners looking for something a little more elaborate can opt for the banana nut French toast topped with bananas and pecans ($8.99). 

Sunny’s Breakfast & Lunch

1068 W. Chandler Blvd., Chandler, 85224
(480) 508-4301
The Chandler location of this local, family-owned restaurant chain is known for its huge portions and extensive menu. When it comes to French toast, you have three options at Sunny's Breakfast & Lunch, starting with the full order of three thick slices dusted with powdered sugar and cinnamon ($6.49). 

The banana nut French toast adds fresh bananas and pecans on top ($7.99), but why stop there? Go all out on National French Toast Day, and try Sunny’s Signature French Toast—three slices topped with fresh strawberries, banana slices, pecans, a strawberry reduction, powdered sugar, cinnamon, and whipped cream. 

Meridiem Kitchen and Lounge

2727 W. Frye Rd., Chandler, 85224
(480) 659-5875
A recent addition to the breakfast scene in Chandler, Meridiem Kitchen and Lounge serves a simple version of French toast made from four slices of fried French bread. The slices are covered with fresh berries and powdered sugar and served with butter and maple syrup ($11).  Add bacon, sausage patties, turkey sausage, seasonal fruit, or two eggs any style to round out your meal. 

Even Stevens Sandwiches 

11 W. Boston St., Chandler 85225
(480) 305-0127
Sandwiches and social causes may have put Even Stevens Sandwiches on the map, but if you want an indulgent plate of French toast, Even Stevens is a must. The brioche French toast features buttered brioche bread dipped in a citrus-infused batter and dusted with cinnamon sugar ($3.75). Its stuffed French toast is filled with a sweet cream cheese mix, topped with bananas and a warm berry compote, and dusted with powdered sugar ($5.95). 

The Living Room Wine Bar & Lounge

2475 W. Queen Creek Rd., Chandler 85248
(480) 855-2848
If you can’t celebrate National French Toast Day during the week—it’s on a Tuesday—head to The Living Room Wine Bar & Lounge the weekend after. The Living Room serves brunch from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. on the weekends and has an excellent French toast on the menu that comes with your choice of strawberry, maple cream, or candied pecan topping ($11.95). Make brunch even better with a bottomless mimosa or other adult beverages.

First Watch 

4955 S. Alma School Rd., Chandler 85248
(480) 659-4995
4910 W. Ray Rd., Chandler 85226
(480) 752-3754
Both Chandler locations of First Watch serve exceptional French toast. The basic version begins with thick-cut brioche bread that is dipped into a custard and fried on the griddle. It’s dusted with powdered cinnamon sugar and topped with whipped butter ($8.99). 

The Floridian French Toast® is sprinkled with wheat germ and powdered cinnamon sugar, then blanketed in fresh banana slices, kiwi, and seasonal berries ($9.79). 

Kneaders Bakery and Café

1090 W. Queen Creek Rd., Chandler 85248
(480) 355-0533
Can’t get enough French toast? Kneaders Bakery and Café serves all-you-can-eat French toast all day every weekend. The thick slices are so hearty, though, you may not be able to make it past the first plate. On weekdays, enjoy two pieces topped with strawberries and homemade caramel syrup come with whipped cream on the side ($5.99). If you’re in a hurry, the French toast can be ordered online and picked up to-go.

Black Bear Diner

2805 S. Alma School Rd., Chandler 85286
(480) 500-5753
This family-friendly, bear-themed restaurant dishes up two French toast options: thick-cut French toast and cinnamon roll French toast. Opt for the thick-cut recipe if you prefer a simple, straightforward French toast ($7.99), but if you want a decadent, coma-inducing breakfast, dig into the cinnamon roll French toast ($8.99). Made from three thick slices of cinnamon roll, it is grilled, dusted with powdered sugar, and drizzled with icing are yours at the Black Bear Diner. 

BLD Chandler

1920 W. Germann Rd., Chandler, 85286
(480) 779-8646
Locally-owned BLD Chandler (short for Breakfast Lunch Dinner) likes to get creative in the kitchen, something that holds true for its French toast as well. Its Hawaiian French toast, smothered in powdered sugar and bananas, is routine enough, but order it Captain Crunch style—dredged in pieces of the crushed cereal before hitting the griddle—for an extra special treat ($8.95, add $1 for Captain Crunch style). 

Biscuits Café

2040 S. Alma School Rd., Chandler 85286
(480) 899-0758
2090 N. Dobson Rd., Chandler 85224
(480) 726-6852
Biscuits Café offers an a la carte French toast plus five variations. French toast with berries is served with either strawberries or a 5-berry mix and whipped cream while the cinnamon apple French toast is topped with roasted cinnamon apples and a cream cheese glaze. 

There’s also a cinnamon roll French toast, served simply with a butter and syrup, and an almond-crusted French toast with chopped almonds, powdered sugar, and butter. You can get plain French toast with two eggs, any style, too. 

All five French toast combo meals come with your choice of ham, bacon, or sausage (from $9.49).

headings.text: Celebrating Martini Day in Chandler, AZ

bodyHtml:
You don’t need to leave Chandler to celebrate National Martini Day on June 19th, 2026, or any day for this classic cocktail! In honor of one of the greatest martini drinkers, James Bond 007, here are four local bars where you’ll find a great martini in Chandler.

The Brickyard Downtown

Although the cocktail menu doesn’t list a traditional martini—the line-up includes takes on classics as well as more creative selections—the bar here knows how to make one of the best you’ve ever tasted.  

If you’re particular about the vodka or gin used in your martini, The Brickyard Downtown offers a solid selection. Vodkas range from Tito’s to Belvedere Lake, while gins run the gamut from Tanqueray No. Ten to St. George Terroir. 

Another option: For craft cocktails, including martinis, check out The Ostrich, located below Crust in Downtown Chandler.

Firebirds Wood Fired Grill

The cocktail menu at Firebirds Wood Fired Grill features two martinis: the Double Black Diamond and the Dirty Bird. The Double Black Diamond is the bar’s signature martini made with New Amsterdam® Pineapple Vodka that has been infused with fresh pineapple for 21 days. Enjoy it for $7.95 during happy hour.

For a more traditional martini, try the Dirty Bird, made with chilled Tito's Vodka and garnished with bleu cheese olives. Or, order a custom martini with your choice of vodka or gin.

More martinis: If you love a good martini with your steak, Firebirds isn’t your only option. The Keg Steakhouse + Bar and DC Steak House can also satisfy your craving.

CHoP Chandler

CHoP Chandler also qualifies as a steakhouse but adds a little more casual fare to its menu, such as seven hamburger offerings and linguini with meatballs. All work well paired with a chilled martini.

If you want something light and fruity to sip during the summer, try the Peachtini.

Stone & Vine Urban Italian

Don’t let the “vine” in Stone & Vine Urban Italian fool you—this restaurant’s bar pours a great martini, too. The classic martini is always a good choice, but staff can also mix up the Cucumber Basil Martini, made with Effen Cucumber Vodka, simply syrup, basil, and muddled limes. After dinner, sip an Espresso Martini, featuring Tito’s Vodka, Baileys, espresso, and Kahlua.

Tip: Both of the specialty martinis are $2 off during happy hour.

headings.text: Chandler, Arizona: A Fun Family Adventure

bodyHtml:
This article was created in partnership with Visit USA Parks.

Welcome to Chandler, Arizona!  Chandler is a thriving city in the tech industry located minutes away from the Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport.  While business may take you to Chandler, we recommend bringing the entire family!  There are many fun family activities just waiting for you.  Here are our family’s favorite things to do, see and eat in Chandler.

FAMILY-FRIENDLY ACTIVITIES:

Chandler puts a huge emphasis on public parks.  Their goal is to have a city park within 1 mile of every house, and they have come close to achieving that goal!  The city is 70 square miles, and they currently operate more than 60 parks.  Perhaps one of the most popular parks is Playtopia! at Tumbleweed Park.  Check out the gigantic covered playground, and don’t miss the kid’s zipline!  The inner child in you will love Playtopia! too!

For a different type of park experience, visit Veterans Oasis Park to see a glimpse of the desert without leaving the city.  When you follow the paved trail around the lake, you will be greeted by ducks and fishermen trying to bring in their daily catch.  But if you explore on the gravel paths, you will enjoy even more wildlife like jack rabbits, cottontails, lizards and lots of species of birds.

The Chandler Museum is a fantastic piece of architecture!  It is located across from the second largest mall in Arizona in the Chandler Fashion Center area of town.  The entry courtyard is absolutely beautiful, covered in stunning shadows and light.  The awning and its cutouts create this pattern of light and dark which reminded me of a traditional tapestry.  Even if you only have a few minutes, play in the light created by this beautiful art!

If you are looking for a relaxing morning, stroll the streets of downtown Chandler, popping into original, local stores and a cozy coffee shop along the way.  The water benches at City Hall were a big hit with Ephraim!  And of course there are delicious restaurants in the area when you get hungry for lunch.

RESTAURANTS AND BREWERIES:

Chandler is very diverse, and the Chandler foodie scene reflects that diversity.  We stayed true to our motto, “Eat our way through vacation.”  Our first stop at Chon Thai Food led us to delicious and authentic Thai food such as this panang curry beef, not exactly what you would expect in the desert.

We were pleasantly surprised to find a colorful, family-friendly venue at one of Chandler’s breweries, The Perch.  Conveniently located in downtown Chandler, The Perch Brewery is home to more than 50 rescue birds, including parrots, macaws and cockatoos.  Relax on the outdoor patio in the shade of a large umbrella while surrounded by colorful, exotic rescue birds.  Sample a flight of their brews and pick from a tasty menu for lunch, brunch or dinner.  I loved the Irish Cast Iron Skillet, filled with corned beef, poblano hash, Oregon Street beer cheese and cabbage.  What a unique dining experience!

Chandler is also the home of the well-know SanTan Brewing Company, so we stopped in for dinner one night.  They offer down home cooking, like the Southwest Fried Chicken with green chili gravy, poblano mashed potatoes and Mexi street corn.  The atmosphere is fun, but they were also prepared to cater to kids, loaning Ephraim a Magna Doodle (magnetic drawing board) which entertained him for the whole meal.

Before leaving Arizona, we were craving some Mexican food, and thankfully we visited El Sol Mexican Cafe & Bakery.  Their tacos were wonderful…try the carnitas and carne asada.  The green chili is superb, in a burrito or by itself by the bowl.  To top it off, the service was super friendly.  Ephraim ended up with a colorful cookie that he graciously shared with Mom and Dad!

SWEET TREATS IN CHANDLER:

Great food and beer are not the only foodie options in Chandler…there is also dessert!  Depending on the time of your visit, Arizona may be a bit hot. But don’t worry, Chandler offers many fun and creative ways to stay cool.  While splash pads are common, we preferred the cold sweet treats option!

Snowtime features a modern take on traditional Korean shaved ice.  I could not understand what that meant until I tried their cold, fluffy, delicious take on shaved ice, covered with Oreo dust and chocolate drizzle!  For a second twist on a classic favorite, Rewind Ice Cream + Tea infuses your favorite breakfast cereals into creamy vanilla soft serve.  Ephraim and I loved the perfectly-blended Reese’s Puff with Brownie Bites ice cream cone!  

We loved our family-focused trip to Chandler!  Arizona fascinated me as a state.  After all, they were the 48th state of the Union, and they are proud of it!  I look forward to visiting again to explore more of Chandler and Arizona, with the state’s sunny skies, gorgeous ecosystem and charming residents!

bodyHtml:
When in Chandler, do as the locals do and feast on the city’s must-have eats. From tacos drowned in a savory broth to pizza toppings stuffed in a muffin, Chandler is home to some of the most creative and unique dishes in Arizona. If you’re looking to expand your culinary horizons, stop by these local restaurants and indulge in their signature creations.

Floridino’s Pizza & Pasta

It’s only natural that a Chandler landmark like Floridino’s Pizza & Pasta would have an iconic dish. Open since 1996, this family-owned and -operated pizzeria offers traditional pizzas and pastas. But for something truly unique, try their famous pizza muffins, doughy pockets of cheese-filled love. Selections include the original style stuffed with ham, ground beef and sausage; barbecue chicken filled with chicken breast, bacon and onions; and the gourmet white, featuring Floridino’s secret white sauce, a blend of herbs and tomatoes. Or try the staff favorite: the spicy chicken wing muffins.

Map: 590 N. Alma School Road, Chandler AZ 85224 or by phone (480) 812-8433

Chodang Tofu & BBQ

A true hidden gem north of downtown Chandler, Chodang is where you go for authentic Korean cuisine. The menu features a vast array of barbecued meats, steaming bowls of bibimbap, dumplings and cold noodles. But if you want to try a true taste of Korea, have the soft tofu soup. The dish begins with a hot earthen bowl filled with a bubbling spicy red broth and filled with silken tofu and scallions. From there, add an assortment of extras, including seafood, beef, kimchi, dumplings, bean paste or fish roe.

Map: 501 N. Arizona Av., Chandler AZ 85225 or by phone (480) 855-7712

Strips and Cones, Elmer’s Tacos

While these may sound like things you wouldn’t think to eat, at Elmer’s Tacos, they’re what puts this popular taco spot on the must-eat list. Armed with his mother’s Sonoran-style recipes, Elmer Cuen opened his namesake restaurant in 1974 and continues to dish out tasty tacos, from chicken, beef and potato served in a crisped shell.

But for something fun and different, try the strips. Freshly made with corn tortilla chips, it’s topped with shredded cheese and Elmer’s famous sauce (get it with a side of beans for a well-rounded meal). Elmer’s is also known for its chili cone, a tortilla fried in the shape of a cone and filled with mild red chili, spicy green chili or machaca. Fill it with your choice of bean and cheese, red beef, machaca beef or chicken, or green chile beef or chicken.

Map: 355 N. Arizona Ave., Chandler AZ 85225 or (480) 963-6763

Mighty Superstition, Chase’s Diner

If you’re of the notion that breakfast is the most important meal of the day, Chase’s Diner is the place for you. If you’re also of the notion that bigger is better, you’re guaranteed you’ve definitely come to the right spot.

Dubbed the Mighty Superstition, this breakfast icon is essentially a giant buttermilk pancake (big enough to feed four) that you can almost hear groan under the weight of hash browns, sausage gravy, bacon and cheddar cheese. Come with an appetite because this delicious behemoth of a meal means serious business!

Map: 2040 N. Alma School Road, Chandler AZ 85224 or (480) 855-3663

Smoked Egg Salad Sandwich, American Way Smokehouse

For a true taste of nostalgia, American Way Smokehouse will satisfy any craving you may have for food prepared with premium ingredients the old-fashioned way. The farm-to-table smokehouse, bakery and café, offers everything from handcrafted salads to ribs smoked daily.

But it’s the restaurant’s famed smokehouse sandwiches that will have you coming back for more. While there are 14 delicious sandwiches on the menu, the must-try is the smoked egg salad sandwich. Made with hard-boiled eggs that are smoked then mixed with celery and red onion, it’s served with spring mix on artisan white bread. Wash it down with vintage soda—there are more than 150 flavors to choose from—and you’ll feel like you’ve been transported to the heart of small-town America.

Map: 1509 N. Arizona Ave., Chandler AZ 85225 or (480) 772-1877

headings.text: A Guide to Running in Chandler, AZ

bodyHtml:
By Lisa Van Loo

For anyone looking to stay active or train for an upcoming race, this time of year is the perfect time to run outdoors. And for those living in or near Chandler, finding a good trail to explore or a running event couldn’t be easier. Here are a few to try or visit when in Chandler, AZ.

Desert Breeze Park

Desert Breeze Park, near Chandler Blvd. and Rural Road, offers a one-mile loop that is ideal for any skill level or pace. The view is pretty nice, too, as the loop passes around a lake and weaves through the park, which can get busy with families, especially on weekends. As a bonus, dogs are allowed on leashes.

Veterans Oasis Park

If you’re looking for a bit more distance, Veterans Oasis Park—near Chandler Heights and Lindsay Roads—offers a 4.5-mile paved trail that takes users around a lake and includes a beautiful mountain backdrop. Don’t be surprised, especially around the magic hour, to see wildlife.

Downtown Ocotillo

Looking for a more urban experience? Try a route through and near Downtown Ocotillo, a mission-style dining and retail district near Price and Queen Creek Roads. The people-watching will be great during busy times and during off-peak hours, you’ll have the sidewalks to yourself. 

Paseo Trail

Maybe you want options? Try the Paseo Trail, a 6.5-mile trail that offers a 10-foot-wide paved surface, as well as a dirt surface for those who would rather hear the crunch under their sneakers. The popular trail, which runs along the canal, begins at Galveston Street and continues to Riggs Road. Expect to see cyclists, strollers, and maybe even a few horses along the way.

Price Corridor

It’s known as a hub for tech companies, but the Price Corridor may also be a good area to clock some miles on concrete in preparation for road races, including two notable events returning to Chandler in the coming months.

Upcoming Races in Chandler, AZ

The #AZ48 Chandler half marathon occurs in October, offering runners a chance to earn a medal for clocking 13.1 miles on a flat and fast road course that goes through Downtown Chandler. Race organizers also offer a 5K option.

The popular SHE Power Half Marathon & 5K, which is Arizona’s largest all-female racing event held in late January (January 22, 2023) giving everyone a reason to kick off their New Year’s resolutions a bit early. This road race, dedicated exclusively to women runners, also takes participants along a road course through Downtown Chandler.

Races in Chandler are frequently added to the calendar with visitors frequently drawn to Chandler for some of the best 5K races in Arizona. Upcoming racing events in Chandler for 2023 include: 

  • SHE Power Half Marathon & 5K on January 22, 2023
  • Lucky Clover 5K on March 12, 2023
  • Shot in the Dark Whiskey Run on March 25, 2023
  • Hakuna Mimosa 5K on April 2, 2023
  • Donut Judge Me 5K on April 22, 2023
  • BOOM Shakalaka Endurance Run on April 29, 2023
  • ZOYO FroYo 5K on May 13, 2023
  • #AZ48 Half Marathon & 5K in October
  • Strut Your Stuffing 5K in November

bodyHtml:
It's a food lovers paradise here in Chandler with return of the Arizona Restaurant Week (ARW)! The 2026 Spring ARW is a 10-day, statewide dining event that kicks off on May 15th and will run through May 24th.

Presented by the Arizona Restaurant Association, participating restaurants will feature specific three-course prix fixe menus at a variety of restaurants. It's a great opportunity to pop in to that restaurant you've been wanting to try or visit a favorite and enjoy a three-course, prix-fixe dinner for $25, $33, $44 or $55 per person, depending on their chosen restaurant (unless noted: dinners exclude beverages, tax and gratuity). In Chandler, SanTan Brewing Co. and Spirit House are offering a prix-fixe menu for two.

Participating restaurants generally offer a select menu featuring a few appetizers, entrees and desserts not typically found on their menu offering diners a taste of something new. With over 200 participating restaurants in the Phoenix area serving up a variety of cuisine - from upscale comfort food to high-end, white-tablecloth linens, there is something to tempt your palate.

Find participating Chandler, AZ restaurants in the list below and treat yourself to a lovely and tasty spring evening.

Reservations are encouraged.

bodyHtml:
When Benjamin “Benny” McPhee and Hans “YoHans” Van Dan Elzen go to work they “walk the dog” and “pop the clutch.” But their tricks of the trade are all in the name of the toy business. In 2004, the two yo-yo enthusiasts and professionals (both have won multiple national and international competitions in the sport) founded the YoYo Factory in Uptown Chandler.

The YoYo Factory is considered the largest manufacturer and designer of yo-yos in the world, producing several lines of premier plastic and metal yo-yos with a retail storefront that features its toys on a string.

No novelty act, the factory creates yo-yos that are considered works of art—an intersection between functional technology and gaming that is reviving interest in a century-old pastime—with products like the Velocity, which incorporates a design element that allows players to simply twist a dial to tune their yo-yo.

The global company employees five full-time people and its products are used by both amateurs and top professionals who have nabbed Guinness World Records with YoYoFactory yo-yos, including most tricks in one minute, most yo-yo spinning simultaneously and world’s largest yo-yo (13 feet in diameter).

Follow the YoYo Factory on Instagram (@yoyofactory) for inspiration or stop by their retail store or check out their website at www.yoyofactory.com to shop their on-line store or learn tricks of the trade.

bodyHtml:
No one celebrates food better than Chandler. With back-to-back-to-back festivals from spring to fall, the city revels in all things delicious, from barbecue to brunch, tacos to tequila. Mark your calendars with these Chandler food fests guaranteed to satisfy all your food cravings.

Southwest Cajun Fest

Celebrate Cajun culture, cuisine, and music at the Southwest Cajun Fest, where you’ll be treated to the down-home-delicious dishes New Orleans is known for. Feast on a bevy of Southern-style bites, including jambalaya, fried alligator, catfish, etouffee, creole shrimp, hush puppies, red beans and rice, and more.

The festival will also feature live music from jazz, blues and contemporary swing revival bands. Other highlights include themed areas, a kids zone, and a family-friendly Big Easy Lounge, where guests can escape and take a break from all the action.

If You Go

  • Date: April 20, 2019
  • Time: Noon to 9 p.m.
  • Location: Dr. A.J. Chandler Park, 178 E. Commonwealth
  • Admission: $8 to $45 in advance, $10 to $55 at the gate

Arizona Craft Spirits and Cocktail Festival

Sip to your heart’s content at this 21-and-over-only event featuring the best spirits, beer, wine and craft cocktails Arizona has to offer. The event, formerly known as the Chandler Craft Spirits Festival, will spotlight award-winning vodka, bourbon, tequila, rum and more from a variety of Arizona distillers.

Local food vendors will also be on hand to serve up snacks and bites, as well as live music and a spirits competition. Led by a panel of industry professionals, the competition will judge spirits in the following categories: whiskey, rum, vodka, brandy, gin, and agave.

If You Go

  • Date: April 27, 2019
  • Time: 3 to 9 p.m.
  • Location: Dr. A.J. Chandler Park, 178 E. Commonwealth
  • Admission: $8 to $100 in advance; price increases at the gate

Moms & Mimosas

Treat Mom to a Mother’s Day to remember at Moms & Mimosas, a fun-filled day guaranteed to spoil the special women in your life. Sip on craft cocktails and nosh on brunch bites as you shop for gifts only a mother would love. You can also treat her to a blowout, manicure or massage, or participate in a brunch-themed scavenger hunt.

Tasty bites include waffles, crepes, donuts, biscuits and gravy, breakfast burritos, barbecue, burgers and more. There will also be a photo booth station, Champagne toast, Bloody Mary bar, and a greeting card making station.

If You Go

  • Date: May 11, 2019
  • Time: 9 a.m. to 4 p.m.
  • Location: Dr. A.J. Chandler Park, 178 E. Commonwealth
  • Admission: $7 in advance, $10 at the gate. Food and drink sold separately.

Rockin’ Taco Street Fest

Join 10,000 of your closest friends to partake in and celebrate one of our most beloved foods: tacos. Now in its eighth year, the Rockin’ Taco Street Fest has grown from a small parking lot event to one of the largest food festivals in the Valley.

Indulge in classic and unique taco offerings from 20 local restaurants and food purveyors, then wash it down with a frosty Margarita, cold beer or cool vodka cocktail. For tequila lovers, get your pass to the tequila tavern to sample tequilas from across the Southwest.

Throughout the day, you’ll also enjoy musical performances by mariachi bands, a custom lowrider show, and Lucha Libre Voz wrestling matches. For the kids, there will be games, bounce attractions and a piñata party.

If You Go

  • Date: September 14, 2019
  • Time: Noon to 9 p.m.
  • Location: Dr. A.J. Chandler Park, 178 E. Commonwealth
  • Admission: $10 in advance, $15 at the gate, food, and drink sold separately; $30 tequila tavern, $100 VIP in advance only​

​

SanTan Oktoberfest

Nobody does Oktoberfest like Chandler does Oktoberfest. Now it it’s 12th year, the annual event kicks off the autumn season with a celebration of Bavarian foods and German-style beers from SanTan Brewing Company. Favorites like Devil’s Pale Ale and Epicenter will be on hand, as well as seasonal brews like the HefeWeizen and Oktoberfest.

Feast on bratwurst and pretzels as you enjoy the sounds of authentic polka music. In years past there has been a brat-eating contest, stein-holding competition and live musical entertainment.  2019 Details will be announced soon!

Arizona Harvest Fest

Shop ’til you drop at this fall-focused festival and open-air market featuring local produce and artisan gourmet foods, as well as holiday items, home décor, jewelry, art and apparel. Come hungry because there will also be food vendors serving everything from wood-fired pizzas to authentic street tacos.

Enjoy live entertainment from local musicians and performers, and participate in fun competitions such as a pie-eating contest, cake walk and corn shucking battle. For the kids, there will be a kids zone, games and prizes.

If You Go

  • Date: November 10, 2019
  • Time: 9 a.m. to 4 p.m.
  • Location: Dr. A.J. Chandler Park, 178 E. Commonwealth
  • Admission: Free; food and drink sold separately.

* Please note, event dates, times, location and ticket prices are subject to change.

headings.text: Chandler Happy Hour Food with a Twist

bodyHtml:
Whatever your call it—beer o’clock, the magical moment, or the time of joy—we all love happy hour. And especially the appetizers that accompany the daily drink special experience. If you want to elevate your snack game at the next happy hour, check out these best bets for Chandler happy hour at restaurants and bars that offer appetizers with a twist.

Pita Jungle

Pita Jungle’s Mezze Board is the small plate you want to pass at happy hour. The assortment of tapas, based on the Mediterranean diet, includes hummus and chicken with pine nuts, fresh mozzarella and tomato, baked pita chips, kafta mini pockets, feta, pickles and cucumbers. Vegetarian? Choose the hummus and garbanzo confit, fresh mozzarella and tomato, baked pita chips, falafel mini pockets, feta, pickles and cucumbers.  The Arizona restaurant has two locations in Chandler.

Central Chandler location with lakefront patio at Anderson Springs:

Map: 1949 W. Ray Road, Chandler AZ 85224 or (480) 855-3232

South Chandler location at The Steelyard:

Map: 5025 S. Gilbert Rd., Chandler AZ 85249 or (480) 219-0747
 

The Sicilian Butcher

You expect an Italian eatery to deliver meatballs its own way, but the Bucket of Balls at The Sicilian Butcher restaurant by Chandler Fashion Center mall, part of the Maggiore Group of restaurants that includes Tomaso’s, makes an appetizer statement. The bucket features Tomaso’s famous meatballs made with ground veal, prime beef and pork, pine nuts, raisins, pecorino cheese, garlic and fresh herbs, with Sunday sugo sauce and toast points. Now that’s amoré!

Map: 3151 W. Frye Road, Chandler AZ 85226 or (480) 573-8550
 

Hop Social Tavern

You had us at 52 craft beers…but the relationship was sealed with the Smoked Gouda and Roasted Jalapeño Fondue. The eclectic food and brew spot focuses on American grub, but tips its hat to the Swiss-inspired melted cheese tradition for happy hour with a dash of Southwest flavor. Expect to share the velvety fondue concoction, which is made with roasted jalapeño and 8th Street Pale Ale smoked gouda and served with pretzels.

Map: 3405 W. Chandler Blvd., Chandler, AZ 85226 or (480) 485-4677

Murphy’s Law Irish Pub

The folks from the Emerald Isle didn’t invent the concept of nachos but leave it to this Irish pub to reimagine the standard happy hour appetizer—in a pleasing way at this Downtown Chandler happy hour hot spot. No need to ask for salsa as a topping for the drinking hole’s Nachos for One, which includes Murphy’s Law pub chips loaded with Murphy’s cheese sauce and corned beef with a sprinkle of green onions served in a skillet. Slainte!

Map: 58 S. San Marcos Place, Chandler AZ 85225 or (480) 812-1588

Thirsty Lion Gastropub & Grill

Rest assured the Spicy Fried Cauliflower at the Thirsty Lion Gastropub & Grill doesn’t resemble grandmother’s social hour crudité platter. In fact, the blossoming cruciferous vegetable is taken up a few notches in this modern-day appetizer interpretation that is fried with sesame tempura, spicy black bean hoisin sauce, toasted cashew, scallions, cilantro and Sriracha aioli.

Map: 3077 W. Frye Road, Chandler AZ 85226 or (480) 786-5799
 

Z’Tejas

Fries are a universal happy hour food—the perfect accompaniment to a late afternoon beverage deal—but at Z’Tejas, the Yuca Fries deviate a bit from the normal appetizer script. With a flair for the zesty, this version of tubular golden fries are packed with tons of Southwest Mexican attitude and heat—and infused with chili oil, sriracha aioli, cotija, tajin and cilantro.

Map: 7221 W. Ray Road, Chandler AZ 85226 or (480) 893-7550

bodyHtml:
The season of festive giving is here, and Chandler makes it easy to check off every name on your list. From Chandler Fashion Center to independent makers throughout town, you’ll find memorable gift ideas along with new ways to browse through the Choose Chandler program.

What’s New for the Season

Chandler Fashion Center added several notable stores in 2025. Among them is gorjana, a jewelry brand known for modern pieces designed with layering in mind. JD Sports, a leading athletic fashion and sneaker retailer, also opened this year with trend-forward styles across its footwear and apparel collections.

Big Stops First: Chandler Fashion Center & Scheels

Start your gift hunt at Chandler Fashion Center, a major hub with more than 180 shops and dining options. Dillard’s, Macy’s, Coach, and the Apple Store make the center a strong jumping-off point for practical picks and splurge-worthy finds.

At the center, SCHEELS stands out as a 220,000-square-foot sports retailer with 75 specialty shops. Attractions include an indoor Ferris wheel, arcade games, and an aquarium. It is a great place to build holiday gift ideas centered on outdoor gear, fan apparel, and active-lifestyle accessories.

Sweet, Savory, & Sippable Gifts for Every Food Lover

Our city is full of options to make the foodies on your list smile. Check out downtown’s d’Vine Gourmet to find Arizona-made gourmet foods, handcrafted candies, snacks, and gift baskets that showcase state flavors. Nearby, Mingle + Graze prepares charcuterie boards, gourmet sandwiches, and other delights to serve as ready-made spreads for gatherings or night-in surprises.

Any sweet lovers on your list? Chandy’s Candies features handcrafted chocolates and seasonal creations suited for host gifts or workplace exchanges. And for a truly indulgent holiday surprise, there’s nothing quite like a sweet or savory pie. PIEfection elevates the experience with seasonal specials and a featured pie of the month, giving you plenty of delicious ways to share something truly memorable.

For something a little more spirited, consider a unique find for the beer enthusiast in your life. SanTan Brewing Company offers their unique, 32-oz. CanZilla Growlers, allowing guests to transport their favorite SanTan beer from the pub to their location of choice. The recyclable cans are single-use, packaged, labeled, and sealed on-site at the pub, and the beer stays fresh for up to seven days.

If you’re hunting for a fun, unexpected gift, check out The Sugar Bar’s lively, event-centric atmosphere. Treat someone to one of their specialty tasting options, like a Beer & Candy Flight or a Wine & Candy Flight, each pairing curated pours with matching candy for a playful, memorable twist. Pop in to enjoy a drink, soak up the upbeat vibe, or grab a bottle or can to go.

Choose Chandler Holiday Pass Highlight

The free Choose Chandler Holiday Pass gives shoppers a digital way to discover boutiques, eateries, and attractions while earning points to win prize giveaways. 

Featured pass businesses include Copper Brim Hat Co., Highland Yard Vintage Market, and Zia Records, all offering locally rooted items and specialty finds. Three Dog Bakery serves human-grade treats for pets, while Bricks & Minifigs Chandler carries LEGO sets, minifigures, and accessories. The NOW Massage Chandler sells gift cards for services that work well as self-care offerings.

With every stop you explore and every point you earn, the Holiday Pass turns shopping local into a rewarding adventure, making it easier (and more fun) to fill your season with meaningful gifts and memorable experiences.

Fresh Gift Categories for Every Kind of Shopper

Experience seekers will love receiving activity passes available throughout the city, including open-skate sessions at Ice Den Chandler or an ESCAPE:chandler gift card for a challenge-driven outing built around teamwork and problem-solving. Another idea is a Makutu’s Island gift card that gives families an unforgettable day of adventure filled with active play and imagination.

For friends who cherish locally made and Arizona-inspired finds, seek out small-batch goods and distinctive items that reflect the community. The Downtown Chandler Farmers Market is a reliable stop for regional flavors and locally produced items, while independently owned shops around downtown offer creative pieces with a strong sense of place.

Plan Your Perfect Chandler Shopping Day

To map out your shopping route, pair this guide with the Choose Chandler Holiday Pass and the planning tools on our Plan Your Visit page. Build a full day that moves from Chandler Fashion Center to downtown and turns your search for seasonal finds into a fun getaway in our desert city.

headings.text: Chandler Local Bite Spotlight: Espo's Mexican Food

bodyHtml:
It’s rare that a restaurant stays in business for more than 50 years. But Espo’s Mexican Food in Chandler isn’t just any restaurant.

In 1974, David Espinoza opened this storied Chandler spot (located just west of Chandler Fashion Center), where he started out serving hamburgers and American fare. Soon after, the restaurant began offering authentic Mexican cuisine, based on the recipes of David’s wife Olga. Eight years later, the couple’s son Leon Espinoza took over the restaurant in 1982 and continues to manage it today.

Food-wise, the restaurant is best known for its green chile. It’s the most requested item on the menu and the No. 1 best-seller at the restaurant. “It’s a recipe that everyone wants and everyone wants to know about it,” says Espinoza. “And that secret is right inside of me.”

The menu is rounded out by burritos, tacos, flautas, tostadas, quesadillas, enchiladas, chimichangas, taco salads and tamales. The drink menu includes beer, micheladas, agua fresca and Papi Chulo lemonade. For one of the best bargains in town, the restaurant’s Taco Tuesdays are a steal. Customers can enjoy great deals like 10 tacos for $10 and margaritas for just $2. Espo’s is also known for providing a fun, lively atmosphere with its weekly DJ and entertainment on the patio (currently suspended due to the pandemic).

As much as Espinoza has stayed true to serving Mexican food made from his mother’s original recipes, he also says change is a key part of his restaurant’s sustained success. He’s seen success with many of the restaurant’s vegetarian dishes, as diners have become more health conscience.

Espinoza grew up cooking alongside his mother. Aside from stints in advertising and marketing, and as a paralegal, he’s always worked at the restaurant. He says as a young person, he didn’t always appreciate the connection he had with his family when he was working at his parent’s restaurant. But that all changed after his mother passed away. Espo’s closed for about a year. After fielding many questions about what he would do next, he decided the answer was clear: start cooking again.

“Once I got back in the kitchen, I could feel it. I felt my mother and her presence, and her drive and her understanding. She used to say, ’You cook for technique. I cook for love.’ ” says Espinoza. “After I could feel my mother and her presence cooking, then I began cooking out of love. The difference is amazing. I think that’s what’s important about carrying on these traditions and the family values in the recipes that we grew up with.”

Espinoza says his goal is to be there forever, and that there’s no way that the restaurant would ever leave Chandler. “It’s part of Chandler and that’s a big deal. That’s a big honor,” he says. “I’m proud of that. So as long as I can keep it going, I will.”

headings.text: Chandler Local Bite Spotlight: Fruit Daddy

bodyHtml:
By Lauren Saria

Tasty snacks and treats are always in demand.  And Chandler, undoubtedly has some of the best spots for ice cream and frozen treats around. Including some unexpected and unique twists to indulge your sweet and savory snack craving. It’s been almost one year since Fruit Daddy started serving Mexican street food-inspired treats, just north of Downtown Chandler. And these days, it’s not uncommon for customers to come to the small snack shop from all over the Valley, drawn by the menu of colorful, over-the-top snacks and frozen sweets.

But husband-and-wife owners Laura Solano and Jose Moreno didn’t open Fruit Daddy with the intention to become a snack destination known for offerings like the Chamoyada, a vibrant orange and red mango smoothie made with Tajin (pronounced “ta-heen” and made from dried chiles, dehydrated lime and salt), chamoy (a variety of savory sauces and condiments), diced fruit and tamarind candy.

The couple’s plans started with a much simpler idea.

Chandler residents Solano and Moreno have owned a barbershop in the same strip mall as the Fruit Daddy for nearly six years. They were both working there cutting hair before opening the snack shop.

“We got really busy and customers used to wait outside,” Solano says. “So we were like why not put a little snack shop next door where they can get a snack while they wait?”

So they opened Fruit Daddy as a place where their barbershop customers could wait for their appointments or stop by for a snack after getting a haircut. The concept is relatively straightforward: To offer “just fresh” snacks inspired by the couple’s Hispanic heritage, Solano says.

Some of the most popular items include drinks like the Chamoyada. Other popular items include Mangoneada, a shaved ice made with Chamoy, Tajin and mango syrup and topped with dried mango and a tamarind stick; or the Tornado, a drink made with Sprite, sparkling water, oranges, pineapple, Tajin, Chamoy and lemon.

Other menu options include snacks, which range from street corn and ice cream, to fresh ceviche. On the restaurant’s social media, fans can find photos of Instagram-able items like elote-topped ramen, Cheetos-covered elote, and Hot Cheetos smothered in cheese. There are some lighter options, too, including fresh fruit with Tajin or crema.

Fruit Daddy has already become so popular that Solano says they’re adding a trailer soon so that they can bring their drinks and snacks to customers around town. Some day they hope to have multiple locations in metro Phoenix.

“We’re family-owned, but we’re here to help people grow into Fruit Daddy, too,” she says. “We want people who work with us to grow and eventually be able to own their own Fruit Daddy.”

In the meantime, the couple is focusing on giving back to their Chandler community. They offer discounts for Chandler High School students, as well as for law enforcement, teachers and military members. Solano also says they hope to work with local schools and organizations to host fundraisers at Fruit Daddy.

“We’re always open to do anything like that or events to help out with the community,” she says.

headings.text: Chandler Local Bite Spotlight: Hash Kitchen

bodyHtml:
Breakfast may be the most important meal of the day, but Hash Kitchen makes brunch the most fun.

Disco balls hang overhead, a DJ spins party tunes, and every wall features an Instagram-able saying or backdrop. Not to mention, the restaurant’s 5,000-square-foot Chandler location boasts a build-your-own Bloody Mary bar with more than 60 add-ons, ranging from pickles and bacon, to deep fried ravioli and hush puppies.

The fun continues on the menu. Executive chef Joey Maggiore reimagines breakfast staples to create new dishes such as Blue Corn Banana Fosters Pancakes with caramelized bananas, candied pecans and cinnamon whipped cream; and Lucky Charms French Toast encrusted with the popular cereal and topped with dehydrated marshmallows and gold dust.

Waffles, eggs Benedict, frittatas and scrambles compliment the restaurant’s signature hashes. Try the Hangover Short Rib Hash featuring jalapeno corn bread and potato hash, poached eggs, onion rings and demi hollandaise sauce. Or opt for an out-of-the-box offering like Breakfast Cannelloni, rolled pasta sheets stuffed with bacon, short rib ragu, cheeses, bechamel, fried eggs and fried leeks.

Those who favor lunch can dine on salads, burgers and sandwiches. Hash Kitchen also offers gluten-free choices and has a kids menu for diners under the age of 12.

Food is only half of the fun at Hash Kitchen—alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages are an important part of the brunch experience, too. At the Bloody Mary bar, guests can choose from salt rim offerings, several types of tomato juice, and base vodkas, including house-infused options, in addition to the seemingly endless toppings.

Overwhelmed by the possibilities? Order the restaurant’s original version, or sip a premade Bloody Mary from a drink pouch, instead. The Bloody in a Bag comes in flavors like Type O, bacon vodka with “chili and peppers bloody mix.”

Mixologist Sheldon Wiley’s bar serves other boozy drink pouches, rum slushies in a disco ball topped with cotton candy and mimosa flights. But the Cereal Shooter Flight—four coconut milk-based cocktails that mimic classic childhood cereals like Fruity Pebbles and Cap’n Crunch—are a Hash Kitchen favorite.

The goal is for Hash Kitchen to be “fun, over-the-top and completely one-of-a-kind,” according to Maggiore, who co-founded The Maggiore Group along with his father, Tomaso Maggio, the man behind Valley favorite Tomaso’s. Their restaurant concepts include The Sicilian Butcher, which boasts a make-your-own meatball meal, and The Sicilian Baker, which has a cannoli bar.

headings.text: Chandler Local Bite Spotlight: Mingle + Graze

bodyHtml:
By Lauren Saria

On any given Friday afternoon, you may find Mahfam Moeeni-Alarcon catering a party, greeting customers at her downtown Chandler shop—or somewhere in between. The on-the-go lifestyle is a side effect of the success of the business she owns with her husband, Cristobal.

“What we call it is an elevated cheese shop,” Moeeni-Alarcon says.

Open since January, Mingle + Graze is a restaurant, cheese shop and catering kitchen all rolled into one. “We’re small but mighty,” she says.

On one hand, the shop serves as home base for Moeeni-Alarcon's catering business, which specializes on “grazing tables.” These stunning displays can cover an entire 8-foot table, so guests feast—and feast their eyes—on an impressive bounty of cheese, dried fruits, pretzels, cured meats and more.

At the store, customers enjoy smaller versions of the displays. But the storefront is more than just a place to pick up a great wedge of Welsh cheddar or potato chip-studded Gouda.

“It’s not a crunchy cheese,” Moeeni-Alarcon explains of the latter. “The chips just add body. It’s really cool.”

“You won’t find that at Whole Foods,” she adds.

In addition to selling top-quality cheese and charcuterie, Mingle + Graze also serves light fare including sandwiches, salads and soups. And since it’s BYOB, diners can bring in their favorite bottle of wine or beer from nearby breweries, including SanTan Brewing Company and The Perch.

The space itself is a part of Mingle + Graze's charm. Formerly home to Wimpy’s Paradise, the storefront now is decorated with an eclectic mix of chairs, tables and mirrors that Moeeni-Alarcon found and upcycled herself.

But before she could begin refinishing the floors and hanging art, Moeeni-Alarcon had to convince the landlord she should get the space; it was no easy feat. Almost immediately after the long, narrow space became available, interested businesses began inquiring about the lease. Moeeni-Alarcon, who had never owned a business before, knew she'd be a long shot but decided to give the landlord a taste of her idea anyway.

“I was like, you know what, I’m going to make him a Mingle Box,” she remembers. “I was like, there’s no way I’m going to get it. But I gave him the Mingle Box and he thought it was really cool.”

In the end, she got the store, which allows both her and her husband to work just minutes from their home in Chandler.

“We’re a part of the community so it’s really nice to circle back and have it all come together,” she says. “It just felt like it was kind of meant to be.”

bodyHtml:
By Lauren Saria

Decades ago, Yoshi and Sanae Otomo lived a serene life in a lakeside Chandler neighborhood. The couple moved to Arizona from Japan in 1994. He worked for a Japanese trading company and she was a stay-at-home mom raising the couple’s daughter on home-cooked Japanese cuisine.

Then the Japanese economy took a turn for the worse.

“My option was basically to go back to Japan and continue as a salaryman or find some other employment here,” Yoshi remembers. “Well, we love Arizona very much and we thought let’s do something different.”

“It was easy thinking,” Sanae says with a laugh.

The couple opened Shimogamo in a Chandler strip mall in October 2003. They had never owned their own restaurant, but nevertheless decided to sublease a 1,600-square-foot space from the adjacent Asian market to open up their own sushi bar. The restaurant still is small, sleek, but casual.

At the time, Yoshi says there were few “high-quality Japanese restaurants” in the area. So the goal was clear: to provide traditional Japanese food made with quality ingredients to the East Valley community.

Sanae used her experience as a talented home cook to create the kitchen menu, which still includes dishes like Saikyo-Miso Cod and Teriyaki Spare Ribs made using her recipes. A team of Japanese sushi chefs brought in and broke down fresh fish to offer diners beautiful pieces of sashimi including the restaurant's signature White Truffle Amberjack garnished with red onion, truffle oil, ponzu and microgreens.

The dedication to quality ingredients and simple techniques attracted top talent to the Chandler restaurant sushi bar. Some of Phoenix’s top Japanese chefs have worked at Shimogamo, including chef Yasu Hasino, who later went on to open his own Yasu Sushi Bistro in north Phoenix.

Today, Zach Rodenburg is the restaurant’s head sushi chef. And dedication to quality still drives his every move behind Shimogamo's 12-seat sushi bar. “There are no shortcuts,” he says.

Shimogamo’s chefs still butcher fresh fish and now seek out the rarest, most delicious fish they can find to feature on the restaurant’s special board. On any given day, diners might find tuna belly or fresh oysters available at the restaurant.

Rodenburg, who’s been with the restaurant since 2011, says it’s not just the food that’s made Shimogamo such a lasting business in Chandler. It’s also the people.

“We’ve been around for so long, we have tons of regulars,” he says. “Our chefs have always been good about getting to know everyone.”

Plus, there’s the presence of the owners themselves. Sanae often comes to the restaurant with her young grandson to cook food for the family and the staff. Yoshi also still works at Shimogamo regularly.

“It’s very much a family business. We can't get Yoshi to take a day off," Rodenburg says with a smile.

headings.text: Chandler Local Bite Spotlight: The Hidden House

bodyHtml:
Its cheeky name might suggest The Hidden House is off the beaten path. But the 1939 cottage-turned-restaurant in historic Downtown Chandler is no longer a mystery.

Launched in August by restaurateurs Gavin Jacobs and Jackie and Elliott Hall—the team behind The Brickyard—The Hidden House brings a new level of sophistication to the Chandler restaurant scene. Located west of SanTan Brewing Company on Commonwealth Avenue, the historic cottage has been in the Hall family for years and sat empty for a long time.

Now, the 850-square-foot house, where some of the original elements have been preserved, has a renewed life that harkens back to a Colonial, cozy vintage look with white wainscoting and dark wood floors—and plenty of room for modern hospitality options.

Though the footprint of The Hidden House is small (it seats 34 guests), beyond the iron entrance gate, the property offers four different dining experiences in one location, according to Jacobs. The concept includes a formal dining space in the cottage (think white linens), a front outdoor patio and bar, and a casual indoor/outdoor terrace and bar area that connects to a 2,200-square-foot hanger decorated with real trees and chandeliers, where patrons can dine and which also doubles as an event venue and live music spot.

“No matter where you sit, we created options for customers that are both affordable and offer an opportunity to splurge,” says Jacobs of the transitional ambience and chef-driven, New American-inspired menu, which is flavored with Spanish, Italian and Asian influences that appeals to diverse palates.

The seasonal fare, overseen by chef Aaron Rickel, includes appetizers like avocado toast, pork belly tacos, lobster mac & cheese, and Hamachi crudo. Entrée selections include such dishes as Peking duck breast, Scottish salmon, Korean barbeque short rib and a variety of soups and salads, and signature desserts.

The Hidden House’s draft cocktail program, led by beverage director Bobby Kramer and head mixologist Michael Regan, also provides a nostalgic nod to simpler yet elegant dining times. The cocktail book lineup includes generation-specific drinks such as sidecars, Hemingway daiquiris, and chartreuse swizzles from pre-Prohibition, Prohibition, Tiki and New Age eras—designed lightest to darkest—and tap cocktails that are made in-house. In addition, approximately 100 wines, eight beers on tap, and more than 30 canned beers are available.

“There was more than a need for the concept,” says Jacobs of The Hidden House’s multi-dining vibe, a focus the team put a lot of thought and detail into before opening the doors for business last summer.

“We wanted to offer an upscale, outdoor dining experience to the community with something new and innovative that hasn’t been done before. There’s really nothing else like it across Arizona…and maybe in the United States.”

The Hidden House offers flexibility to diners with reservations for on-site dining, delivery options or take out for their various entrees and cocktails to go.

headings.text: Chandler Local Bite Spotlight: The Kind Bean

bodyHtml:
Kindness matters in life. It also matters in business, say Clay and Jen Novick, husband/wife owners of The Kind Bean, a neighborhood café they opened in 2017 that serves coffee, specialty drinks, grab-n-go breakfast and lunch, and handmade sweets.

The self-proclaimed foodies, who met while working in the hospitality industry in Tucson, share a common passion for delivering high-quality food and beverages, along with genuine customer service. The couple had previously owned a video and audio business in Chandler and were partners in a chocolate franchise in New York. Dismayed by the lack of common kindness in corporate America, they wanted to create something different.

“The world needs a little bit more kindness. Our thought was we could at least do our part. We wanted to build our own community, make friendships, and bond with people and customers. For us, the best way we knew how to do that was through food and people, and being able to mix them together,” explains Clay of their “kind coffee” approach.

The duo’s brand of business—entrepreneurship with a heart—goes above and beyond what they offer at their 1,000-square-foot coffee and sweet shop located at Pecos and McQueen roads. That includes getting to know customers, greeting them by their names, and understanding what they might need that particular today, whether it’s coffee, avocado toast or hugs.

“We give customers things they need, like coffee and treats. We also want our customers to tell us what they need to start their day,” Clay says.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by The Kind Bean (@thekindbean) on Apr 15, 2020 at 8:31am PDT

Customers run the gamut from teachers, parents and students, to healthcare workers, first responders and law enforcement.  “We have all walks of life who come in. It doesn’t matter who you are, what you look like or what you order. We give everyone the same experience,” he adds. “For us, it should happen without being said or being asked. It should be the norm.”

While The Kind Bean serves diverse micro-roasted selections, lattes, botanicals and teas, as well as an array of light nibbles, pastries and sweets handcrafted by Jen, it offers something much more than the average coffee pit stop.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by The Kind Bean (@thekindbean) on May 7, 2020 at 7:30am PDT

“Customers often say, ‘I never get a greeting like that from my own family.’ And that’s why they keep coming back,” Jen says of the repeat patron base. “Kindness is pushed out the door and into customers’ lives and their jobs.”

As part of the domino, feel-good vibe. The Kind Bean’s Pay It Kind program gives customers the opportunity to load money onto gift cards for other customers, a favor that is routinely returned without recognition. The kind effect also has cast a wide, but familiar net, leaving a lasting impression on visitors who come from near and far to experience the café’s menu lineup and positive coffee shop culture.

“We get customers from all over—from places like New York and Minnesota—and they can’t believe we’re in a big city, but have a small-town feel,” says Jen. “I’m proud of that.”

headings.text: Chandler Local Bite Spotlight: The Sicilian Butcher

bodyHtml:
The butcher board and meat cleaver wall, along with the wine bottle chandeliers, at The Sicilian Butcher Craft Meatball and Charcuterie Bar in Chandler aren’t just clever “transport me to Italy” decorating touches. The visuals have meaning to co-founder and executive chef Joey Maggiore, whose family ties are deeply connected to the food and restaurant business.

His father Tomaso is an Italian culinary expert who opened Tomaso’s, the award-winning fine dining establishment 43 years ago in Phoenix, and also owns a winery outside of Palermo, Italy. In addition, his grandfather was a butcher in Sicily and his father-in-law is a pastry chef.

Like its sister property in north Scottsdale, the Italian eatery, located in the Chandler Viridian Primegate at Chandler Fashion Center, pays homage to family recipes handed down over the years that Maggiore has tweaked for the chef-driven menu.

“Everything here feels like a touch of home,” explains Maggiore of the restaurant, which was conceived by the chef, his wife Cristina, and their business partner Flora Tersigni. Adjacent to the dining space is The Sicilian Baker, a cannoli bar, pastry counter and café.

“The concept is about family history and Sicilian-inspired cuisine, and we put it all together in one place. Every little detail is a resemblance of how I grew up in this business,” adds Maggiore.

Based on a build-your-own meal dining adventure, The Sicilian Butcher features 10 hand-rolled meatballs made daily with steak, lamb, lump crab, shrimp and meatless options, plus Tomaso’s Sicilian version with ground veal, prime beef, pork, pine nuts, raisins, and pecorino cheese. Meatballs can be paired with several house made sauces, among them garlic-basil marinara, pesto trapanese, parmigiano cream, truffle mushroom, and spicy arrabbiata, and served with bases such as house-extruded pasta, polenta or risotto.

The restaurant also offers flatbreads, sandwiches, desserts, and Sicilian-style bruschetta and charcuterie selections, including the granddaddy of them all, the Sicilian in Strada, a five-foot-long charcuterie board with panelli fritters, arancini, cazzilli, artisanal meats and cheeses, craft meatballs with polenta, pickled vegetables and house preserved jams.

“We have a limited menu, but every dish is perfect,’ says Maggiore.

The 6,500-square-foot restaurant includes a craft cocktail program, which boasts the usual suspects like Aperol spritzes and the earth’s largest Negroni (a Guinness World Record cocktail created by mixologist Sheldon Wiley), a pasta room, a chef’s table, an indoor-outdoor bar, and an outdoor lounge and dining space with fireplaces.

Chandler was an easy choice for the Sicilian Butcher’s second location, according to Maggiore. “Our Tatum location took off so well that we wanted to bring it to another part of the Valley,” he says. “We’ve always loved Chandler and we were welcomed with many open arms. When we saw the location at the Viridian, we know it was the perfect Butcher spot.”

Maggiore attributes The Sicilian Butcher’s relaxed and open, but upscale feel to Cristina, the restaurant’s lead designer. He credits the feel-good, modern spin on the Sicilian-influenced cuisine to his family’s decades-long passion for creating an exceptional dining experience.

“You don’t have to travel to Italy to have amazing Italian food,” says Maggiore. “Come to our restaurant. You’ll get great hospitality, an Italian kiss and food so remarkable you’ll think you are in Italy.”

bodyHtml:
Walk through the doors of Chase’s Diner in Chandler, AZ, and you’re instantly transported to the 1950s. Neon lights bounce off the checkered floor, the jukebox hums familiar oldies, and plates stacked with pancakes and burgers glide past on their way to hungry guests.

As charming as the retro vibe is, however, the real secret ingredient is the people who make the diner one of the best places to eat in Chandler. Regulars swap stories with staff who greet them like family, and if you’ve visited more than once, don’t be surprised if someone remembers your favorite order.

A Family Tradition at Chase's Diner

Since 1997, Chase’s Diner has been proudly family-owned—not just in name, but in spirit. Owners Skip and Nancy Chase—who grew up in Buffalo, New York, where diners are woven into daily life—brought that tradition west when they opened their Chandler spot. Over the years, three generations of Chases have taken part in running the restaurant, with a fourth already eager to join in when she’s old enough. That sense of continuity is why so many locals count Chase’s among the best locally-owned restaurants Chandler AZ has to offer.

What to Eat at Chase's Diner (Hint: Don’t Skip Dessert)

Breakfast lovers rave about the Kitchen Sink Skillet, a hearty plate that piles eggs, potatoes, veggies, meat and cheese into one delicious scramble. If you’re craving something classic, the half-pound burgers are a shining example of classic American diner food in Chandler—big, juicy and cooked to order.

But here’s the insider move: Save room for dessert. Grandma Shirley’s carrot cake is a legend in its own right with moist layers, rich frosting and a reputation that draws fans back again and again.

Want to branch out? Try the homemade meatloaf served “Matt’s Style,” with spicy green pork chili and gravy. Or go off-menu and let Chef Andre surprise you. Plenty of regulars say, “make me anything,” and never leave disappointed.

Family-Friendly Dining in Chandler

This is a place where everyone finds something to love. Kids get a kick out of dropping coins in the jukebox and pointing at the quirky Christmas ornaments hanging from the ceiling year-round. Grandparents settle into booths surrounded by décor that feels like home. Parents appreciate the scratch-made meals and relaxed vibe that works for Saturday morning pancakes or a no-fuss family dinner. No wonder Chase’s is one of the most family-friendly restaurants in Chandler.

Chase's Diner in the Chandler Community

The diner has always had deep roots in the community. Over the years, Chase’s has supported Chandler schools, youth sports, the Boys & Girls Club, and, most recently, raised more than $20,000 for the Chandler Law Enforcement Association during a Dessert Night fundraiser. Here, a good meal often comes with the satisfaction of supporting a restaurant that gives back to the local community.

Why Locals Love Chase's Diner

Sure, the food is memorable, but what really lingers is the experience: a wave from your server across the dining room, the sound of the jukebox playing a song you forgot you loved, and that slice of carrot cake you swore you couldn’t finish but somehow did.

So when you’re mapping out the best places to eat in Chandler, don’t skip this retro gem. At Chase’s Diner, you’re not just another customer, you’re part of the story.

Chase's Diner: 2040 N Alma School Rd., Chandler AZ 85224

ld.keywords: Local Spotlight, Date Night, Downtown Chandler, Happy Hour, Music, Nightlife

bodyHtml:
With “Local” being the buzzword in the dining industry, Craft 64 in Downtown Chandler is not just marketing lip service. The wood-fired restaurant and bar, which is known for its craft pizza and beer, specializes in scratch, organic fare and is committed to making sure its supply footprint stays in the neighborhood.

All the produce and vegetables at Craft 64 are harvested from McClendon Select, the flour used in the pizza dough is from Hayden Mills, most of the beer featured is brewed in Arizona, and the extra virgin oil hails from Queen Creek Olive Mill.

“We have a love of local,” explains James Swann, one of the four co-owners of Craft 64, which opened in Chandler three years ago on Buffalo Street. “We source everything we possibly can locally. We don’t own a freezer, we don’t own a microwave. And everything comes in day by day from local vendors, and is prepared in our kitchen fresh that day or the day before, depending on what it is. And of course, if we source things that aren’t actually made in Arizona, they’re coming from a locally-owned company in Arizona.”

The ingredients might be community-driven, but the restaurant’s centerpiece—a Mugnaini wood-burning pizza oven—is direct from Tuscany, Italy. The Rolls Royce of pizza ovens allows Craft 64 to create artisanal pizzas that are a bit different from its competitors.

“We run our ovens at a much lower temperature. Our ovens usually sit at about 650 to 700 degrees and the pizzas tend to come out with a little more char, a little more than what you see with the everyday classic, which is what we believe separates us from the others,” says Swann.

And at Craft 64, it’s not just about creating the perfect pie—it’s about using its novelty oven to cook a range of dishes, including root vegetables, salmon, mac-n-cheese and baked chicken options.

“We prefer to think of ourselves a little differently than a pizza joint. \. We really prefer to think of ourselves as a wood-fired restaurant,” says Swann. “If you check our menu, you’ll see that we have steak and specialty dishes on a regular basis just to highlight the different things that can cook in a wood-fired oven alongside the pizza.”

The eatery takes its beverage program just as seriously as its cooking methods, which is developed to accentuate the flavors of the wood-fired menu. Craft 64 creates and brews its own beers in partnership with SunUp Brewing Company featuring staples and seasonal selections such as Smooove Hoperator IPA, Frolic Pale Ale, Belgian Bombshell, and Mango Shandy. It also has a robust global wine list including its own in-house varietal 64 Pinot Noir made in Willamette, Oregon. Plus, the restaurant offers premium spirits, and signature craft and specialty cocktails.

The result is a dining experience that entices your senses with distinct food and beverages, superior customer service and a chill environment the minute you walk through the door, according to Swann.

“The first thing that hits you is the aroma. And you’re going to [be greeted with] friendly smile and be presented with items and options that are made in-house and sourced locally. There’s a lot of care and attention given to those facts,” says Swann. “In addition, we do a little bit of live music on the weekends but it’s all acoustics. It’s just a nice, comfortable atmosphere to enjoy.”

Map: 68 W. Buffalo St., Chandler, AZ 85225 or (480) 247-3002
