headings.text: Chandler Local Spotlight: Feringhee Modern Indian Cuisine

bodyHtml:
The name translates to “foreigner,” but at the upscale Feringhee Modern Indian Cuisine restaurant, the hope is to connect diners through a common, cultural interest: exquisite food.

Madhavi Reddy—a Chandler resident who owns Pastries N Chaat in Tempe and Saffron Indian Grocery N Restaurant outlets in Phoenix, Scottsdale and San Antonio—developed the restaurant concept along with co-founder and celebrated international chef Sujan Sarkar. Reddy, who has worked in IT and marketing, has always had an interest in agriculture and food, and wanted to fill a noticeable gap in the fine-dining Indian scene in the Valley.

“I was in the industry and thought we can do more than this. We can elevate Indian cuisine, bring it to the mainstream, and demonstrate what it is and how flavorful it is. I just wanted to show the journey of India—the different flavors, different states, different cuisines,” she explains.

Whether you’ve eaten Indian cuisine or not, Feringhee, is a surprising dining departure, according to Reddy. The menu features traditional flavors from diverse regions of India with a contemporary twist on the aromatic cuisine.

The team tapped chef Karan Mittal, whose background includes working in Michelin-starred restaurants and earning the Rising Star of the Year 2018 by Food & Wine Magazine Ireland, to execute their vision.

Mittal references his upbringing in Delhi, recipes from his grandmother, and travels throughout India and the world—as well as experimenting with local and seasonal ingredients such as huckleberries, avocados, finger limes and mushrooms—for inspiration and to bring a greater depth and flavor to Feringhee’s interpretative menu.

“The biggest passion of my life is to explore more of Indian food, get into the detail and showcase that to the world,” he says.

Diners can enjoy small and sharing plates such as chutney flights, masala ricotta kulcha and coastal scallops. Larger plates include seasonal squash and vegetable kofta, Hyderbadi eggplant, Old Delhi butter chicken, dum jackfruit biryani and Kashmiri lamb.

Dark chocolate cremeux, coconut panna cotta, kulfi popsicles, and house ice cream and sorbets are available for dessert. Some menu items are vegetarian and gluten-free.

“We make sure that we portray Indian food as it should be. Even in terms of the spices and the taste. We present authentic, traditional food in a new light using local ingredients, some seasonal touches, interesting textures and a lot of innovation so that it feels modern to the eye,” says Mittal. “But when you dig in, it transports you back to the memories that we’ve all grown up with. That is what the experience that we want to recreate here—nostalgia through a modern lens.”

The upscale, chic space has a main dining area with a bar, private dining room, patio and banquet hall and is decorated in golden saffron, blues and browns and warm woods indicative of authentic Indian design. The extensive beverage component includes Indian whiskies and spirits, specialty cocktails, and global wine and beers.

Since the restaurant's opening in 2022, the Chandler Indian restaurant has been recognized for excellent food and service, receiving numerous accolades. Here are some of Feringhee's restaurant awards:

  • Devour 2025 Silver Medal Winner
  • 100 Best Restaurants 2025 by Phoenix New Times
  • Foodist Award Finalist 2024 - Best World Flavor 
  • 100 Best Restaurants 2024 by Phoenix New Times
  • 100 Best Restaurants 2023 by Phoenix New Times
  • Best of the Valley 2023 - Editorial Pick for Best Indian restaurant
  • 2022 Best New Restaurant of the Year by Phoenix Magazine

“Our goal is to have the finest cuisine in the valley. My message to everybody is we did our best to bring the best food, not only to the Indian community but to the mainstream,” says Reddy. “Come see what kind of journey we are going to walk you through.”

headings.text: Chandler Local Spotlight: Hop Social Grill

bodyHtml:
In today’s world of fast food, fast-casual, fusion cuisine and concept mash-ups, the idea of a tried-and-true tavern gets lost. Somewhere between the relaxed watering hole of a pub and the high-end dining of a steakhouse, tavern hospitality offers the just-right balance of good drinks, good food and friendly service. It’s a bill the aptly named Hop Social Grill fills in spades.

Friends and business partners David and Christie Burnett, and Bud and Kelly Gabriel opened Hop Social near the Chandler Fashion Center in late 2017. Based on a similar concept they created in Oregon, it is the team’s first Arizona restaurant.

The décor sets the tone for this restaurant’s welcoming vibe. The wrap-around bar with TVs to watch the latest game, a dining area with plush booths and chairs, and a comfortable outdoor patio all offer spots for its diverse mix of guests.

“Chandler is such a busy, hustle and bustle. There’s so much going on in Chandler—which is a good thing,” says general manager Annemarie DiTizio. “We really wanted a solid place for both lunch and dinner.”

The menu also goes beyond traditional expectations. It starts in the scratch kitchen where the Hop Social crew makes nearly everything in house, from the hand-cut fries to the dressings and aiolis.

There’s a focus on comfort foods, like meatloaf, mac and cheese, and a pot pie meant to make you feel at home. “Our pot pie is our owner’s grandmother’s recipe,” says DiTizio. “He really takes so much pride in that. He loves that the guests enjoy that.”

But the tavern also features pizzas from its wood fire oven and even some Asian-inspired dishes. “We really try to provide great food and a really genuine experience, but also a unique experience,” DiTizio explains.

Dishes are easily paired with a draft beer from one of Hop Social’s 52 taps. The tap list emphasizes local brews and also includes popular national brands and even a hard seltzer. For those who prefer other libations, the tavern has a full bar and wine list.

Locals know Hop Social for its generous happy hour, with food and drink specials offered nightly from 3 to 6 p.m. and again from 9 p.m. to close. DiTizio explains the happy hour is good throughout the restaurant, making it easy for anyone to try it out.

DiTizio says the varied selections appeal to everyone from families and winter visitors to business workers and couples on a night out. She continues to say these guests are what Hop Social loves about being a part of the Chandler community.

“We pride ourselves on that genuine experience. There are a lot of different choices out there and we really want to take the time to appreciate any and all guests who come in. Whether its once a week or once a year,” she says. “We realize it’s a choice that people make every day when they go out to eat and we want to appreciate those guests.”

 

Hop Social Grill

headings.text: Chandler Local Spotlight: JINYA Ramen Bar

bodyHtml:
When you want something done right, do it yourself. That’s the ethos that Japanese restaurateur Tomo Takahashi embraced when he moved to the United States and couldn’t find a ramen bar to suit his tastes. So, he opened one.

In 2010, Takahashi launched JINYA Ramen Bar in Los Angeles, the original location of what would go on to become a beloved Japanese restaurant with 40 locations throughout North America.

Actually, make that 41. The newest iteration recently opened its doors in Downtown Chandler’s New Square. Like Takahashi, local franchise owner Daradee Olson longed for a good bowl of ramen upon her return from living in Southeast Asia for six years. Then she tried the offerings at a JINYA restaurant in Utah and was so impressed that she decided to bring the concept to her home state of Arizona.    

This is great news for ramen fans. JINYA takes their noodles and broth seriously, hand-making every noodle before it undergoes an aging process and slow-simmering the broth for 20 hours in FUJI brand water. The result? Full-flavored ramen, made with exacting precision and starring authentic Japanese ingredients.

Of the 12 signature ramen creations—each one customizable thanks to more than 25 add-ons—popular choices include the perfectly balanced spicy chicken with chicken chashu, kikurage, spicy bean sprouts and green onion, or the Sprouting Up Ramen with rich pork and chicken broth, pork chashu, kikurage, spicy bean sprouts, green onion, half seasoned egg, Brussels sprouts, black pepper and ginger.

Guests can also opt for non-ramen dishes such as rice bowls featuring Tokyo-style curry and poke bowls stacked with fish. There’s also a generous lineup of vegetarian and vegan plates. Exhibit A: The Vegan Bun, a plant-based steamed bun with a pea protein patty, guacamole, cucumber and vegan mayonnaise.

To complement the cuisine, JINYA brings its infamous attention to detail to the cocktail menu as well. The Lycheetini, which pairs Jinro Soju with lychee syrup and fresh lychee, is a standout, as is the Suntory Toki High Ball. Icy, fizzy and smooth, it’s a fun take on a whiskey and soda. JINYA also gets high marks for offering the state’s internationally awarded Arizona Sake, made in Holbrook.

Rounding out the JINYA experience is the restaurant’s modern interior, a design blend of posh contemporary and urban industrial. A buzzy community table takes center stage, a mural artwork adorns a giant, exposed-brick wall and the ramen bar affords direct sightlines into the lively kitchen.

Map: 130 S. Arizona Ave., Chandler AZ 85225 or (480) 758-5198

headings.text: Chandler Local Spotlight: Mic Drop Comedy

bodyHtml:
Laughter is alive and well in Downtown Chandler…thanks to a revamped venue with some exciting new upgrades. Formerly ImprovMANIA and Mic Drop Mania, Mic Drop Comedy Chandler still offers traditional stand-up and improvisational shows, but the entertainment spot has turned the laugh factor up a few notches.

David and Colleen Specht put Chandler on the comedy map when they opened ImprovMANIA in 2016. But a relocation to the historic building on Boston Street in January 2023 launched a full rebranding of the club, which now provides an improved boutique comedy experience.

The venture—a partnership between the Spechts and Casey Currier and Hillary Hutson, owners of Mic Drop in San Diego—has allowed downtown’s newest hotspot to focus on comedy programming, increase its floor space and expand show times, says David Specht.

The club is now open Thursday to Sunday and features newcomers, seasoned professionals—including alums from “Saturday Night Live”—and other nationally-known comedians. “It’s a true slice of what the comedy world is all about,” Specht says of the ability to attract more stand-up performers. “All kinds of talent come through town.”

Customers can expect familiar offerings such as open mic night, where anyone can try their hand at comedy with a four-minute set. The lineup also continues to include family-friendly shows, special engagements and events such as Back to the Brunch, which showcases comedy, trivia and a lip sync battle based on the hit film “Back to the Future.” And, of course, the popular ImprovMANIA show returns to the stage once a month where the audience gives the comedy troupe suggestions to help set the tone for the performance.

While many comedy clubs in the Valley accommodate a larger audience, Mic Drop Comedy’s setting puts customers up-close-and-personal with performers. “We’ve always offered an intimate entertainment experience. Every seat is within five rows of the stage,” Specht says.

The reimagined modern spot provides a subtle yet whimsical décor homage to Snow White and includes two showrooms: a 125-seat main indoor space with exposed brick and luxury booths; and a comedy garden, an open-air courtyard that seats 75.

The new focus comes with an expanded dinner menu, too, thanks to a fully equipped kitchen. This new feature gives guests the option to order a complete dinner with a show or choose from a rotating menu of a la cart items. Customers also can select from a large selection of local beers, wine and inventive cocktails. And, unlike other venues, Mic Drop Comedy doesn’t require a two-item minimum.

The comedy club hosts stand-up and improv classes and can customize private events for holiday parties, luncheons, mixers, award ceremonies, fundraisers, corporate functions, business meetings, networking events and weddings.

At the end of the day—and show—it’s about the laughter. “We’re still here,” says Specht. “It’s a small business mentality in which everyone has a five-star experience. It’s the same people, the same comedy atmosphere, but it’s a more elevated experience.”

Address: 51 E. Boston St., Chandler AZ 85225

headings.text: A Chandler Café Rooted in Family and Craft

bodyHtml:
Tucked away from the hustle and bustle of Chandler Fashion Center is a charming spot where you can escape to enjoy a moment of quiet calm, where coffee takes center stage at Momentto Café. Located in West Chandler, this family-owned café and roastery is more than a place to grab your morning cup – it’s a celebration of quality, culture, and connection.

 

“We don’t have Wi-Fi or allow laptops because we don’t want this to be a working space,” says Mina Vukovic, owner of the café and Momentto Coffee Roasters. “We want people to come in, relax, have a conversation, meet up with friends, have a date, things like that. Whenever someone brings a book to read, I even give them a free macaron.”

A Chandler Café Rooted in Family and Craft

Owned by Vukovic and her father Peter, the roastery and coffee shop prioritizes high-quality, ethically sourced coffee from family-owned farms and lots. The father and daughter duo share a love for coffee that dates to their roots in Montenegro, where Vukovic’s grandfather roasted coffee in his garage.

 

“In Montenegro, your whole day is based around coffee,” Vukovic says. “You have it with breakfast, with lunch, maybe before lunch, and then at dinner. When you meet up with your friends or family, it’s to drink coffee. You’re always drinking coffee.”

 

Using his talent for engineering and background in restaurants, Peter created a proprietary roasting process with nine filtration systems. He opened his first shop in Montenegro in 1989, and a little over 10 years later, they opened their first shop in the U.S. in 2001. After having locations around the Valley, Momentto Caffe found its home in West Chandler in 2022.

 

“It’s been wonderful to be in Chandler. The city has been so welcoming to families and businesses,” Vukovic says. “We did a lot of research before deciding on Chandler. We settled here because we wanted to be in a safe area where we could expand.”

 

The quality of coffee is central to the café’s mission. In addition to only purchasing from fair trade, family-owned coffee producers and using specialized equipment to filtrate the coffee (up to seven times more than is industry standard), Momentto Caffè roasts its coffee per order, so guests are served the freshest coffee possible.

 

During the roasting process, they also remove the outer layer of the coffee beans called the chaff, to ensure more potent coffee without the filler. The result is a smooth, low-acid cup of coffee with no bitterness.

Sip, Savor, and Slow Down

Since opening, Momentto Caffe—whose name comes from the Italian word for “moment”—has become a place customers can enjoy good company and good coffee in a peaceful setting,” says Vukovic. “We want people to take a moment for themselves.”

 

From the moment you walk in, you’ll notice the café’s inviting, minimalistic aesthetic. With only six tables, Momentto is designed for intimate conversations, quiet reflection, and – you guessed it – enjoying the moment. But if someone does want to work, they have the option of renting out the on-site conference room.

 

And for the perfect pairing, patrons can enjoy European-style desserts and savory pastries, all handmade by Vukovic’s mother.

 

It’s the perfect stop for a mid-morning treat, a relaxed afternoon date, or a peaceful start to the day.

 

Visit Momentto Café

4114 W. Saturn Way, Chandler, AZ 85226 

(480) 948-8501

headings.text: Chandler Local Spotlight: Patent 139 Brewing Company

bodyHtml:
Tim Hass is paying tribute to his family’s history the best way he knows how—by planting new roots. Nestled in a Chandler, Arizona neighborhood off Ray and Dobson roads, the new Patent 139 Brewing Company is an homage to the Hass family’s contribution to the food and beverage world.

The patent in question refers to the Hass avocado. Hass’ great grandfather Rudolf created the varietal on his farm in California nearly a century ago. A fortuitous accident of cross pollinating Fuerte avocados with other seeds from Central and South America yielded a fruit with rough black skin on the outside and a rich and creamy interior.

Rudolf was issued Patent No. 139 for the creation in 1935, but did not live long enough to see avocados gain their now revered place in mainstream food culture. While the patent expired in 1952, the Hass variety now represents 90% of avocados sold in the world.

For Tim, the family passion for making and sharing great food didn’t fall far from the tree. After getting his degree in hotel and restaurant management from Northern Arizona University, Hass built a 20-year career with high-end resorts, breweries and restaurants. When he found himself furloughed during the pandemic, he started putting ideas for his own place on paper. Patent 139 opened in January 2022 in a Chandler neighborhood that immediately caught Hass’ eye.

“We’re right in Anderson Springs and so our patio backs up to the lake there,” he says. “Being able to sit by the water, that’s kind of what drove me to wanting to be in this neighborhood and bring something different that they haven’t seen in the complex here.”

The restaurant features a mix of sharable appetizers, burgers and sandwiches, but Hass says it’s “not the typical brewery menu.” Adventurous dishes like a grilled octopus with Spanish chorizo, potato and avocado verde accompany elevated standards like the BBQ Nachos with barbecued pulled pork and smoked cheddar. And the Figgy Piggy Smashburger with fig jam, fig balsamic, bacon and fried goat cheese are already creating a buzz.

“We’ve been getting a great response,” says Hass. “We’ve built a regular clientele of people coming and wanting to see what we’re about.”

Hass is quick to acknowledge his partner in the kitchen, chef Jared Martinez. The two had worked together at other resort concepts and Martinez has family ties to Arizona.

“It was nice to (have him) come out here and really use his talents with the venue and also be closer to family, too,” he says.

While the brewery completes its licensing with the state, Hass is working with local breweries to create two signature beers for the spot. And just as the menu highlights the avocado, the brews are loving nods to his family. A raspberry blond beer called the Neon Nancer Blaster tips its hat at his mother’s nickname. And the Willowood is a West Coast IPA named for the street he grew up on.

Hass says sharing his family story and the community response has been great.

“The family history, being able to tell story…it’s just such a great conversation with people, you know,” he continues. “Because no one really knows the real, true ‘how black-skinned Haas Avocados came about.’ It’s nice to tell people about that story.”

Map: 1949 W. Ray Road #11, Chandler, AZ 85224 or (480) 597-7138

bodyHtml:
Pickleball is one of the fastest growing recreational activities in the country—about 4.8 million Americans play it at least once a year. And now in Chandler, those hooked on the paddle sport that combines elements of tennis, ping pong and badminton have their own domain to play in West Chandler at Pickleball Kingdom.

Located on the northeast corner of Rural and Ray roads, Pickleball Kingdom is exactly what is sounds like: An entire complex devoted to the low-impact, super-social sport that is played on a badminton-style court about half the size of a tennis court with two or four players.

The indoor facility is the largest of its kind in the U.S. and is the brainchild of founder and CEO of Pickleball Kingdom Mike Rodrigues, a self-described serial entrepreneur and avid pickleball player who realized the Valley presented some unique pickleball challenges and needed a dedicated space for the game.

“I remember saying this is the greatest sport ever. And shortly after as my ability started to grow, my understanding of the game started to grow,” he says. “I became very aware of the downsides: You can’t reserve a court, the sun is an issue, and maybe the biggest problem is the winds. I never thought of Arizona as windy, but because you play with a waffle ball, it’s dramatically impacted by wind.”

And so, in early January 2021, Rodrigues began thinking that, if only there were an indoor facility in Arizona, all of these problems would go away.

That vision became Pickleball Kingdom, which opened just over a year later in May 2022. The facility has 15 courts, full locker and shower rooms, racquet/ball rentals, mezzanine viewing, two lounges, snack bar, pro shop and party room. And despite the stereotype of being an “older” person’s activity, Pickleball Kingdom welcomes all ages and athletic levels to its complex.

“That's the thing that's attractive about pickleball—anyone can play. You see grandparents playing with their grandchildren, and you don’t have to be blessed with a certain amount of height or strength or speed. If you put some time and energy into it and learn the fundamentals, you can get pretty good pretty quickly,” explains Rodrigues.

Guests can drop in and play a game, which costs $15, or buy annual memberships with different perks. In addition, newcomers to the sport can take “Pickleball 100,” a free, one-hour introductory class held daily at Pickleball Kingdom that launches visitors into the game fairly quickly.

“It’s for the person who says, ‘I’ve heard about pickleball, but I don’t know the first thing about it.’ We take it from there,” Rodrigues explains. “You just have to bring your tennis shoes and we provide everything else, including the paddle and ball, and all the information that you need to get up and running.

“The barriers to entry of this great sport have been the lack of knowledge, lack of equipment, and lack of court space to play. With this free, instructional class, we’ve eliminated all those roadblocks.  For anyone who's wanted to give pickleball a try but didn't know where to go or how to get started, the answer is to come down to the Kingdom!”

Since opening, membership is three and half times what Rodrigues expected, confirming what he already knew: Pickleball is fun and it’s here to stay. In fact, he plans to open more Pickleball Kingdom locations in Arizona and throughout the country.

“I think the short learning curve of pickleball pulls people in. What keeps them in is the fact that the ceiling is limitless. You can keep growing and keep getting better, and we love introducing them to the game,” he says. “I feel like in some ways we're ambassadors to the game.”

bodyHtml:
Local brewing giant SanTan Brewing Company has been a major fixture in Downtown Chandler for more than a decade. But recently, it’s cast a wider reach in the community with its award-wining style at SanTan Gardens, an indoor/outdoor private event and public space.

The new concept opened in late 2022 and features an al fresco patio along with a larger tasting room at the brewery’s 35,000-square-foot production facility at 495 E. Warner Road. SanTan Gardens is ideal for Arizona weddings, reunions, corporate functions, and ticketed music events, according to Jamie Hoffman, director of operations.

“We’ve had the tasting room here for the last five years, but decided we needed to have a private event space, too. So we expanded the casing room,” explains Hoffman of the causal, intimate entertainment venue. “It’s the same overall vibe as the downtown pub, though different things are happening at SanTan Gardens. We sell a lot of food at the restaurant, but people who come in here are looking to discover our beer and spirits more than the pub.”

Both the tasting room and 2,000-square-foot patio are open daily to the public, Monday to Friday from 3 to 8 p.m. and weekends from noon to 8 p.m. (except when closed for private parties). SanTan Gardens features SanTan’s signature seasonal rotation of IPAs, lagers and stouts, including Juicy Jack IPA, Moon Juice IPA, Sky Harbor Lager and its lineup of artisanal spirits such as vodka, gin and whiskey, as well as canned cocktails.

“For newbies, it’s the perfect way to explore everything we do. It’s also a place for those who know what we do to stop by on their way home from work,” adds Hoffman. “There’s always a seat.”

While SanTan Gardens doesn’t have a kitchen, the brewery offers custom catering services and has a food truck available with different menus making it a great option for private events. Since the original pub is only 10 minutes from the production operations, public guests can order food from its menu, and have it delivered to SanTan Gardens while they enjoy their beers and spirits.

The addition of the patio at the brewery’s production facility also gives SanTan an opportunity to host regular live music and special events with a nominal cover charge that are open to the public with themed nights including Pub Trivia on Tuesdays, Grateful Dead Wednesdays, and family-friendly outings such as Beer, Bourbon, BBQ + Band, featuring a pig roast.

With the launch of SanTan Gardens, tours of the production facility have expanded with additional days and hours. The popular educational tours give a sneak peek into the science behind the production of SanTan’s craft beers and spirits. Led by SanTan experts, visitors get a history lesson and experience 10 stops along the manufacturing “trail” to learn about all facets of beer and spirits brewing and distilling, including the grain process, aging and canning with opportunities to sample tastings at various stages of development. Tours range from $15 to $40, and reservations are recommended.

headings.text: Chandler Local Spotlight: Singing Pandas Asian Restaurant & Bar
Singing Pandas & Bar Strikes a Perfect Chord

bodyHtml:
Susie Wong thought she was going to purchase an auto repair shop in 2023. What she got instead was a Chandler restaurant known for its fresh and hearty take on American-Chinese cuisine along with a complimentary side serving of nightly entertainment.

In May, Wong took ownership of Singing Pandas Restaurant & Bar from its original owner Sherry Chen. A longtime customer of the dining spot that opened in 2016, Wong had been in negotiations to buy an automotive garage, an industry she’s worked in for years. When the process of buying the auto garage met with obstacle after obstacle and fell through, she had a conversation with Chen about the situation.

“I joked and said, ‘Then I’ll just buy a restaurant in Downtown Chandler.’ [Chen] said ‘buy mine’—and then I did,” says Wong, who grew up in a family-owned grocery store and has worked in the hospitality and call center sectors.

The transition from car care to the restaurant business hasn’t been much of a leap for Wong. “It’s about the relationships. As long as you love people, anyone can step into it,” she says.

Besides adding a website, online ordering and third-party deliveries through services such as UberEats, Wong, a Chandler resident, hasn’t changed much at the restaurant since becoming the proprietor.

“The restaurant is successful because the concept is so unique, the food is good, and the customer service is amazing. The recipes are all the same and so are the cooks,” she says of maintaining Singing Pandas’ winning formula.

Singing Pandas’ extensive lunch and dinner menu remains intact with familiar items influenced by American, Chinese and spicy ingredients and flavors including sweet and sour chicken, and more authentic Cantonese items such as ma po tofu made with fresh soft tofu, minced pork and green onions sautéed in a spicy brown sauce.

“We appeal to Americans, Asians and have something on the menu for everyone,” says Wong, who’s added cocktails to the existing spirits and beverage options. Standouts include the Susie Wong, a mandarin orange martini; and The Fortune Cookie, made with vanilla vodka, Bailey’s Irish cream and amaretto. The restaurant also has its own signature craft beer, Panda Light, produced by locally-owned Huss Brewing Company.

And, of course, there’s the free nightly entertainment that’s been a staple at Singing Pandas since its inception. On Talent Tuesday, Wong books a rotating list of singing talent—some even discovered in the audience. On Wednesdays, diners can eat while listening to acoustic guitar performances. On Thursdays and Sundays, customers are treated to a lounge-style experience. Wong’s husband, Mark Love, also gets in on the act and occasionally takes the stage impersonating Louis Armstrong.

The new weekend lineup features more Vegas-style dinner shows celebrating iconic sounds on Friday and Saturday evenings, according to Wong. “You’ll hear everything from Dean Martin and Liza Minnelli to Frank Sinatra and Adele. The shows appeal to all ages, with recognizable songs from the ’50s to the 2000s.”

Wong highly recommends reservations for the weekend performances in the showroom, which are seated at 5:30 p.m. and 7:30 p.m. Plus, large groups can reserve spots for lunch meetings.

“Walk-ins are welcome too,” she says. “Who knows? Maybe you’ll get lucky.”

headings.text: Chandler Local Spotlight: Stinger's Golf Club

bodyHtml:
If you’re looking for a more-than-just-your-average golf game, Stinger’s Golf Club checks all the boxes.

Just ask owner Tyler Wilson, who started toying with the idea of opening an indoor golf facility after, naturally, having a golf outing canceled due to rain.

“I was in Chicago visiting some friends. We scheduled a golf game, which, unfortunately, got rained out,” he explains. “The folks at the club recommended a local indoor golf facility and when I walked in, I was kind of shocked that this type of thing existed. I mean, it makes a lot of sense, but I hadn’t ever heard of one, especially coming from Arizona where it would be a great fit.”

No stranger to running a business—Wilson owned a freight and shipping operation—he started researching similar facilities and, ultimately, found his calling. “I knew I wanted to get into a new venture, something that I was more passionate about,” he says. “I was always finding myself trying to get out and golf, so I knew this was it.”

Opened in 2023, the family-owned business combines the thrill of a round of golf with the convenience of a high-tech, climate-controlled environment. Thanks to their state-of-the-art golf simulators, you can tee off on some of the world’s most famous courses without ever leaving Arizona. The technology is so advanced that you'll feel like you’re right there on the course with every drive, chip and putt—minus the sunburn.

“The technology has come a long way, and people are definitely more open minded to the idea of playing inside and on a computer, if you will,” Wilson says. “Plus, you can ‘play’ some of the world’s most famous courses, which is a pretty cool opportunity.”

If you’re looking for a spot for your next team-building event or group outing, Stinger's is an ace in that department, too. With flexible spaces and customizable packages, it’s a great place to bring your crew together for some friendly competition.

“We love to host any kind of event, from birthday or bachelor parties to corporate outings,” says Wilson. “The group can be as small eight to 10 people using one bay, to up to 100 people for a full buyout of the venue.”

But Stinger’s isn’t just about golf. It’s also the perfect spot to kick back with friends, grab a bite, and enjoy a drink or two. Their menu offers everything from classic bar bites to more elevated options, perfect for refueling after a round or just hanging out and watching others play.

And when it comes to drinks, their selection will have you feeling like you hit a hole-in-one. Whether you're into craft beers, cocktails, or something non-alcoholic, they've got the perfect pairing for your day of play.

Named for the low-flying shot that Tiger Woods made famous, Stinger’s currently has one location in Chandler. But based on the positive reception the venue has received since opening in 2023, Wilson is excited about future growth.

“We do hope to grow and establish a footprint in which anyone who goes to a Stinger’s will know they're getting the exact same thing no matter which location they go to,” says Wilson.

For now, you can find Stinger’s conveniently located in east Chandler. They’re open daily, making it convenient to stop by any time—whether it’s for a quick round after work or a weekend hangout.

So if you’re ready to putt your way to a good time, head over to Stinger’s Golf Club, where the love of the game and a great day out come together.

headings.text: Chandler Local Spotlight: The Ashley Castle

bodyHtml:
Opened in 2006, The Ashley Castle in Chandler has become one of the Valley’s best-loved wedding and event venues, having hosted all kinds of gatherings, including weddings, birthday parties, corporate events, anniversary celebrations and more.

“We’re all family here, which is special,” says the castle’s namesake, Ashlee Guerrero, who works in the office and the catering department. “My parents own the castle, my uncle owns the bartending company, my mom is running the floral division right now, one of our coordinators has been with us several years and goes to church with my parents, and our setup team member has been with us since the very beginning. We’re all just one big happy family.”

The Ashley Castle, which is hidden down a long driveway in one of Chandler’s business districts not far from Chandler Fashion Center, looks like an authentic castle, with its design centered around its one-of-a-kind, 200-year-old doors that are believed to have come from a castle in Asia.

“It’s very much designed to look like a Medieval castle,” Guerrero says. “We have tapestries on the walls, the whole outside is stone, we have three turrets inside, and hand-painted walls. Outside we have a beautiful garden, a gazebo and statues. It feels like you’re walking around in Europe.”

The castle sets itself apart with all-inclusive packages that cover everything from catering to bar service to florals and rentals, making it easy to plan an unforgettable event. For weddings, there are seven different package options to suit every couple—whether they want relaxed, brunch-time nuptials, or an all-out evening soiree.

For other varieties of events, The Ashley Castle offers a prom package and corporate event package for easy planning.

“It takes the stress out planning your day,” says Guerrero. “We have an in-house catering team and florist. The only think people need to bring in themselves are the photographer, alcohol and officiant, and we even have preferred photographers and officiants, in case they need recommendations.”

In addition to being a fantastic event venue, The Ashley Castle’s picturesque grounds and interior are also available for photoshoots.

The venue has become increasingly busy, now even booking weddings into 2025.

“As one of the aftereffects of the pandemic, I think people are realizing not to wait on things. They’re following their passions and getting married when they want to get married, instead of putting it off. Because we never know what’s going to happen in this world,” says Guerrero.

The Ashley Castle has several nearby hotels within walking distance, making it a convenient location for the wedding party and guests. Nearby hotels include Courtyard by Marriott Phoenix Chandler, Marriott Phoenix Chandler, Hampton Inn & Suites Phoenix Chandler-Fashion Center, Homewood Suites by Hilton Phoenix Chandler Fashion Center, Drury Inn & Suites Phoenix Chandler Fashion Center, Home2 Suites by Hilton Phoenix Chandler, and Residence Inn by Marriott Phoenix Chandler/South.

The Ashley Castle

bodyHtml:
Chandler just got a whole lot tastier with the opening of The Mexicano, the newest spot shaking up the local dining scene.

This vibrant, high-energy restaurant—nestled right next to Chandler Fashion Center—is the latest creation from the family-run The Maggiore Group. From the moment you walk in, it’s clear this place isn’t just about food—it’s an experience. Think bold Mexico City vibes, a lively crowd, and some of the most colorful cocktails you’ve ever seen.

The mastermind behind The Mexicano is Chef Joey Maggiore, who gave us Hash Kitchen and The Sicilian Butcher. With this new concept, he’s bringing Mexican food to Chandler with a fresh, elevated twist. The dishes are packed with flavor, the presentation is next-level, and the whole vibe leans way into fun. Whether you’re there for a full dinner or just dropping in for margaritas, there’s something exciting waiting for you.

Speaking of margaritas, can we talk about the build-your-own margarita bar? It might just be the star of the show. You can customize your drink with over 30 toppings—from spicy Tajín rims to gummy bears, cotton candy and more. It’s part drink, part dessert, part party. And if you’re feeling extra, order the BYO Fuego Margarita served in a souvenir piñata cup that’s yours to keep.

Inside, the space is a feast for the eyes. Designed by Chef Joey’s wife Cristina Maggiore, it’s filled with vibrant colors, handpicked furniture imported from Mexico, and a custom DJ booth—because why not? Music plays a big role here, with rotating DJs spinning Latin beats every night of the week. You might catch a fire dancer wowing the crowd or even a live mariachi band making the rounds. It’s got that electric, anything-can-happen feel, which makes it a perfect pick for birthdays, girls’ nights, or just a spontaneous dinner out.

The food holds its own, too. A few standouts include the Guacamole & Salsa Ferris Wheel, a total showstopper that’s fun to look at and seriously tasty. The Birria Bao Buns are an awesome fusion of Mexican and Asian flavors, and the Lava Rock Molcajetes arrive at your table traditional molcajete bowl still bubbling, loaded with sizzling meats, veggies and bold spices.

There’s indoor and outdoor seating, including a spacious patio that’s great for groups. While there’s no private room, they do offer semi-private options if you’re planning something a bit more intimate. And don’t miss their happy hour, which runs every day from 2 to 5:30 p.m. in the bar area, with small bites and drinks that won’t wreck your budget. Mondays are especially fun with half-off margaritas.

After spending the day shopping at Chandler Fashion Center, The Mexicano is the perfect place to unwind, refuel and soak up the lively atmosphere. With its bold menu, upbeat energy, and one-of-a-kind margarita bar, it’s easy to see why this new addition is quickly becoming one of Chandler’s most talked-about spots—and honestly, it’s easy to see why.

ld.articleBody: We all have those days on the road when there isn’t time for a sit-down restaurant meal or when a pet or sleeping child prevents us from eating inside. The answer? A drive-thru, of course. But, if you’re like me, you probably don’t know which restaurants (beyond the national chains) have one.

bodyHtml:
We all have those days on the road when there isn’t time for a sit-down restaurant meal or when a pet or sleeping child prevents us from eating inside. The answer? A drive-thru, of course. But, if you’re like me, you probably don’t know which restaurants (beyond the national chains) have one.

Luckily, Chandler has plenty of options—from local restaurants to regional favorites. Here are seven to consider the next time you’re on the road and need a bite to eat. 

Senor Taco

4200 S. Chandler Ave., Chandler 85248
(480) 895-5580

The Chandler Avenue location of this Phoenix chain has a drive-thru where you can order huge breakfast burritos, hard- and soft-shelled tacos, or one of 16 different burritos, including the shrimp burrito that put Senor Taco on the map. You’ll also find tortas, quesadillas, and seafood on the menu. 

Everything is made fresh to order, so at times, there can be a slightly longer than usual wait in the drive-thru, but don’t let that deter you. The authentic Mexican cuisine is definitely worth it. Tip: Come on Tuesday for $1 tacos. 

Planet Sub

1920 W. Germann Rd., Chandler, 85286
(480) 245-6503
In the mood for a sub sandwich? Try Planet Sub. For a sandwich shop, it has a surprisingly extensive menu featuring not only the classics like turkey or roast beef but unique offerings like the bacon mushroom melt. It also has nine vegetarian sandwich options, Romaine lettuce wraps, and tortilla wraps on the menu. 

Everything is made fresh to order and even the bread is made on site. (Note: Bread for the sandwiches is always toasted unless requested otherwise.)

Planet Sub is a chain with locations mostly in the Midwest and Texas. If you don’t mind chains, Potbelly Sandwich Shop on Chandler Boulevard also has a drive-thru. 

Salad and Go

5985 W. Chandler Blvd., Chandler, 85226
Salads probably aren’t the first food that come to mind when you’re looking for a drive-thru, especially when you’ll be eating on the road, but Salad and Go gives you the option to order any of their salads as a wrap. Choose from a traditional Caesar or Cobb salad or get more creative with options like the roasted sweet potato and strawberry salad. You can add chicken, steak, shrimp or organic tofu for a heartier meal. 

This Phoenix area chain also serves breakfast burritos and organic smoothies for breakfast if you want to pick something up in the morning on your way into work.  

China Way Restaurant

3021 N. Alma School Rd., Chandler, AZ 85224
(480) 839-0905
Surprisingly, one of Chandler’s most established Chinese restaurants offers drive-thru service. China Way Restaurant serves a la carte entrees, rice bowls, and combo meals at lunch and dinner. Combo meals ($1.50 more) come with an egg roll, crab angel, and white or fried rice. Although most menu items are Chinese favorites, the restaurant also has a limited number of Thai dishes.

Because the food is cooked-to-order, it’s best to call ahead and let them know you’ll be coming through the drive-thru. 

BLD Chandler

1920 W. Germann Rd., Chandler 85286
(480) 779-8646
Open for breakfast, lunch, and dinner (BLD), this local favorite has a drive-thru for barista-made beverages, protein shakes, and smoothies. You can also call ahead and pick up food to go at the drive-thru window. In the morning, you may be limited to breakfast burritos if you’ll be on the road, but you can also order benedicts, omelets, and hashes to go. 

At lunch, you can get a salads, sandwiches, tacos, and burgers to go. In the evening, BLD Chandler expands its menu, adding entrees like short ribs, fried chicken, and risotto. The restaurant also serves BBQ throughout the day, including sandwiches, ribs, and brisket.

Black Rock Coffee

4050 S. Alma School Rd., Chandler 85248
(520) 477-2134
Just want coffee? Black Rock Coffee, a Portland-based coffee house with locations in Oregon, Washington, California, Idaho, and Arizona, serves excellent hot and cold coffee drinks, chai, smoothies, hot chocolate, and Italian sodas. What it doesn’t serve is food so it can focus on making connections with its customers. 

That means when you drive-thru at Black Rock Coffee, the barista won’t just stick out a hand for money and shove a cup in your face. Instead, you’ll be greeted with genuine warmth and a smile. If you ever get the chance to go inside for coffee, baristas will spend extra time explaining the menu, and if the drink is not to your liking, they’ll happily remake it.

Other options

Some larger chains are worth mentioning. For example, although In-and-Out Burger has an impressive network of restaurants spread across California, Arizona, Nevada, Oregon, Texas, and Utah, it consistently ranks as one of the top burger chains in the nation. There are three In-and-Out locations with drive-thru windows in Chandler, one on Chandler Boulevard, one on Ray Road and one on Germann Road. 

Culver’s is another popular burger chain with restaurants mostly in the Midwest, Idaho, Utah, Colorado, and Arizona. In addition to its Butterburger served on a buttered and toasted bun, Culver’s is known for its fresh frozen custard and frozen treats.

If you’re in the mood for chicken, Slim Chickens’ Chandler location has a drive-thru where you can get made-to-order, hand-breaded tenders, fresh chicken sandwiches, and wings with house-made dipping sauces. Raising Cane’s Chicken Fingers has a similar menu and a drive-thru at its Chandler restaurant. 

Another option is Filberto’s Mexican Food, a regional Mexican chain with four restaurants in Chandler. Two of those—the one on Arizona Avenue and the one on Pecos Road—have drive-thru windows. 

Finally, the Chandler location of Kneaders Bakery and Café has a drive-thru serving breakfast, lunch, and dinner. Order pancakes, pastries, and egg sandwiches to go for breakfast. For lunch and dinner, opt for soups, salads, and sandwiches.

The answer? A drive-thru, of course. But, if you’re like me, you probably don’t know which restaurants (beyond the national chains) have one. Luckily, Chandler has plenty of options—from local restaurants to regional favorites. Here are seven to consider the next time you’re on the road and need a bite to eat. Senor Taco 4200 S. bodyHtml:
The Stillery has brought an authentic piece of Nashville to bustling Downtown Chandler with its nightly live country music performances, mason jar cocktails, and spicy Nashville hot chicken sandwiches. The gastropub’s first two locations were opened by business partners Steve Sargent and Steve Kovach in the heart of Nashville and in late 2020, the two Arizona natives decided to bring the concept to their home state.

“The spot in Chandler became available to us a couple of years ago and it felt right,” says Sargent. “We both have a bunch of friends out here, so we had that connection. And since it’s Steve Kovach’s hometown, it made sense.”

When guests arrive, they’re welcomed by country music, a warm atmosphere, and a horseshoe bar serving up local beers, wines by the glass, and a variety of classic and creative cocktails. Start your experience with the sweet, bourbon-heavy Stillery Sour with blackberry jam or the best-selling Blueberry Smash crafted with blueberry vodka, smashed blueberries, simple syrup, lime, and soda.

For lunch and dinner, diners can look forward to rustic pizzas, hearty sandwiches, creative burgers, and salads. However, before you pick your entrée, you won’t want to skip the selection of starters, which range from the meat-and-cheese-topped snack board to the cast iron wings and Sriracha deviled eggs. While it’s hard to go wrong with a main course, you’ll get the full Nashville experience with the Hot Chicken sandwich made with a generous portion of crispy chicken, fried pickles, lettuce, tomato, and creamy bleu cheese.

“We’ve become known for our Hot Chicken sandwich,” Sargent says. “It’s a Nashville thing and it’s probably our No. 1, most popular item.”

When it comes to burgers, it’s hard to top the one-of-a-kind MC Burger with cheddar, bacon, prosciutto, fried egg, and roasted garlic aioli on an oversized English muffin. Plus, each burger is sure to satisfy with its double patties made with a house-ground mix of brisket, chuck, and pork belly.

There are also nearly a dozen brick oven pizzas to choose from. Stick with the hot chicken theme with the Hot Chicken Pie served on a ranch crust, opt for an elevated pepperoni, or try the mouthwatering Brussels sprout pizza made with garlic oil, caramelized onion, roasted Brussels sprouts, bacon, mozzarella, parmesan, and fresh herbs. House specialties include mac ‘n cheese, Hot Chicken tenders, and catfish with house-cut fries. The must-have is the hanger steak grilled to perfection and topped with compound butter served alongside fries and greens.

The Stillery is also the perfect spot for a Southern weekend brunch with its shareable beignets, variety of eggs Benedict dishes, house-made biscuits with gravy, hot chicken and waffles, and chorizo pizza with scrambled egg, queso, mozzarella, cheddar, and a generous portion of chorizo— all which pair perfectly with one of the three Bloody Mary offerings, a mimosa or Bellini. 

While the grub will keep you coming back for more, the live country music—which diners can enjoy seven nights a week—will make you a fan for life.

“On Friday, Saturday, Sunday evenings, we feature a full band,” says Sargent. “It draws a good crowd, and you get a lot of people dancing, having a good time. During the weekend, we even fly one of our artists from Nashville in to play three or four shows. It brings that authenticity.”

Map: 130 S. Arizona Ave, Chandler, AZ 85225 or (480) 590-1409

bodyHtml:
Chicken wings have become a favorite amongst sports fans and a staple at many Chandler sports bars and restaurants. If you’ve ever needed an excuse to eat chicken wings all day, this is it. July 29th is National Chicken Wing Day, and there’s no better way to celebrate this finger lickin’ good food than with a plateful of tasty wings (and maybe a napkin or two).

Quite a few Chandler restaurants serve chicken wings, but we've curated a list of the best places for chicken wings in Chandler making it convenient to enjoy these crowd pleasers out and about in Chandler or by takeout to enjoy in the comfort of your Arizona hotel. Here is where wing experts can expect to find some of the best chicken wings in Chandler, AZ.

ATL Wings

A local favorite wing chain, ATL Wings serves theirs both traditional bone-in and boneless with a dry rub, hot sauce or BBQ sauce. Rub varieties include ATL style, lemon pepper, ranch, garlic parmesan and garlic pepper while hot sauces range from mild to toxic. If you prefer sauce, choose from their 18 award-winning wing sauces including BBQ, honey habanero, honey mustard, citrus chipotle, teriyaki and more .

Wings come with homemade blue cheese or ranch dressing and can be rounded out with sides ordered separately like fries, cheese fries, beans or homemade biscuits. If the wings get too spicy, douse the heat with fountain drinks or Kool-Aid on tap.

Map: 70 W. Warner Rd., Chandler AZ 85225 or (480) 722-9464

Sawtooth Bar & Grill

This neighborhood sports bar is a go-to for local chicken wing fans. Diners may opt for boneless or bone-in wings and select from two dozen sauce options including a variety of honey hot and garlic parmesan sauces ranging from mild to hot including a mango habanero, a citrus chipotle, salt & pepper and salt & vinegar chicken wing sauce. More traditional hot sauces from mild to hot are available.

Wings at the Sawtooth Bar & Grill are served with or without tots and come with celery, carrots and your choice of bleu cheese or ranch dressing. 

Map: 4929 W. Ray Rd., Chandler AZ 85226 or (480) 753-4772

The Hungry Monk

This local Chandler sports bar specializes in pub grub, so it’s no surprise it does wings right. Choose between bone-in or boneless wings available fried or grilled. Then, decide on how much heat you think you can take: regular, hot, extra hot or nuclear. Finally, pick your sauce. Options include original Buffalo, Cajun, honey hot, lemon pepper, Jamaican, honey mustard, parmesan garlic, roasted garlic, teriyaki and Thai peanut.

Wings at The Hungry Monk come with complimentary house-made ranch or bleu cheese dressing. Enjoy yours with a pint of craft beer from local Arizona breweries including Chandler's very own SanTan Brewing Company and Four Peaks Brewery.

Map: 1760 W. Chandler Blvd., Suite #2, Chandler AZ 85224 or (480) 963-8000

Louisiana Fried Chicken & Wings

Louisiana Fried Chicken & Wings claims its owner perfected a chicken recipe he personally received from New Orleans chef Paul Prudhomme. Whether true or not, the Chandler restaurant knows its chicken. And that includes wings.

This quick-serve restaurant sells bone-in and boneless wings in orders from six to 96 pieces and offers convenience with its drive-through window. Flavors include plain, mild, hot, medium hot, honey BBQ, lemon pepper, Asian, teriyaki ginger and spicy honey garlic with a few fun additions like salt and jalapeno. 

Map: 1016 N. Arizona Ave., Chandler AZ 85225 or (480) 726-0741

SanTan Brewing Company

SanTan Brewing Company dishes up some of the tastiest pub food of any craft brewery in Arizona. Its wings are no exception. The pub-style wings come dressed in your choice of Buffalo, pineapple habanero BBQ or Cajun sauce with bleu cheese or ranch dressing on the side. Carrots and celery are available on request.

Add an order of buttermilk onion rings or basket of ale-battered fries paired with the award-winning Mr. Pineapple or flagship brew, Devil’s Ale, for a tasty meal. If you prefer IPAs, the HopShock IPA perfectly offsets spicy wings.

Map: 8 S. San Marcos Pl., Chandler AZ 85225 or (480) 917-8700

Murphy's Law

An Irish bar probably isn’t the first place that comes to mind when you think wings, but Murphy’s Law has some of the tastiest, unconventional chicken wings in Chandler. The bar smokes, then fries, its wings before tossing them in its special Jameson Irish Whiskey wing sauce. While you can still order your wings in a Buffalo sauce, you would be missing out if you do.

Murphy’s Law has a great selection of craft beer to accompany its wings as well as an extensive whiskey menu featuring Bulleit, Jack Daniel’s, Knob Creek, Maker’s Mark, Woodford Reserve and others.

Map: 58 S. San Marcos Pl., Chandler AZ 85225 or (480) 812-1588

Fun facts about Chandler's Ostrich Festival history and everyone's favorite flightless bird:

bodyHtml:
The Ostrich Festival is a beloved annual tradition and festival in Chandler owned by the Chandler Chamber of Commerce and produced by Steve LeVine Entertainment. The annual event is held each March and is Chandler's largest festival and celebrates Chandler's rich history and early ostrich ranching when ostrich plumes were all the rage in fashion. 

The 2026 Arizona festival will be held at Rawhide Western Town and Event Center. The Ostrich Festival will be held over two weekends in March featuring live music, more than 35 carnival rides, food, games, activities and more in a fun tribute to our favorite bird, the ostrich.

FESTIVAL DATES AND TIMES:

WEEKEND ONE

Friday - March 13, 2026: 2 p.m. - Midnight

Saturday - March 14, 2026: 10 a.m. - Midnight

Sunday - March 15, 2026: 10 a.m. - 11 p.m.

WEEKEND TWO

Friday - March 20, 2026: 2 p.m. - Midnight

Saturday - March 21, 2026: 10 a.m. - Midnight

Sunday - March 22, 2026: 10 a.m. - 11 p.m.

MAIN STAGE HEADLINERS:

WEEKEND ONE

KANSAS - Friday, March 13, 2026

Ravyn Lenae - Saturday, March 14, 2026

Jo Dee Messina - Sunday, March 15, 2026

WEEKEND TWO

TBA - Friday, March 20, 2026

The Commodores - Saturday, March 21, 2026

TBA - Sunday, March 22, 2026

A hallmark of the event has been the main stage music performances and the 2026 Ostrich Festival is no exception. Each year the main stage hosts a variety of Ostrich Festival concerts from national talent and a number of music styles. With a new location in store for 2026, there will be a new exciting space to explore.

A favorite festival element of the younger Ostrich Festival attendees are the carnival rides. From a Zipper ride, "Giant Wheel" a large Ferris wheel, Wave Swinger and many more - the rides are sure to delight.

Important things to know and additional FAQ about the festival:

Admission 

General admission tickets are priced per day and do not include rides. Adult, Children, VIP tickets which include a meal & 2 drinks, and VIP access and front of stage viewing area are available for advance purchase through the Ostrich Festival website.

Parking

Details TBA.

Clear Bag Policy

To provide a safer environment for the public and significantly expedite entry, the festival has implemented a CLEAR BAG policy that limits the size and type of bags that may be brought into the festival. Bags larger than 4.5" x 6" must be clear and clear bags not exceeding 20″ x 15″ x 9″ are the ONLY bags permitted into the festival. Exceptions to the enforced Clear Bag Policy include diaper bags, medical, event staff, and artists/performers. Metal detector screening and a search of all items being carried in will take place at festival gates.

Map and Schedule

Attendees may download a Chandler Ostrich Festival Schedule and Map from the event website.

Ride Tickets

Individual Ride Tickets are $1 per ticket. The amount of tickets needed for each ride ranges from 3 to 10 tickets depending on the type of attraction.

Cash Policies

The only cash that will be accepted at the Ostrich Festival will be at the ticket box office, carnival kiosks (rides and carnival games), and the wristband reload tents.

Frequently Asked Questions

Find details about accessible parking, prohibited items, officially designated drop off/pick up areas and more on the Chandler Ostrich Festival FAQ section.

For more information regarding any of the Ostrich Festival events, please contact the Chandler Chamber of Commerce at (480) 963-4571 or by email at info@chandlerchamber.com.

Fun facts about Chandler's Ostrich Festival history and everyone's favorite flightless bird:

  • The Ostrich Festival began in 1989. (That's almost 40 years now!)
  • The event was originally held in Downtown Chandler before expanding to new locations to accommodate more visitors and larger attractions.
  • The festival was featured in the 1995 Whitney Houston film, Waiting to Exhale. 
  • The event was the setting for "Lover Boy", a Harlequin Romance book.
  • A fun fact about Chandler's ostrich ranching history, Dr. A.J. Chandler owned one of the largest Ostrich herds in the valley. 
  • The ostrich is the largest living bird in the world.
  • An ostrich can run at speeds of up to 40 miles per hour.
  • Ostrich eggs are the largest of any bird.
  • The wingspan of an ostrich is over six feet.
  • An ostrich has a mighty kick, with a force of about 2,000 pounds per square inch.
  • Ostriches don't have teeth.
  • An ostrich has three stomachs, each serving a different function.

bodyHtml:
Located in the heart of Chandler, Christopher Fine Diamonds offers visitors a chance to slow down, connect with local craftsmanship, and create something meaningful during their stay for a unique shopping experience.  For fine jewelry, engagement rings, and one-of-a-kind custom pieces, Christopher Fine Diamonds has been at the heart of gift-giving, celebrations, and special milestones for more than two decades.

Founded in 2003 by Chris and Kelly Uptain, Christopher Fine Diamonds is a locally owned Chandler jewelry store where much of the experience happens right in front of you. Chris, a master bench jeweler with nearly four decades of experience, leads a team that includes an on-site Graduate Gemologist, experienced jewelry professionals and in-house master jewelers.

 

Design Jewelry That’s Truly Yours, Right Here in Chandler

One of the most distinctive experiences at Christopher Fine Diamonds is its in-person CAD Jewelry Design Experience. Rather than simply describing a custom ring and waiting to see the finished piece, guests can participate in the design process and watch their ideas begin to take shape on screen.  For couples visiting Chandler, designing a piece together in the showroom offers a unique opportunity to connect with local craftsmanship while creating something meaningful to remember their experience.

Whether creating an engagement ring from the ground up, redesigning a family heirloom or celebrating a milestone with a custom piece, the process makes jewelry design personal, interactive and memorable.

Visitors can also see the jewelry workshop from the showroom, offering a rare glimpse at the craftsmanship that goes into creating and caring for fine jewelry.

 

Explore Engagement Rings, Natural and Lab-Grown Diamonds in Chandler

For couples shopping for an engagement ring in Chandler, the showroom features a dedicated Bridal Island with more than 400 engagement ring styles, along with both natural and lab-grown diamond options. Guests can compare diamonds side by side and receive guidance based on their priorities rather than navigating the process alone.

Beyond bridal jewelry, the showroom offers more than 3,000 ready-to-wear pieces and a loose gemstone gallery filled with color and inspiration.

Local Craftsmanship Meets Chandler Hospitality

After serving more than 15,000 clients, Christopher Fine Diamonds has grown while remaining focused on the personal service of an independent neighborhood jeweler.

“We want people to feel comfortable here, whether they are choosing their first piece of fine jewelry or designing something they hope will stay in their family for generations,” says co-owner Kelly Uptain. “Jewelry is connected to some of life’s most important moments, and we never lose sight of that.”

Christopher Fine Diamonds is located at 3245 W. Ray Road, Suite 4 in Chandler, Arizona. Whether you're shopping for an engagement ring, comparing natural and lab-grown diamonds, designing a custom piece, celebrating a milestone or simply looking for a memorable Chandler shopping experience, visitors are welcome to stop in and explore the showroom or schedule a private appointment.

bodyHtml:
Chandler’s cafés and coffee shops offer more than a quick caffeine stop. The city’s roasters give visitors and locals a taste of how specialty coffee takes shape, from sourcing and processing to roast development and brew methods. Their hands‑on approach sets them apart, with experts selecting high‑quality beans, evaluating their flavor potential, and shaping each batch to bring specific characteristics forward in the cup. 

Coffee Roasters in Chandler 

Aristocrat Coffee Roasters 

Among the city’s independent roasters, Aristocrat Coffee Roasters offers a welcoming space. This artisanal coffee shop sources beans from producing regions around the world, giving the roasting team a wide range of origins to evaluate and develop into distinct flavor profiles. The café has a modern, comfortable setting with indoor seating and a patio, along with a clean, contemporary design that reflects its focus on specialty brews and in-house roasting. 

You can expect a menu centered on espresso-based drinks, including options like cappuccinos, lattes, cortados, Americanos, and freddo espresso, along with cold brew, pour-over coffee, and a small selection of teas and other non-coffee drinks. 

Momentto Caffe 

Momentto Caffe brings another model to the mix. A family-owned café and roastery, the team has more than 30 years of roasting experience. To produce their ethically sourced and fair-trade offerings, Momentto works directly with family-owned farms across Central and South America and uses a proprietary roasting process designed to enhance natural sweetness, reduce acidity, and remove bitterness.  

The Italian Roast features smoky notes and lingering sweetness, while the Colombian Supremo Roast produces a balanced, smooth cup with impressive sweetness and hints of citrus and grape in the finish. The shop offers a lineup of espresso drinks, in-house-baked pastries, and an atmosphere modeled after European cafés. 

Peixoto Coffee 

Peixoto Coffee gives the city one of its clearest origin-to-roast stories. A “crop-to-cup” operation, Peixoto’s roasting philosophy highlights the coffee’s terroir and processing characteristics. The company’s sourcing foundation is unusually deep: Peixoto roasts coffee from its own family farm in Minas Gerais, Brazil, a farm that has been producing coffee for more than a century, along with select coffees from other exceptional producers worldwide.  

Roast development begins with green‑bean evaluation, sample roasts, and cupping before moving into small‑batch production. Their Cítrico Blend shows how roast decisions translate into flavor, with tasting notes that include dark chocolate, sweet cream, and orange. The café also features single‑origin pour‑overs, nitro cold brew, affogatos, and seasonal drinks crafted with attention to flavor detail. 

Sagebrush Coffee 

More than 95% of the product Sagebrush Coffee sells comes from producers and farms the team has met. The roaster describes many of its offerings using taste profiles such as “smooth and chocolatey” or “bright and fruity” in addition to processing details. This helps you understand how different beans will taste in the final product, since small‑batch roasting allows tighter control, clearer flavor expression, and shorter timelines between roasting and brewing. 

The roastery uses a fluid‑bed roasting system, which relies on heated air rather than a drum, giving the team tight control over roast development. The café also serves pour‑overs, espresso drinks, and seasonal lattes made with house‑crafted syrups. 

What Is Specialty Coffee?  

In long-standing industry use, specialty coffee refers to coffee that scores 80 points or higher on a 100-point scale from the Specialty Coffee Association Cupping Form. The SCA now defines specialty coffee more broadly as “a coffee or coffee experience that is recognized for its distinctive attributes, resulting in a significantly higher value within the marketplace.” 

For coffee lovers, the practical point remains the same: specialty coffee focuses on traceable quality, distinct taste, and careful evaluation. The art of processing plays a major role in shaping flavor. Washed coffees often taste cleaner and brighter. Natural or dry-processed offerings are dry with the fruit still attached to the beans, a method that often produces fruitier characteristics. Honey processing leaves some or all of the mucilage on the bean layer during drying, preserving the bean’s natural sweetness. 

Roasters then choose roast levels to highlight the characteristics created by origin and processing.  

  • Light roasts preserve more of a bean’s origin traits, often revealing brighter acidity and clearer fruit or floral notes.  
  • Medium roasts balance origin character and roast development, with deeper sweetness and more body.  
  • Dark roasts emphasize roast-driven flavors such as chocolate and cocoa, toasted sugar, or smoky notes while softening acidity. 

The brewing method further shapes how those qualities appear. Espresso condenses flavor while intensifying the body and amplifying sweetness. Pour-over brewing highlights clarity and separation, allowing individual notes to stand out. Cold brew extracts more slowly in cool water, producing a smoother, lower-acidity cup with a rounder chocolate or nut-forward profile. 

Together, origin, processing, roast level, and brewing method shape what you taste. The same beans can produce highly different cups depending on roast development and brewing methods. 

Why Locally Roasted Coffee Matters 

For Chandler visitors, locally roasted cups offer a direct benefit: a shorter path from roast to cup. Here, regional producers can evaluate a batch, refine a profile, and serve or ship coffee without a long handoff between producer, roaster, and retailer. Many local roasters rely on regular cupping and profile development, roast in small batches, and maintain direct relationships with producers. These practices help keep freshness, consistency, and clear sourcing standards, all of which lead to excellent outcomes.  

Local roasting also creates a tighter feedback loop between makers and the people drinking their products. Because coffee is roasted and sold within the same community, roasters can hear directly from customers, adjust roast profiles, and refine offerings based on real-time feedback. Supporting these businesses also keeps more spending in our economy. 

Discover Chandler Through Its Coffee Craft 

Chandler’s specialty scene invites visitors to slow down and experience the city through thoughtful craft. Each stop offers a window into careful sourcing, skilled production, and distinct flavors shaped with intention. It’s a simple way to connect with the community and discover the character behind every cup; something you won’t often find in national chains. Use our Plan Your Visit page to explore more of the region’s coffee craft.

headings.text: CSR/Volunteer Activities for Groups in Chandler, AZ

bodyHtml:
Whether you own a small start-up or head up a large corporation, your company’s mission probably isn’t just about profit margins. It’s about giving back to the community that invests in your business and finding volunteer opportunities for companies that mirror or are related to your organization.

Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) activities have become an important element to many meetings as planners seek experiences to strengthen attendee engagement and have a positive impact on a community as a part of their Arizona meeting. In Chandler, several opportunities are available for companies and in-person events to be socially responsible and support volunteer initiatives that benefit children, families and serve the overall well-being of the Chandler community. Here are some organizations where groups can make a difference throughout the year:

Feed the Children 

Feed the Children is a national nonprofit relief organization that has tackled childhood hunger—as well as provided clothing, medicine, and other necessities—for 40 years. Feed the Children operates a distribution and volunteer center in Chandler to better serve families in the Southwest who live below the poverty line.

Volunteers can sort and screen products, and help assemble boxes of food and household essentials distributed to families in need. There are also opportunities to staff the Feed the Children Teacher Store, which gives teachers in Chandler and Mesa Title 1 schools a place to shop for free classroom supplies and books. Companies also can make corporate product donations, sponsor a child, start a fundraiser, participate in workplace giving programs and donate a vehicle.

feedthechildren.org

For Our City - Chandler

The group of nonprofits, faith-based organizations and businesses in Chandler started For Our City - Chandler in 2009. It collaborates with different organizations to host seasonal projects such as heat relief, Operation Back to School, For Our City Day, Thanksgiving food boxes and holiday drives. Volunteers are needed for all events, including providing prep before and on the day of events. In addition, volunteers and companies can donate water, food and school supplies, sponsor events, provide in-kind donations and serve on planning committees.

For Our City also supports several ongoing projects, including Let’s Pull Together, ChangeUp, and I-HELP. In addition, volunteer groups can perform yard work and home repairs, and cook meals for the homeless. An ongoing project at Willis Jr. High School helps collect school supplies and clothing, and seek bus drivers and mentors.

forourcitychandler.org

AZCEND

Formerly Chandler Christian Community Center, AZCEND was founded in 1966 and supports many community endeavors that nourish the mind and body. Besides operating a food bank and supplying emergency and supplemental food boxes (as well as running two family resource centers), it manages I-HELP: Interfaith Homeless Emergency Lodging, offers case management, emergency and rent utility assistance through the Community Action Program (CAP), and early childhood literacy programs for child under the age of 5. AZCEND also manages the Chandler and Gilbert senior centers, which includes providing nutritious home delivery meals and activities for seniors.

Group and individual volunteers assist in a variety of programs including the Family Resource Center, Community Action Program, food bank, senior centers and I-HELP. For example, volunteers can sort and bag food for distribution, deliver meals, work on special events, be a literacy mentor or activities assistant. Bilingual skills are an added bonus.

azcend.org

Feed My Starving Children

As a Christian nonprofit, Feed My Starving Children works with organizations and ministries to end global childhood hunger through distribution of food packs. Arizona is one of four states with permanent packing sites. Volunteers are needed for two-hour shifts—at the permanent facility in Mesa and at MobilePack events—to hand-pack rice, soy, dried vegetables and a nutritionally complete blend of vitamins and minerals into bags, which are then sealed, boxed, placed on pallets and shipped to partners around the world.

Other ways to give back include sponsoring an online fundraiser, donating to a MobilePack, contributing to the organization through a payroll giving program, and making a matching gift or monthly donation.

fmsc.org

For more ideas and information about adding CSR activities into your next meeting, please connect with the Visit Chandler sales team.

bodyHtml:
Planning a casual first date or marking a meaningful milestone? Chandler offers plenty of fun things to do, with options that range from outdoor adventures to low-key evenings. The city’s creative energy, scenic spaces, and nightlife make it easy to connect, or reconnect, at your own pace. Whether it’s a sunset ride, a rooftop toast, or getting creative together, the options are as varied as your idea of a great time.

Find Your Perfect Chandler Date

Not sure where to start? Match the mood to one of these Chandler date ideas:

  • For a classic dinner date: Settle in for steak and seafood at CHoP Chandler or share a coal-fired pie at Grimaldi’s Pizzeria.

  • For something outdoors: Take a sunset horseback ride at KOLI Equestrian Center or enjoy a scenic stroll through Veterans Oasis Park.

  • For a creative date: Paint pottery together at Burst of Butterflies or try a wheel-throwing class at PIP Coffee + Clay.

  • For a little friendly competition: Bowl at Bowlero Kyrene, race go-karts at Andretti Indoor Karting & Games, or work together to escape the room at ESCAPE Chandler.

  • For a laid-back date: Grab coffee at Maple House or Sagebrush Coffee and enjoy some time together without a packed itinerary.

  • For a special occasion: Take in panoramic Sonoran Desert views on a hot air balloon ride with Rainbow Ryders.

Jump to:

Dinner Dates & Nightlife | Outdoor Adventures | Creative & Crafty Activities | Playful Indoor Dates | Coffee, Sweets & Chill Vibes | Unique Chandler Experiences

 

Dinner Dates & Nightlife

When it comes to date night restaurants, our city delivers ambiance and flavor in equal measure. Steak and seafood lovers will feel right at home at CHoP Chandler, where dim lighting and polished decor set the tone for fine dining. If you’re craving something casual yet intimate, share a coal-fired pie and cannoli at Grimaldi’s Pizzeria, or enjoy an evening of food and smiles at Singing Pandas, featuring on-stage entertainment that pairs wonderfully with flavorful Chinese cuisine.

 

After dinner, keep the charm alive with a change of scene. Savor local brews and listen to live music at QuartHaus, or swing by The Stillery for country tunes and mason jar cocktails. For swoon-worthy views and a laid-back rooftop vibe, The Perch Brewery offers the perfect spot to toast to the moment. A slow-paced finish to the outing might mean tickets to a Chandler movie theater and a shared bucket of popcorn.

 

Outdoor Adventures for Two

Take a Sunset Ride. Some of the most romantic outings happen outside. For a western-style experience, take the reins on a sunset ride at KOLI Equestrian Center, one of the best spots for horseback riding in Chandler.

Prefer something low-key? Ease into your day with a scenic stroll through Veterans Oasis Park, and discover groomed dirt trails, wetlands, and wildlife viewing areas. If you’re up for a bit more elevation, lace those boots for a sunrise hike at South Mountain Park, just a short drive from the city and well worth it for that early morning glow.

Creative & Crafty Activities

For sweethearts who love working with their hands, our craft-focused scene offers experiences that are equal parts fun and meaningful. Paint pottery side by side at Burst of Butterflies or try a wheel throwing class at PIP Coffee + Clay and leave with personalized keepsakes. Sign up for a DIY session at AR Workshop to craft custom signs and home decor in a warm, welcoming space.

 

Playful Indoor Dates

Inject some energy into your time as a couple with a little friendly competition. Hit the lanes at Bowlero Kyrene. The neon lights and music create an upbeat energy ideal for a lighthearted match-up. For an action-packed adventure, race go-karts or challenge each other to arcade games at Andretti Indoor Karting & Games.

 

Mini golf fans will love testing their aim on glow-in-the-dark courses, while puzzle lovers can team up at ESCAPE Chandler to crack codes and escape the room.

Coffee, Sweets, & Chill Vibes

Not every shared experience needs to be an all-day event. Sometimes, a quiet hour at a neighborhood café is all it takes. Cozy up at Maple House, known for seasonal drinks and a relaxed atmosphere. Or swing by Sagebrush Coffee, where warm interiors and thoughtfully brewed espresso make for the perfect start to any day.

 

If you’re looking to mix in something sweet, enjoy a boba at a popular tea spot, or grab dessert and a board game at a local hangout. Some cafés even offer pup cups, making it easy to bring your furry third wheel along.

 

Unique Chandler Experiences  

For anniversaries or just-because splurges, our city provides unique experiences that are hard to forget. Hot air balloon rides with Rainbow Ryders serve up panoramic views of the Sonoran Desert, ideal for proposals, milestones, or simply crossing something off your shared bucket list.

 

Beer lovers can book a behind-the-scenes tour at SanTan Gardens Brewery & Distillery, complete with tastings and insight into the craft process. It’s an immersive way to sip, learn, and spend quality time together.

 

This guide makes it easy to find the right fit for your next outing, no matter if you’re craving a quiet connection or a full-on adventure. Mix and match these charming ideas to fit the season, your mood, or that special occasion on the calendar. Start planning your romantic getaway today!
