headings.text: Finding the Best Donuts in Chandler
Make a Day of It in Chandler

bodyHtml:
Doughnuts have a way of turning an ordinary morning into something magical — a little indulgence, a little nostalgia, and a whole lot of flavor. Whether you’re celebrating National Donut Day (June 5, 2026) or simply craving something sweet, Chandler, AZ is home to some of the most delicious doughnut shops in the Valley.

Before you dive into these irresistible treats, make your morning even better by pairing your pastry with a great local breakfast spot. Explore breakfast in Chandler or keep the foodie adventure going with even more local restaurants.

Here’s where to find the best doughnuts in Chandler.

Bosa Donuts

 A longtime Chandler favorite, Bosa Donuts has three locations in Chandler (North Chandler, Central Chandler, and South Chandler), delivering the classic doughnut shop experience. No frills, just consistently great pastries. With three convenient Chandler locations, it’s easy to pop in for a fresh apple fritter (a local favorite), a perfectly glazed raised doughnut, or a classic bar. Their fritters are especially beloved for their crispy edges and generous apple chunks.

Mochinut 

If you’re craving something a little different, Mochinut brings a fun fusion of American‑style doughnuts and Japanese mochi. Their signature ring of eight chewy, airy dough balls creates a texture unlike anything else in town. Flavors rotate often and include Asian‑inspired favorites like Yuzu, Ube, and Matcha, along with playful twists like Cookies & Cream. You’ll find Mochinut inside Ranch 99, a perfect stop during a day of exploring Chandler’s diverse culinary scene.

 

Rainbow Donuts and Smoothies

A family‑owned gem, Rainbow Donuts and Smoothies offers a wide variety of pastries, from classic glazed doughnuts to inventive creations such as their Maple Bacon Doughnut or powdered green tea cronut. Their cronuts (croissant‑doughnut hybrids) are especially popular, and the shop also serves savory croissant sandwiches, smoothies, and boba drinks. It’s a great stop for both sweet and savory cravings. 

Hash Kitchen

Known for its over‑the‑top brunches and creative cocktails, Hash Kitchen also serves up one of Chandler’s most craveable doughnut treats: Cannoli Donuts. Fried to order, filled with sweet cannoli cream, and dusted with powdered sugar, these little bites disappear fast. They make a great starter before diving into one of Hash Kitchen’s signature brunch dishes.

 

Make a Day of It in Chandler

Once you’ve satisfied your sweet tooth, keep exploring! Chandler is full of vibrant experiences, from outdoor adventures to arts, culture, and family‑friendly fun. Discover more things to do in Chandler and turn your doughnut run into a full day of local adventure.

headings.text: Downtown Chandler Murals That Will Inspire You

bodyHtml:
If you’re a true art lover, follow a trail through Downtown Chandler, where you’ll encounter colorful street art and murals that give you a glimpse into the city’s diverse community. From vibrant works that revisit Chandler’s rich history to dynamic depictions of the burgeoning city and all that it has to offer, downtown’s murals are a wonderful mix of expression and storytelling, and there's plenty of free parking. Here are several murals that are sure to inspire you.

Commonwealth Canal

At 225 feet, spanning a portion of the Commonwealth Canal, this mural adds to Downtown Chandler’s collection of street murals bursting with color and creativity. Located just south of the Crowne Plaza Phoenix Chandler Golf Resort, on the southern exterior wall of the property, the eye-catching piece is the work of artist Ariana Enriquez. The Chandler resident—and Chandler High School alum—says the mural is inspired by water as a vital element in our desert, giving life to desert foliage, local wildlife, and the king protea flower, a symbol of courage and diversity.

SanTan Brewing Company

Also bringing color and energy to the downtown scene is the mural outside SanTan Brewing Company. Awash in bright colors, the mural depicts a trio of gleaming beer distillers surrounded by desert cactus. Created by the graffiti artist team of Noe “Such Styles” Baez and Champ Styles, the project was led by the Chandler Arts Commission, in collaboration with the Downtown Chandler Community Partnership and SanTan Brewing Company.

Overstreet

With its modern façade and shiny exterior, downtown’s Overstreet development brings new and exciting things to Chandler—including a series of floral-themed murals by artist Kasten. Specializing in spray-paint art, the Realtor-turned-artist is known for his vibrant colors inspired by his affinity for vintage floral wallpaper. The murals—which quote the famous line, “I have a feeling we’re not in Kansas, anymore,” from “The Wizard of Oz”—call out Chandler’s growth and change from a small-town community to a burgeoning urban center.

Monuments to Chandler

An ode to Chandler’s past and present, this Downtown mural, located in the breezeway between Original ChopShop and Saba's Western Wear, takes a look back at 100 years of the city’s history. Created by artists Joey Salamon and Cam DeCaussin, the sweeping mural combines geometric, zig-zag patterns with old-fashioned portraits, signifying Chandler’s rich history and evolution. To ensure he captured the city’s character, DeCaussin researched Chandler’s archival photos and used them to paint portraits of desert landscapes, farm fields, and the Chandler City Hall complex.

Don't miss!

Other murals to look out for are at QuartHaus, created by father-son graffiti artists Such and Champ Styles. The pair are also known for their artwork at SanTan Brewing Company.

bodyHtml:
Step through the doors of d’Vine Gourmet in the heart of Downtown Chandler and you’ll quickly realize this isn’t your average gift shop. The scent of handmade caramel drifts from the kitchen. Shelves are lined with Arizona wines & beverage experiences — perfect Arizona souvenirs and locally made gifts for visitors. Visitors linger over wine flights and tastings while locals stop in for birthday gifts, corporate baskets or simply a bottle of Arizona wine to enjoy with friends.

Arizona Flavor in Every Gift

It’s less of a store and more of a celebration of Arizona.

“We’re Arizona’s version of Harry & David,” says owner Denise McCreery with a smile. “We want everybody in Arizona to know they can buy from us and support local.”

How d’Vine Gourmet Got Its Start

Twenty‑three years ago, while making peanut butter and jelly sandwiches for her young children, she glanced across the kitchen counter at her husband Andrew’s wine samples. “I should make wine jelly,” she remembers thinking. She and her sister‑in‑law had no idea how to make jelly. “We said, ‘Let’s figure it out.’” They did.

The first batches were sold at Arizona street fairs, where customers quickly became fans searching for unique Arizona‑made gifts and foodie souvenirs and foodie souvenirs.

From Wine Jelly to Gift Baskets

As demand grew, customers asked if the jellies could be packaged as gifts and shipped to family and friends. “They’d ask, ‘Can you make this into a gift basket?’ That’s really how it evolved,” McCreery says.

Today, d’Vine Gourmet is one of Arizona’s few remaining independent gift basket companies and the state’s only professional gift basket provider to the NFL.

A Showcase of Arizona Makers

Inside the Downtown Chandler store, shoppers will discover products from roughly 150 Made in Chandler – local makers and food producers alongside d’Vine Gourmet’s handcrafted specialties, truly a one‑stop shop for Arizona souvenirs, gourmet treats and local artisan products.

Arizona Wines, Oils & Gourmet Foods

The selection ranges from Queen Creek Olive Mill oils & products and Arizona wines to locally roasted coffee, salsa, beer, chocolates, books, apparel, artwork, candles and gourmet snacks alongside d’Vine Gourmet’s own line of handcrafted specialties

McCreery proudly points to longtime partners like Relish, Sting ’N Linger Salsa, Urban Oven Crackers, and numerous Arizona wineries that have grown alongside the business. “We want to support everybody,” she says.

Events at d’Vine Gourmet

That commitment extends beyond the shelves. d’Vine Gourmet regularly hosts wine flights, tastings, sip‑and‑paint nights, book clubs, community gatherings and private events, listed on Visit Chandler’s Events Calendar.

Tastings, Flights & Community Events

Guests settle into the wine lounge with friends, sample local wines or simply enjoy the welcoming atmosphere that has made the shop a favorite gathering place.

“We really are the hub of downtown,” McCreery says. “We’ve created a community of vendors. We’ve created a community of locals that want to shop here. We’ve created a community for corporate gifts. Everybody has a place here.”

That sense of place feels especially fitting in historical Downtown Chandler.

What’s Next for d’Vine Gourmet

Plans are underway for the next chapter. d’Vine Gourmet is expanding its Arizona wine selection to 100 labels, adding lounge space and introducing a nostalgic candy bar filled with handmade sweets and gourmet confections, ideal for visitors seeking tasty Arizona souvenirs and handcrafted treats.

Souvenirs for Visitors & Locals Alike

“But even as the business grows, its mission remains refreshingly simple,” McCreery says. “Whether someone needs a Chandler souvenir or local gift, a corporate gift, a bottle of Arizona wine or something special to take home, we want them to find it here.”

bodyHtml:
You don’t have to sacrifice healthy eating when you go out for a meal in Chandler. Whether you’re looking for a quick bite on the run or a sit-down meal with a glass of wine, Chandler has plenty of options for healthy eating. Here are five restaurants you’ll want to check out if you want to eat healthy in Chandler, AZ.

Tryst Café

This award-winning restaurant serves more than 100 different menu items for breakfast, lunch and dinner, ranging from gluten-free banana quinoa pancakes for breakfast to a barbecue bacon burger and Thai shrimp lettuce wraps for dinner. Happy hour runs daily from 3 to 6 p.m. with food, cocktails, beer and wine specials. Enjoy Chandler’s incredible weather on the patio and talented local musicians on select nights.

Map: 4205 S. Gilbert Road, Chandler, AZ 85249 or (480) 656-1011

Green Corner

For healthy eating with a twist, try Green Corner, a quaint Mediterranean restaurant in south Chandler that offers vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free, and halal options for lunch and dinner. Try the falafel plate, which comes with a Greek salad, hummus and rice. Or consider the two-skewer chicken kabab served with rice and pita bread. The restaurant has splurge-worthy dishes, too, like gyros and shawarma.

Map: 1065 W. Queen Creek Road Suite 2, Chandler, AZ 85248 or (480) 553-7011

Koibito Poke

Former Major League Baseball pitcher Todd Stottlemyre named his poke restaurant chain Koibito, the Japanese word for love because he hoped guests would “love” their bodies by eating the healthy foods served there. Because you can create your own poke bowl, it’s easy to make it vegan, vegetarian, low-carb, or gluten-free. Overwhelmed by the options? You can order one of the restaurant’s signature bowls, like the chicken and shrimp bowl topped with cucumber and shaved brussels sprouts.

Map: 4041 S. Gilbert Road Suite 1, Chandler, AZ 85249 or (480) 361-6533

Original ChopShop

Located in a historic building that has served as four banks and a newspaper over the years, Original Chop Shop Co. is a popular downtown Chandler restaurant for healthy eating. In the morning, opt for bagels, fresh-baked pastries and muffins (including gluten-free options), parfaits and fresh juices. For lunch or dinner, order a chopped salad, sandwich, or protein bowl.

At the counter, check out the chart pointing you to gluten-free, vegan, vegetarian, peanut-free, lactose-free, and soy-free menu selections. Most items are around $10.

Map: 35 W. Boston St., Chandler, AZ 85225 or (480) 426-0216

Fruta Healthy Eating

Kick off your day with a cold-pressed juice, fresh smoothie, or your choice of acai or dragon fruit bowl at Fruta Healthy Eating. In the mood for something heartier? Order up a stack of the gluten-free pancakes or a bowl of good-for-you oatmeal. All dishes are preservative-free and GMO-free, and there’s even a kids’ menu. The café also has salads and sandwiches made with your choice of sourdough, wheat, or gluten-free bread for lunch.

Map: 222 E. Warner Road #106, Chandler, AZ 85225 or (480) 361-4341

bodyHtml:
Arizona is a premier golf destination, and Chandler, located in southeastern Phoenix, is at its heart. Boasting everything from Arizona’s first grass golf course to PGA championship links and executive layouts ideal for a quick round, Chandler offers golfing experiences that are second to none.

While the focus is on the exceptional courses, you’ll also find options for year-round practice at indoor venues like Stinger's Golf Club and The Back Nine Golf Club. Need to gear up? Stop by SCHEELS at Chandler Fashion Center or the PGA Tour Superstore in Uptown Chandler for apparel and equipment.

Whether you’re looking for public courses, private country clubs, or lessons to refine your swing, this is a must-visit destination for casual and expert players. Here are some of the best golf courses in Chandler, AZ.

Bear Creek Golf Complex

Bear Creek Golf Complex has two distinct courses to suit players of all skill levels. The 18-hole, par-71 links-style Bear Course spans approximately 6,825 yards, delivering a challenging experience for seasoned golfers. Meanwhile, the 18-hole, par-59 Cub Course is perfect for beginners or those looking for a shorter game. Bear Creek welcomes all players as a public facility and provides amenities such as a well-stocked pro shop, practice areas, and professional golf lessons. Golfers can also enjoy The Bears Den, an on-site restaurant offering an excellent spot for post-round relaxation.

Ironwood Golf Course 

Ironwood Golf Course is a semi-private facility located within the IronOaks at Sun Lakes community. This Chandler golf course has earned a top-10 short-course rating from Golf Advisor for its par-67 layout spanning 5,100 yards. The course winds through lush grounds with two water features, offering a fast and rewarding round with a well-balanced mix of pars. Amenities include a golf shop, practice facilities, professional instruction, and excellent dining and drinks. 

Lone Tree Golf Club

Lone Tree Golf Club is a semi-private, traditional-style course featuring a PGA-worthy, par-71, 18-hole layout. With four sets of tees, it accommodates golfers of all skill sets. The club boasts a comprehensive practice facility, a top-notch driving range and putting green, and a well-appointed clubhouse with a pro shop. Overlooking the 18th hole, The Grille restaurant is known for its welcoming atmosphere and delicious dishes, and it’s also available for group rentals. For those seeking additional privileges, the club provides membership options. Nestled against the scenic backdrop of the San Tan Mountains, this destination stands out as one of the finest golf courses in Chandler, Arizona.

Ocotillo Golf Club

Ocotillo Golf Club, recipient of Golf Digest's 4 1/2 star rating and a "Top 50 Resort" designation by Golf World, is a first-class, Ted Robinson-designed course featuring 27 holes traversing lush fairways, scenic waterfalls, and numerous lakes. Amenities include a comprehensive practice facility, a well-stocked pro shop, and Tillo's Kitchen & Patio for dining. The club is open to the public and offers various membership options, including the Arcis Players' Membership.

San Marcos Golf Course 

San Marcos Golf Course is a historic gem that blends tradition with modern amenities. Established in 1913 as Arizona’s first grass golf course, this 18-hole, par-72 course spans 6,540 yards and underwent an extensive renovation in 2014. Featuring lush fairways, mature trees, and scenic surroundings, it offers a balanced challenge for golfers of all skill levels. The facility includes a fully equipped clubhouse, a pro shop, and excellent post-round dining and drinks at Grill 60.

San Marcos is a public course that welcomes both locals and visitors. Located adjacent to the Crowne Plaza Phoenix-Chandler Golf Resort, it’s an ideal destination for stay-and-play experiences. With its rich history and impeccably maintained greens, this course is a must-play for golf enthusiasts.

Springfield Golf Resort

Springfield Golf Resort is a public executive course known as "the best-kept secret in Chandler” for its fun-loving atmosphere, beautiful course, and friendly staff. The course features a par-61 layout, providing players with a quick yet fulfilling round. Amenities include a pro shop, practice facilities, and dining at the Grill 61. The resort also offers perks such as annual passes and range memberships for frequent players and is a popular choice for a relaxed and enjoyable golfing experience.

SunBird Golf Club

SunBird Golf Club, a semi-private executive course with a par-66 layout spanning 4,384 yards, is affectionately known as the “Jewel” of Phoenix East Valley. The course challenges golfers with 10 water hazards while remaining enjoyable for players of all skill levels. Amenities include a pro shop, a 170-yard driving range, professional golf instruction, and clinics. The club features dining at The Horizon Room and hosts various leagues and tournaments year-round. Open to the public, SunBird also offers pass programs for frequent players. Golfers consistently praise the club’s well-maintained course, welcoming staff, and unique decor, highlighted by stunning wood carvings from local artist Bob Jordan.

Tee Off at San Marcos Golf Courses

Chandler stands out as a premier golfing destination, offering courses that combine natural beauty, top-tier facilities, and layouts suited for golfers of all skill levels. Whether you're looking for a challenging round or a relaxing day on the greens, Chandler delivers an unforgettable experience. So grab your clubs and hit the fairways!

headings.text: Elevated Entertainment at Andretti Indoor Karting & Games

bodyHtml:
Those with a penchant for speed have an outlet to go fast at Andretti Indoor Karting & Games in Chandler. Named for legendary Italian-American racing family the Andretti’s, the Chandler entertainment venue was the first location to open in Arizona.

Billed as a “non-stop thrills” destination, the centerpiece of the 95,000 square-foot facility features the company’s signature electric superkarts, including four multi-level go-kart tracks, with hairpin turns and long straightaways. The pay-as-you-go space caters to all ages and skill levels, with adult, intermediate and junior races for seasoned and rookie drivers. And for young drivers, there’s a Mini Mario race experience on a single level track.

Besides the thrill of testing one’s racing chops on climate-controlled high-speed tracks, visitors can get an adrenaline rush through state-of-the-art arcade experiences with:

  • Immersive duckpin bowling
  • 150-plus video games
  • A two-story, 2,600-square-feet Delta Strike laser tag arena
  • Virtual reality attractions such as Limitless VR and Hologate VR

For the ultimate experience, there’s a 7D Xperience Motion Theater where up to 12 riders compete against each other with laser blasters while battling on-screen enemies against a backdrop of 3D graphics and leading special effects.  

Open daily, Andretti Indoor Karting & Games also gives visitors plenty of opportunities to dine and unwind. The Bowling, Main Bar, Dining Room and Mario Suite feature a full restaurant menu that focuses on homemade American favorites, while the cantina offers a taco bar and brick oven pizza. There are also two full bars and lounge areas and plenty of HD TVs and large projection screens to catch all the sporting action.

In addition, more than 10,000 square feet is dedicated to event and meeting space, which is available with in-house catering and event packaging to accommodate large groups, birthday parties, wedding receptions, bar mitzvahs and other special occasions.

Andretti Indoor Karting & Games is also a great venue for corporate events, where team building meets thrilling competition. Participants can foster friendly competition and camaraderie with races on the state-of-the art tracks and arcade games, making it an ideal spot for team building and corporate bonding. The entertainment venue also provides opportunities to work CSR (Corporate Social Responsibility) into any potential team building event through the CheckIt4Andretti Charitable Foundation.

Indoor Ideas that Break the Ice
Chandler Local Spotlight: Mic Drop Comedy
A Little Friendly Competition Never Hurt

bodyHtml:
Need a break from the office grind? Or maybe you’re planning some corporate team-building in Chandler AZ beyond the usual Zoom calls and networking events? Whether your crew is getting to know each other, know each other like the back of their hands, or somewhere in between, Chandler—in the East Valley near Phoenix—is full of creative, unexpected ways to bring people together. From brewery tours and paint nights to desert trails and golf greens, these Chandler group outing ideas are anything but boring.

Looking for something chill? Staying indoors is the perfect way to bond, especially with Arizona’s warm temps.

Start off easy with a tour at SanTan Brewery and Distillery. The behind-the-scenes vibe, plus some top-notch samples, makes it one of the best icebreakers around. It’s hard not to relax when great beer is involved.

Feeling artsy? Bottle & Bean hosts paint-and-sip nights that turn even the most serious coworkers into creative (and hilarious) artists. It’s not about painting skills—it’s about shared laughs, messy canvases, and maybe a mimosa or two.

If your group could use a good laugh, head to Mic Drop Comedy Chandler, a cozy comedy club right in Downtown Chandler. It’s perfect for blowing off steam and, honestly, there’s something magical about seeing your usually-serious coworker laugh until they cry.

If your team needs a little adrenaline or some fresh air, Chandler’s outdoor options deliver big time.

Saddle up for a group ride through the desert at KOLI Equestrian Center, where scenic trails and wide-open skies make for a surprisingly peaceful day of team-building in the East Valley of Phoenix. Not into saddles? Take your crew sky-high with Rainbow Ryders or Hot Air Expeditions. Floating over the desert at sunrise is an experience your team will never forget.

For something more down to earth, Chandler’s golf scene is unrivaled. Book a casual round at one of the local courses or make it a mini-tournament. Either way, it’s a fun way to talk shop between swings.

If your team prefers exploring the city, try the gamified art adventure, the Chandler Mural Quest. It’s part scavenger hunt, part puzzle challenge and all fun. End your route at a local brewery or cocktail spot for bonus points.

Want to sneak in some problem-solving without it feeling like work? Chandler’s immersive entertainment rooms totally deliver.

Try Game Show Battle Rooms if you’ve ever wanted to hit a buzzer like you’re on TV. Or go full mystery mode with ESCAPE Chandler or Exit 4 Escape Rooms Chandler. You’ll need all hands on deck at these fun spots to solve the puzzles before time runs out. It’s intense, hilarious and secretly great for communication skills.

Some teams thrive on competition. Thankfully, Chandler is packed with places to turn that energy into pure fun.

At Stinger’s Golf Club, you can run a tournament with golf simulators. Plus, there’s a full bar to keep things interesting. Over at Taroko Sports, you’ll find everything from high-tech batting cages to solid food and drink options.

Got any pickleball fans on your crew? Pickleball Kingdom is massive and perfect for team brackets. And if you want to keep it classic (with a twist), book a few lanes or try a few crane games at Round1 Bowling & Arcade. Karaoke is totally optional, but highly encouraged.

If your crew has a need for speed, Andretti Indoor Karting & Games is wild. Between the racing, laser tag and great food offerings, it’s hard not to have a blast.

If your company values community, consider a volunteer-based group adventure in Chandler. From food-packing events to helping at local charities, giving back together can spark a deeper connection than any happy hour ever could.

Whether you’re clinking glasses at a brewery, laughing at a comedy club, or solving your way out of an escape room, Chandler in the East Valley offers the perfect mix of fun and purpose. These Chandler group outing ideas go beyond typical activities; they’re the kind of team-building memories your crew will talk about for years to come.

headings.text: Explore Culture, History & Creativity at Chandler Museums

bodyHtml:
Chandler is a city rich in culture, heritage, and innovation, offering a diverse and rewarding museum scene that is perfect for anyone interested in culture and art. Local institutions feature a range of exhibitions—from regional history and visual art to science and hands-on learning. Many combine permanent collections with rotating shows, offering something new with each visit. Browse current and upcoming exhibits to plan your next stop.

 

Step Into These Must‑See Exhibits

The spotlight shines on locally produced and nationally traveling collections at the Chandler Museum. It then extends to interactive experiences at the nearby Tumbleweed Ranch, an authentic 1917 home that features tools, farm equipment, and immersive activities, such as corn grinding. 

 

The exhibit “Pony Up! Cowgirls of Chandler” runs through November 2, 2025, and focuses on the women and girls who helped shape the city’s Western roots. Archival news articles, rodeo memorabilia, oral histories, and photography all contribute to a fuller picture of the region’s past.

 

Across town at Vision Gallery, two exhibitions are on view through August 16, 2025. “Creatures and Cosmos” presents a collection of artwork that blends science fiction with fine art, imagining alternate worlds, life forms, and cosmic landscapes. Alongside it, Germán Benincore’s “Red Dawn” installation explores humanity’s drive to colonize space through a thought-provoking display that questions the ethics, ambitions, and consequences of colonizing other planets.

Discover Upcoming Exhibits & Events

At Vision Gallery, two exhibitions will open in August 2025. “Con cariño siempre” (August 9–November 8) by Arizona visual artist Ariana Enriquez presents an intimate showcase of the artist’s story-driven work, built around the symbolism of flora and fauna, that celebrates intergenerational love and cultural legacy. Enriquez, who has completed several murals in Chandler—including a notable piece along the Commonwealth Canal—draws from personal and cultural narratives to shape her distinctive artistic voice.

 

“So Fun! An Exploration of Maximalism” (August 23–November 2) dives into the joyful aesthetic of excess, using color, pattern, and repetition to explore identity, internet culture, and the deeper meaning behind the playful design. While details are still to be confirmed, both exhibitions may include opening receptions and opportunities to engage with the artists during gallery talks. 

 

The Chandler Museum will open “Sonoran Shapes + Structures: Desert-Inspired Architecture and Design” on September 20, 2025. Running through February 1, 2026, the exhibition examines how the desert landscape has shaped visionary architecture, from Frank Lloyd Wright’s organic forms to Paolo Soleri’s bold innovations. The installation invites attendees to view the Sonoran environment as both a canvas and a collaborator.

 

Exhibits That Always Inspire

The Arizona Railway Museum—open weekends, typically early September to late May—celebrates the Southwest’s railroading heritage with an impressive collection of historic locomotives, passenger cars, and equipment. Museumgoers can step inside several vintage train cars and tour meticulously restored interiors.

 

Self-guided tours of the rail yard provide close-up views of rare engines and cabooses, accompanied by informative placards that share the history of each artifact. Indoors, the recreated Chandler Depot houses railway memorabilia, a model train layout, and a gift shop, making this a favorite stop for history buffs and families alike.

 

The Chandler Museum features the permanent “Chandler: A Great Place to Grow” display, a presentation that traces the area’s transformation from its agricultural roots to a modern suburban community. Visitors can uncover stories of early settlers through historic photographs and preserved relics from the city’s formative years.

 

Know Before You Go

Most of the Chandler Museum’s exhibits are free. The museum is open Tuesday to Saturday from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. and Sundays from 1 p.m. to 5 p.m. You’ll find a good deal of free, on-site parking.

 

Vision Gallery offers free admission and is open Monday through Friday from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. and Saturday from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. Free parking is available in the Washington St. Parking Garage. 

 

The Arizona Railway Museum is open on weekends, 10 a.m. to 4 p.m., from September to May. There is plenty of free parking in the lot. 

 

Make the most of your day by starting downtown with galleries and public art, then heading to the Railway Museum for a look at the region’s railroading past. Since hours and displays may vary seasonally, be sure to check each museum’s website for the latest updates and special events. Chandler’s museum scene combines art, history, and hands-on discovery, making it perfect for explorers of all ages. Start planning your next cultural outing today.

headings.text: Exploring Chandler with Your Pet: A Guide to Dog-Friendly Vacations
Where to Eat with Your Pup
Pet Tips for the Arizona Heat

bodyHtml:
Travelers increasingly plan adventures with furry companions in mind, and Chandler, Arizona, is rolling out the welcome mat for both humans and their four-legged friends. Whether you’re searching for pet-welcoming accommodations, dining al fresco with your pup, or sniffing out the best local dog parks, this desert city delivers a full lineup of comfort, fun, and convenience. Keep reading for a tail-wagging guide to a dog-friendly vacation, from hotel check-ins to off-leash romps at the park.

 

Pet-Friendly Places to Stay

You’ll find a variety of pet-friendly hotels in Chandler that make traveling with your companion easy and enjoyable. Crowne Plaza Resort Phoenix-Chandler Golf Resort allows two tail waggers per room (max 40 lbs. each), charges a $75 non‑refundable deposit per pet, per stay, and features an on-site dog-walking area. It’s also a short walk from the dog-friendly patio at SanTan Brewing Company.

 

Home2 Suites by Hilton Phoenix Chandler welcomes your adventure buddy with a $75 non‑refundable fee for up to five days (increasing to $125 for longer stays). This one is under a 10-minute drive from the Snedigar Sportsplex dog park. Fairfield Inn & Suites Phoenix Chandler/Fashion Center permits two four-legged guests per room (weight limit 60 lbs.) and charges a $75 non‑refundable fee ($125 for stays of six nights or more). Wagging friends are welcome in an on-site outdoor seating area.

 

Located across the street from Chandler Fashion Center mall, the Cambria Hotel Phoenix Chandler - Fashion Center provides complimentary treat bags upon arrival, an outdoor waste station, and a dog water bowl in the lobby. Maximum pet weight is 75 lbs. and nightly pet fee of $50.

Where to Eat with Your Pup

Chandler is home to a range of canine-friendly eateries, many of which have spacious patios and bowls of fresh water for furry guests. The Perch Brewery features a garden patio surrounded by tropical rescue birds, where your leashed pal is highly welcome. Helluva Brewing Company and SanTan Brewing Company also open their patios to happy tails and offer water and treats, creating a laid-back atmosphere perfect for relaxing and taking in the slow-paced Arizona vibes. 

 

Parks, Playgrounds & Pawsitive Fun

For off-leash fun, head to one of Chandler’s dedicated dog parks. Shawnee Park has a fenced area where your buddy can run and socialize, while Nozomi Dog Park is a favorite among locals thanks to its separate sections for large and small breeds. Be sure to bring waste bags and supervise your pawed pal at all times.

 

For a more leisurely outing, take a stroll through Veterans Oasis Park, where leashed pals are welcome to join you on trails that wind past desert landscapes and a scenic wetland. If you’re visiting during one of Chandler’s community events, like the Downtown Chandler Farmers Market, expect a pet-friendly scene.  

 

Pet Tips for the Arizona Heat

Arizona sunshine is no joke, especially in the summer. To keep your furry friend safe, plan outings early in the morning or after sunset when pavement temperatures are lower. Even during these hours, overall temperatures remain high, so always check to make sure your sidekick is comfortable and safe. Carry a collapsible bowl and plenty of water, and consider booties or other forms of paw protection to prevent burns from hot surfaces.

 

Seek out trails and parks that provide shade and rest stops, and take breaks often. On especially hot days, let your furball cool down indoors by visiting Chandler’s animal supply stores, such as Pet Planet or PetSmart, where you can grab essentials or simply enjoy the A/C.

Know Before You Go 

Laws in Chandler require that all dogs be kept on a leash no longer than six feet when outside of enclosed areas, including parks and trails. They must also be licensed and vaccinated to meet county requirements. If you need gear, snacks, or a new toy to reward your well-behaved travel buddy, Chandler’s local pet shops have you covered. In addition to Pet Planet and PetSmart, consider Bark & Luv, a boutique-style shop that offers wholesome food, stylish accessories, and self-service wash stations. 

 

You can also stop by Three Dog Bakery, another favorite where pastry chefs bake treats on-site using simple, healthy ingredients. Their playful seasonal creations, gourmet pastries, famous Pupcakes, and personalized canine cakes make it a must-visit for celebrating your tail-wagger.

 

The city offers a pet-friendly vacation experience perfect for both weekend getaways and extended trips, filled with warmth, activity, and convenience. With dog-friendly hotels, restaurants, and parks, every element for a memorable trip is at your fingertips. Ready to plan your next adventure? Start here, and bring your best friend along for the ride.

bodyHtml:
Surrounded by cozy neighborhoods in southeast Chandler, Veterans Oasis Park isn’t just a park—it’s a place where you can connect with nature, explore the wonders of the desert, and honor those who have served our country. Whether you’re a local or a visitor, the park offers a respite from the hustle and bustle of daily life. Here are a few of our favorite things about this iconic Chandler destination.

Desert Trails

Just because you’re in the city doesn’t mean you can’t get up close and personal with nature. The desert trails at Veterans Oasis Park give you the perfect opportunity to explore the arid landscape, encounter fascinating cacti and native plants, and—if you’re lucky—catch a glimpse of an array of desert animals, including roadrunners, herons, ducks and rabbits.

Urban Birding

Considered a true bird-watcher’s paradise, Veterans Oasis Park in Chandler attracts an array of migratory and local birds to its riparian environments lush with native vegetation. In fact, more than 153 species have been documented, many of which can be seen during guided bird walks conducted by the Desert Rivers Audubon Society. Held the first Saturday of the month from November to April, the walks are designed for new and experienced birders alike. Find the current birding programs here.

Field of Honor

In tribute to Arizona’s past, present and future veterans, the Field of Honor is a poignant and peaceful space for quiet reflection. The multi-level memorial was designed to match the exact ratio of the American flag, and represents six memorial themes: freedom, recognition, reflections, sacrifice, memories and family. Overlooking the memorial is the Williams Air Force Base Memorial Plane, which features a plaque that honors the military men and women who served at the base from 1941 to 1993.

Fishing

If you’re angling for some outdoor fun, cast your line into the five-acre lake stocked with everything from catfish and rainbow trout to bluegill and largemouth bass. But before you reel in the big one, be sure to obtain a fishing license from the Arizona Game & Fish department in advance.

Self-guided Chandler Solar System Walk

Take an informative journey through “space” as you explore the park’s solar system walk. Stretching 2,500 feet, the path will take you around the lake where along the way you’ll discover a series of monuments and signs representing the sun, planets and celestial objects. Both educational and relaxing, this fascinating experience is must-do when visiting the park.

Wildlife Viewing Areas

With 78 of its 113 acres designated for groundwater recharge and wetlands, Veterans Oasis Park attracts an abundance of desert wildlife. For some of the best views, make your way to any of the designated viewing areas where you can see animals in their natural habitat. Bonus: If you fancy yourself a photographer, bring your camera, capture a stunning moment and share it with Visit Chandler here for a chance to be featured on a page.

Sonoran Sunset Concert Series

Enjoy live music against the backdrop of a stunning Arizona sunset at this unique concert series set in Veterans Oasis Park. Featuring local musicians and entertainers performing everything from jazz to country to American classics, the event is a wonderful reason to gather with family and friends under a star-filled sky. Seasonal concerts held October through March.

Chandler Nature Center

Explore the region’s unique flora and fauna at the Chandler Nature Center, located inside the park. Offering a variety of programs and activities, visitors of all ages will be able to go on educational nature hikes, learn garden maintenance, and participate in “meet the creature” exhibits featuring scorpions, spiders, snakes and tortoises, among other local wildlife.

Owl’s Nest Nature Store

Make your visit to the Chandler Nature Center even more memorable with a memento from the Owl’s Nest Nature Store. Filled with nature-oriented and environmentally sustainable gifts, souvenirs and educational materials, you’re sure to find the perfect item to remind you of fun-filled day spent at the park. The store is open during City of Chandler operating hours and is subject to holiday closures.

Covered Ramadas

Ideal for everything from a small picnic gathering with friends and family to a large, fun-filled celebration, the park’s shaded pavilion areas are the perfect setting for any memorable event. With five ramadas available to rent, reservations can be made up to 12 months in advance for any day of the week between 9 a.m. and 10 p.m.

Park Details

Chandler Veterans Oasis Park Address: 4050 E. Chandler Heights Road, Chandler AZ 85249

Hours: 6 a.m. to 10:30 p.m.

Restrooms: There are two restroom facilities in the park.

Parking: There is a public parking lot located at the entrance of the park on Chandler Heights Road. It can also be accessed from Lindsay Road; take a right past the police substation.

What to bring: To make the most of your visit, bring sunscreen, a hat, sunglasses and comfortable walking shoes.

bodyHtml:
The evenings are starting to cool off, you know what that means? It's time to start dining on patios again! Cooler weather also means the arrival of Arizona Restaurant Week, the fall edition.

Arizona Restaurant Week returns to Chandler on September 18-27, 2026, and invites patrons to celebrate their inner foodie and enjoy a three-course, prix-fixe dinner for $33, $44 or $55 per person. Please note dinner prices exclude beverages, tax, and gratuity.

20 Chandler restaurants are participating in the statewide affair offering a variety of dining experiences from upscale dining to a casual, neighborhood eatery featuring soothing comfort food. Take advantage of the many dining opportunities and treat yourself and your loved ones to a night on the town.

Benihana

Experience the art of Teppanyaki (otherwise known as hibachi) right near Chandler Fashion Center at Benihana. Choose your steak, chicken and shrimp or steak and scallops entree to be specially prepared in front of you in this fun Japanese style restaurant. $55 per person.

Bonsai

Enjoy the authentic flavors of Japanese cuisine in a modern, social setting at Bonsai, in the heart of Downtown Ocotillo. On the prix fixe menu this year, choose from a selection of hand-crafted sushi rolls or Japanese-inspired entrees, along with an appetizer and desert. $33 per person.

CHoP Chandler

Located in Downtown Ocotillo, CHoP Chandler is an ideal dining destination featuring a wide selection of wines, juicy steaks and succulent seafood with top-notch service. $55 per person.

Cien Agaves Chandler

The vibrant Mexican cantina known for its scratch-made menu and premium tequila offerings. Cien Agaves Chandler's restaurant week menu features a three course meal with optional upgrades for an additional cost. Enjoy a main course of fajitas or tempiquena and finish off with a churro sundae. $44 per person.

Cooper's Hawk Winery & Restaurant

Known for their perfected wine parings with their American cuisine, Cooper's Hawk Winery & Restaurant offers an inviting, modern upscale dining experience. Their restaurant week menu features a three course meal with suggested wine pairings (additional cost). $44 per person.

Cuisine & Wine Bistro

The quaint, Chandler French bistro is known for its elevated and chic menu. Their restaurant week menu features a three course meal with a sommelier on-site for recommended wine pairings (additional cost). Enjoy a main course of pan seared salmon or grilled lamb chop and finish off with a tartelette or creme brulee. $55 per person or upgrade the main course to beef wellington for an additional $30.

Feringhee Modern Indian Cuisine

Arizona's only fine dining, Indian restaurant, Feringhee is a modern restaurant that uses the finest produce, exquisite ingredients and humble Indian spices to reimagine the way we perceive Indian food. $44 per person.

Fleming's Prime Steakhouse & Wine Bar

Experience fine dining in West Chandler at Fleming's Prime Steakhouse & Wine Bar. Find specialty plated American dishes with the option to upgrade to some of their premium entrees like filet mignon. $55 per person.

Galeto Brazilian Steakhouse

Located in West Chandler, Galeto Brazilian Steakhouse offers a unique dining experience featuring the authentic flavors of Brazil with fire-roasted meats served tableside. $55 per person.

George & Gather

George & Gather is a trendy spot that serves up a variety of specially crafted plates, prepared fresh, with no seed-oils, and gluten-free options available. Enjoy dining in a vibrant modern atmosphere with touches of upscale vibes. $44 per person.

High Tide at the Steelyard

Experience some of the freshest seafood in the Valley at High Tide at the Steelyard. Find salmon, striped bass, crab and veal on the menu. $55 per person.

LUCCA Coastal Kitchen

Savor on the flavors of Italian cuisine with a coastal seafood touch at LUCCA Costal Kitchen. This spot offers an elegant patio and dining room along with a large selection of hand-crafted cocktails and wines that pair perfectly with every meal. $55 per person with the option to add a featured cocktail for an addtional cost.

SanTan Brewing Co.

SanTan Brewing Company is an Arizona-based, award-winning producer of hand-crafted beers made with uncommon quality for everyday occasions. This local favorite is located in the heart of Downtown Chandler and features a full pub with craft beers on draft and a full menu. $44 per couple.

SanTan Spirit House Coffee & Cocktails

This well-known spin-off of SanTan Brewing Company, SanTan Spirit House Coffee & Cocktails is an intimate neighborhood cocktail bar and tasting room. They have been distilling their own liquors and liqueurs since 2015 and offer a wide variety. $44 per couple.

Shimogamo

Voted as one of the best sushi restaurants in the Phoenix area, Shimogamo serves up traditional Japanese cuisine and sushi in a vibrant and modern atmosphere. $55 per person.

The Keg Steakhouse + Bar

Centrally located in Chandler, near Chandler Fashion Center, The Keg Steakhouse + Bar has long been celebrated for its relaxing atmosphere, juicy steaks, and seafood. Enjoy a choice between the $44 per person menu or the upgraded $55 per person menu.

The Mexicano Chandler

Enjoy the bold flavors of Mexican cuisine with a modern twist with each dish at The Mexicano. This popular spot offers a huge outdoor patio along with live entertainment every day for a lively dining experience. $33 per person with an optional $18 per person cocktail pairing.

The Sicilian Butcher

Known for their craft meatballs, charcuterie bar, and customizable cannoli bar, The Sicilian Butcher has some great options for Arizona Restaurant Week. $44 per person.

Thirsty Lion Gastropub & Grill

Located in Chandler, right near Chandler Fashion Center, Thirsty Lion Gastropub & Grill has lively and modern atmosphere with a menu that includes classic American favorites, seafood, and great craft drinks. $33 per person.

Warren's Supper Club

Located in west Chandler, Warren's Supper Club offers a unique dining experince immersed in the sounds of jazz music alongside American fare and handcrafted cocktails. Choose from salmon, steak, ribs, or chicken for your main course with the option to upgrade to so of their premium offerings. $55 per person.

bodyHtml:
Finding exceptional family-friendly restaurants in Chandler is easy, thanks to the city’s welcoming locals, playful atmosphere, and menus designed with all ages in mind. As one of the most family-centric destinations in the Valley, it offers a variety of dining options where everyone can enjoy a great meal together. From casual eats to themed spots and weekend brunch, these restaurants have something for every appetite.

Reliable Family Favorites

When it comes to trusted local favorites, Floridino’s Pizza & Pasta tops the list with its famous pizza muffins and cozy Italian classics. Their Junior 7″ Pizza from the kids’ menu is always a hit with younger diners. At the Thirsty Lion, the little ones enjoy having their own special menu, featuring favorites like chicken strips and mini sliders. The restaurant’s warm, welcoming atmosphere makes it a great spot for the whole family to unwind over a satisfying meal.
 

Crust Simply Italian also earns high marks for its well-priced menu, serving up familiar plates like spaghetti and meatballs, chicken tenders with fries, and cheesy slices that satisfy the whole table. For a scenic setting, Stone & Vine Urban Italian has a spacious lakeside patio along with popular comfort dishes like creamy mac and cheese that guests of all ages can enjoy. Nearby, Bella Gusto Urban Pizzeria stands out for its creative pies and shareable starters that make family-style dining a breeze.

Fun Weekend Breakfasts & Brunch Spots

Start your weekend on a delicious note with a family-friendly breakfast or brunch at these beloved local spots. Over Easy has a delightful kids’ menu with pancakes, eggs and tots, and waffle dogs. For those with a sweet tooth, the cinnamon roll French toast is a must-try.
 

Inside a Chandler airport hangar, Hangar Café delights aviation fans of all ages with soaringly good food and views of planes taking off. Chase’s Diner adds a dose of nostalgia with its retro ambiance and comforting dishes, including fun bites like mini corn dog nuggets. 

Dining with a Twist: Entertainment & Themes

These fun restaurants in Chandler offer more than just a meal—they’re a whole experience! Start with Singing Pandas Asian Restaurant & Bar, where flavorful Asian cuisine is paired with live musical performances, creating a lively, memorable outing alongside your kid’s favorite Asian dishes.
 

The Perch Brewery provides a tropical atmosphere where families can dine near dozens of exotic rescue birds. Great kid-friendly options are tots, soft pretzels, and wings. For a playful twist on Italian dining, The Sicilian Butcher brings big-time fun with its Meatball Ferris Wheel that fills tummies and creates long-lasting smiles.

Shareable Menus & Crowd-Pleasers

When dining with a crew, these fun places to eat in Chandler offer variety and value. Hop Social Grill also welcomes families with a cozy environment and a menu with favorites like grilled cheese, peanut butter and jelly with fries.
 

For a relaxed outing at a local favorite, SanTan Brewing Company offers a welcoming atmosphere that’s perfect for the whole family. Their thoughtfully crafted children’s menu features classics like mini hamburgers and buttered noodles.

More Great Spots for Families

Rounding out Chandler’s family-friendly offerings are places like Pita Jungle where nutritious Mediterranean dishes meet a well-rounded menu for the younger crowd. American Way Smokehouse hits the mark with mouthwatering barbecue and affordable meals that let everyone at the table dig in.
 

Chandler’s dining scene makes eating out with the whole family fun and stress-free. With so many welcoming spots to explore, there’s something for every taste and occasion. Whether it’s a casual weeknight or a weekend treat, the city is ready to serve up something delicious. Ready to dig in? Start planning your next family visit today!

Ready to plan your AZ family weekend getaway?

bodyHtml:
Planning a quick family getaway? Whether you’re driving through Arizona or flying in for a weekend escape, Chandler is a hidden gem that offers big fun for little travelers for a perfect weekend in Chandler with kids. Think big skies, fun museums, lots of great food, and more ice cream stops than your kids will know what to do with. Here’s a fun-filled itinerary with family things to do this weekend in Arizona that is guaranteed to please everyone in the family.

Day 1: Planes, Trains & Pizza

Get your trip off on the right foot with breakfast at Hangar Café, a local favorite for families. This kid-friendly restaurant in Chandler sits right at Chandler Municipal Airport, so while you’re sipping coffee or savoring a sweet cinnamon roll, you can watch planes take off just a few feet away.

 

From there, pick your vibe. Want something hands-on and history-packed? Head to the Arizona Railway Museum, where train enthusiasts of all ages can explore old railcars—one of the best things to do with kids in Chandler. If nature’s more your thing, go for a light hike at Veterans Oasis Park, a perfect family-friendly activity in Chandler. Bonus points if you’re there the first Saturday of the month (November to April), when Desert Rivers Audubon leads a free guided tour.

 

By lunch, wander over to Downtown Chandler. Grab a table at The Perch Brewery, where tropical birds hang out while you eat (yes, really), or dig into a wood-fired pizza at Craft 64. Dessert is a no-brainer: The Screamery is close by and totally worth the stop for ice cream.

 

While you’re walking off the sugar rush, check out the street art. Be sure to stop at the colorful “Monuments to Us” mural located in the downtown breezeway. It’s practically begging for a family selfie.

 

Later, head back to your hotel and chill by the pool for a bit (especially if you’re staying at a family-friendly hotel in Chandler like the Crowne Plaza or Cambria Hotel, where the pool setups are on point). When evening hits, go big with a stop at Andretti Indoor Karting & Games. With go-karts, laser tag, and a massive arcade, it’s the ultimate teen-friendly activity in Chandler.

Day 2: Museum Explorers & Mall Madness

Fuel up at Over Easy at their West Chandler or Downtown Chandler location (insider tip: order the apple crumble French toast), then hit up the Chandler Museum. It’s small but packed with hands-on exhibits—an easy win if you’re looking for things to do with kids in Chandler that also sneak in a little learning.

 

Next stop? Chandler Fashion Center. The kids can hop on the indoor Ferris wheel at SCHEELS or hit the bowling lanes at Round1 Bowling & Arcade, another top teen-friendly activity in Chandler. For lunch, head to The Mexicano, where they serve guac on a mini Ferris wheel. It’s guaranteed to wow your Instagram followers and keep the kids entertained.

 

Cool down afterward at the mall’s spray pad, then make your way to Sweeties, Arizona’s largest candy store. Back at the hotel, squeeze in another pool break, then wrap up the night at Singing Pandas Asian Restaurant & Bar. Between the Mongolian beef and Elvis impersonators, it’s dinner and a show rolled into one.

Day 3: Diner Vibes & Indoor Adventures

For your final morning, keep it classic with Chase’s Diner, serving up made-from-scratch American fare, or go wild at Hash Kitchen with their over-the-top pancakes and famous Bloody Mary bar.

 

Then head west for a little more fun: Swingin’ Safari Mini Golf is quirky, colorful, and the perfect family-friendly activity in West Chandler for all ages. Or, if you’re melting in the sun, cool off at Ice Den Chandler, where ice skating is a blast for both kids and teens.

 

Last stop: Merchant Square for some treasure hunting and vintage finds. Wrap things up with lunch at American Way Smokehouse and don’t skip the cookies from Tattered Aprons.

Ready to plan your AZ family weekend getaway?

From kid-friendly restaurants in Chandler to high-energy attractions and family-friendly hotels in Chandler, it’s easy to pack your weekend with memory-making moments. Whether you’re traveling with toddlers, tweens or teens, the city delivers a perfect mix of family-friendly activities in Chandler and unique fun for every age.

headings.text: Burger Bliss: Where to Find the Best Burgers in Chandler, AZ
Brews – A Taphouse and Gourmet Burger Joint

bodyHtml:
Craving a juicy, stacked, fresh-off-the-grill burger? Chandler’s got you covered. From retro diners to hip gastropubs, just like Chandler’s craft beer scene, the burgers here are anything but basic. Whether you’re in the mood for comforting classics or inventive creations, this guide to the best burgers in Chandler, AZ, will help you find your next favorite.

Brews – A Taphouse and Gourmet Burger Joint

Brews has quickly become a go-to for locals, with two Chandler locations and a chill, come-as-you-are vibe. Their beer list is always changing, so there’s something new to try with every visit. As the saying goes, when in Rome (in this case, Arizona) do as the locals do and order the State 48, featuring pepper jack cheese, fried corn tortilla, pico de gallo, avocado and house-made jalapeno cheese sauce. Add a side of onion rings and you’re winning. 

Map to Brews location in West Chandler: 5055 W. Ray Road, Chandler AZ 85226

Map to Brews location in South Chandler: 2040 S. Alma School Road, Chandler AZ 85286

Lennys Burgers

If you’re craving a throwback, Lennys hits the spot. This old-school burger joint serves up no-nonsense classics with a side of nostalgia. The double cheeseburger is messy in the best way, thanks to two all-beef patties covered in American cheese and 1000 Island dressing. And the chili cheese fries? Totally worth it.

Map to Lenny’s Burgers: 2156 N. Alma School Road, Chandler AZ 85224

Hop Social Grill

Among the burger restaurants Chandler AZ locals swear by, Hop Social Grill stands out for both its energy and its menu. The wagyu beef burger brings bold flavors with goat cheese, fig spread, crispy onions and garlic aioli. Pair it with one of the 50-plus craft beers on tap and you’re guaranteed to be back for more.

Map to Hop Social Grill: 3405 W. Chandler Blvd., Chandler AZ 85226

Thirsty Lion Gastropub

Looking for gourmet burgers in Chandler with a twist? Thirsty Lion combines creative comfort food with a gastropub feel. And speaking of gastropub, order the Gastropub Burger. Infused with gorgonzola, the patty is grilled with sweet onion, maple pepper bacon, white cheddar and horseradish cream. 

Map to Thirsty Lion: 3077 W. Frye Road, Chandler AZ 85226

Cold Beers & Cheeseburgers

One of the top Chandler restaurants with hamburgers, Cold Beers & Cheeseburgers, has a serious burger lineup. Mmmac & Cheeseburger, anyone? As tempting as these hits are, though, tap into your creative side and go for the build-your-own-burger experience—pick your protein, toppings and sides, and a masterpiece is born. Don’t forget the crispy onion rings. It’s loud, fun, and full of flavor.

Map to Cold Beers & Cheeseburgers: 1980 W. Germann Road, Chandler AZ 85286

Patent 139 Brewing

Right by the water, Patent 139 combines house-brewed beers with Arizona flair (yes, the name nods to the avocado patent). Their Origin Burger is a flavor-packed masterpiece—think a generous helping of Hass avocado, smoked cheddar, thick-cut bacon, and a killer house “shoosh” sauce. This is definitely one of the more unique hamburger places in Chandler AZ.

Map to Patent 139 Brewing: 1949 W. Ray Road, Chandler AZ 85224

DTC Sports Grille

TVs on every wall, crowd energy and burgers that bring the heat…literally. The Diablo Smash at the DTC Sports Grille in Chandler is bold and spicy, made with melted pepper jack cheese, crispy bacon, crunchy onion strings and topped with their signature Diablo sauce. Add some DTC Trifecta Wings for the table and you’ve got a solid pick for a lively night out.

Map to DTC Sports Grille Chandler: 55 W Chicago St., Chandler AZ 85225

Legends Showcase Bar & Grill

More than just food, Legends Showcase is a full experience. Expect tribute shows, cocktails and hearty eats all in one place. The burger of choice here is the Legends, topped with American cheese, tomato, caramelized onions and 1000 Island sauce.

Insider tip: Check their event calendar before you go. Elvis and dinner? Yes, please!

Map to Legends Showcase Bar & Grill: 2386 N. Alma School Road, Chandler AZ 85224

Dog Haus Biergarten

Known for hot dogs, but seriously underrated when it comes to burgers. The Holy Aioli Burger is loaded with smoked bacon, caramelized onions and gooey white American cheese. There’s also an Impossible Burger at the Dog Haus Biergarten for plant-based folks and a line of Big Belly burgers, guaranteed to satisfy the heartiest of appetites.

Map to Dog Haus Biergarten: 2780 W. Chandler Blvd., Chandler AZ 85224

ld.articleBody: It’s a fast-paced world, where fast food is often the meal of choice. bodyHtml:
It’s a fast-paced world, where fast food is often the meal of choice. Wouldn’t it be fun, instead, to slow down and treat yourself to a fine dining restaurant in Chandler where you can savor thoughtful, chef-driven menus, and enjoy attentive service complete with real tableware in high-end surroundings? For that special, celebratory dinner or romantic date night in Chandler, here are six of the best restaurants in Chandler that promise a memorable meal upgrade.

Cuisine & Wine Bistro

At this upscale, family-owned restaurant, chef-owner Fabrice Buschtetz takes diners—many who are faithful longtime regulars—on an international culinary journey with a menu influenced by his native France. The rotating lineup includes the chef’s signatures such as a French-cut pork chop and filet de boeuf barde de bacon. In addition, the menu features twists on classic starters and sides including escargot and cuisses de grenouille (frog legs). Killian Buschtetz, the bistro’s level one sommelier, also can guide diners with pairing options from the bistro’s extensive wine list that spotlights French regions, as well as wines from around the world that make it a great option for a date night in Chandler.

Map: 4991 S. Alma School Road, Chandler AZ 85248 or (480) 275-6700

CHoP Steakhouse

Despite the requisite wood paneling and tufted booths, CHoP Steakhouse is not your parents’ steak joint. Rather, the locally-owned restaurant and lounge—with an extensive wine list, craft beer and specialty cocktails—puts a chic spin on fine dining. Creative burgers, prime steaks, and seasonal seafood, as well as timeless favorites including pork chops, center-cut filets, and rib eye steaks, cooked on a 7-foot mesquite grill, are on the lineup. The neighborly spot also features house specialties of braised beef short ribs, and steakhouse linguini and meatballs; and weekly specials such as rib night on Mondays, when diners can choose from slow-cooked baby back ribs or roasted prime rib with a side and a bottle of wine.

Map: 2625 W. Queen Creek Road, Chandler AZ 85286 or (480) 821-0009

Cooper’s Hawk Winery & Restaurant

When you check in at Cooper’s Hawk it’s a multi-component dinner affair. The modern casual restaurant in Chandler is the second Arizona location of the lifestyle concept that offers fine dining, a full-service bar, private dining, and a Napa-style tasting room that features the brand’s own wines produced in the Midwest from grapes sourced worldwide. All items from the contemporary American fusion menu are made from scratch with fresh, seasonal ingredients and suggested pairings with a hand-crafted selection from Cooper’s Hawk Winery. Customers also can join the monthly wine club that features discounts on the brand’s catalog of wines, dining rewards, and access to special events.

Map: 3325 W. Chandler Blvd., Chandler AZ 85226 or (480) 936-7711

DC Steakhouse

One of the best steakhouses in Chandler, DC Steakhouse wears its chop shop traditions with pride. The downtown Chandler restaurant, located in the New Square, is shiny and sophisticated, but offers old-school surf ‘n turf warmth with a full bar and expansive patio. New York strip, porterhouse, and a Wisconsin veal chop, as well as Walleye pike, Alaskan crab legs, and lobster tail, are some of the classic comfort menu selections at this family-owned restaurant. Guests also can choose from ribs, chicken and pasta dishes, hearty side dishes such as lobster mac ‘n cheese, and appetizers including shrimp cocktail, calamari, and big-cut onion rings.

Map: 180 S. Arizona Ave., Chandler AZ 85225 or (480) 899-4400

Fleming’s Prime Steakhouse & Wine Bar

Flemings interprets traditional steakhouse offerings with a contemporary take on USDA prime steak selections from classic to specialty cuts including filet mignon and bone-in ribeyes with the usual side accompaniments. On Tomahawk Tuesday, carnivores can share a 35-ounce tomahawk, a package that includes starters, sides, and dessert. More than a steakhouse, Fleming’s also features seafood selections including truffle poached lobster, barbecue Scottish salmon filet, and double breast of chicken, as well as plant-based options for non-meat eaters. As expected, Fleming’s wine and signature craft cocktails are on point with the best picks from Napa and global varietals, and steak-friendly pours such as Fonseca sours, tiki mules and old fashions.

Map: 905 N. 54th St., Chandler AZ 85226 or (480) 940-1900

The Hidden House

On the surface, The Hidden House evokes feelings of simpler times. But the repurposed, 1939 cottage is no ordinary dining spot in historic downtown Chandler. A mix of fancy and friendly, the not-so-secret restaurant creates a sense of intimate whimsy with a casual outdoor bar, linen-draped tables inside, a greenery-rich backyard patio and a special event hangar complete with chandeliers. And while you feel like you’ve been transported to a bygone era, the New American menu reimagines starters such as foie gras mousse, and entrees that include Korean barbecue short ribs, and espresso-crusted filet. The sentimental cocktail lineup also pays homage to vintage favorites Tom Collins, mojitos and the French 75, among others.

Map: 159 W. Commonwealth Ave., Chandler AZ 85225 or (480) 275-5525

1. Arrive Early for the Best Parade Views
2. Carpool and Know Where to Park in Downtown Chandler
3. Bring Lawn Chairs or Blankets to the Tumbleweed Tree Lighting & Parade of Lights
4. Explore the Holiday Fun Around Downtown Chandler

bodyHtml:
The most wonderful time of the year is almost here—and there’s no better way to kick off the season than by joining us for a Chandler tradition dating back to 1957: the 2026 Tumbleweed Tree Lighting and Parade of Lights. This year’s celebration takes place on Saturday, December 5, 2026, from 4:30–9 p.m. in the heart of Downtown Chandler and promises an evening filled with holiday cheer, family fun, and one of Arizona’s most iconic seasonal sights.

 

As you stroll through the festivities, enjoy live entertainment, arts and crafts, festival food and beverages, an appearance from Santa, and more merry moments.

 

To elevate your experience, consider making dinner reservations at a Downtown Chandler restaurant or plan a festive weekend getaway by booking a stay at one of the Downtown Chandler hotels, which will allow you ample time to explore the historic square. The magical Tumbleweed Tree Lighting Ceremony—the moment that Arizona’s only tumbleweed tree comes to life—takes place at approximately 8 p.m. and is a must-see.

 

Whether this is your first time attending or you’re a long-time fan of this storied celebration, these insider tips will help you make the most of your visit to this free, family-friendly event.

Top Tips for First-Time Tumbleweed Tree Visitors

 

1. Arrive Early for the Best Parade Views

The Parade of Lights begins at 6:45 p.m., but the most popular viewing spots fill up quickly. Savvy attendees arrive between 4:30 and 5 p.m. to secure their place along the parade route.

 

2. Carpool and Know Where to Park in Downtown Chandler

This beloved event attracts thousands of locals and visitors. To make parking easier, carpool when you can and review the Downtown Chandler Parking Map before you arrive.

3. Bring Lawn Chairs or Blankets to the Tumbleweed Tree Lighting & Parade of Lights

Make your parade experience more comfortable by bringing foldable chairs or blankets. Once you claim your viewing spot, you can settle in and enjoy the pre-parade entertainment around historic downtown.

 

4. Explore the Holiday Fun Around Downtown Chandler

Don’t stay in one spot the whole time—there’s so much to see and do!

  • Enjoy live music, dancers, and entertainment
  • Grab delicious food from local restaurants or festival vendors
  • Visit Santa’s House for photos (please note that Santa's House is closed while Santa is in the parade from 6:30 - 8 p.m.)
  • Help your kids write and decorate letters to Santa

Stick around after the parade, because the star of the night—the lighting of the Tumbleweed Tree—happens at approximately 8 p.m.

 

5. Capture the Magic & Share the Joy

Take plenty of photos to remember your evening and share your favorites on social media using #TumbleweedTree. You’ll be joining a community-wide celebration and spreading holiday cheer online.

 

Bonus Tips for First-Time Visitors

Enhance your evening with these extra suggestions:

  • Dress in layers—desert evenings can get chilly in December!
  • Bring a reusable water bottle and stay hydrated while exploring.
  • Plan ahead if visiting with young children—look for quieter viewing areas or corners near family zones.
  • Turn the event into a weekend escape by exploring Downtown Chandler, check out local shops, arts and culture, or Chandler’s top attractions.

Plan Your Visit

Visit the Tumbleweed Tree Lighting & Parade event page for additional details. To discover more seasonal happenings, explore the Chandler Holiday Event Guide and plan the perfect holiday getaway in Chandler, Arizona.

Hiking South Mountain Park and Preserve - Best for Big Views and Iconic Desert Vibes

bodyHtml:
One of the best things about visiting Chandler? You don’t have to go far to get a solid dose of desert beauty. Whether you’re up for a real hike or just want a chill walk in the sunshine, there are plenty of hiking and desert walking trails nearby—some with lakes, others with mountain views, and all of them offering that classic Sonoran desert feel.

Before you head out, make sure to take precautions, like bringing water, wearing real shoes (no sandals, trust us), and slathering on the sunscreen. You’ll thank us later.

Hiking South Mountain Park and Preserve - Best for Big Views and Iconic Desert Vibes

  • Main Entrance: 10919 S. Central Ave., Phoenix, AZ 85042
  • Pima Entrance: 9904 S. 48th St., Phoenix
  • Phone: (602) 262-7393
  • Hours: 5 a.m. to 7 p.m. (Trails remain open until 11 p.m.)
  • Fee: None

If you want sweeping views and dramatic desert backdrops, South Mountain Park is the move with more than 50 miles of crisscrossing trails. It’s actually the largest city-owned park in the country, so there’s a lot to explore.

For a solid challenge, check out the Holbert Trail. It’s a 2.5-mile climb (one way) up to Dobbins Lookout, where the views of Phoenix and the Valley are totally worth the sweat.

Just getting started? Try the Kiwanis Trail, a beginner-friendly, 1-mile out-and-back with cool stone dams from the 1930s scattered along the way.

More experienced? The National Trail runs the full length of the park (14.5 miles) with trail access from Pima Canyon near 49th Street and Guadalupe Road. You can mix and match routes for a longer hike if you’re feeling ambitious.

San Tan Mountain Regional Park - Best for Trail Runners & Desert Solitude

  • Main Entrance: 6533 W. Phillips Rd., Queen Creek, AZ 85142
  • Phone: (480) 655-5554
  • Hours: Sunday - Thursday, 6 a.m. to 8 p.m.; Friday and Saturday, 6 a.m. to 10 p.m.
  • Fee: $7 per vehicle

San Tan is a bit quieter than other spots around the Valley, and that’s part of its charm. You’ll get wide-open skies, saguaro-studded trails and that peaceful desert stillness at this regional park.

Try the Moonlight Trail (just over 1 mile) for a mellow loop that’s close to the visitor center. It’s great for a quick outing or beginner-friendly jog.

Want more? Park at Rock Peak Wash Trailhead, hike to Malpais Trail, and you’ll get a 6-mile round-trip through volcanic rock and rugged terrain.

The Goldmine Trail (2.5 miles one way) offers views from two overlooks and even passes the graves of two old miners near the north end (random, but kind of cool).

Bonus: After your hike, swing by the Arizona Fallen Heroes Memorial or check out the Desert Tortoise Habitat near the visitor center.

Veterans Oasis Park - Best for Water Views & Bird-Watching

  • Address: 4050 E. Chandler Heights Rd., Chandler, AZ 85249
  • Phone: (480) 782-2890
  • Hours: Monday - Thursday, 8 a.m. to 8 p.m.; Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.; Saturday, 8 a.m. to 3 p.m.
  • Fee: None

Right in town, Veterans Oasis Park is one of the easiest places to enjoy the outdoors without going full “hiker mode.” There are 4.5 miles of trails, including a paved loop around a 5-acre fishing lake—great for strollers, wheelchairs or just lazy Sunday strolls.

One super cool feature is the self-guided Chandler Solar System Walk. A stretch of path is lined with mini planets spaced out to scale (each step equals 1.5 million miles in space).

Head off the pavement to find butterfly gardens, hummingbird spots, elevated viewing decks, and even a little waterfall (yep, in the desert!).

The park is a birdwatcher's paradise, with more than 150 species having been spotted here. From November to April, Desert Rivers Audubon offers free, guided bird-watching tours on the first Saturday of each month.

And don’t miss the Chandler Nature Center, a great spot to learn about local wildlife or grab a fun, desert-y souvenir at the Owl's Nest Nature Store.

Paseo Vista Recreation Area - Best for Quiet Walks & Open Space

  • Address: 3850 S. McQueen Rd., Chandler, AZ 85286
  • Phone: (480) 782-2754
  • Hours: 6 a.m. – 10:30 p.m.
  • Fee: None

Once a landfill (really!), the Paseo Vista Recreation Area has been transformed into a unique park with over a mile of walking trails, a disc golf course, a dog park, an archery range, and more.

It’s perched on rolling terrain, so even though the hills are man-made, the 40-foot-high overlooks give you surprisingly great views of the East Valley.

From here, you can also hop on the Paseo Trail, which follows the Consolidated Canal. Go south for about 2 miles for a short, scenic outing. Or head north for roughly 4.5 miles if you’re looking to stretch your legs a bit more.

The paved side is perfect for walking, biking, or jogging, while the dirt path on the other side is open for horseback riding.

headings.text: Fun Things to Do with Teens in Chandler

bodyHtml:
Keeping teens entertained? It’s not always easy, but Chandler actually has lots of fun things that even the pickiest teens will enjoy. From heart-pounding adventures to some seriously good eats, Chandler’s got you covered. Here’s your ultimate guide to keeping your teen off their phone…at least for a little while.

 

Entertainment & Adventure

If your teen loves an adrenaline rush, Andretti Indoor Karting & Games is where it’s at. We’re talking high-speed go-kart racing, a cutting-edge arcade, laser tag and even VR experiences. Another great place for heart-racing fun is Slick City Chandler, where you’ll find massive indoor slides—no water involved, just straight-up sliding madness. Perfect for teens who love a good challenge (and maybe a little competition).
For something super interactive, check out Game Show Battle Rooms. It’s like stepping into a real-life game show complete with buzzers, fast-paced questions and a whole lot of laughs. If your teen is more into physical action, Big Air Trampoline Park and Taroko Sports have got you covered with trampolines, foam pits, and some intense batting cages.

 

Outdoor Fun

If your teen prefers fresh air, Chandler’s got plenty of outdoor options, too. Veterans Oasis Park and Desert Breeze Park have scenic hiking and bike trails, perfect for burning off energy. And if it’s blazing hot (which, let’s be real, it can be), head over to Mesquite Groves Aquatic Center. With water slides, a lazy river and a lap pool, it’s the perfect place to cool off and hang out. Plus, there are plenty of shaded spots for you to chill while the teens do their thing.

 

Shopping

Let’s face it, teens love to shop. Chandler Fashion Center has all the big names like H&M, Urban Outfitters, and Lululemon, while Phoenix Premium Outlets offers sweet deals on brands like Nike, Adidas, and Kate Spade. Pro tip: Give them a spending limit and let them go nuts. It’s a win-win—they’ll feel independent, and you won’t blow the budget.

 

Dining

Food is life when you’re a teen, right? Luckily, Chandler’s got some top-tier teen-approved spots.
Bella Gusto Urban Pizzeria – Wood-fired pizzas with creative toppings that hit just right.
The Taco Spot – Street-style tacos packed with flavor—cheap and delicious.
Two Hands Corn Dogs – Korean-style corn dogs with the perfect crispy crunch.
Lenny’s Burgers – Classic juicy burgers and crispy fries. Enough said.
Jeremiah’s Italian Ice – Soft ice cream layered with Italian ice—refreshing and addictive.
The Screamery – Creative ice cream flavors that’ll make them want to come back for more.

 

Arts & Culture

If your teen leans more creative, check out the Chandler Center for the Arts. They’ve got concerts, comedy shows and even theater performances—perfect for teens who love a little artsy flair.
