headings.text: Getting to Know Downtown Ocotillo in Chandler, AZ

bodyHtml:
Downtown Ocotillo, with its Santa Barbara-style buildings and tree-lined boulevards, is where the locals from Chandler and the East Valley go to eat, sip wine, and socialize. 

Whether you’re on vacation or just looking for some place new, check out one of these restaurants at the corner of Queen Creek and Price roads in Downtown Ocotillo.  

The Living Room

2475 W. Queen Creek Rd.
Chandler, AZ 85248
(480) 855-2848

A casual wine bar with padded seating and couches throughout, The Living Room is a great option for wine, cocktails, and small plates. Happy hour (Monday through Friday, 11 a.m. to 6 p.m. for drink specials and 3 p.m. to 6 p.m. for food specials) draws a crowd from nearby businesses, and when the weather is good, the patio, equipped with heaters for the winter and misters for the summer, is packed. 

Wine—served by the glass, bottle, or in one of five flights—is the drink of choice at The Living Room although the restaurant does have a selection of cocktails and beers on draft or by the bottle. The menu changes seasonally and features bruschetta, sushi, flatbread, and an extensive list of salads. Only three heartier meals are available: salmon, lamb chops, and a NY strip steak cut in-house. 

La Sala Tequila Cantina

2475 W. Queen Creek Rd.
Chandler 85248
(480) 307-9412

The flavors of Latin America come to Chandler at La Sala Tequila Cantina. The menu is simple—there’s an enchilada, a chimichanga, and a burrito offering in addition to the taco platters showcasing mesquite-grilled meats such as carne asada, brisket, chicken, pork carnitas, rock shrimp, and rock fish.

La Sala, which means “the living room” in Spanish, serves only the freshest ingredients and makes everything it can in house and only as needed. The corn tortillas, for example, are made by hand each morning using freshly ground masa from heirloom blue and yellow corn, and the guacamole is made tableside with the option to add pomegranates, onion, lime, grapefruit, jalapenos, and raisins. 

The bar offers Mexican beers, tequila and mescal cocktails, and wines by the glass to wash down your tasty South-of-the-border meal. 

Rock Lobster

2475 W. Queen Creek Rd.
Chandler, 85248
(480) 821-9000

When you step inside Rock Lobster, you’ll feel like you’ve teleported to Japan. The red walls are simply decorated, Japanese lanterns hang overhead, and steam rises from the three tables with teppan grills. Sushi is a favorite here. Try the Spicy Chandler, a mix of spicy tuna and crap, or the Santan, a roll featuring yellowtail, jalapeno, and cream cheese. 

In addition to sushi, you can order bento boxes, tempura, salads, and lettuce wraps. Or, make a reservation for a seat at the teppan grill. Teppan meals include a shrimp starter, salad, soup, steamed rice, and your choice of meat (or meats). 

Wine is available by the glass or bottle as well as Asian beers. Rock Lobster also boasts an impressive sake selection, including hot and cold options. 

CHoP Steakhouse

2625 W. Queen Creek Rd.
Chandler, 85248
(480) 821-0009

The kitchen opens every day at CHoP Steakhouse where you can savor classic dishes like shrimp cocktail, prime rib, and grilled salmon. Even though it’s one of the more upscale restaurants in Downtown Ocotillo, the restaurant serves comfort foods, too, such as slow-cooked baby back ribs, burgers, and mac ‘n’ cheese. 

Owned by the same creative team behind The Living Room, La Sala Tequila Cantina, and Rock Lobster, CHoP Steakhouse also has a great selection of wines by the glass and cocktails as well as craft beer.  If you love wine, come on Wednesday when select bottles are 1/3 off. 

Sauce Pizza & Wine

2551 W. Queen Creek Rd.
Chandler, 85248
(480) 388-3640

For a kid-friendly restaurant, try Sauce Pizza & Wine. The signature combinations such as rosemary potato and prosciutto and fig will appeal to foodies young and old, or you can build your own pizza from a list of high quality ingredients like sausage from local favorite Schreiner’s Fine Sausage. 

(Be sure to ask for the hand-stretched crust if you prefer yours thicker. Otherwise, pizzas come on the original, cracker thin crust. Gluten-free crust is also available.) 

Sauce Pizza & Wine also serves pasta, panini, and salads, and as its name suggest has an impressive selection of wines. The menu changes seasonally, especially when it comes to the salads. 

Not in the mood to go out? You can order online, and either pick up your food to go or have it delivered by Doordash Delivery, Bite Squad, or GrubHub Delivery. 

Press Coffee Roasters

2577 W. Queen Creek Rd.
Chandler, 85248
(480) 699-6239

Kick start your day or sip an after dinner brew at Press Coffee Roasters. Named the best coffee in Arizona by Food Network and awarded Best Coffee Roaster the last two years in a row (2015 and 2016) by the Phoenix New Times, Press Coffee roasts their beans in small batches and is served at some of the Valley’s best restaurants, including Binkley’s, Citizen Public House, and The Gladly. 

In addition to exceptional coffee, Press Coffee serves cold drinks. You can order cold coffee on tap, on nitro (giving it a thick head), or in a grab-and-go flask for later. For something different, try one of three flavors of kombucha from local Wild Tonic Kombucha, served on tap. Five flavors of cold pressed juice from Radish are also available.

More at Downtown Ocotillo

Besides the restaurants, you’ll find local businesses at Downtown Ocotillo, including a dentist, hair salon, insurance agency, and marketing company. Oenophiles who live in the area can take advantage of Vinum 55, a facility that will store their wine collection in a climate-controlled cellar. Vinum 55 members enjoy special tastings, wine pairing dinners, and exclusive opportunities to purchase select wines. 

Don’t want to leave Downtown Ocotillo? You don’t have to. Luxury condos can be purchased at The Cays at Downtown Ocotillo. Or book a stay at the new Home2 Suites by Hilton Phoenix Chandler hotel located across the street.

headings.text: Go Beyond the Boardroom in Chandler AZ

bodyHtml:
There’s a reason that when meeting planners seek a different experience, they turn to Chandler, AZ. Just outside Phoenix, Chandler has all the amenities, including space and accessibility, planners seek for their Arizona meeting.

Your group will feel like a big fish in the desert here. From the Visit Chandler staff to the hospitality community and down through the community at large, Chandler is as welcoming a destination as you will find. And when your group is ready for a break from the daily grind—particularly in spring or fall—this is the place to be.

Cool air can be refreshing, but nothing quite beats Chandler’s mild winter weather, filled with blue skies and sunny days. It really does feel like a breath of fresh air. That’s what sets Chandler apart from the many other fine destinations meeting planners may consider – it’s almost always sunny here.

Chandler’s more than 300 sunshiny days make it ideal for year-round activities and meetings. When the weather isn’t a restrictive factor, planners have the freedom to test the limits of their imagination. Hence, attendees walk away beaming from their experiences. You see, this won’t be the same old, typical meeting here.

Chandler invites you and your group to break the mold and go beyond the meeting room. Appointments and education are important, but memories and connections often develop in unpredictable moments during a two- or three-day stay. Dining, drinks and disrupting expectations are some of this destination’s specialties.

Play to Chandler’s strengths when planning a gathering here. Your attendees—and your boss!—will thank you for it when they see the way Chandler rejuvenates and inspires top-tier performances. Here’s why Chandler will surprise and delight at your next meeting.

Getting Here

When we say Chandler will score points before a meeting begins, we mean it. Chandler hotels are a mere 20-minute drive from Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport, with connected nonstop daily service to more than 100 domestic destinations. More than 20 airlines fly into Phoenix, making travel scheduling some of the easiest you will encounter in your planning career.

Downtown Chandler

Boutique shopping, local restaurants, Chandler breweries, and a litany of other attractions await visitors in Downtown Chandler. A night on the town can include a pub crawl, dinner at one of the more than 40 area eateries and enjoying live music at one of 14 venues, or a simple stroll around the historic square gazing at unique street art and murals showcasing the vibrant art scene. Attendees at the Crowne Plaza Phoenix Chandler Golf Resort and Hilton Garden Inn Chandler Downtown need only walk outside their hotel to start exploring. If staying elsewhere, don’t worry—downtown parking is plentiful. This is a hassle-free environment.

Go for a Ride

Depending on your group’s speed, planners have two very different types of activities to get attendees moving. Horseback riding at Koli Equestrian Center is an excellent way to enjoy Mother Nature’s surroundings here. Rides are either 60 minutes or 90 minutes and designed to accommodate any skill level or experience. This is the type of teambuilding outing that Instagram was built for.

Speed demons may prefer Radford Racing School, which puts you in the driver’s seat. Karts and race cars are available depending on the package you choose, and a 4,500-sq.-ft. event center and on-site gourmet catering are available to transition from a racing event into a reception. Corporate groups are sure to enjoy this thrilling outing.

Hit the Greens

Build in recreation time or add a charity fundraiser to take advantage of the region’s lush golf courses. The historic San Marcos Golf Course, first grass golf course in Arizona, and the lush Ocotillo Golf Club, with its striking man-made lakes and waterfalls, can be accurately described as an oasis. Beyond trading birdies and bogeys over shoptalk, the venues make for excellent settings for private corporate events.

Dine and Drink

Chandler’s food and drink scene is vibrant and delicious. Attendees will be abuzz with excitement at the award-winning microbreweries and local restaurants. SanTan Brewing Company is an authentic experience, featuring Southwestern-style ales that amp up the carbonation and taste. Craft 64 Chandler dishes out homemade pizzas and 36 local brews; The Perch Brewery lives up to its billing with 40 draught beers and tropical-inspired garden filled with rescued tropical birds.

Intimate groups will eat up an evening at Greenhouse Gardens, an urban working farm where the farmers work with a restaurant team and local chef to serve up a meal sourced from local, seasonal ingredients – much of which is grown on the premises.

The Hotels

Finding the perfect venue for your meeting is a priority for the Visit Chandler team, and rest assured, Chandler hotels offer a wide range of options to meet your taste and budget. Chandler’s largest hotels include:

  • Crowne Plaza Phoenix-Chandler Golf Resort has 249 guest rooms, 16 meeting rooms and 32,000 square feet of event space and anchors Downtown Chandler.
  • Marriott Phoenix Chandler located in Chandler’s tech corridor, the hotel features 264 guest rooms and 28,000 square feet of meeting space, highlighted by a 10,100-sq.-ft. ballroom.

  • Hyatt Place Phoenix/Chandler Fashion Center has 129 rooms and 1,456 square feet of event space between three meeting rooms.
  • Cambria Hotel Phoenix Chandler located by Chandler Fashion Center mall has 136 rooms and a 1,312 square foot meeting room.

Visit Chandler’s destination experts are committed to making your meeting a success and offer many free services to meet your planning needs. The close-knit community and combination of stellar amenities is a can’t-miss proposition. We’ve taken the hassle out of transforming a meeting into an experience, one that attendees will build on back in the office.

The results speak for themselves. We encourage you to choose Chandler for your next meeting and see how our easy-to-access destination with unusual activities and delicious cuisine will create a memorable meeting no attendee will soon forget.

headings.text: Great Places for Craft Cocktails in Chandler

bodyHtml:
Some nights call for more than just a drink; they call for a really good cocktail. Whether you’re starting your night with creative cocktails, pairing a cocktail with dinner at a neighborhood lounge like Cork & Craft, or winding down with a perfectly balanced drink at a lively downtown bar (see our Nightlife guide), you'll find plenty of spots worth checking out. Here’s our guide to some of the best places to savor a cocktail in Chandler.

 

Cork & Craft

Tucked away in south Chandler, Cork & Craft feels like one of those places you’re glad someone told you about. Built on the legacy of Wild Vine Uncorked, it blends a strong wine program with a surprisingly creative cocktail list. Drinks like the velvety Espresso Martini or a bright Blood Orange Cosmo stand out, especially when paired with their chef-driven tapas. Add in live music throughout the week and a comfortable patio, and it’s easy to settle in for the evening.

 

Miel de Agave

If you’re looking for something lively, Miel de Agave delivers. Right in Downtown Chandler, it leans into bold, agave-forward cocktails that pair well with its upscale Mexican fusion menu. Expect well-made margaritas, a deep selection of tequila and mezcal, and fun options like the Conejo Malo (mezcal, coconut puree, grapefruit juice). On nights with DJs or live entertainment, the energy really picks up, making it a solid choice for date nights or celebrations.

The Hidden House

Set inside a historic 1939 cottage, the Hidden House offers a completely different pace. It’s one of Chandler’s more charming spots to sit back with a thoughtfully made cocktail. The bar program leans into premium spirits, including Japanese whisky and rare ryes, as well as rotating draft cocktails. The French Intervention is a standout, and happy hour makes it even easier to try something new.

 

The Ostrich

For something a little more unique, head underground to The Ostrich, a speakeasy-style bar tucked beneath Crust. The menu pulls from different eras of cocktail history, so you’ll find classics like the Vesper Martini or Trader Vic’s Mai Tai done right. Tiki Tuesdays bring a rotating lineup of tropical drinks, and the Flamingo Bowl—a shareable mix of rum, gin, and citrus—is a fun way to start (or end) the night with a group.

 

The Parlay Kitchen + Cocktails

At The Parlay, the bartenders clearly take their craft seriously. The Rosemary Poppin’—finished with a rosemary smoke bubble—is one of those drinks people remember, while the Cactus Bloom leans into bold Arizona flavors. If you’re more of a classic cocktail person, they’ve got those covered, too. With live music on weekend evenings, it’s an easy place to linger.

 

The Brickyard Downtown

With exposed brick, a polished interior, and a menu designed for sharing, The Brickyard Downtown strikes a nice balance between upscale and approachable. The cocktails are thoughtfully put together and pair well with their globally inspired tapas. It’s a reliable pick for date night or when you want somewhere that feels just a little elevated.

 

SanTan Spirit House Coffee & Cocktails

SanTan Spirit House Coffee & Cocktails stands out because it makes everything behind the bar in-house. Operated by SanTan Brewing Company, this small, cozy space focuses on spirits aged right in Chandler. The cocktail menu includes multiple takes on the Old Fashioned, along with well-executed classics. It’s a great spot if you’re interested in the craft side of cocktails—and worth pairing with a brewery or distillery tour if you have time.

 

Tryst Café

At Tryst Café, the focus is on ingredients. Organic liquors, fresh juices, and locally sourced elements all play a role in the cocktail menu. Drinks feel clean, balanced, and a little lighter than what you might find elsewhere. The Mango Mule, made with jalapeño vodka and fresh lime, is a standout if you’re in the mood for something refreshing with a kick.

 

St. Amand Kitchen + Cocktails

St. Amand rounds out the list with a cocktail menu that leans creative without going over the top. Options like the Smoking Citrus or Lavender Haze bring bold flavors, while the mule variations offer something familiar. It’s an easygoing, welcoming spot that works well whether you’re stopping in for drinks or staying for dinner.

As the night wraps up—or kicks into high gear—you’ll find even more to explore in Chandler. Keep the good times rolling by checking out the Cocktails & Wine Bars guide to discover hidden gems and rotating menus featuring seasonal sips

For a broader scene, our Nightlife page highlights top spots for drinks, live music, and laid‑back patios downtown and beyond

If you’re thirsty to learn more about local craft beverages, don’t miss a behind‑the‑scenes experience at SanTan Gardens – Brewery & Distillery Tours.

And to make the most of your visit, sync your evening with fun events via the Chandler Events Calendar, spotlighting everything from live music to seasonal market happenings

headings.text: Great Restaurants Near Chandler Fashion Center

bodyHtml:
Hungry shoppers headed to Chandler Fashion Center are in luck. One of the Valley’s premier retail destinations is also home to a variety of top-notch restaurants. From an outpost of a popular sports bar to a Mexican chain from a local family, here are more than a dozen stellar restaurants near Chandler Fashion Center mall.

Cooper's Hawk Winery & Restaurant

Wine connoisseurs will adore the modern, upscale Cooper’s Hawk Winery & Restaurant. The inviting restaurant pairs their exceptional wines, which are produced and aged in Illinois, alongside a refined menu of dishes that best complement the wine. Diners will enjoy the upscale casual Chandler restaurant, its full-service bar, private barrel-aging room, and Napa-style tasting room, patio, and retail gift store. And did we mention that they offer one of the nation’s largest wine clubs? The Chandler Cooper's Hawk location also offers two private dining rooms which can be combined to host events of up to 48 people.

Map: 3325 W. Chandler Blvd., Chandler, AZ 85226 or (480) 936-7711

Feringhee Modern Indian Cuisine

This charming, fine-dining Indian restaurant features a delightful menu and a dining experience you won't soon forget. The menu at Feringhee Modern Indian Cuisine highlights northern and southern Indian dishes with a modern twist, incorporating local ingredients and global techniques thanks to its two award-winning chefs: Chef Sujan Sarkar and Chef Karan Mittal.  In addition to its creative menu that is big on presentation, the Chandler restaurant features a full bar with a cocktail menu of unique drinks infused with Indian ingredients and spices. Perfect for a date night, Feringhee features a large dining room and a private dining room for a group celebration.

Map: 3491 W. Frye Road, Chandler, AZ 85226 or (480) 534-7178

Hop Social Tavern

Oregon-based Crossroads Restaurant Group opened its very first Arizona restaurant with Hop Social Tavern. The highlight: 52 local beers on tap, from IPAs to cream ales. Can’t choose just one? Then try a beer flight featuring your five top selections. Pair your brews with locally sourced, scratch-made cuisine. Customers can pick hearty fare like fish and chips and house-made potpies, as well as sandwiches, burgers and brick-oven pizzas to enjoy in the dining room or on the patio. For fancier dining options, consider booking the chef’s table that seats eight. The elegant space features 20-foot high ceilings and even a chandelier.

Map: 3405 W. Chandler Blvd. Chandler, AZ 85226 or (480) 485-4677

The Sicilian Butcher

Located south of Chandler Fashion Center mall, The Sicilian Butcher is one of the latest offerings from the Maggiore Group (the folks behind popular haunts like Hash Kitchen and Tomaso’s Italian Restaurant). Customers can look forward to craft meatballs, handcrafted pasta and sauces and a charcuterie bar, as well as mozzarella, meat and cheese and bruschetta boards served in a modern-industrial setting or on the expansive patio. The food menu is rounded out by a selection of craft cocktails, beer and wine.

Map: 3151 W. Frye Road, Chandler, AZ 85226 or (480) 573-8550

Someburros

Thirty-plus years ago, the first Someburros opened in the Valley by the Vasquez family. Since then, the restaurant has taken pride in honoring time-tested family recipes made with high-quality ingredients. At this fast-casual eatery, diners can look forward to everything from chimichangas, quesadillas and burritos; to tacos, tostadas, tamales and enchiladas. Or try such specials as the Pollo Fundido, heaping with marinated chunks of chicken breast wrapped in a flour tortilla that’s deep-fried and topped with jalapeno cream cheese, grated cheese and green onions. Someburros also caters to early risers, who can enjoy breakfast options including the La Sonrisa, two cheese enchiladas served with beans, red or green sauce, and topped with a fried egg. The restaurant also offers a casual patio for outdoor dining.

Currently open for in-person dining or takeaway with their convenient drive-up window (orders must be placed in advance).

Map: 3461 W. Frye Road, Chandler, AZ 85226 or (480) 726-8226

Crème and Chocolats

If you’re a fan of cool treats—especially in the height of our Arizona summers—make a beeline for Crème and Chocolats, a charming, European-inspired ice cream shop and creperie located at the open-air courtyard at Chandler Fashion Center. Offering soft ice cream cones dipped in Belgian chocolates, with flavors ranging from vanilla and chocolate, to black cherry and dark sea salt. Looking for something savory? The shop also offers crepes filled with everything from ham and cheese to shrimp, crab, and a creamy rosé sauce.

Map: 3155 W. Chandler Blvd., Chandler, AZ 85226 or (623) 999-1947

la Madeleine French Bakery & Café

Founded by Loire Valley native Patrick Leon Esquerré in Dallas in 1983, la Madeleine offers diners breakfast, lunch and dinner, in addition to a wide selection of baked goods. Indulge in croissants, blueberry muffins, chocolate chunk cookies and, of course, lemon madeleines. The breakfast crowd can look forward to custom crepes and omelets, while lunch and dinner diners can dig into heartier fare like soups, salads, pastas and sandwiches. Fun fact: One of the restaurant’s signature items was a happy accident. Ten cases of Roma tomatoes were ordered instead of one and the chef had to come up with something to do with the surplus, so he created the chain’s signature (and must-try) tomato basil soup.

Currently open for in-person dining and offering curbside pickup and contactless delivery.

Map: 3605 W. Chandler Blvd., Chandler, AZ 85226 or (480) 999-2095

The Keg Steakhouse + Bar 

Leather booths and dim lighting broken by the glow of a fireplace lend an old-school, fine dining vibe to The Keg Steakhouse + Bar. The steakhouse serves dinner only that kicks off with the customer-favorite fresh and fluffy sourdough bread. Look forward to traditional steakhouse fare like ribs, steak, seafood, chicken and salads. Happy hour specials are popular among guests. Customers can nab daily drink specials on cocktails, beer and wine and order shared plates like teriyaki steak bites, tuna tacos and prime rib sliders. The Keg also features a kid’s menu and a gluten-free menu for those with dietary concerns. 

Map: 3065 W. Chandler Blvd., Chandler, AZ 85226 or (480) 899-7500

Thirsty Lion Gastropub & Grill

Perfect for a meal with colleagues or casual celebration, Thirsty Lion Gastropub & Grill features a globally-influenced scratch kitchen, cocktails, and seasonal menu alongside a hefty selection of draft beers and sports.  Diners will enjoy the expansive dining room, lively bar or dining al fresco on the patio.

Map: 3077 W. Frye Road, Chandler, AZ 85226 or (480) 786-5799

Benihana

Dinner and a show is the name of the game at Benihana, where guests are seated at communal tables to watch a hibachi chef slice and dice and fry up their meal. The five- and six-course feasts here are the stars of the show. Pick your protein—like twin lobster tails, scallops, steak and tuna—then pair it with a long list of sides including Benihana onion soup, salad, vegetables, homemade dipping sauces, steamed rice and Japanese hot tea. Customers can also enjoy sushi, sashimi/nigiri, noodles, tofu and steak/chicken. For dessert, consider the near-legendary banana tempura. 

Map: 3025 W. Chandler Blvd., Chandler AZ 85226 or (480) 812-4701

Wildflower Bread Company

Enjoy fresh food in a warm and contemporary atmosphere at this favorite Chandler spot, where diners can dig into sandwiches, salads, pastas, a kid’s menu and soup, in addition to breakfast and dinner fare. Fresh baked goods, including bread that’s made daily, are a highlight at Wildflower Bread Company. Although the cuisine rotates seasonally, diners can indulge with a variety of pies, carrot cake, cheesecake, lemon coconut cake and the ultimate chocolate cake. Pair your decadent dessert with a plethora of coffee drinks including mochas, lattes and fresh-brewed coffee.

Map: 3111 W. Chandler Blvd., Chandler, AZ 85226 or (480) 821-8200

Famous Dave’s BBQ

Known for its authentic barbecue smoked in a wood smoker with genuine hickory logs, Famous Dave’s BBQ has been cooking up award-winning (no kidding—the restaurant has won more than 700 awards to date) ribs, beef brisket and made-from-scratch items. Meats are hand-rubbed with a custom blend of spices, cooked for hours, and then finished off on the grill to create a chargrilled sweetness on the outside. Head here for big, hearty eats including fried pickles, cheese curds, barbecue nachos and wings. Entrees include ribs, burgers, country-roasted chicken, smoked turkey and smoked jalapeno cheddar sausage. 

Map: 3250 W. Frye Road, Chandler AZ 85226 or (480) 782-1212

bodyHtml:
Jeannine and Cameron McChesney have always been passionate about gardening. So when the harvest from their home garden exceeded their food needs, the couple took a leap and planted the seed for a new business opportunity.

Initially, they bought a house with an empty backyard— the perfect beta site for garden growth.

“Gardening was a super therapeutic alternative to the daily grind,” explains Jeannine, who, along with her husband, ran a graphic artist business for 17 years before venturing into full-time farming. “We were happier doing the gardening. We were able to provide food for five families. We wondered if we could scale that and decided to pursue the idea.”

They began selling their crops at the Power Ranch farmers market in Gilbert and quickly realized they needed to expand their growing footprint. In 2016, the McChesneys bought the Riggs family homestead, the first non-family members to own and farm the land since the Riggs’ purchased the property in1950.

“The whole idea was to give the community a place to see where their food was grown,” says Jeannine of Greenhouse Gardens, an urban garden, market and event venue.

You won’t find tractors or pesticides at Greenhouse Gardens, but you can purchase naturally-grown, seasonal crops including leafy greens, root vegetables, herbs, fresh-cut and edible flowers, citrus fruits and free-range chickens adopted from other farming operations at their weekly farmers market in Chandler.

“We describe it as beyond organic,” says Jeannine. “We’ve created a neighborhood space where you can get fresh, seasonal organic produce, visit the garden, see where it’s grown and talk to the farmer.”

Customers also can pick up mid-week produce boxes and visit Greenhouse Gardens every Saturday from 9 a.m. to noon to browse the farmers market that features weekly vendors and makers from Chandler including Crème de La Baa, V Roastery, Arizona Soaps and More, CM Handmade Masks & Designs and Sweet as Honey.

To help maximize their growing efforts and be able to offer a variety of produce, the McChesneys partner with Lauren and Frank Infurna, owners of La Campagna Homestead, as part of a crop planning program.

In addition, the historic, four-acre property is the perfect backdrop for hosting events such as weddings, and to showcase seasonal produce and the talents of local chefs through public dinners held in the barn.
“And, more recently smaller, intimate gatherings due to COVID,” says Jeannine.

Greenhouse Gardens has two World War II storage buildings, one that serves as a cold room for vegetables and a former migrant workers’ house used during the ranching. “It was important to maintain some of the property’s history and vintage qualities,” Jeannine explains. “It’s a unique space. We’ve put effort into keeping the property quaint and simple. At the end of the day, our focus is vegetables. It’s a wonderful space to visit and walk around and get back in touch with your neighborhood garden.”

While the McChesneys aren’t reinventing the wheel at Greenhouse Gardens, they are cultivating something important in the community.

“We’re sharing how you can grow fresh, nutritious food and pick it right here. Farmers and gardeners have been doing for this centuries. Food education inspires other people to grow and garden in their own backyard,” she says.

“We love gardening, watching things grow and feeding the neighborhood. We’re exhausted every day, but we share all the conversations we’ve had. We fuel our fire for growing our business and produce by the feedback we get from our customers.”

headings.text: Halloween Events & Activities in Chandler, AZ
Pumpkin Patches & Haunted Attractions Near Chandler

bodyHtml:
Chandler’s Halloween season brings costume parades, pumpkin crafts and trick-or-treating to your October calendar. Horror shops keep the movie monsters close, while nearby pumpkin patches and spooky attractions add pumpkin hunting and nighttime thrills.

Chandler Halloween Spooktacular

The city’s signature Halloween celebration, the free Halloween Spooktacular, takes place on Friday, Oct. 30, from 5:30 to 8:30 p.m., at Dr. A.J. Chandler Park’s Stage Plaza. All ages can enjoy the festivities, which include carnival games, trunk-or-treat stations and a spooky prize wheel. Don’t forget your trick-or-treat bag to collect all the goodies.

Youngsters 5 and under have their own Little Monsters Zone with gentle thrills and fun activities. Also give Musical Headstones a whirl, try a pumpkin sack race or check out the inflatable games. When you’re ready for a bite, you’ll find food, snacks and drinks for sale.

Come in costume and join the Catwalk Costume Parade at 6:15 or 7:30 p.m. There’s no fee or registration, and children 12 and under receive a glowing souvenir while supplies last.

Explore Chandler’s “Horror Corridor”

At the intersection of Alma School and Elliot Roads, three nearby businesses form what local fans call the “horror corridor.”

At Spooky’s Swirls, the scares come with something sweet: creepy cookies, Halloween-themed cupcakes and other gluten-free desserts set the mood. There’s also a great mini museum exhibiting science-fiction and horror movie props and wardrobe pieces.

You can also browse Terror Trader’s horror-themed toys, apparel, masks and memorabilia. More than 70 vendors contribute to the shop, including local artists, and its Crypt of Curiosities holds thrilling experiences, scary dolls and antiques.

Asylum Records continues the spooky vibe with signed movie props and collectibles on display, along with eerie décor throughout the shop.

Sweet Treats & Family-Friendly Halloween Events

Arizona’s largest candy store, Sweeties Candy of Arizona, packs nearly 13,000 square feet with sweets. Stock up on Halloween candy and shop their exclusive seasonal selection, which includes candy corn, ghost-shaped DOTS and Gummi body parts.

At Vision Gallery’s “Make and Take: Vintage Halloween Tassel,” everyone from little ones with adult assistance to grown-ups can create their own decoration to take home using miniature trick-or-treat buckets and ribbon. This free self-led activity goes from 11 a.m. to 3 p.m. on Saturday, Oct. 17. Drop-ins are welcome, though registering for a time slot helps the gallery prepare.

After dark, more than 5,000 hand-carved art pumpkins light up the Riverwalk at Rawhide. Follow the illuminated trail past dinosaurs, superheroes and pop culture characters. Glowing Pumpkins occurs on select nights from Oct. 1-31; book a scheduled ticket time and plan on about 45-75 minutes. Parking is complimentary, children 2 and younger get in free and there are no live actors or jump scares.

Family-friendly costumes fit the occasion; skip full-face masks and realistic weapons or props, which organizers prohibit. The paved trail accommodates strollers and wheelchairs.

Pumpkin Patches & Haunted Attractions Near Chandler

Queen Creek and Mesa offer additional seasonal outings beyond Chandler’s city limits. Schnepf Farms’ Pumpkin & Chili Party in Queen Creek runs Oct. 1-31, Wednesdays through Sundays. The experience combines a pumpkin patch, petting zoo, corn maze, hayrides and amusement rides. Ticket options include different activities and add-ons, so compare the packages and their details before you buy them.

Mesa’s Scarizona Scaregrounds ramps up the fright, admitting guests to three haunted attractions on one timed-entry ticket. Expect loud noises, darkness, fog, strobe lighting and a lot of intensity. Organizers do not recommend the event to children under 12. Reserve your entry slot and wear closed-toe shoes (which two attractions require). Review the official website for further guidance on what to wear and what to leave in your vehicle.

Planning Your Halloween Adventure

If an event brings you to Downtown Chandler, add dinner at Crust Simply Italian or George & Gather. For popular October weekends, reserving a table ahead of time is a smart move.

Check each event’s hours and ticket requirements, especially for attractions with assigned entry times. You might pair an afternoon of candy shopping with an evening festivity, leaving enough time for the drive if your plans take you beyond Chandler. If drinks are part of the celebration, arrange a rideshare or designate a driver. For overnight stays, compare hotels near the attractions on your itinerary.

With a little planning, it’s easy to turn a Halloween outing into a full weekend of seasonal fun and memorable experiences around the city. Gather your crew, pick a few can’t-miss activities and start planning your October getaway.

headings.text: How to Plan a Quinceañera in Chandler
Step 1: Set Your Budget, Timing, & Guest Count

bodyHtml:
A quinceañera marks a meaningful cultural milestone on a girl’s 15th birthday, celebrating heritage, faith, family, and the transition into young adulthood. Families planning this cherished event coordinate ceremonial traditions alongside budgeting, venue selection, vendor coordination, and guest arrangements. 

Chandler’s event spaces, hospitality partners, and visitor amenities support both regional families and out-of-town attendees. With thoughtful organization and early decisions, your celebration can unfold smoothly and reflect your family’s vision. This guide walks you through planning a quinceañera step by step, using trusted local resources and a realistic, easy‑to‑follow process. 

Step 1: Set Your Budget, Timing, & Guest Count 

Start with three foundational decisions: your overall investment, your preferred date, and your estimated attendance. On average, quinceañeras in Arizona range from approximately $5,000 to $20,000, though larger gatherings can exceed $60,000 depending on guest count, location, and overall service level. 

Most begin planning nine to 12 months in advance to secure venues and vendors. Establishing a clear budget early allows you to prioritize what matters most, whether that is a grand ballroom setting, elevated décor, professional photography, or a catered multi-course meal. Headcount directly impacts event facility size, catering totals, table arrangements, staffing, and transportation. Many providers charge per person, so the guest count affects the overall cost. 

Step 2: Choose Your Venue 

Selecting a venue sets the tone for the entire experience. The city offers distinctive settings that accommodate formal receptions, court presentations, and large dance floors. Families seeking a spacious event hall often consider Crystal Reception Hall, known locally for hosting large celebrations, customizable décor, and being highly accommodating to requests. 

Those envisioning a castle-inspired setting should explore The Ashley Castle, which features dramatic architecture and landscaped grounds well suited for formal entrances and portraits. Bella Rose Estate offers an elegant outdoor garden setting paired with an expansive grand ballroom, creating a seamless transition from open-air festivities to a polished indoor gathering. 

When evaluating party spaces for quinceañeras, confirm maximum capacity, available layouts, vendor flexibility, setup windows, and any included amenities such as tables, chairs, or audiovisual equipment. Touring the space in person allows you to visualize the grand entrance, father-daughter dance, and reception flow.  

.

Step 3: Book Your Core Vendors  

A skilled quinceañera photographer understands ceremonial pacing, formal portraits, and evening lighting conditions. Request full event photo collections rather than highlight reels and confirm coverage hours and photo delivery timelines. Many families also include videography to capture speeches, choreographed dances, and candid reactions that photography alone cannot preserve. 

Catering should align with venue policies and your projected guest count. Clarify how food will be served, who will staff the event, and what the menu will look like before committing. Tastings help you fine‑tune selections and confirm portion expectations. 

Music shapes the evening’s energy. DJs familiar with quinceañeras coordinate introductions, court presentations, traditional dances, and open dance periods. Review rehearsal timing and equipment needs in advance. Décor and floral design unify the event’s aesthetic. Detailed proposals should outline centerpieces, backdrop installations, lighting elements, and breakdown schedules.  

Step 4: Dresses, Attire, & Theme  

The gown anchors the visual identity of the milestone. Begin shopping well in advance to allow time for fittings and alterations. Coordinate attire for the court and immediate family, so colors complement the selected palette. Keep fabrics, dress styles, and accessories aligned with the overall theme to create a cohesive look across formal photos and key ceremonial moments.  

Schedule final fittings well before the function to ensure proper tailoring and day-of comfort. If you’re establishing a dress code for guests, such as formal, semi‑formal, or a specific color palette, communicate it clearly on invitations, so attendees can plan accordingly. 

Step 5: Finishing Touches

Successful quinceañeras rely on thorough preparation and clear day‑of execution 

Coordinate Final Logistics 

If your venue does not provide on-site event management, book a day-of coordinator long before the occasion. Confirm rehearsal times with your church and venue, and reserve any car services early if you plan to arrange a private shuttle or limo service. You can also share hotel recommendations with guests traveling from outside the area using official hotel listings.  

Additionally, Visit Chandler staff is available to assist with securing hotel room blocks for out‑of‑town attendees, helping ensure convenient accommodations for family and guests. For additional dining, shopping, and entertainment ideas, encourage visitors to explore our Things to Do in Chandler page. 

Wrap Up Details  

Use the final months to refine the details already in place. Create a written master timeline outlining important details, including hair and makeup schedules, photography, ceremony start time, formal dances, dinner service, speeches, and the cake cutting. Distribute the finalized schedule to all vendors and reconfirm arrival times. Verify staffing counts with caterers and venue representatives based on your guest total, and reconfirm transportation timing to support smooth, on‑time arrivals. 

Quinceañera Checklist 

Use this checklist as a quick reference while working through the more detailed planning sections above. 

  • Set a budget, preferred date, and estimated guest count. 

  • Reserve venue and confirm capacity, layout options, amenities, and vendor policies. 

  • Book a photographer, videographer, caterer, DJ, and décor and floral services. 

  • Select gown and coordinate court attire; schedule fittings and alterations. 

  • Hire a day-of coordinator (if needed) and verify rehearsal schedules. 

  • Secure transportation arrangements early.  

  • Offer lodging and local transportation details for traveling guests. 

  • Send invitations with adequate time for travel arrangements. 

  • Create and distribute the detailed event schedule to all vendors. 

  • Confirm vendor timing and staffing levels. 

  • Verify coordinated arrival times for the birthday girl and court members. 

For families traveling to Chandler for the celebration, have them check out our Plan Your Visit page to help ensure a smooth, well-coordinated experience.

headings.text: Late Night Dining in Chandler, AZ
Murphy’s Law Irish Pub & Ale House

bodyHtml:
It’s late. You’re hungry. Where do you go?

You don’t have to settle for a late night drive-thru run if you have the munchies in Chandler. Plenty of restaurants stay open until the clock strikes midnight—and some even much later than that. So the next time you want to chow down late at night, check out one of these Chandler restaurants.

Jolie's Place

140 W. Warner Rd., Chandler, AZ 85225
Phone: (480) 786-0436
Open until 2 a.m. daily
For a satisfying late-night meal, head to Jolie’s, a family-owned joint known for its welcoming comfort foods, including their award-winning wings. Tucked away in a cozy strip mall, this Chandler bar and grill also serves up good old-fashioned fun with such things as Texas hold ‘em, Buffalo Bills football games playing on the tube, trivia nights and pop culture bingo.

The Parlay Kitchen + Cocktails

1245 S. Price Road, Chandler, AZ 85286
Phone: (480) 500-5247
Open until 11 p.m., Sunday to Thursday; 1 a.m., Friday and Saturday
Nestled in the bustling Price Corridor, this gastropub serves a tasty mix of casual foods like burgers and sandwiches, along with hearty entrées like filet mignon and lemon rosemary chicken. If you just need a quick snack to end the night, the charcuterie board, grilled wings, deep-fried avocado and other small plates are perfect for sharing.

Good Time Charli's

6045 W. Chandler Blvd., Chandler, AZ 85226
Phone: (480) 556-1420
Open until 2 a.m. daily
While this neighborhood pub stays open until 2 a.m. every night of the week, come before 11 p.m. to dine on burgers, fajitas, salads and sandwiches. After that, appetizers like pepperoni and cheese garlic knots, and Mexican totchos (nachos made with tots instead of chips) are available until close. The restaurant also has entertainment most nights ranging from live bands to karaoke.

Sawtooth Bar & Grill

4929 W. Ray Road, Chandler, AZ 85226
Phone: (480) 753-4772
Open until midnight, Sunday to Tuesday; 2 a.m., Wednesday to Saturday. Kitchen open until 10 p.m. daily
For a cozy and welcoming late-night dining spot, make your way to this popular west Chandler bar and grill. Sawtooth brings a taste of Idaho to the desert with such favorites as finger steaks, baked potatoes and patty melts. Known for their mouthwatering wings and lively karaoke nights, it’s the perfect place to unwind with good food, good drink and good friends.

SanTan Brewing Company

8 S. San Marcos Pl., Chandler, AZ 85225
Phone: (480) 917-8700
Open until 11 p.m., Monday to Thursday; midnight, Friday to Saturday
Hungry and thirsty? SanTan Brewing Company is the perfect place to stop late at night. The brewery serves pizza, burgers, tacos, sandwiches, and a slew of appetizers along with their award-winning beers. Try the flagship Devil’s Ale, a smooth American pale ale, or Mr. Pineapple, a crisp wheat infused with fresh pineapple. 

Bourbon Jacks Bar & Grill

11 W. Boston St., Chandler, AZ 85225
Phone: (480) 664-1738
Open until 2 a.m. daily
This self-described “urban country bar” features a solid line-up of ½-pound Angus burgers, ribs, fried chicken, and sandwiches like pulled pork and smoked brisket. It’s also the home to some of the Valley’s best mac n’ cheese, made with homemade cheese sauce and topped with fried hot chicken. And, of course, there’s bourbon—140 different bourbons and whiskeys to be precise. Hear live music nightly or catch your favorite team playing on one of the bar’s large HD TVs.

Murphy’s Law Irish Pub & Ale House

58 S. San Marcos Pl., Chandler, AZ 85225
Phone: (480) 812-1588
Open until 2 a.m. daily
Reverse happy hour: 10 p.m. to close, Sunday – Thursday
The doors are open until 2 a.m. on the weekends, making Murphy’s Law Irish Pub & Ale House one of the last restaurants to close in Chandler. The late-night menu includes traditional Irish fare such as Banger on a Bun (grilled sausage in a pretzel bun), Murphy’s Chips (pub fries) and tumblers (shredded potato, cheddar cheese and bacon fried into potato balls). Enjoy nightly entertainment, including live music, karaoke and trivia events.

The Brickyard Downtown

85 W. Boston St., Chandler, AZ 85225
Phone: (480) 963-1373
Kitchen open until 9:30 p.m., Tuesday to Thursday; 11 p.m., Friday and Saturday; 9 p.m., Sunday; closed Monday
Craft cocktails and shareable plates are the focus at The Brickyard Downtown. Order a charcuterie board, pork banh mi tacos or steak skewers to share with friends as you sip an Old Fashioned or negroni. The drink menu also a wide variety of wine, beer, spirits and whiskey.

Fibber Magees

1989 W. Elliot Rd., Chandler, AZ 85225
Phone: (480) 722-9434
Open until 10 p.m. Sunday to Thursday; 1 a.m. Friday and Saturday
It may not look like much on the outside—Fibber Magees is located in a strip mall—but once you step inside, you’ll feel like you’ve been transported to an authentic pub in Dublin. On the menu is traditional Irish fare like Shepherd’s Pie as well as burgers and sandwiches. You can also chow down on potato skins, chicken tenders, wings and other appetizers. Live music play Wednesday to Saturday, with trivia events and group games on Monday and Tuesday.

headings.text: Make Chandler Your Destination for an Arizona Couples Getaway

bodyHtml:
For many couples, a romantic weekend getaway might include lounging poolside under the shade of a private cabana, a memorable farm-to-table dinner served in a charming cottage, or a hot air balloon ride floating over the desert as the sun rises in the horizon. Fortunately, you and your significant other can enjoy all this and more with a couple's trip to Chandler, Arizona. Here’s a look:

Desert Oasis

For couples looking to unwind, a luxury cabana is the perfect place to sit back, relax and let your cares melt away. If you’re looking for the ultimate poolside respite, check-in at the CAMBRiA Hotel Phoenix Chandler Fashion Center, where spacious cabanas at the resort-style pool welcome weary travelers to enjoy drinks and nibbles in between refreshing dips in the water. When you’re ready to call it a day, retreat to your spacious, modern-style guestroom, complete with luxury amenities.

Map: 3165 W. Frye Road or (480) 899-2203

Date Night

Tucked away in a quiet corner of bustling downtown Chandler, The Hidden House is where couples go to cozy up with a romantic dinner served in a charming historic cottage. The unique restaurant offers distinct dining experiences: a formal dining space, an outdoor patio and bar, and an indoor/outdoor terrace where couples can enjoy live music. The New American-inspired menu also appeals to adventurous diners with its Spanish, Italian and Asian influences, while the cocktail program provides a nostalgic nod to elegant cocktails and drinks.

Map: 159 W. Commonwealth Ave. or (480) 275-5525

Set the Mood

If you’re in the mood to groove to the soulful sounds of some of the Valley’s top entertainers, spend an evening at The Wild Vine Uncorked. The south Chandler hotspot serves up Latin-style tapas, small plates and an impressive wine list along with live music that ranges from classic rock to country to soul. Performers take the stage Thursday, Friday and Saturday nights, and play well into the evening. Check the restaurant’s website calendar for performers and start times.

Map: 4920 S. Gilbert Rd. or (480) 883-3492

Up, Up and Away

Nothing is more awe-inspiring—or romantic—than a desert sunrise. Except, perhaps, a desert sunrise seen from above, floating across the sky on a hot air balloon ride. To get your day off to an inspiring start, rise with the sun with Hot Air Expeditions, a local hot air balloon company that offers rides that offer stunning views of Chandler and surrounding areas as day breaks. After landing, celebrate with a champagne toast and hors d’oeuvres.

Phone: (480) 502-6999

Saddle Up

If you prefer to explore Chandler’s natural desert scenery from the ground and looking for a desert hike alternative, reserve a private trail ride at the Koli Equestrian Center. Suitable for both beginner and advanced riders, the ride takes you through 2,400 acres of equestrian trails on the Gila River Indian Reservation. With majestic mountains looming in the distance, you’ll be surrounded by native trees and plants, and magnificent views of the desert. For something truly romantic, however, reserve a private carriage ride for two. It’s the perfect way to enjoy the beauty and serenity of the Southwest.

Map: 6940 W. Broken Ear Road or (602) 796-3495

Market Fresh

Spend an easy, breezy Saturday morning perusing local products at the Chandler Farmers Market. Held year-round at Dr. A.J. Chandler Park West, the market features more than 30 vendors specializing in fresh-made produce and goods, including salsas, pastries, relishes, honey, tea, natural beauty products, and crafts. With more than 30 local restaurants, it's easy to enjoy a leisurely outing in Downtown Chandler. For a great date night idea, stock up on locally grown fruits and vegetables, sauces and spices from the market in the morning, and whip up a healthy and romantic at-home dinner (or in your extended-stay hotel) for two in the evening.

Map: 3 S. Arizona Ave. or (480) 855-3539

ld.articleBody: Chandler might not be the first place that comes to mind for sushi, but one good bite might change that. Over the years, the city has quietly built one of the best sushi scenes in the Valley, with everything from intimate omakase counters to laid-back neighborhood gems and creative fusion spots.

headings.text: Must-Try Sushi Spots in Chandler, AZ

bodyHtml:
Chandler might not be the first place that comes to mind for sushi, but one good bite might change that. Over the years, the city has quietly built one of the best sushi scenes in the Valley, with everything from intimate omakase counters to laid-back neighborhood gems and creative fusion spots. Whether you’re after a special night out or just a really solid roll, here are nine places worth pulling up a chair.

Shimogamo

If you ask locals where to find the best sushi in Chandler, this is usually the first name that comes up. Shimogamo has been a staple since 2003, known for its authentic approach and high-quality ingredients, some flown in directly from Japan. The chef’s background in Tokyo fine dining shows in every detail. If you can, book a seat at the sushi bar and go for the omakase. It’s the kind of experience people come back for again and again.

Address: 2051 W Warner Rd, Chandler, AZ 85224

Kodo Sushi Sake

Kodo leans modern, but without losing its roots. One of its standout touches is the use of black (forbidden) rice, which adds a slightly nutty flavor and a unique look to every roll. The atmosphere is relaxed, the sake list is solid, and the weekday happy hour is a bonus. The Arizona Roll gets a lot of love, namely for its creative use of salmon, tobiko (flying fish roe), and alfalfa.

Address: 2430 S Gilbert Rd suite 5, Chandler, AZ 85286

Hi 5 Sushi

Tucked into a strip mall, Hi 5 Sushi is easy to overlook. But regulars know better. The fish is consistently fresh, and the rolls are more creative than you might expect. It’s the kind of place people discover once and then keep coming back to. Try the Feisty Spider Roll (soft shell crab, spicy yellowtail) or the Sahara Rainbow Roll (shrimp tempura, spicy salmon, tuna, yellowtail, albacore). And if you’re into bluefin tuna, you’ll want to take a closer look at the menu.

Address: 225 W Warner Rd #3, Chandler, AZ 85225

Yama Sushi House

All-you-can-eat sushi can be hit or miss, but Yama makes a strong case for “hit.” Their menu goes beyond the usual with options like wagyu torched tableside, uni, toro, and seasonal oysters alongside the classics. The space feels modern, but comfortable, making it a good pick for everything from a casual dinner to a group night out. The Baked Lobster Roll, featuring Norway lobster meat, is one people tend to talk about long after the meal.

Address: 1175 W Ray Rd Ste 1, Chandler, AZ 85224

Mikado Sushi

A longtime South Chandler favorite, Mikado has been around since 2002. And for good reason. It’s dependable in the best way. Under new ownership since 2023, the restaurant has kept its reputation intact while bringing in a little fresh energy. They use premium Koshihikari rice and follow the Japanese principle of omotenashi, or thoughtful hospitality. If you’re looking for value, the daily (except Sunday) happy hour (3 to 6 p.m.) is worth timing your visit around.

Address: 3125 S Alma School Rd #3b, Chandler, AZ 85248

Nozomi Sushi House

One of the newer additions to the area, Nozomi has quickly found its footing. It’s family-owned, personal, and focused on freshness. A nice touch: if there’s a specific fish you’re craving that’s not on the menu, you can call ahead and they’ll order it for you. Start with the Hamachi Kama (grilled yellowtail collar with ponzu) and go from there.

Address: 4955 S Alma School Rd #4, Chandler, AZ 85248

Mido Sushi

Mido has been a west Chandler go-to since 2006, and it’s easy to see why. The atmosphere is relaxed, the service is consistent, and the sushi speaks for itself. There’s no flash here, just solid execution and a loyal customer base. The Pancho Roll (shrimp tempura, avocado, cucumber and crunchy topping) is a reliable favorite.

Address: 5965 W Ray Rd, Chandler, AZ 85226

Gosan Poke & Roll

Can’t decide between sushi and poke? Gosan makes it easy. This family-owned Korean-Japanese spot lets you mix and match, building a poke bowl alongside fresh rolls. Portions are generous, the ingredients are fresh, and the vibe is casual. Pair a classic salmon bowl with the Spicy Shaggy Dog Roll (spicy tuna, shrimp tempura) and you’re set.

Address: 2875 W Ray Rd Suite 3, Chandler, AZ 85224

Maguro Sushi & Ramen

Balancing sushi and ramen on the same menu isn’t easy, but Maguro pulls it off. With more than 15 years of experience in the kitchen, the quality shows in both the fish and the presentation. It’s also a great place to slow down a bit, especially if you grab a seat outside when the weather’s nice. A bowl of miso ramen with a side of salmon nigiri makes for a seriously satisfying lunch.

Address: 3855 W Ray Rd # 6, Chandler, AZ 85226

Eastwind Chandler

Located in Downtown Chandler, on the north side of the historic square, Eastwind is the neighborhood sushi spot everyone wishes they had nearby—comfortable, casual, and delicious. With its Kaiten-style conveyor belt, it's perfect for those who enjoy sampling a little bit of everything at their own pace. Plates glide by, offering a mix of classic and creative rolls, and the quality is surprisingly high for such a laid-back setup. The atmosphere is fun, approachable, and consistently reliable. And if you see the Eastwind Roll passing by, be sure to grab it, but don't forget to check out the rotating nigiri selections on the belt. Whether you're stopping in for a quick lunch or enjoying a leisurely dinner, Eastwind makes sushi feel easy and enjoyable.

Address: 58 W Buffalo St, Chandler, AZ 85225

A great sushi meal is just the start of what Chandler has to offer. If you’re hungry for more, you can keep exploring the city’s dining scene, from local favorites to hidden gems that go far beyond sushi. Pair your meal with a craft beer from one of Chandler’s breweries, dive into the city’s lineup of events and attractions, or start mapping out your next visit with the official Chandler Visitors Guide. It’s all here waiting for you, and it’s easier than ever to plan your perfect trip.

bodyHtml:
Chandler may be thousands of miles from the bustling streets of Ho Chi Minh City or the picturesque beaches of Da Nang, but the city’s Vietnamese restaurants bring a true taste of this special place right to your plate. Whether it’s a delicious bowl of pho, banh mi filled with flavor, or light and refreshing spring rolls, you’ll enjoy authentic Vietnamese cuisine at these Chandler restaurants.

Pho Chandler

One of the most popular Vietnamese restaurants in the East Valley, Pho Chandler serves 13 different types of pho, a traditional Vietnamese soup made with a rich broth, rice noodles, herbs and meat. For the ultimate pho experience, try the House Pho-nomenal, a combination of sliced eye of round, brisket, flank, tendon, tripe and beef meatball. Other authentic dishes include the spring rolls, crispy rice crepe and papaya salad for starters, as well as noodle, rice and stir-fry dishes.

Map: 4055 S. Arizona Ave. #8, Chandler 85248 or (480) 895-9090

Saigon Pho & Seafood

While this popular Chandler restaurant may have a hefty menu filled with a wide variety of Vietnamese dishes, it’s the seafood that makes it so special. Offering live lobster and live crab, you can choose such dishes as the Saigon special (available with either lobster or crab), the lobster with ginger and onion, the lobster or crab with salt and pepper, or the sweet and sour crab. More authentic dishes include the whole fish (steamed or pan fried), clam with basil leaf, sautéed shrimp with black pepper, and the salt and pepper squid.

Map: 1381 N. Alma School Road, Chandler 85224 or (480) 786-8828

Pho Cyclo

Named for the three-wheeled, hooded passenger vehicle pedaled by drivers in Asia, Cyclo takes a fresh, modern approach to traditional Vietnamese cuisine. Chef/owner Justina Duong has a keen eye for design, which she infuses in the menu. The result is an eye-catching assortment of dishes that are filled with the tastes and aromas of Vietnam. Begin with the ginger green mussels with basil, follow with the Hanoi rice vermicelli (grilled pork, sausage, herbs, sweet and sour fish sauce), and end with the heart-shaped sticky rice dessert with mango and coconut milk.

Map: 1919 W. Chandler Blvd. #2, Chandler 85224 or (480) 963-4490

AZ Pho & Grill

Serving more than just pho, vermicelli and rice dishes, AZ Pho & Grill offers so much more, including a menu of stir-fried specials and soups made with egg and rice noodles that are thicker than what you’d find in traditional pho. Feast on the stir-fry with lemongrass-turmeric sauce, made with chicken, shrimp or fried tofu. Or if you’re feeling especially adventurous, try the crab paste noodle soup filled with minced shrimp, tofu, crab paste and tomato. With two locations in Chandler, you’re never too far away from some of the most unique and authentic Vietnamese dishes in the Valley.

Map of Location 1: 3140 S. Gilbert Road #1, Chandler 85286 or (480) 802-5356

Map of Location 2: 885 N. 54th St. #5, Chandler 85226 or (480) 825-7767

Lee’s Sandwiches

Considered the go-to spot for banh mi in Chandler—or shall we venture to say Arizona—Lee’s has been serving Vietnamese sandwiches for 40 years. Founder Chieu Le opened his first shop in San Jose, California, in 1980 and, since then, has brought his unique concept to Texas, Oklahoma, Nevada, Oregon, Utah and, of course, Arizona. When it comes to fillings, pork is king, from pork meatball, shredded pork and pork roll, to cured pork and barbecue pork. Other options include grilled chicken, sardine and vegetarian.

Map: 1901 W. Warner Road Suite 8, Chandler 85224 or (480) 855-1778

Urbanh Café

Also serving up hearty banh mi sandwiches is Urbanh Café, named for the iconic Vietnamese delicacy. Served on a crispy baguette, choices include such favorites as chicken, grilled pork and pork sausage. For something out of the ordinary, try the Sunny Side Up, made with three fried eggs, pickled carrot and daikon, veggies and their house special sauce. The pork belly is also a must-try, thanks to its filling of Chinese barbecue char siu-style pork belly. Whatever you choose, wash it down with a refreshing tea, from milk and flavored to fresh fruit and sea salt.

Map: 2015 N. Dobson Road #9, Chandler 85224 or (480) 248-6859

Fu Belly

Family owned and operated, Fu Belly is a welcome addition to Chandler’s Asian dining scene thanks to its playful menu offerings. Here you’ll find shareable appetizers like spring rolls, dumplings and papaya salad, as well as pho and noodle soups, and rice bowls. Standouts include the garlic parmesan noodles made with egg noodle stir-fried with garlic, butter and parmesan cheese and served with house jalapeno sauce; and the Vietnamese curry, featuring yellow curry served with potato, onion, bell pepper and carrot. End your meal with Vietnamese donuts or ice cream. Better yet, a donut-and-ice-cream combo!

Map: 5055 W. Ray Road #8, Chandler 85226 or (480) 306-6692

KimThao’s Bakery and Food To Go

Part bakery, part market, part take-out eatery, KimThao’s is owned by Kim Tran and Thao Nguyen, friends who decided to open a unique concept serving ready-made Vietnamese soups, sandwiches, tofu dishes and desserts. Genuinely authentic, popular items include Banh Cuon Cha Lau (pork mince rice rolls) and the Dau Hu Chien Sa Ot (lemongrass chile tofu). But what you’re really here for are the desserts. While availability may change, offerings have included steamed banana cake, tofu pudding and mung bean dessert.

Map: 2050 N. Alma School Road, Chandler 85224 or (480) 687-9132

bodyHtml:
New Year’s Eve in Chandler brings together exceptional dining, entertainment, and a nightlife scene that keeps the energy high well past midnight. You can plan a refined evening out or dive into a lively countdown with friends, with plenty of options to welcome 2026 in your own style. From Downtown Chandler restaurants to live music venues and performing arts, this guide highlights reliable places to enjoy a memorable celebration while exploring the best of Chandler nightlife.

Chandler Restaurants to Spend New Year's Eve 2025

A strong New Year’s Eve starts at the table, and our restaurant scene has options that feel celebratory without seeming forced.

Cuisine & Wine Bistro

Cuisine & Wine Bistro in south Chandler, remains a favorite for special occasions thanks to its polished ambiance, French-inspired menu, and carefully curated wine list. Enjoy an exclusive three-course menu with your choice of starters from a savory puff pastry, lamb lollipop, escargot, or salad; entrees from filet mignon, lobster tail wellington or duck breast; and tasty desserts. It is a natural starting point for couples or small groups seeking an elevated dinner before heading further into the evening.

Address: 4991 S. Alma School Rd., Chandler AZ 85248

Feringhee Modern Indian Cuisine

Celebrate the new year with delicious Indian cuisine in and elevated fashion. For those guest looking for an elegant relaxing dinner before late night celebrations, Feringhee Modern Indian Cuisine is offering a four-course Golden Hour Supper from 5 p.m. - 7 p.m. for $75 per person starting off with a welcome Prosecco, amuse bouche, and your choice from select appetizers. For the main dish, choose from authentic offerings such as pan-fried fish curry, on-the-bone goat curry, spiced soya chaap, Portobello mushrooms, or a cottage cheese sandwich all served with garlic naan and green pea pulao. Save room for dessert and choose between the masala chai tiramisu or the ragi chocolate brownie. If you're looking for an all-night experience, The Midnight Reserve also offers the four-course dinner with a much larger celebration for $85 per person. From 8 p.m. to midnight, savor on unlimited cocktails with your evening meal while enjoying in-house music and a special Prosecco toast at midnight.

Address: 3491 W. Frye Rd., Chandler AZ 85226

The Brickyard Downtown

The Brickyard in Downtown Chandler combines bold flavors with an energetic vibe that eases the transition from dinner into more vibrant nightlife. This New Year’s Eve enjoy a four-course, prix-fixe dinner starting your meal off with a complimentary amuse bouche. For your first course, you'll choose from the tempura cauliflower, mushroom toast, or squash & goat cheese dumplings. With your second course, choose between a green goddess salad or miso & maple salad. The third course includes a choice of scallops, short rib, or duck breast. Closing out your meal with the fourth course, your dessert features a choice between cinnamon & golden raisin cobbler or yuzu cheesecake. Prices are based on your course selection with additional cost for cocktail pairing. Reservations are required.

Address: 85 W. Boston St., Chandler AZ 85225

After dinner, Downtown Chandler becomes the heart of the celebration. Walkable streets connect bars, breweries, and live music venues, allowing the evening to unfold naturally.

The Perch Brewery

Those who prefer live music and an immersive setting will find an even more energetic celebration at The Perch Brewery, where craft beer meets all‑night New Year’s Eve festivities. Make it a full evening here and enjoy a three-course New Year's Eve dining experience at this craft brewery located in Downtown Chandler. Indulge in your choice of crisp apple & arugula salad or Chef's garden salad to start. Main course options include a 12oz prime rib, grilled aji amarillo shrimp, or frenched pork chops, followed by desserts for $59.99 per person. Reservations are required and includes access to the rooftop NYE party. Guests can ring in 2026 with music, dancing, and a midnight champagne toast, all set against the brewery’s unique backdrop featuring its signature exotic bird sanctuary. Tickets are sold separately starting at $10 pre-sale online for the party.

Address: 232 S. Wall St., Chandler AZ 85225

Clark's Countdown Chaos NYE Party

For a more elevated experience, The Living Room and Sea & Smoke in Downtown Ocotillo are hosting Clark's Countdown Chaos NYE Party. Imagine celebrating the night away with a New Year's Eve, Grisworld style pop-up party featuring passed appetizers, live music by Lisa Hightower & Her Band from early evening until midnight, a DJ taking over after the countdown, and a midnight champagne toast. With so many ways to celebrate, now is the perfect time to secure your plans. These experiences fill quickly every year, so be sure to make your reservations soon and welcome the new year exactly the way you want. Tickets are required and cost $100 per person.

Address: 2475 W. Queen Creek Rd., Chandler AZ 85248

Live Entertainment in Chandler for New Year's Eve 2025

All About Broadway: A New Year’s Eve Celebration

On the big night, Chandler Center for the Arts presents "All About Broadway: A New Year's Eve Celebration," a high‑energy showcase that fills the theater with favorite show tunes, powerhouse vocals, a live orchestra, and plenty of pre‑midnight excitement. Kick off the new year with musical performances, a champagne toast, photo ops, balloon drop, and party favors. It’s the perfect option for anyone who wants to welcome 2026 with big voices and that unmistakable Broadway-style magic right here in Chandler. Tickets range from $34, to $44 and $54.

Address: 250 N. Arizona Ave., Chandler AZ 85225

Pratt Brothers New Years Eve 2026 Celebration

Kick off your 2026 celebrations with the Pratt Brothers New Year's Eve party at Rawhide. This event puts on a fantastic light show, along with other entertainment activities including parades, train rides, stunt shows, and more! Stick around till 10pm for a New Year's Eve countdown and their famous Boot Drop. Tickets start at $33 with the option to purchase packs.

Address: 5700 W. North Loop Rd., Chandler AZ 85226

Plan Your Perfect Celebration

The best New Year’s Eve plans balance flexibility with intention. Start with a memorable dinner, choose one or two nightlife stops, and leave room for discovery. Downtown Chandler's walkability makes it a breeze to adjust plans on the fly while staying close to the action. For lodging options, transportation tips, and help crafting an itinerary that fits your ideal getaway, visit our Plan Your Visit page and start mapping out your celebration in Chandler.

headings.text: Peixoto Coffee: Crop-to-Cup in Chandler, AZ

bodyHtml:
There’s a reason you don’t hear much about crop-to-cup coffee shops, according to Julia Peixoto Peters—only a handful exist in the United States, and Peixoto Coffee in Downtown Chandler is one of them. Not only does Peixoto Coffee, pronounced “Pay-sho-tow,”  roast and brew its own beans but it sources them directly from the farm, something very few coffee shops are able to do. 

“Some people say they are crop-to-cup, but they only do two of the three things—source, roast, brew,” she explains. “We’re one of the few that does all three.”

Peters admits she does have a bit of an advantage, though—the beans come from her family farm in Brazil. 

“Coffee has been in my family for the last four generations, at least 150 years,” she says, adding it almost ended with her parents, who wanted her and her siblings to pursue well-paying, professional jobs. After watching her parents struggle with the fluctuations in the coffee market, it didn’t take much convincing.

She accepted a scholarship to study law at the University of Arizona in Tucson, graduated in 2002, and went to work as an attorney for DHL in Phoenix, always intending to return to Brazil at some point to practice there. Then, she met and married Jeff Peters, and returning was out of the question, especially after they had two children.

Occasionally, her thoughts turned to the family farm, though. She realized unless she acted, the Peixoto legacy was in jeopardy after her father retired because her siblings weren’t interested. Even so, she had no definitive plans to get involved with the family business until her grandfather died. Then, she says she had her “ah-ha” moment.

Spurred into action, she and Jeff began acting as distributors of the family’s coffee beans, selling them green to roasters in the United States. But, they quickly realized it didn’t make financial sense to just distribute the beans. Jeff had already been experimenting with roasting the beans they brought home from family visits to Brazil. Why not roast the beans themselves first, then distribute them?

From that point, it only seemed natural to open their own coffee shop. Peixoto Coffee served its first cup in January 2015.

“The more we looked into it, the more we were sucked into the whole process of crop-to-cup,” she says. 

Look closely when you visit, and you’ll find reminders of the family farm and crop-to-cup concept throughout the shop. Hanging above rustic shelves of bagged coffee for purchase near the entrance, a sign reads, in part, “Our Peixoto coffee is grown with over 100 years of family tradition.” On the opposite wall, a white outline of North and South Americas is painted on bricks; small placards reading “crop” and “cup” represent the location of the family farm and the coffee shop.

The vibe here also reflects life on the Peixoto farm. Although people do order coffee to go, most choose to linger, spending time with family and friends at tables inside the coffee shop or on the patio just as the Peixoto family gathers with loved ones over fresh cups on the farm. 

“It took me many years to realize what we had in Brazil was very special,” Peters says. Behind her, business associates hash out ideas, moms with strollers exchange parenting tips, and a couple on a date hold hands in the coffee shop.

Whether at the family farm in Brazil or Peixoto Coffee in Chandler, coffee brings people to the table. The coffee served matters, though. Peters grew up drinking a brew made simply from hot water poured over the ground beans without sugar. When she came to Tucson to study, she was astonished by how Americans drank their coffee—loaded with artificially flavors, sweetened to dessert intensity, and often topped with a thick cap of whipped cream. 

Instead, Peixoto Coffee serves coffee-forward drinks, so while you can still get a cappuccino or latte, you won’t find iced caramel macchiatos or white chocolate mochas on the menu. That’s not to say Peters doesn’t like to get creative. Peixoto Coffee’s seasonal menu includes options such as Cascara Cider, a spiced dried coffee cherry tea with fruit juices, and an Espresso Tonic, a shot of espresso poured over the house-made tonic. 

The coffee shop was also the first in the Valley to offer nitro coffee, fresh brew dispensed from a tap like a beer. With its rich, creamy mouthfeel, it’s reminiscent of a Guinness beer but without the hops or alcohol. 

Everything at Peixoto is made from scratch and sourced locally, Peters says. The half and half comes from a local dairy, and they make their own syrups, such as vanilla and toasted coconut, instead of using the bottled stuff you find behind the counter at other shops. And, of course, the coffee beans are roasted in-house. 

The concept of local and fresh carries over to the food they serve. All baked goods are brought in daily from local providers, including Phoenix Public Market, Welcome Chicken + Donuts, La Dolce Vita Biscotti, Bubby Goober’s Baked Goods, and Tracy Dempsey Originals. What doesn’t sell is removed from the case at the end of the day—Peixoto Coffee never holds product to resell the next day, and it never freezes leftovers to sell later. 

On Sunday mornings, from 8 a.m. until noon, pop-ups in the back of the shop offer more substantial fare like fresh egg dishes and pancakes. Past pop-ups have included Curbside Crepes, Casa Reynoso, and Honey Sugar Bakery dishing up a Brazilian breakfast. (Check out  Peixoto Coffee’s Facebook page to learn which pop-up will be there next Sunday.)

In addition to the pop-up Sunday breakfasts, the coffee shop also holds classes on what goes into making a cup of coffee, how to appreciate quality coffee, and how to make your own drinks. (Check Facebook for the next class.) 

Peters believes the class is one of the best ways to truly appreciate the crop-to-cup experience at Peixoto Coffee, but you’ll taste the difference even if you only have the time to grab a cup and go while visiting Downtown Chandler.
