headings.text: Top Vegan-Friendly Spots in Chandler AZ

bodyHtml:
To appeal to a health-savvy diner, many family-friendly Chandler restaurants are going beyond adding a simple veggie burger to their menus. Instead, they’re offering very inspired and creative vegan dishes that even the most die-hard, animal-protein lover will find hard to resist.

The Kind Bean

Kindness matters in life. It also matters in business, say the husband-and-wife owners of Kind Bean, a neighborhood café that has been serving Chandler since 2017. Self-proclaimed foodies and vegans, Clay and Jen Novick offer a variety of organic coffees, specialty drinks, grab-n-go breakfast and lunch options, and handmade sweets baked daily using organic flours, sugars and other ingredients when possible.

Standouts include the hummus bruschetta toast topped with house made hummus, sweet tomatoes, garlic, basil and Himalayan sea salt; and the green chile corn chowder made with creamy coconut milk, potatoes, corn, green chile, onions, carrots, celery and spices.

Map: 1020 E. Pecos St., Chandler AZ 85255 or (480) 726-8300

Ruchi Indian Cuisine

For the ultimate vegan experience, Ruchi Indian Cuisine delivers. The 100%-vegetarian restaurant offers a vast array of menu items from southern India, many of which are vegan and gluten-free. House specialties include the Gobi Manchurian, a deep-fried cauliflower sauteed with garlic, ginger chili and soy sauce; and the Chana Batura featuring puffy bread served with chickpea curry.

A visit to Ruchi wouldn’t be complete without having a taste of their dosa, a thin crepe made from lentils and rice. There are a whopping 20 varieties to choose from, some filled with potatoes and onions; garbanzo beans and spices; or mint, cilantro and spices. Wash it down with a mango lassi, available in a vegan-friendly, dairy-free option.

Map: 2051 W. Warner Road, Chandler AZ 85224 or (480) 786-3333

Nana’s Kitchen

Contrary to popular belief, soul food doesn’t need to be all chicken, catfish or pork chops. Just ask the good folks at Nana’s Kitchen, where their version of down-home cooking brings a vegan-friendly twist to some of the classics. Must-try dishes include the Wangz Trio Platter, featuring fried cauliflower tossed with lemon pepper, buffalo, and barbecue sauces; and the Ultra Meeesy Fries, made up of potato French fries, jackfruit, salsa and Nana’s own “magic sauces.”

For the ultimate taste of Southern hospitality, you can’t go wrong with Nana’s Soul, offering your choice of barbecue fried cauliflower, fried “chicken” or plant-based ribs, collard greens, mac ‘n cheese, and baked beans. End your feast with a serving of heart-warming peach cobbler.

Map: 777 N. Arizona Ave., Chandler AZ 85224 or (480) 963-9490

Tryst Café

Located in way-down-south Chandler, Tryst Café aims to please diners of all kinds. That’s because the café offers a wide variety of options for breakfast, lunch and dinner (we counted more than 100), many of which are created specifically for the vegan diner.

Get your day off to a good start with the banana quinoa pancakes or the Asian jackfruit bowl, made with warm quinoa, chickpeas and jackfruit tossed in a chipotle peanut sauce. For lunch or dinner, try the kale wrap filled with hummus, kale, spring mix and vegetables; the hemp seed tamale topped with roasted poblano and corn sauce; or the house made sweet potato veggie burger. Served open faced, the patty is made with sweet potato, chickpea and oat, and is served on non-GMO wheat bread with a side of avocado and red pepper aioli.

Map: 4205 S. Gilbert Road, Chandler AZ 85249 or (480) 656-1011

Flower Child

At The Shoppes at Casa Paloma, Flower Child Chandler brings peace, love and an enlightened menu of bowls, grains, greens and wraps and lemonade, kombucha, and organic wine and beer to generate good vibrations.

While most of the menu is vegetarian-friendly, vegan dishes are generously peppered throughout. Try the Ginger Miso Crunch salad, or the Glow Bowl, made with spicy sweet potato noodle, bok choy, shiitake mushroom, coconut milk and sunflower butter. Vegan entrees are plentiful and include the butternut squash “risotto,” Indian spiced cauliflower, and the red chile glazed sweet potato. Make it a sweet ending with the vegan chocolate pudding.

Map: 7131 W. Ray Road, Chandler AZ 85226 or (602) 834-0070

Start Planning Your Chandler Jazz Festival Weekend Getaway

bodyHtml:
While April is commonly known for "showers" that "bring May flowers", here in Chandler it signals the time of year for the annual Chandler Jazz Festival. This festival brings in 4-days of live jazz music filling the streets and main stage in Downtown Chandler and is the perfect opportunity to plan a weekend getaway.

Get inspired by this jazz-filled weekend itinerary and start planning your getaway to Chandler.

Your Nearby Chandler Stays

Two hotels anchor Downtown Chandler, with the convenience of a quick walk to jazz festival performances and over 40 local restaurants, shops, and entertainment. Whether you’re planning a romantic getaway for two or a spring break family adventure, Chandler offers comfortable hotels located just minutes away from the festival grounds.

A Resort Getaway

Looking for a resort-style stay for a relaxing 4-day weekend? The Crowne Plaza Phoenix Chandler Golf Resort is the perfect hotel to unwind with a cocktail while laying out by the pool after or even before a day of live jazz performances. Enjoy resort amenities along with convenient access to Downtown Chandler's brimming dining scene, shopping, and nightlife.

An Urban Escape

Find stylish modern rooms with an on-site grill & bar at the Hilton Garden Inn Downtown Chandler. This hotel is a great place to stay with walkability to vibrant mural art, Downtown Chandler's local shops & restaurants, and the Jazz Festival activities.

Explore more lodging options on the Visit Chandler hotels page.

Must-Try Dining Spots Before & After the Festival

Kick Off with Breakfast

Start the day off strong with breakfast or brunch favorites around Downtown Chandler. From hearty breakfast plates to coffee and mimosas, Chandler has a variety of options to choose from no matter how you like to kick off your day.

  • George & Gather, an award winning spot, offers a healthy alternative to the breakfast & brunch scene with seed oil-free dishes and great options for other dietary restrictions. Their market breakfast is available Monday - Friday, but make sure to come back and try their brunch offered both Saturday & Sunday with mimosas and Bloody Marys to pair with your meal.
  • Downtown Chandler Cafe and Bakery is the perfect spot if you're looking for a grab & go breakfast. Here you'll find a large selection of freshly baked pastries including their popular jumbo cinnamon rolls, croissants, danishes, and muffins along with classic breakfast favorites that can also be enjoyed in their cozy dining area.
  • Maple House offers a both a modern coffee shop by morning and a wine, beer, and spirits spot by night. Enjoy your favorite morning sip along with a pastry outside on the patio.

Discover more morning spots on the Visit Chandler Breakfast & Brunch guide.

Afternoon & Evening Favorites Downtown

Fuel up and keep your energy going throughout your Chandler Jazz Festival weekend with a variety of nearby cuisine options. Whether fine dining or a casual eatery is your style, Chandler is no stranger to great lunch and dinner spots.

  • SanTan Brewing Company is a favorite among locals and is known for it's locally crafted beer and spirits. The Downtown Chandler location is the perfect place for a cold drink paired with flavorful pub-style plates that can be enjoyed inside their lively dining room or out on their patio.
  • Hidden House offers the perfect blend of upscale and patio dining in the heart of Downtown Chandler. This spot offers an intimate dining experience with a chef-driven menu featuring modern American dishes and craft cocktails.
  • Craft 64 is a highly ranked pizzeria, known on the national level for their delicious, made-from-scratch pizzas. Enjoy your favorite style pizza pie along with one of 30 different beers on tap.
  • Acqua Di Mare is a unique Italian restaurant offering dinner with a European tableside cooking experience. Here you'll find fresh flavors from Italy paired with fine wines in a cute and intimate atmosphere. This dining experience fills up fast, so be sure to make a reservation before heading out.

Explore more local places to eat on the Visit Chandler local restaurants dining page.

Explore More Around Chandler

While the Chandler Jazz Festival performances span throughout April 9-12, 2026, there are so many things to do in Chandler in between the concert schedules. Discover exciting attractions, entertainment, and more things to add to your weekend getaway plans.

Desert Adventures

If you're looking to get out and enjoy a little bit of Arizona's nature during your visit, you'll want to check out these unique desert experiences.

  • KOLI Equestrian Center offers guided horseback rides through the Sonoran desert where you can venture through the desert landscape and possibly even catch a glimpse of wild horses roaming nearby.
  • Veterans Oasis Park is a 113 acre park featuring a beautiful lake surrounded by scenic desert trails, with a variety of wildlife and outdoor recreation to explore.

Energizing Fun

Whether you're a thrill seeker or looking for a little bit of fun for everyone on your weekend getaway, there are plenty of Chandler attractions offering memorable experiences all-day (or night) long.

  • Andretti Indoor Karting & Games has lots of thrilling entertainment in store where you can zip around multi-level go-kart tracks, immerse yourself in VR, venture through a two-story laser tag arena, and so much more.
  • Taroko Sports is the perfect spot for sport lovers, with high-tech batting cages, 5D racing simulators, and basketball challenges as just some of the notable favorites at the West Chandler location.
  • Round1 Bowling & Arcade offers a blend of exciting entertainment including bowling, popular Japanese claw machines, classic arcade games, karaoke, and even more for you to discover at their location in Chandler Fashion Center.

Retail Therapy

Discover locally owned shops in Downtown Chandler where you'll find the perfect souvenirs to take a little bit of Chandler home with you.

  • d'Vine Gourmet is a boutique shop with a variety of locally hand-crafted artisan products including their signature caramels & candies, wine, gifts for everyone on your list, and more!
  • Copper Brim Hat Co. offers a unique shopping experience where you can customize your very own hat to add to your wardrobe. Shoppers can choose from a flat brim, western-style cowboy, or trucker hat to personalize with accessories and engravings that suit their style.
  • Downtown Chandler Farmers Market is held on Saturdays from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m in the spring and is the perfect opportunity to shop dozens of local food vendors and artisans all in one spot.

Start Planning Your Chandler Jazz Festival Weekend Getaway

For more itinerary inspiration, check out our 2026 visitors guide and start planning your Chandler Jazz Festival weekend getaway now. There's always more to explore in Chandler!

headings.text: Ocean Blue Caribbean Restaurant and Bar

bodyHtml:
Along Interstate 10, West Chandler makes an ideal base for those who want to explore Chandler, Arizona and beyond. Whether you are here for a business trip or looking for an Arizona vacation, West Chandler offers excellent access to award-winning hotels, diverse dining, regional attractions and major sports venues.  If you are coming for business, be sure to extend your business trip and bring the family for a mini getaway the whole family will enjoy.  

West Chandler Hotels

Whether you intend to stay in the area or visit some of the best attractions in metropolitan Phoenix, you’ll have your choice of excellent properties in West Chandler. For a good night’s sleep (on a plush Serta Posturepedic bed, mind you), book a stay at Sonesta Select Phoenix Chandler. Or get cozy at the DoubleTree by Hilton Phoenix Chandler, where you’ll receive a warm chocolate chip cookie at check-in.

Hampton Inn & Suites Phoenix Chandler-Fashion Center combines the convenience of being close to the second-largest mall in the Phoenix metropolitan area, with the comfort of full suites. Similarly, Homewood Suites by Hilton Phoenix Chandler Fashion Center is also a stone’s throw from the mall and has a complimentary social hour in the evenings. Staybridge Suites Phoenix-Chandler features all this and more, plus laundry facilities.

Other West Chandler options are available, too, but make your reservations early during the high season in the winter and especially in March, which is peak travel season. 

Restaurants in West Chandler

You don’t have to leave West Chandler for a mouthwatering meal. Fleming’s Prime Steakhouse & Wine Bar makes any night special with its dry-aged beef, fresh seafood and vegetarian options. Pair your entrée with premium wines by the glass as you dine inside or on the patio.

Looking for something different? Ocean Blue Caribbean features flavorful Jamaican dishes like jerk chicken, curry goat and saltfish, but it also serves more familiar fare like burgers. Don’t miss the craft cocktails made with fresh juices for a taste of the islands without leaving Chandler.

Access to Sports

A hotel stay in West Chandler, keeps you close to all the sports, from NHRA National races at Wild Horse Pass Motorsports Park to cheering on the local soccer team, at USL’s Phoenix Rising FC stadium. Both are located a few minutes south of West Chandler.  Within a short drive, sports fans will find easy access to all four major professional leagues: The NFL’s Arizona Cardinals, MLB’s Arizona Diamondbacks, NBA’s Phoenix Suns and NHL’s Arizona Coyotes. 

Family fun in West Chandler

West Chandler delivers, especially when it comes to family fun. At the Ice Den Chandler, lace up rented ice skates and take a spin around the rink on designated public skate days (advanced reservations required.) Or climb, bounce, jump and test your balance at Rush Xtreme. Kids will have a blast at Makutu’s Island, an indoor play area with towering trees, climbing nets and dark caves. There’s even a bungee jump and a 35-foot slide.

Take advantage of Chandler’s beautiful weather while you have the chance and spend a day at Desert Breeze Park. In addition to a playground and splash pads, the park features a one-third-scale locomotive that loops around the park. After a ride in one of its open-top cars, ride a 1950s-era carousel, stroll around the lake, enjoy a picnic or a reflective moment in the Hummingbird Habitat.

Regional Attractions

Enjoy an afternoon of shopping at one of Chandler’s largest outdoor shopping malls. The Shoppes at Casa Paloma hosts local fashion and home décor boutiques, national favorites, and number of eateries in an upscale center along the western side of I-10 at Ray Road.

Plan a visit to the breathtaking Desert Botanical Garden in Phoenix. Whether you are looking for a stroller-friendly day with the family, or a place to enjoy the outdoors – the garden, located in Phoenix, is a short drive from West Chandler and home to thousands of species of cactus and flora from around the world.

Located by the garden, is another great outdoor attraction not to be missed, The Phoenix Zoo, the nation’s largest, privately owned non-profit zoo. The zoo offers fun activities year-round including animal encounters and experiences and seasonal events including their beloved ZooLights which brings millions of twinkling lights, animal lanterns and music for a memorable holiday event from November to early January.

bodyHtml:
From horseback riding to exploring the Sonoran Desert, you can experience what makes the West so unique when visiting Chandler, Arizona. No cowboy boots required.

Go horseback riding

What’s more Western than riding a horse across a saguaro-studded desert? At KOLI Equestrian Center, wranglers guide you through the Gila River Indian Community Reservation, sharing its rich history and pointing out desert plants along the way. It’s not uncommon to see jackrabbits, quail, and even wild horses from the saddle, so keep your eyes open.

KOLI offers group and private rides for all experience levels. However, because the desert terrain is so uneven, all group rides are kept to a walk. Feel free to break the nose-to-tail formation usually enforced on trail rides, though. KOLI lets you ride alongside others in your group.

Map: 6940 W. Broken Ear Rd., Chandler, AZ 85226 or (602) 796-3495

Hike through the Sonoran Desert

To appreciate the West’s beauty, you’ll want to spend some time exploring the Sonoran Desert. Chandler and the East Valley have countless trails. In Chandler, stroll 4.5-miles of trails through arid landscapes and lush wetlands at Veterans Oasis Park, or connect to the 315-mile Maricopa Trail at Paseo Vista Recreation Area. Click here for more ideas of where you can hike in Chandler and the East Valley.

Before you hit the trail, be sure to dress appropriately and wear closed-toe shoes. You’ll also want to apply sunscreen, even in winter, and take more water than you think you’ll need. Learn more about hiking safely in the desert here.

Spot wild horses

Wild horses, thought to be the descendants of horses brought to the area 300 years ago, thrive along the Salt River in the East Valley, and if you’re lucky, you can see them. You’ll have the best chance spotting them by renting a kayak from nearby Saguaro Lake Guest Ranch and paddling downriver.

If you’d rather see them from the back of a horse, the ranch also offers horseback riding. Or you can see the wild horses roaming the Gila River Indian Community Reservation on a private trail ride with KOLI Equestrian Center.

Take flight

For a new perspective on the Sonoran Desert, book a hot air balloon ride. At lower altitudes, you may see a rabbit, coyote, deer or javelina. At higher altitudes, you’ll gain an appreciation for how vast—and ruggedly beautiful—the desert is. The experience begins with the inflating of the balloon and end with a champagne toast.

While most balloon companies launch north of Phoenix, Aerogelic Ballooning lifts off south of the Valley and often flies over Chandler, Arizona.

bodyHtml:
In the southwest, tamales are synonymous with the holiday season. Featuring a steamed corn dough, masa, filled with a variety of meats, vegetables, and chiles, the tamales are wrapped and steamed in corn husks and often topped with a spicy sauce.  These delicacies are a real labor of love involving many hours and many hands to get the job done. But if you’re craving tamales for your holiday meal - we have great news for you – you can Choose Chandler and support local by ordering your tamales from these Chandler Mexican restaurants.

 

We’ve put together a list of Chandler restaurants that offer tamales by the dozen, from roughly Thanksgiving through New Year’s. But don’t worry, these restaurants also offer tamales year-round on their menu, making it a snap to satisfy your tamale craving any time of year. 

 

Please note that availability and pricing are subject to change. Most restaurants require a minimum of 48-hour notice for large orders.

Carolina's Mexican Food

While Carolina's may be best known for having amazing, and HUGE, fresh tortillas - they also serve up a wide selection of traditional-style Mexican food. Closed on Sundays, the Chandler restaurant features tamales by the platter with two options, red beef or green corn. Carolina's tamale platters come with 30 tamales, start around $85 and require a minimum of 24-hours advance notice. 

 

Map: 1972 N Alma School Rd., Chandler, AZ 85224 or (480) 493-1020

Elmer's Tacos

Just north of Downtown Chandler is a family-owned and operated restaurant, Elmer's Tacos which opened in Chandler in 1974. The Chandler Mexican restaurant has been serving great, authentic Mexican food for generations. Every year, Chandler residents and visitors can hardly wait for the holiday season to place their order for their pork tamales. For the 2025 holiday season, Elmer's offers two options for purchase, red chili or elote (corn) tamales. The tamales are $30.00/dozen and Elmer's offers many additional platters to complement your meal, including the Chip 'n' Dip Pack - featuring house-made chips and your choice of three dips. Tamale orders should be placed at least 48-hours in advance.

 

Map: 355 N Arizona Ave., Chandler AZ 85225 or (480) 963-6763

La Ristra New Mexican Kitchen

Located in Downtown Chandler, La Ristra brings its classic, New Mexican cuisine to Chandler featuring New Mexican Chile harvested from the Hatch Valley farms of New Mexico.  Diners can enjoy a tamale any time of year as an entree, but during the holiday season, the family-owned restaurant offers their scratch-made tamales by the dozen. They're rolled, filled, folded, steamed, frozen, and ready for pick-up. Choose from their red chile beef or green chile corn for $35/dozen or mix it up and order half of each. The tamales are fully cooked, ready to reheat and available while supplies last! Order online at this link. 

 

Map: 140 N Arizona Ave., Chandler AZ 85225 or (480) 590-0002

Someburros

Order Someburros’ authentic tamales from one of their family-owned and operated Chandler locations and spread Christmas cheer with tamales by the dozen. The Chandler restaurant sells tamales by the dozen for $46 or complete tamale platters featuring 15 full-size red chili beef tamales with red sauce or 15 vegetarian green chili and cheese tamales with green sauce and cheese making it a breeze to cater your holiday meal. These delicious tamale platters are traditionally crafted with house made corn masa and ordered ahead of time by contacting the location of your choice, ordering on Someburros.com, or emailing catering@someburros.com. Tamale orders must be placed at least 24 hours in advance.

 

Dine in at a Someburros location or visit one of their Chandler drive-thrus to order tamales as a meal or savor the tamale combo plate with a tamale, taco, rice, and beans.  

 

All tamale menu items and the tamale platters are available during the holidays and year-round.

Location near Chandler Fashion Center: 3461 W. Frye Road, Chandler AZ 85226 or (480) 726-8226

Location in South Chandler: 5095 S. Gilbert Road, Unit 1, Chandler AZ 85249 or (480) 597-6043

Valle Luna Mexican Grille

Whether you choose to order them by the dozen to cater a large meal at home or as an entree while dining waterfront at the Chandler restaurant, you’ll find these delicacies year-round at Valle Luna Mexican Restaurant.  Select from their classic shredded beef and pork blend or the flavorful green chile and corn for a meatless option, $42.00 per dozen. 

 

Map: 1949 W Ray Road, Chandler AZ 85224 or (480) 786-3100

bodyHtml:
Sing, Sip & Shine with the Ultimate Guide to Chandler’s Karaoke Nightlife

Looking to turn your night out into a full-blown performance? Whether you're a karaoke veteran with pipes to impress or just want to have fun with friends over cocktails and catchy tunes, Chandler, Arizona, has your next mic-drop moment covered. From low-key local bars to private karaoke suites and even live-band karaoke, there's a spot for every mood and music lover.

 

And if karaoke isn’t your thing? No problem. Chandler has plenty of live music venues where you can kick back and vibe without ever touching a mic. Check out our guide to live music in Chandler for adult-friendly entertainment to help you unwind after dark.

 

Let’s explore the best places in Chandler to sing your heart out and enjoy the nightlife scene!

Quick Look: Where to Find Karaoke in Chandler, AZ

Private Karaoke Suites in Chandler AZ

  • The Forum Lounge - Upscale, stylish, and trendy

  • Round1 Bowling & Arcade - Chandler Fashion Center - Fun, family-friendly with an adult twist

Classic bar Karaoke in Chandler AZ

  • Dirty Blonde Tavern - Energetic, neighborhood vibe

  • Stadium Club - Sports-themed fun, local feel

  • 480 Neighborhood Bar - Chill, neighborhood vibe

Traditional Karaoke in Chandler AZ

  • Good Time Charli's - Casual, neighborhood vibe

Live-band Karaoke in Chandler AZ

  • Rebel & Rogue - Rockstar Experience in Downtown Chandler

 

Rock Out in Style at The Forum Lounge

If you’re the type who prefers your karaoke with a side of glam, check out The Forum Lounge, located within The Forum Complex, offering some of the best private karaoke rooms in Chandler. Think mood lighting, touchscreen song selectors and, yes, bougie cocktails. It’s a solid pick for birthday parties, a girls’ night, or even a “let’s pretend we’re a band” kind of group hang. Grab some flatbreads or sliders, warm up those vocal cords, and get ready to belt it out like it’s your Grammy moment. This is Chandler karaoke with VIP energy.

 

Belt It Out at Round1 Bowling & Arcade

Round1 Bowling & Arcade Chandler inside Chandler Fashion Center is a karaoke playground. You get private suites and options to bowl, shoot pool, or crush it in the arcade. It’s a full-on night out under one roof. Order up some wings or mozzarella sticks between sets and recharge before diving into your next power ballad.

Insiders Tip: Open late, till 2 a.m.

 

Local Bar Energy at Dirty Blonde Tavern

Dirty Blonde Tavern is where you go for that classic karaoke vibe—just you, a mic and a local bar full of enthusiastic strangers and probably a few regulars who really own their go-to song. The energy’s rowdy, the drinks are cold, and the vibe is pure fun. Come ready to cheer people on and maybe discover your new favorite duet partner.

Insiders Tip: Check their weekly karaoke schedule.

 

Good Times, Good Vibes

Good Time Charli’s lives up to its name. It’s casual, lively and known for hosting a solid night of karaoke in West Chandler. Their Mexican Totchos have a bit of a rep—crispy, spicy, excellent. Grab a drink, flip through the songbook and get your moment in the spotlight. No judgment here, just good vibes.

Insiders Tip: Karakoe is usually on weekends.

 

Game On, Mic On at Stadium Club

Stadium Club brings karaoke into the sports bar zone. With wall-to-wall TVs, pool tables and a crowd that’s there to have fun (and maybe shout-sing some Journey). Their beer list is long, their nachos are loaded, and their playlist? Packed with throwbacks and bangers. It’s a low-pressure, high-fun kind of place.

 

Chill, Sing, Repeat at 480 Bar

Chandler's 480 Neighborhood Bar is your go-to for low-key karaoke fun. It’s cozy, the crowd is cool, and the playlist stretches from ’80s power ballads to the latest pop hits. If you’re a little nervous about getting on stage, this spot’s a great entry point. Order a whiskey and Coke, snag a table and get ready for some unexpected magic.

 

Rockstar Mode: Activated at Rebel & Rogue

Ready for something unforgettable? Rebel & Rogue offers live-band karaoke - yes, actual musicians backing you up while you sing. It’s as epic as it sounds. Whether you’re a confident vocalist or just want to feel like a star for five minutes, this Downtown Chandler place is a must.

bodyHtml:
Pie lovers, rejoice! Pi Day, which takes place on March 14 (as the date mirrors the first three figures of the symbol π) is almost here! Whether you’re planning to celebrate with a sweet pie, savory hand pie, or even a pizza pie, there are plenty of places around Chandler to recognize this fun and quirky holiday. Here are just a few:

 

Pie Snob

With three Valley locations, Pie Snob in Chandler, goes above and beyond the usual flavors with a rotating menu of pies that includes caramel apple, razzleberry crumb, and butterscotch, while still offering favorites like apple crumb and key lime, sold by the pie or slice. If you can’t decide, you can opt for the Frankenpie, which features six slices of any pie flavors on the weekly menu. Pie Snob also offers all your favorite flavors in mini, four-inch versions, perfect if sharing isn’t an option!

 

PIEfection

PIEfection prides itself on having pies made with the best ingredients made fresh, in-house every day. Their team makes everything from scratch, from their fruit fillings to the fresh whipped cream, and sources the best ingredients such as Belgian chocolate, apples from Washington state, and wild blueberries from Maine. There are also 70 variations of pie, including vegan versions (upon request) and gluten-friendly pies.

 

No pie list (and no Pi Day!) is complete without mentioning pizza pies, one of the best loved foods in the country that’s perfect for celebrating 3/14.

Craft 64

Craft 64 is a downtown Chandler favorite that has a dozen pizza options, including the Honey Bee with mozzarella, parmesan, pepperoni, jalapenos and honey; the Uovo white pizza with mozzarella, parmesan, ricotta, spinach and bacon, topped with two eggs; and a rotating specialty pizza. Make any pizza your own with their assortment of toppings that range from beef meatballs to smoked onions.

 

Bella Gusto Urban Pizzeria

Bella Gusto is the go-to for authentic Neapolitan pizzas with a creative twist. If you just can’t choose between pasta and pizza, get a taste of both with the Cacio e Pepe pizza topped with fresh mozzarella, parmesan, butter, pecorino Romano and black pepper. Or keep it simple with the Mary Margherita topped with fresh mozzarella, basil, and sliced garlic.

 

Crust Simply Italian

Crust Simply Italian offers all the classic pizzas, from a New York-style with shredded mozzarella to a supreme with pepperoni, sausage, bell peppers, mushroom and black olive. Thick crust lovers rejoice because every variety can be made Sicilian style. Go all out with one of their Sicilian-style specialties, like the Big John topped with extra cheese, extra sauce, meatballs, pepperoni and sausage.

Dive Deeper into Chandler’s Culinary Scene

bodyHtml:
Chandler, AZ, boasts a thriving culinary scene, and its array of Indian restaurants promises a rich and diverse dining experience. Whether you favor warm, earthy tandoori dishes, robust biryanis, or fragrant curries, there’s a variety of flavors awaiting your taste buds. Discover some of the best Indian food in Chandler to help you find your next favorite meal.

Bawarchi Biryanis

Biryani lovers won’t want to miss this Indian restaurant. The boneless chicken biryani and chicken dum biryani stand out for their layers of fragrant basmati rice and perfectly spiced poultry. Other popular menu items include Chicken 65, a tangy and spicy fried chicken appetizer, and the flavorful gongura goat curry. Bawarchi’s casual ambiance is perfect for dining in, and there is a take-out option if you prefer. 

Biryani Pot

Biryani Pot specializes in hearty portions of India’s signature rice dish alongside a variety of curries and tandoori options. Its goat biryani, cooked with tender, marinated meat and aromatic spices, is a crowd favorite. The family-friendly atmosphere and attentive service make this one of the top Indian restaurants in Chandler. With ample seating, it’s perfect for large groups, and they also offer catering for special events. Reservations are recommended, especially on busy weekends.

Feringhee Modern Indian Cuisine

Feringhee Modern Indian Cuisine stands out as Arizona's only fine-dining Indian restaurant, reimagining traditional Indian dishes with a contemporary flair. Unique offerings like Feringhee’s Fish Curry and Kashmiri Lamb Chops are delightful delicacies, while the Kerala fried chicken showcases the chef’s creativity. The sleek, modern decor adds to the upscale vibe, making it a perfect venue for date nights and special occasions. Reservations are recommended for this popular dining spot. 

Ruchi Indian Cuisine

Ruchi Indian Cuisine enhances traditional recipes with a touch of creativity. Signature dishes like Gobi Manchurian, a deep-fried cauliflower recipe, and Aloo Panak are big hits, and diners consistently praise the perfectly soft and buttery naans. Vegetarians will appreciate options like Bisi Bele Bhath and the hearty vegetable biryani. The restaurant’s elegant yet relaxed setting makes it suitable for casual meals and celebratory gatherings. Ruchi also offers to-go options. 

New AZ India Gate

New AZ India Gate offers a diverse menu spanning North and South Indian cuisines, ensuring there’s something for everyone. Highlights include lamb, chicken, and beef vindaloos simmered in a Kashmiri-seasoned gravy, as well as a variety of Tandoori specialties cooked to perfection in clay ovens. Mango Kulfi, an Indian-style ice cream, is a must-try dessert. The restaurant’s warm, welcoming ambiance and friendly service make for an enjoyable dining experience. For those on the go, takeout options deliver the same high-quality flavors as dining in. You may want to come at lunchtime for a buffet-style feast.  

Turmeric Grocery

A blend of grocery store and eatery, Turmeric Grocery brings authentic Indian street food to Chandler. The samosas receive rave reviews, while the biryanis and roasted goat dishes are popular choices. The casual setup is perfect for a quick bite, and the adjacent grocery section offers a variety of ingredients for those looking to recreate their favorite Indian dishes at home. Turmeric Grocery is a unique destination for Indian food in Chandler, combining dining and shopping in one convenient spot.

Woodlands Vegetarian South Indian Kitchen

Woodlands Vegetarian South Indian Kitchen is a paradise for vegetarians and South Indian food enthusiasts. Its dosas, including the Mysore Masala Dosa with a spicy chutney spread, are unparalleled. The uttapams, a thicker, pancake-like dosa, offer a nice alternative to the thin, crispy version, and you’ll find a nice selection of curries on the limited but tasty menu. The warm and inviting atmosphere, paired with a focus on fresh and authentic ingredients, makes Woodlands a standout choice. Catering services are also available, making it an excellent option for gatherings and celebrations.

Dive Deeper into Chandler’s Culinary Scene

When you’re craving a flavorful journey packed with aroma, spice, and variety, Chandler has you covered. Traditional recipes blend seamlessly with modern culinary innovations in the city’s vibrant food scene, offering something to satisfy every palate. Dive into our Indian spots and discover all the delicious dining options Chandler has to offer!

bodyHtml:
Let’s be honest. Few foods inspire loyalty quite like a great burrito. Whether you’re team breakfast burrito, all about carne asada, or always asking for extra salsa, Chandler’s got you covered with burritos worth going out of your way for. From drive-thru classics to sit-down spots where burritos come big and bold, here’s your guide to where locals (and in-the-know visitors) head for burritos done right.

Rita's Burritos

Rita’s is all about doing burritos right: simple, fast and full of flavor. This south Chandler gem is known for its hearty breakfast burritos and classic fillings like chipotle pulled pork, carne asada, and bean and cheese, all wrapped in fresh, house-made tortillas. Rita’s is a grab and go kind of spot, making it quick and easy to get your meal.

Address: 4040 S Arizona Ave #17, Chandler AZ 85248

Carolina's Mexican Food

Carolina's Mexican Food brings a Valley favorite to Uptown Chandler, and the star here is the tortilla. Handmade throughout the day in 12- and 15-inch sizes, these tortillas wrap around fillings like red or green chile, machaca, and beef chorizo to create burritos that are warm, pillowy and packed with comfort.

Address: 1972 N Alma School Rd, Chandler AZ 85224

The Taco Spot

Best known for their birria tacos, The Taco Spot’s burrito menu is just as crave-worthy. Think birria, surf-and-turf, juicy chicken, and carne asada—bold, satisfying and made for serious appetites. With two locations—one in West Chandler near I-10, and the original location just east of Downtown Chandler—it’s always close when a burrito craving hits.

West Chandler Address: 885 N 54th St Suite 3, Chandler AZ 85226
Original Chandler Address: 698 E Chandler Blvd Suite B, Chandler AZ 85225

Valle Luna Mexican Restaurant

Set along the water in the Boardwalk at Andersen Springs development, Valle Luna offers a relaxed, family-friendly atmosphere with Sonoran-style favorites. It’s a great pick for classic burritos, casual patio dining, and generous portions that keep everyone full and happy.

Nando’s Mexican Café

A longtime south Chandler staple, Nando's delivers comfort food in a laid-back setting. From smothered burritos to simple bean and cheese, the menu hits all the favorites. With a roomy dining space and welcoming patio, it’s easygoing, reliable and always satisfying.

Address: 1890 W Germann Rd, Chandler AZ 85286

Moreno’s Mexican Grill

Known for their Sonoran hot dogs, Moreno’s Mexican Grill also serves up standout burritos: carne asada, pork adobada, chile verde, and more. With three Chandler locations (North Chandler, Airpark Area, and South Chandler), it’s an easy, no-fuss choice for flavorful, comforting Mexican food that locals love.

North Chandler Address: 601 N Arizona Ave, Chandler AZ 85225
Chandler Airpark Area Address: 2100 S Gilbert Rd, Chandler AZ 85286
South Chandler Express Address: 4981 S Arizona Ave, Chandler AZ 85248

Someburros

A longtime Valley favorite, Someburros specializes in Sonoran-style dishes made from family recipes—and the burritos are the stars. Hearty, bold and reliably tasty, they’re easy to grab at either Chandler location (one near Chandler Fashion Center, one in South Chandler).

Chandler Fashion Center Area Address: 3461 W Frye Rd, Chandler AZ 85226
South Chandler Address: 5095 S Gilbert Rd Suite 1, Chandler AZ 85249

Burrito Express

Burrito Express is a local legend, known for oversized burritos packed with perfectly seasoned meat, rice and cheese. A great spot for both breakfast burritos and mid-day cravings. Feeding a whole crew? Order a burrito box filled with four, six and even 12 times the yum!

Address: 985 W Elliot Rd #6, Chandler AZ 85225

Los Favoritos Taco Shop

Fast, casual and always satisfying, Los Favoritos is beloved for its hefty burritos, no-fuss vibe, and salsa bar that lets you customize every bite. The carne asada and ground beef options are especially popular. Visit a location in South Chandler or near Dobson Rd & Chandler Blvd.

South Chandler Address: 4850 S Gilbert Rd # 8, Chandler AZ 85249
2nd Chandler Address: 1900 W Chandler Blvd #18, Chandler AZ 85224

Maskadores Taco Shop

Maskadores brings serious flavor and personality. Case in point, the Bandera Wet Burrito, an extra-large tortilla filled with your choice of protein, rice, beans, lettuce, cheese, and sour cream, covered in red sauce, green sauce and cream. It’s a great pick when you’re craving something bold and different in South Chandler or North Chandler.

South Chandler Address: 3140 S Gilbert Road, Suite #3, Chandler AZ 85286
North Chandler Address: 2100 W Chandler Blvd, Suite 38, Chandler AZ 85224

Elmer's Tacos

Elmer's Tacos keeps it simple and satisfying with classic Sonoran flavors served fast. Burritos are straightforward, filling and always fresh—perfect for lunch on the go or a no-fuss dinner. Pro tip: Try the hot and spicy grilled chicken burro. You’ll thank us later.

Address: 355 N Arizona Ave, Chandler AZ 85225  

Taqueria Factory

One of Chandler’s newer go-tos, Taqueria Factory has earned a quick following with its flavorful grilled meats, house-made salsas, and well-balanced burritos. With two locations in town (one north of downtown, the other in the Ocotillo area), it’s an easy and delicious stop.

North Chandler Address: 55 E Ray Rd, Chandler AZ 85225
Ocotillo Address: 1155 W Ocotillo Rd Ste #1, Chandler AZ 85248

bodyHtml:
Chandler, Arizona, is a vibrant community known for its warm hospitality, local flavor, and lively social scenes. When it comes to gathering with friends, colleagues, and fellow fans for a major game day, this city truly delivers. From laid-back neighborhood bars to energetic sports grills and breweries with plenty of screens, you’ll find the perfect spot to enjoy all the action, whether it’s national football playoffs, basketball, soccer, golf and more.

 

Whether you’re visiting Chandler for the weekend or have an open evening, here are some of the best places to grab delicious food, enjoy icy drinks, and watch multiple TVs featuring the day’s biggest matchups.

 

Top Sports Bars & Grills in Chandler

 

DTC Sports Grille

A standout downtown favorite, DTC offers an elevated twist on classic pub fare, multiple big screens, and plenty of room to gather with friends while cheering on your favorite team.

Location: 55 W Chicago St, Chandler, AZ 85225 or (480) 397-1380

 

Lucky Lou’s American Grill

A local favorite for watching sports, Lucky Lou’s is known for its comfort-style food and dog-friendly patio, making it a popular choice for both national and international sporting events. 

Location: 3245 W Ray Road #7, Chandler, AZ 85226 or (480) 814-1400

MVP Sports Bar and Grill

This lively, casual spot features big screens everywhere, a full drink menu, and a fan-friendly vibe that makes every game a celebration. The expansive dog-friendly patio at MVP also includes outdoor games for everyone to enjoy. 

Location: 980 E Pecos Road Suite #5, Chandler, AZ 85225 or (480) 935-2537

 

Sidelines Grill

A local favorite, Sidelines offers classic bar bites and numerous TVs showcasing the day’s featured match-ups—ideal for groups of friends looking for a spirited scene. 

Location: 2980 S Alma School Road #2, Chandler, AZ 85286 or (480) 792-6965

 

Stadium Club

This traditional neighborhood bar pairs cold drinks with darts, trivia, and karaoke, all while broadcasting sports on TV, making the Stadium Club a perfect spot for a relaxed game-day experience. 

Location: 940 N Alma School Road #109, Chandler, AZ 85224 or (480) 963-3866

 

The Trophy Bar

Known for its fun atmosphere and large video wall, The Trophy Bar in Downtown Ocotillo offers refreshing drinks, delicious food, and a community feel that brings crowds together on game day. For major sporting events, this upscale sports bar often features a lively party atmosphere, making it a popular choice among sports enthusiasts. 

Location: 2551 W Queen Creek Road, UNIT 4, Chandler, AZ 85248 or (480) 590-3595

 

Brews – a Taphouse and Gourmet Burger Joint

With two locations in Chandler, Brews is perfect for craft beer lovers and burger fans alike. This relaxed venue combines a welcoming vibe with plenty of screens, ensuring you catch every play. 

South Chandler Location: 2040 S Alma School Road #12, Chandler, AZ 85286 or (480) 590-3901 

West Chandler Location: 5055 W Ray Road #2, Chandler, AZ 85226 or (480) 284-6320

 

More Ways to Enjoy the Day in Chandler

Chandler isn’t just about bars; its local breweries, patios, and casual eateries offer plenty of options for enjoying the day. Many of Chandler’s breweries have big screens and ample space to hang out with a cold, local brew in hand.

 

If you’re visiting with family or friends and prefer a more relaxed experience, consider grabbing a bite to eat while watching from an outdoor table or fire pit seating at one of Chandler’s many gastropubs. The city’s dining scene is rich with options, so you’re never far from great cuisine alongside the spirited energy of game day.

 

Insider Tips for Enjoying a Great Game Day in Chandler

  • Arrive early: Popular sports bars and grills fill up fast on busy game days.
  • Make it a package: Pair your outing with activities like shopping, brewery tours, seasonal outdoor events or many of the top things to do when in Chandler.
  • Ask about specials!  Many local bars offer food and drink  deals during major games that are worth checking out before you go!

headings.text: Why Chandler AZ is Your Small Meeting Headquarters

bodyHtml:
Chandler is the perfect choice for your small meeting. The city is teeming with optimal spaces to host your meeting and when the day is done, you can retreat to one of the area’s many hotels, enjoy top-notch dining, or enjoy the local arts scene. Plus, Chandler offers easy access to Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport, making it ideal for out-of-state business travelers. Here are just a few more reasons why Chandler is a great place to host your next meeting or an epic team-building event.

Hotels

From a full-fledged Arizona resort to a hotel that’s mere steps from the city’s largest mall, Chandler is home to hotels to meet your every need. For a true taste of Arizona, book a room at the full-service Crowne Plaza Phoenix Chandler Golf Resort. Open since 1912, this is the Grand Canyon state’s first golf resort. Besides luxe resort amenities like a heated pool and spa, this resort is just steps away from all the action in Downtown Chandler—giving all who stay there easy access to downtown shops and restaurants.

The Marriott Phoenix Chandler offers state-of-the-art meeting spaces, expert event planning services, and cutting-edge technology to ensure your gathering is productive and professional. Located near top Chandler employers and local attractions, the Chandler AZ hotel provides convenience and comfort for both local and out-of-town attendees and is home to Chandler's largest ballroom.

The Hilton Phoenix Chandler hotel offers a prime location near leading Chandler employers and blends modern amenities with attentive service. 

The contemporary Courtyard by Marriott Chandler Fashion Center provides guests with easy access to the plethora of shops and restaurants that Chandler’s largest mall—Chandler Fashion Center—offers.

In south Chandler, the  Residence Inn Phoenix Chandler/South offers a boutique, lakeside setting that is perfect for small board meetings and strategy sessions in their intimate boardroom.  The hotel is set in the Downtown Ocotillo district and less than a three-minute walk to a few local restaurants and bars for an easy, off-site dinner.

Meeting Venues

From one of the city’s cultural gems to an elegant private two-acre space, Chandler offers a variety of spaces where you can host your next meeting. For a truly spectacular venue, consider The Chandler Center for the Arts, where theaters and foyer are available for meetings of all kinds. The 800-seat Mainstage theater can seat a maximum number of 1,500, while the 350-seat Hal Bogle Theatre is perfect for a smaller gathering. The foyer space can accommodate as many as 350 and comes complete with soaring ceilings and grand chandeliers for a refined feeling.

The Avion Center in Chandler offers a professional and stylish setting for small corporate meetings, featuring modern amenities and flexible spaces for weekday meetings. The Chandler conference center can accommodate up to 300 people depending on selected seating arrangements.

Although typically used as a wedding venue, the two-acre private Bella Rose Estate offers elegant meeting space. The indoor, 5,000-square-foot Grand Ballroom can seat as many as 300. Attendees can mingle outside and admire the lush setting that includes two waterfalls, five fountains, and fragrant flower beds.

Dining

One of the best parts about traveling for a meeting is getting a chance to check out new restaurants—and in Chandler, a top-notch restaurant is always nearby. Feast on wood-fired Neapolitan pies at Bella Gusto Urban Pizzeria or dig into classic American fare like steaks and prime rib at DC Steak House. Tip: Dine under the stars for an upscale patio dining experience.

Outdoor Recreation

When the working day is done, Chandler offers plenty of outdoor recreation activities. If your way of winding down is catching a glimpse of one of our fine feathered friends, Veterans Oasis Park is one of Arizona’s premier birding sites. Walk the 4.5 miles of paved trails here, and see if you can spot over 150 bird species that call this place home. For a brisk stroll or jog, check out the Consolidated Canal in east Chandler and tackle the 6.5-mile Paseo Trail featuring a 10-foot wide concrete pathway. Or saddle up and take a guided horseback ride at the KOLI Equestrian Center, where you’ll ride through sweeping desert landscapes.

Arts & Entertainment

Chandler is home to a vibrant art and culture scene that visitors can enjoy. The Chandler Center for the Arts offers a plethora of cultural experiences. See top acts like Australian rock band, Men at Work and watch dynamic shows like “STOMP” a sophisticated percussion sensation and browse the 2,000-square-foot Gallery at CCA featuring rotating work from regional and national artists in mediums ranging from textiles to ceramics.

Located in City Hall, the Vision Gallery is a fine arts gallery that showcases the work of more than 300 regional artists. Exhibits rotate frequently, giving visitors the chance to see new works whenever they visit. Learn more about the city’s rich historical roots and see rotating regional and national exhibits when you visit the Chandler Museum, located near Chandler Fashion Center mall which is also conveniently located near many Chandler hotels.

headings.text: 10 Wine Bars and Tasting Rooms to Visit in Chandler, AZ
The Living Room Wine Cafe & Lounge

bodyHtml:
In recent years, wine bars have been popping up all over Chandler, much to the delight of local oenophiles looking for a spot to sip a robust Merlot or light rosé. Whether you’re in the mood to sip and savor at your favorite wine spot, or grab a bottle (or two) to go to enjoy at home, these Chandler wine lounges and bars will have just what you’re looking for.

The Living Room Wine Cafe & Lounge

A hip neighborhood hangout, The Living Room Wine Café & Lounge has a great selection of reasonably priced wines, most for under $10. The deals get even better during happy hour, daily drink specials from 11 a.m. to 6 p.m., when a good number of wines by the glass are $5 and food specials from 3-6 p.m. As you unwind with a glass of wine, nosh on flatbread pizza, sushi rolls, lettuce cups, fondue, and more. 

Map: 2475 W. Queen Creek Road, Chandler 85248 or (480) 855-2848

Cuisine & Wine Bistro

When it comes to French cuisine, nothing goes better together than a gourmet dinner paired with a tantalizing French wine. Just ask the folks at Cuisine & Wine Bistro, where sommelier Killian Buschetz has crafted an innovative wine list featuring wines from all over the world, but with a special emphasis on French wines from such regions as Cote d’Or, Bordeaux, and Rhone, among many others. Pair your glass with the Lobster Wellington, Quiche Lorraine, or the Beef Bourguignon and you’ll feel like you’ve been whisked away to a quaint French bistro in the heart of Paris.

Map: 4991 S. Alma School Road, Chandler 85248 or (480) 275-6700

St. Amand Kitchen & Cocktails

Just east of the Price Road Corridor, St. Amand pays homage to the patron saint of brewers, bartenders and vine growers. A fitting name, of course, for this Chandler restaurant focused on serving an eclectic menu of old and new world flavors with a variety of beverages, including beer, mead, cider, port, sherry, madeira and house cocktails. When it comes to wines, however, St. Amand pulls out all the stops with its impressive list of vintages, from California Chardonnays, to Argentinian Malbec, to Sauvignon Blanc from New Zealand and are perfect to enjoy in the modern dining room or on the patio. If you enjoy your wine with a side of entertainment, have a sip while enjoying the musical stylings of live musicians who frequent the establishment.

Map: 3990 S. Alma School Road, Chandler 85248 or (480) 782-5550

The Wild Vine Uncorked 

Wood floors, brick walls, and leather chairs give The Wild Vine Uncorked an elegant, Old World feel at this tapas lounge and wine bar. Sip wines by the glass while enjoying tapas such as empanadas, ceviche, and artisanal meats and cheeses. Happy hour specials run daily from 4 p.m. to 6 p.m. with $2 off select tapas, and there’s live music on Thursday, Friday, and Saturday nights.

Map: 4920 S. Gilbert Road, Chandler 85249 or (480) 883-3492

Fleming's Prime Steakhouse & Wine Bar 

Although it’s known for the outstanding steaks and seafood served in its restaurant, Fleming’s Steakhouse & Wine Bar also has an award-winning wine program with more than 100 wines by the glass, including several Arizona labels. Diners can select from suggested wine pairings or take part in one of the many wine dinner experiences offered by the west Chandler Fleming's.

Map: 905 N. 54th St., Chandler 85226 or (480) 940-1900

Stone & Vine Urban Italian

If you are looking for a wine bar with an incredible patio, head to Stone & Vine Urban Italian. The 5,000-square-foot patio overlooks a lake and has cozy seating next to a fireplace. Most glasses of wine on the menu will set you back $7 to $10 with select ones available for $6 during happy hour, 3 p.m. to 7 p.m. daily. If you're in the mood for bubbles, make sure to plan a visit to the Chandler restaurant for its weekend brunch, offered every Saturday and Sunday from 10 a.m. - 3 p.m. for bottomless Mimosas, Bellinis and Bloody Marys. 

Map: 1035 W. Queen Creek Road, Chandler 85248 or (480) 659-7438

Craft 64

Known for its artisan pizzas crafted in a 900-degree, wood-fired oven, Craft 64 also boasts an impressive wine menu that includes more than 60 varieties. Featured wines include the Sentall Chardonnay from Napa with hints of fresh lemon, melon, green apple, pear, smoky vanilla and spice; and the eponymous Craft 64, a Pinot Noir Cuvee made in Willamette Valley, Oregon, complete with dark cherry, mulberry and black tea flavors. Whichever wine you choose, enjoy it al fresco at Dr. A.J. Chandler Park as part of Chandler’s Dine in the Park program. Bring a blanket or lawn chair, and enjoy the evening with a glass of wine and one of Craft 64’s signature pizzas.

Map: 68 W. Buffalo St., Chandler, 85225 or (480) 247-3002

DC Steak House

Nestled at the modern New Square development in Downtown Chandler, DC Steak House promises a high-end dining experience perfect for a romantic evening out or a special occasion with family and friends. To celebrate these moments, the restaurant offers a notable wine list featuring an array of vintages from the world’s leading winemakers. Choose from an impressive list of red wines, hand selected white wines, and a sampling of lovely bubbles and rosés. Pair your glass with a delicious appetizer or entrée, including filet mignon, lamb chops, walleye pike, and lobster tail.

Map: 180 S. Arizona Ave., Chandler 85225 or (480) 899-4400

Down Time Wines

Part winery, part tasting room, part retailer, Down Time Wines is the neighborhood wine bar you’ve been longing for. Family-owned by Basil and Colleen Kaspar, the popular spot hand-crafts more than 30 wine varieties with juices sourced from rich wine-producing countries and regions like Australia, Italy, Chile, California and Washington State. Stop by for a wine tasting or place an order for curbside pickup or delivery.

Map: 393 W. Warner Road, Chandler 85225 or (480) 307-9296

Pesto's Italian Kitchen & Wine Bar

This well established. local restaurant is known for serving authentic Italian dishes alongside weekly live jazz sessions. The wine bar offers options for diners  with a robust list of 50 wines available by the glass or a number of wine flights for those who are interested in trying a little bit of everything or are feeling a bit undecided. Each of the six wine flights offered at Pesto's features a two-ounce pour of four different wines.  Food and drink specials are plentiful during happy hour, held daily from 2-6 p.m.

Map: 1960 W. Ray Road, Chandler 85224 or (480) 821-2949

bodyHtml:
While frigid weather takes hold of most of the country this winter, Arizona enviably basks in the warm rays of the desert sun with daily highs in the 60s and 70s —making a bevy of things to do in Chandler this winter even more enjoyable. We've got all the details for making the most of your winter visit to Chandler including exclusive offers and experiences available with the Choose Chandler Pass. 

See what's happening this weekend in Chandler or read on for our list of the top 10 things to do this winter in Chandler.

1. Discover Downtown Chandler

Hip, historic, charming, contemporary—these are just a few words to describe Downtown Chandler, nestled in the heart of the city. The bustling retail district is lined with vintage lanterns and trellis-covered walkways that lead you to a plethora of shops, restaurants, bars, and breweries, not to mention entertainment venues and public art installations.

There’s no better way to spend a sun-soaked winter day in Chandler than with a leisurely stroll through the downtown district, where you can browse locally-owned specialty stores, savor diverse food at more than 40 dining spots, and experience arts/culture on a grand scale in a small, picture-perfect footprint. And if you are looking for convenience, there are two hotels located in the heart of Downtown Chandler.

 

2. Shop ’Til You Drop

While winter days in Chandler are best spent outdoors, one can’t resist the pull a little retail therapy can muster. With the shopping mall very much back in style, make your way to Chandler Fashion Center, the second largest shopping mall in metro Phoenix with roughly 180 retail stores including SCHEELS, a variety of full-service dining choices, and entertainment including a multi-plex movie theater.

If local goods and unique finds are more your style, spend a day in West Chandler at The Shoppes at Casa Paloma for upscale boutique items or the Merchant Square Antique Marketplace for a taste of nostalgia. And don’t forget locally-made artisan pieces found only at the Museum Store at the Chandler Museum.

 

3. Al Fresco Meals is the Norm

Winter in Chandler takes on new meaning when patio dining becomes the most desirable spot in Chandler restaurants. Whether you are looking to enjoy a boozy brunch, a casual lunch with the family, happy hour with colleagues, or a romantic meal for two - you’ll find amazing patio dining options in Chandler during the best months to visit Chandler.

 

 

4. Winter Events in Chandler

Abundant sunshine may make the winter months a prime time to visit Chandler - but it's Chandler's events filled with music, culture, food and more that will keep you coming back for more. You'll finds a great selection of events happening all year long - but come winter, sporting events, music festivals and celebrations of local arts and culture reign supreme.

Female racers come from near and far to Chandler each January for Arizona's largest all-female racing event, the SHE Power 10K and 5K.  And art and wine collectors will make their way to Downtown Chandler in February for the Thunderbird Artists Fine Art & Wine Festival.

In March, one of Chandler's most iconic festivals take place, the Chandler Chamber Ostrich Festival which pays tribute to Chandler's early ostrich ranching history with a celebration of music from national and regional artists, entertainment, amusement rides, and the best in fair-style food from classic funnel cakes to roasted corn and cool treats.

 

5. Play a Round of Desert Golf

No matter what time of the year, Chandler is a true golfer’s paradise. With seven courses set amid stunning desert backdrops, you’re sure to find the perfect spot to hit the links.

Choose from the historic San Marcos Golf Course (Arizona’s first grass course) or the Ocotillo Golf Club designed by course architect Ted Robinson. Other standouts include Bear Creek Golf Complex, the Springfield Golf Resort, Sunbird Golf Club, Lone Tree Golf Club and Ironwood Golf Club. 

 

6. Experience a Western Adventure

Saddle up for a tranquil trail ride through the Gila River Indian Community surrounded by pristine mountain vistas and serene open desert. KOLI Equestrian Center offers several riding options, including 90-minute group rides, morning and sunset rides, a cattle drive with a cattlemen’s dinner with cowboy games, and a hay wagon ride where the horse roam.

 

7. Take in a Birdseye View of the Desert

For a new perspective on the Sonoran Desert, book a hot air balloon ride. At lower altitudes, you may see a rabbit, coyote, deer, or javelina. At higher altitudes, you’ll gain an appreciation for how vast—and ruggedly beautiful—the desert is. The experience begins with the inflating of the balloon and ends with a thrilling landing that will take your breath away. While most balloon companies launch north of Phoenix, Aerogelic Ballooning lifts off south of the Valley and often flies over Chandler.

 

8. Enjoy a Visit to the Desert Botanical Garden

The Southwest’s answer to NYC’s Central Park, the Desert Botanical Garden is just the place to spend a crisp winter’s day in the desert. The urban “jungle” in the heart of Phoenix boasts 50,000 thriving desert plants covering five themed trails in a one-of-kind ecological outing.

Visitors can observe the beauty of the desert plants including towering cacti, intriguing succulent, and colorful wildflowers on five thematic trails at this urban Sonoran Desert oasis. The garden also hosts festive events and unique exhibits and offers various adult and children’s classes on desert landscaping and nature.

 

9. Hike in a Desert Park

What better way to make your Midwest and East Coast friends and relatives green with envy than with a desert hike on a sunny day? The 113-acre Veterans Oasis Park is the perfect place to hike, thanks to its 4.5 miles of trails, including a paved solar system walk showing the relative distances between the sun, planets, and other celestial objects. Watch for birds as you explore—more than 150 species of birds have been spotted in the park.

Or head further south to Paseo Vista Recreation Area. The park’s curved walking path offers 360-degree views of the East Valley as well as access to the 6.5-mile Paseo Trail, a multi-use pathway for walking, jogging, and bicycling.

 

10. Pro Sports

While March signifies the start of spring, most of the country is still trying to dig out from under piles of snow. In 2026, Cactus League Spring Training baseball starts in February and promises to bring with it all the things we love about America’s favorite pastime. Professional baseball teams—and their die-hard fans—will flock to Arizona to get in some swing time before the official season kicks off. The games are affordable and give you a chance to soak up the desert sunshine while watching your favorite athletes play ball.

Keep tabs on our weather page for current conditions and our top 10 list of attractions to visit when in Chandler, AZ.

bodyHtml:
If a brand-new year has inspired you to embark on a journey of health and well-being, explore the serene and invigorating world of yoga. From tranquil studios to dynamic classes, Chandler’s yoga offerings include a wide range of experiences tailored to all skill levels. Whether you’re a pro at channeling your inner zen or stepping onto the mat for the first time, Chandler is filled with studios that will help you explore the path to balance, strength and mindfulness.

FLO Yoga & Cycle

Where mindfulness meets movement, FLO Yoga offers classes that build strength and flexibility in a music-filled setting that bucks conventional yoga programs. Take a “yoga” class for a full-body athletic workout, or a “yin” class that combines poses and breathing for restorative stretching. For the ultimate experience, enroll in a yoga sculpt class, which combines vinyasa flow, strength training and cardio. Heated and non-heated classes available. 

Map: 71 E. Frye Road, Chandler 85225 or (480) 907-5645

Hot Spot Yoga

Discover the transformative power of yoga in the “heat of the moment” at this West Chandler yoga studio. A dynamic range of classes include hot flow (classic vinyasa-style heated class), hot sculpt (incorporates weights to help build muscle) and restorative yin (combines gentle stretching and breath work). Drop-in, package and membership rates are available, as well as heated and unheated classes.

Map: 5865 W. Ray Road Suite 5, Chandler 85226 or (602) 753-7333

Sumits Yoga Chandler

A significant part of the Chandler yoga community since 2009, Sumits Yoga is where you’ll experience a harmonious blend of strength, flexibility and mindfulness. Guided by skilled instructors trained in a variety of yoga disciplines, class offerings span such types and styles as vinyasa, vin, yoga nidra and kids yoga, as well as the signature Sumits 80, a hot yoga class designed to strengthen, calm and re-energize the body and spirit.

Map: 4080 W. Ray Road, Chandler 85226 or (480) 768-1000

CorePower Yoga

Offering a dynamic approach to yoga, CorePower allows you to explore the fundamental principles of vinyasa yoga, where poses are linked with breath in a flowing sequence. Designed for participants of all levels, you’ll engage in such poses as eagles, triangle, side plank, warrior, and downward facing dog. Additional classes include H20 Sculpt, CorePower Strength, Hot Power Fusion, and CoreRestore.

Map: 2875 W. Ray Road #14, Chandler 85224 or (833) 448-2561

HotWorx

Powered by infrared technology, HotWorx classes are set inside a patented sauna that causes your body to sweat and speeds up detoxification. The hot yoga class incorporates various styles and practices with foundational postures, guiding you through balancing and core conditioning. What’s even more, the studio is available 24 hours, seven days a week, giving you the flexibility to work on your fitness goals whenever you want.

Map: 2040 S. Alma School Road Suite 8, Chandler 85286 or (480) 207-1187

headings.text: You’ll Flip Over these Great Pancake Spots in Chandler

bodyHtml:
Few breakfast items are as loved as the humble pancake. Simply made with flour, eggs, milk, and butter, they’re the warm, fluffy goodness we all need to get the day off to a good start. If you’re in search of the perfect stack of grilled-to-perfection pancakes, look no further than these Chandler brunch restaurants, where they take their pancakes seriously.

Hash Kitchen

Known for their over-the-top Bloody Marys, Hash Kitchen also offers some of the most unique pancakes you’ll ever encounter. Case in point, the blue corn banana Fosters, featuring blue corn pancakes topped with caramelized bananas, candied pecans, and cinnamon whipped cream. For a taste of Italy, try the cannoli. Prepared like the traditional Italian dessert, a cinnamon pancake is filled with sweetened ricotta and chocolate chip cream then sprinkled with powdered sugar and topped with maraschino cherries. Other must-tries include the pineapple upside down, s’mores, and corn bread and bacon.

Map: 2855 W. Ray Road, Chandler 85224 or (480) 909-4270

Eggstasy

While eggs may reign supreme at—hence the name—Eggstasy, the equally exhaustive list of pancakes will have stack lovers squealing with delight. From classics like buttermilk, chocolate chip, and lemon ricotta to the more adventurous banana macadamia and cinnamon roll, there are many to choose from. But for something completely out of the box, try the pecan pie topped with salted caramel, Chantilly cream, and graham cracker crumble; or the brunch-time favorite boozy cinnamon crunch toast made with cereal milk and rumchata cream. And speaking of brunch, choose a drink from the “fun bar” offering such favorites as blood orange mimosas, bellinis, chocolate-covered bacon Bloody Marys, grapefruit martinis, boozy salted caramel iced coffee, and Aperol spritzers.

Map: 2430 S. Gilbert Road, Chandler 85286 or (480) 361-9275

Egg n’ Joe

When it comes to pancakes, there’s the classic pancake made with flour, eggs, milk, and butter; and the buttermilk pancake made with, you guessed it, buttermilk. And while you can enjoy both of these versions at Egg n’ Joe, you can’t go wrong with the German pancakes. Also known as “fluffy” or “Dutch baby” pancakes, they’re made with eggs, milk, and flour, and baked in a pan rather than cooked on a griddle. Have the classic German pancake served with lemon wedges, whipped butter, and powdered sugar. For an added treat, top it off with your choice of fruit, including triple-berry, strawberry, cinnamon apple, or lingonberry butter.

Map: 4010 S. Arizona Ave., Chandler 85248 or (480) 207-6138

BLD Chandler

It only makes sense that a restaurant whose acronym stands for “Breakfast Lunch Dinner” would whip up a pretty epic pancake. And by epic, we mean gigantic. Known for their contemporary and oh-so Instagram-worthy styling, this south Chandler spot serves up fluffy, buttery buttermilk pancakes that are, let’s just say, a plateful. Order it solo or, if you’ve got the hearty appetite of a lumberjack, with a side. Selections include the Tre’s Chili sausage patty, green chili pork, jalapeno cheddar sausage, hash browns, eggs, fresh fruit, and more.

Map: 1920 W. Germann Road, Chandler 85286 or (480) 779-8646

Over Easy

At Over Easy, pancakes are cheekily referred to “breakfast cakes.” We love that because what better way is there to start the day than with cake? Served with butter and real maple syrup, traditional pancakes come with such extras as bananas, strawberries, Reese’s Pieces, M&Ms, and chocolate chips. If you’re in the mood for something a little tart, yet sweet, try the lemon ricotta pancakes served with fresh berries. For something more protein-packed, have the protein pancakes loaded with quinoa, pecans, granola, and blueberries. And just for good measure, enjoy your pancakes with a Bloody Mary, morning cocktail, or mimosa available in such flavors as blood orange pama or strawberry rosemary.

Map: 140 N. Arizona Ave., Chandler 85225 or (480) 257-3449

First Watch

With a focus on fresh, menu items at First Watch are made in-house with seasonal ingredients, from cage-free eggs to their made-from-scratch pancake batter. Perfect for the fall season, the pumpkin pancake breakfast is a great way to start the day. The pancakes are made with a pumpkin-spiced batter cooked to fluffy perfection and served with two cage-free eggs and a Jones Dairy Farm all-natural chicken sausage patty. You also can’t go wrong with the lemon ricotta pancakes served with lemon curd and berries, sprinkled with powdered cinnamon sugar, or the multigrain pancakes available in plain, blueberry, chocolate chip, banana granola crunch, and carrot cake.

South Chandler Location - Map: 4955 S. Alma School Road, Chandler 85248 or (480) 659-4995

West Chandler Location - Map: 4910 W. Ray Road, Chandler 85226 or (480) 752-3754

U.S. Egg

Family owned and operated since 1986, U.S. Egg serves hearty traditional breakfasts, from omelets and Benedicts to hot skillets and, of course, pancakes. Choose from whole wheat, buttermilk, banana, and chocolate chip. You can also top your stack off with blueberry or strawberry whipped cream. But what U.S. Egg is famous for are their signature protein pancakes filled with wild Maine blueberries, granola made in-house, cinnamon, and slivered almonds. But be warned: according to the owners, once you try them, you’ll be hooked.

Map: 5840 W. Chandler Blvd., Chandler 85226 or (480) 705-0868

Chandler sits within the bright arc of the Phoenix metropolitan light dome, where urban glow often obscures the cosmic wonders overhead. Still, the city’s convenient location places it within driving distance of desert parks, community observatories, and higher-elevation destinations that offer clearer night-sky visibility. This guide highlights nearby stargazing locations, practical planning tips, gear recommendations, and local astronomy resource guidance to help you make the most of a night under the stars.

Top Nearby Stargazing Spots 

San Tan Mountain Regional Park 

Located southeast of Chandler, San Tan Mountain Regional Park spans thousands of acres of open Sonoran Desert terrain. The park’s undeveloped landscape, higher elevation, and clear air provide noticeably better evening sky visibility than nearby urban neighborhoods. Stargazing here benefits from reduced light pollution, allowing stars and brighter planets to become visible once darkness falls. 

Arriving before dusk allows you to settle in comfortably, orient to the landscape, and take advantage of quieter areas away from road lighting. The setting delivers a calm atmosphere well-suited for casual stargazing and night photography near the city.

 

Veterans Oasis Park 

Set within Chandler’s southeast side, Veterans Oasis Park offers one of the city’s most accessible stargazing experiences. Wide‑open fields and minimal lighting create relatively favorable conditions for an in‑town location, and the park regularly hosts public night‑sky events featuring telescopes and guided viewing sessions led by local astronomy groups. These gatherings highlight planets, star clusters, and bright seasonal objects, making the park a convenient option for beginners, families, and anyone wanting an easy stargazing outing close to home.

 

McDowell Mountain Regional Park 

From Chandler, McDowell Mountain Regional Park sits far enough northeast of the Valley’s brightest light concentrations to offer noticeably darker skies, making it easier to spot constellations and track planetary movement. This location is great for visitors who prefer self-guided stargazing and enjoy bringing their own equipment and finding a quiet picnic or camping area. The setting provides space, silence, and a stronger sense of night-sky immersion than most urban parks.

 

Lost Dutchman State Park 

In the northeast of Chandler near Apache Junction, Lost Dutchman State Park offers some of the darkest skies within a short drive of the East Valley. Positioned at the base of the Superstition Mountains, the park’s openness and reduced light pollution create favorable conditions for spotting constellations, bright planets, and seasonal celestial events. Arriving before nightfall allows time to explore the surrounding desert landscape.

 

Riparian Preserve at Water Ranch & Gilbert Rotary Centennial Observatory 

The Riparian Preserve at Water Ranch in nearby Gilbert pairs wetlands, trails, and wildlife habitat with one of the East Valley’s most accessible astronomy experiences. On select evenings, the Gilbert Rotary Centennial Observatory opens for public viewing sessions. On these nights, volunteer astronomers set up additional telescopes and answer any questions attendees may have. 

This is an ideal option for beginners or families who want a heightened stargazing experience without traveling far. Arrive before sunset to enjoy the preserve’s paths, then stay for evening telescope viewing and informal astronomy education.

Worth-the-Drive Dark-Sky Destinations  

Oracle State Park 

For travelers willing to venture farther, Oracle State Park offers significantly darker skies than locations closer to the Valley. An officially designated International Dark Sky Park, Oracle State’s remote setting and minimal surrounding development create conditions well suited for Milky Way viewing, constellation spotting, and astrophotography.

The park hosts astronomy-focused programs and star parties on select dates, centered on dark-sky conditions and educational context. Planning ensures your visit aligns with these public viewing opportunities.

 

Flagstaff & Lowell Observatory 

Recognized as the world’s first International Dark Sky City, Flagstaff stands as one of the country’s most respected dark-sky destinations, thanks to long-standing lighting protections, low humidity, and higher elevation. The city itself offers enhanced night-sky visibility, while the surrounding areas provide even darker conditions.

Flagstaff is home to Lowell Observatory, adding a structured astronomy experience that combines historic significance with modern research facilities and public telescope viewing. Visitors can explore exhibits, take tours, and observe celestial objects through multiple telescopes. All of this creates an ideal destination for anyone drawn to both science and stargazing.

 

Tips for a Great Stargazing Experience  

Timing matters. Plan outings around the new moon for darker skies and better visibility of faint stars. Clear weather is essential, so check forecasts and cloud cover before heading out. Reaching your spot before full darkness allows your eyes to adjust and gives you time to set up your gear safely.

Reducing light interference makes a noticeable difference. Use a red-hued flashlight instead of white light and position yourself away from vehicle headlights or facility lighting whenever possible. Limit phone light and screen use to essential moments only, keeping brightness as low and brief as possible. If you need your phone for navigation or reference, rely on a stargazing app; its low‑light interface can help you identify constellations and track celestial objects without disrupting your night vision.

A pair of binoculars or a basic telescope enhances views of planets, star clusters, and the moon without requiring advanced setup. For photography, a DSLR or mirrorless camera and a sturdy tripod support sharper, longer‑exposure shots.

Comfort can shape your experience just as much as equipment. Pack a thermos with warm beverages, bring a few easy snacks, and dress in layers to stay warm; desert temperatures often drop quickly after sunset, even on mild days. A blanket or portable seat can make longer viewing sessions more enjoyable, and at higher‑elevation locations like Flagstaff, additional insulation is essential.

 

Events, Clubs, & Local Astronomy Resources 

Local astronomy groups and community observatories host public viewing nights, telescope sessions, and educational programs throughout the year. Checking regional astronomy club calendars and observatory schedules helps align your visit with guided stargazing opportunities and seasonal events.

Plan Your Night Under the Stars 

From nearby desert parks to world-class observatories, Chandler’s location makes it easy to explore Arizona’s night skies. Whether you start with a short evening outing or plan a dedicated dark-sky trip, the region delivers rewarding stargazing experiences year-round. Start mapping out your visit today and see where the stars lead you.
