title: About Chandler, AZ | Canal System, History & Travel Information
metaDescription: Learn about Chandler's rich history, cutting-edge growth, and travel details. A vibrant city blending innovation, culture, and charm.
ogTitle: About Chandler, AZ | Canal System, History & Travel Information
bodyHtml:
About Chandler

Dr. Alexander J. Chandler arrived in the Valley in 1887 and pictured a cutting-edge city where Chandler now sits today. He saw land that held great potential and a surrounding desert that held unimaginable beauty. Utilizing the existing canal system of the Native Americans as a blueprint, Dr. Chandler created one of the most advanced irrigation systems in the country, converting the dry desert into farmable land. Water came from both the Salt River and an untapped resource, ground water, which brought new life to the desert. On May 16, 1912, the Town of Chandler was founded.

Today Chandler, Arizona is still on the cutting edge. Chandler's vision of creating a diverse city with a high quality of life has been realized. Chandler has become one of the leaders in the computer technology field.

Chandler is a city of continuous growth and evolution. One man's dream has become one city's vision, as Chandler enters the 21st century continually looking toward the horizon.

Chandler Travel Information

Population

headings.text: Historic Downtown Chandler - Valley National Bank in the 1930s

bodyHtml:
Chandler History

A veterinarian's vision...

In 1891, Dr. Alexander John Chandler, the first veterinary surgeon for the territory of Arizona, bought 80 acres of land from the federal government south of Mesa. Dr. Chandler studied the relatively new science of irrigation engineering and was instrumental in building an early system of canals.

By the turn of the century, Dr. Chandler owned an 18,000 acre ranch. With the help of planners and architects, Dr. Chandler subdivided his ranch and drew up a town site map. Dr. Chandler's national advertising campaign for the sale of Chandler Ranch sites brought excursion trains filled with 300 speculators. They arrived on the newly completed Arizona Eastern Railroad and spent $50,000 for land that day.

At the time, Chandler consisted of three wooden shacks - the town site office, a dining hall and the Morrison Grocery. A billboard marked the site of the elegant future Hotel San Marcos. Dr. Chandler's ambitious plan was a landscaped central park surrounded by businesses. Walkways in front of the buildings would be covered by a trellis-like roof, supported by colonnades.

Deed restrictions required land owners to build on their land within one year. And in that one year after the first land sale, Chandler had begun to look like an established town. Businesses had been built along the west and south side of the park, including the Bank of Chandler and the Eastern Railroad depot. 

Dr. Alexander J. Chandler

Dr. A.J. Chandler was the Arizona Territory's first veterinary surgeon. Entrepreneurial in spirit, he was a man with a vision. His ambitious plan transformed Chandler from a 3-building town to a beautiful landscaped central park surrounded by businesses. Walkways in front of the buildings were covered by trellis-like roofs, supported by colonnades.

All this was made possible, in part because Dr. Chandler studied the relatively new science of irrigation engineering. He was instrumental in building an early system of canals. For many years, Chandler and the man who founded it thrived. The Great Depression was not a devastating experience for most of Chandler's residents.

The cotton crash of 1920 had a far greater impact on the agriculturally based economy. Dr. Chandler, however, did not fare so well during the depression years. The Bank of Chandler collapsed and he lost the San Marcos to his creditors. Able to retire comfortably, though, he lived in a cottage on the hotel grounds.

Chandler Transportation

Located in the southeast portion of Metropolitan Phoenix; Chandler, Arizona is a community of over 250,000 residents and it's never been easier to get to and from Chandler.

Arriving by Car

For those arriving by car, Chandler is conveniently located and easily accessible by major freeways including US 60 Superstition Freeway, Interstate 10, the Loop 202 San Tan Freeway, and the Loop 101 Price Freeway.  This makes it easy to include Chandler on your great Arizona road trip or utilize Chandler's great location as a home base for your Arizona vacation.

Arriving by Air

Most visitors will arrive to Chandler by air and the community is located about 20 minutes from two airports: Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport (PHX) and Mesa Gateway Airport (AZA) and transportation is relatively easy.  

Private and corporate aircraft owners will find trouble-free access via Chandler Municipal Airport (CHD), located 18 miles southeast of Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport (PHX).  Chandler Municipal Airport (CHD) is an excellent base for charter, transport, and sightseeing excursions with more than 200,000 general aviation operations a year.  

Ground Transportation

Most Chandler, Arizona visitors will rent a car for their Arizona trip, but will find transportation in and around Chandler, Arizona easy to navigate.  In addition to Uber, Lyft, Valley Metro and traditional taxis – group transportation and individualized car services are available to help you explore the very best of Chandler.

Bus & Light Rail In Chandler

Chandler Municipal Airport

Located just 18 miles southeast of Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport, Chandler Municipal Airport is a destination of choice for the traveler to who prefers to move in and out of Greater Phoenix with ease.  Direct freeway access, limited delays and friendly service are among the many reasons for this general aviation airport's growing popularity for business and personal aviation alike.

 The airport's Fixed Base Operation (FBO) Chandler Air Service offers competitive fuel pricing for Jet A and 100LL and parking for visiting aircraft.

Onsite at the Chandler Municipal Airport terminal building, customers will find free Wi-Fi, flight-planning and pilot lounge, bathroom facilities and more. Several Chandler, Arizona hotels are located nearby and many offer complimentary shuttle service to and from the hotel to the Chandler Municipal Airport.  Rental cars may be arranged in advance for pick-up at airport by working with the airport's FBO or local Chandler rental car facilities.

Aircraft Services/Fuel

In for a quick turn or staying a while? Chandler Air Service provides friendly service and 100LL and Jet A at competitive prices. Line service staff are available to cater to business travelers while continuing to meet the needs of the general aviation community. 

Transient parking is located near the base of the ATC Tower just outside the terminal building.

Chandler Air Service can be reached via UNICOM at 122.95 or by calling (480) 963-6420.

bodyHtml:
Greater Phoenix Airports

Chandler, Arizona is served by two airports with most visitors arriving via Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport (PHX), which sees more than 130,000 passengers arriving and departing each day across 24 major airlines. On any given day, America's Friendliest Airport®  has more than 1,200 arriving and departing flights with nearly half of those being nonstop flights, making it easy to find connecting service to anywhere in the world. Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport offers nonstop service to more than 120 domestic destinations throughout the United States and over 25 international destinations. In addition, the airport provides a consolidated rental car center, shared car services, taxi and shuttle services facilitating an easy transfer to Chandler, AZ, which is a short, 20-minute drive. 

To the east of Chandler, AZ, about 20 minutes by car, is Mesa Gateway Airport (AZA) offering service to over 40 destinations across the United States and Canada via Allegiant Airlines and Sun Country Airlines.  

An excellent alternative for private and corporate aircraft owners flying into Phoenix is Chandler Municipal Airport (CHD), one of the nation's 50 busiest general aviation airports with more than 200,000 flight operations a year. Located just 18 miles southeast of Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport, the airport is conveniently located and features a pilots lounge & flight planning room, Air Traffic Control Tower, and Free Wi-Fi. The Hangar Cafe, a local favorite restaurant for breakfast and lunch is located on-site in the corner of a large, aircraft maintenance hangar offering indoor and covered patio seating overlooking the runway.

bodyHtml:
Moving to Chandler

A Sunny, Welcoming Place to Call Home

Thinking about making Chandler, AZ, your new home? We don’t blame you—there’s a reason our community continues to grow and thrive. As Arizona’s fifth-largest city, Chandler blends big-city energy with the warmth and spirit of a close-knit community, all rooted in innovation, opportunity, and an exceptional quality of life.

Chandler: Where Careers Flourish, Close to Home

In Chandler, AZ, exciting careers and family life thrive side by side. Home to globally recognized employers and fast-growing start-ups in technology, healthcare, financial services, and advanced manufacturing, Chandler, Arizona, offers abundant professional opportunities—often just minutes from where you live. Shorter commutes mean more time for the things that matter most: family, hobbies, and enjoying our nearly endless sunshine.

Safe, Innovative & Family-Focused

Attractive from the start, Chandler, AZ is known for being safe, innovative, and community-minded. It’s a place where neighbors look out for one another and local pride runs deep. Families appreciate Chandler’s highly ranked K–12 public school districts, celebrated for innovative programs, dedicated educators, and a commitment to helping every child reach their full potential. With exceptional extracurricular options—from fine arts and competitive athletics to robotics and specialty clubs—students have countless ways to shine.

Endless Amenities for Active, Connected Living

Life in Chandler means access to everything you need for an active, vibrant lifestyle. Residents enjoy outstanding parks and recreation, family-friendly activities and attractions, engaging community events and festivals, higher education opportunities, and a diverse selection of restaurants, entertainment, and some of Arizona's best shopping. It’s all the best of desert living, wrapped in more than 300 days of sunshine.

Homes for Every Lifestyle

Whether you’re searching for a stylish modern apartment, a walkable neighborhood, or a spacious family home, Chandler AZ offers a wide range of housing options designed to fit every stage of life.

Chandler: A City Where Work–Life Balance Comes Naturally

In Chandler, you don’t have to choose between professional success and a fulfilling personal life—you can have both. With a thriving economy, top-tier schools, safe neighborhoods, and a welcoming community spirit, it’s easy to see why young families continue to choose Chandler as one of the best places in Arizona to live, work, and grow.

For Businesses Considering a Move to Chandler

Companies interested in relocating or expanding in Chandler can contact the City of Chandler’s Economic Development Division for expert assistance with site selection, business support, demographic insights, and more.

bodyHtml:
Fun Facts

  • Architect Frank Lloyd Wright and Dr. A.J. Chandler had drawn up plans for a second San Marcos Resort in 1930, "San Marcos in the Desert," but the resort was never built due to the Great Depression
     
  • The City also uses water from 22 wells operating in the City.  Chandler's oldest drinking water well is the Erie well, which has been in service since 1948. Over that time, it has produced an estimated eight billion, 614 million (8,614,000,000) gallons of drinking water.
     
  • Since it's opening in 1989, more than 2 million people have walked through the doors of the Chandler Center for the Arts.  The Center is jointly owned by the City of Chandler and the Chandler Unified School District, which provides the students with the opportunity to perform in a world-class theatre. 
     
  • Minnesota Vikings Quarterback, Donovan McNabb has made his home in Chandler.
     
  • Have you ever heard of Folley Park?  This park was named after Zora Folley, a former City Councilmember who was also a former heavyweight boxer who fought Muhammad Ali.
     
  • The gray water produced by Chandler high-tech companies like Intel, who just recently opened FAB 32, provides the water for all the lakes of Ocotillo.

headings.text: 7. Where kids can bounce, skate, run, and explore

bodyHtml:
10 Things to Love About Chandler

1.  330 days of Sunshine 

That means no snow days and no shoveling! Take advantage of Chandler's wonderful climate. Have business here? Extend your trip and enjoy the sun!

2. Batter up: 

Cactus League Spring Training - From Chandler, easily access any of the 15 Major League teams that make the Valley of the Sun their spring home for baseball.

3. Worldly dining experiences  

Restaurants cover the gamut - from casual to upscale you'll find a world of flavor at Chandler restaurants.  From the house-made pan dulce (Mexican sweet bread) at El Sol Mexican Cafe & Bakery to Mediterranean food at south Chandler's The Ivy, or savor hand-pulled noodles at China Magic Noodles in Uptown Chandler you'll find a number of restaurants to explore.

4. Tee off! 

With seven championship courses including Arizona's original golf resort, Chandler golf offers lush fairways, expansive views and great golf values in the Valley of the Sun.

5. Engaging festivals and events

Find family fun at the annual Ostrich Festival, kick up your boots at the 102.5 KNIX Barbeque & Beer Festival with the hottest country music, craft beer and BBQ and celebrate the holidays at the Tumbleweed Tree Lighting Ceremony.

6. Parks

Tired of miles on treadmills and stationery bikes? Get outside and walk Chandler's park trails, stretch and strive on an exercise course, join a pickup game of basketball or frolic in any of Chandler's more than 60 parks or splash into fun at one of six aquatic facilities. Chandler parks also offer environmental education displays, playgrounds for the kids, a ranch museum, and plenty of room to play!

7. Where kids can bounce, skate, run, and explore

Chandler's family fun centers have wall-to-wall trampolines, family activities at the Chandler Museum, ice-skating and roller rinks and so much more!

8. Vibrant Downtown Chandler 

Stroll the tree-lined square for a collection of uniquely Arizona stores, enjoy the more than 60 pieces of public art then eat and drink in one of the thriving, locally-owned restaurants and bars of Downtown Chandler. 

9. Connect with your inner geek

Chandler embraces scientific pursuits with the year-round Chandler Solar Walk at Veterans Oasis Park and its annual science celebration in February: Chandler Innovation Fair.

10. Access Arizona's best

With its central location, just minutes from two major airports, Chandler makes a great central location to explore Arizona's scenic wonders, family fun adventures and world-renowned attractions.

bodyHtml:
ASU Friends & Family

 Are you planning an Arizona getaway to visit your favorite Arizona State University student?  Centrally located, Chandler has been recently recognized as an All-America City and is a fantastic warm weather destination just minutes from ASU and only 20 minutes from both Phoenix Sky Harbor International and Mesa Gateway airports.   Chandler offers a great variety of hotels, award-winning restaurants, lively arts & culture, entertainment venues, golf, and exciting events.  With 330+ days of sunshine, there is plenty of outdoor recreation....ranging from desert hikes, jeep tours, hot air balloon rides, or lounging poolside.  If you are looking for sports - keep in mind that Chandler is close to all the action including NASCAR, Cactus League Spring Training, and a variety of major professional sports leagues and special events!

The heart of Chandler is found in our Downtown Chandler, which has experienced a dynamic revitalization revealing a vibrant and walkable community featuring locally owned and operated businesses including Arizona's finest and largest brewery and great public art.  Downtown is also an arts and cultural hub with numerous art galleries, the Chandler Center for the Arts, listed on the National Register of Historic Places, murals to explore and a hub for local music.

College is an exciting time for you and your family and Chandler's hotels want to make it easy for you to plan your next getaway to visit your beloved ASU student.  Chandler is conveniently located near all the ASU campuses and minutes from two major airports with terrific hotels, exciting retail destinations, lively dining scene, entertainment venues, award-winning golf, recreational activities and 330 days of sunshine.

headings.text: Plan Your Chandler Trip by Season

bodyHtml:
Chandler Weather & Seasonal Travel Guide

Chandler’s desert climate means sunny skies, hot summers and mild winter afternoons, though the mornings can be chilly. While the city averages more than 300 sunny days per year, your travel month still affects how you’ll dress and when you’ll want to be outside. To make the most of your visit, check the forecast frequently to plan activities around current conditions.

Average Monthly Weather in Chandler

The table below shows average monthly highs, lows and precipitation, revealing how weather patterns change throughout the year. It lists temperatures in Fahrenheit and Celsius; for this guide, we will use Fahrenheit.

  Average High  Average Low  Average Precipitation
 January  67 F/19 C  41 F/5 C  1.01
 February  71 F/22C  45 F/7 C  0.99
 March  77 F/25 C  49 F/9 C  1.19
 April  85 F/29 C  54 F/12 C  0.33
 May  94 F/34 C  61 F/16 C  0.17
 June  104 F/40 C  70 F/21 C  0.06
 July  106 F/41 C  77 F/25 C  0.89
 August  104 F/40 C  76 F/24 C  1.14
 September  99 F/37 C  70 F/21C  0.89
 October  89 F/32 C  59 F/15 C  0.81
 November  75 F/24 C  47 F/8 C  0.77
 December  67 F/19 C  40 F/4 C  0.98

December through February are the coolest months, and temperatures start to warm up in March and April. Hot weather sets in during May and continues through September and even October, with June through August being the hottest stretch. October typically sees highs around 89°F, and November cools down to 75°F.

Rainfall also follows seasonal patterns. The Sonoran Desert gets winter rain and summer thunderstorms, creating two wetter periods each year.

Chandler Weather by Season

For planning purposes here, we’ve grouped seasons by month: spring covers March through May, summer June through August, fall September through November and winter December through February.

Fall

As fall progresses, average highs drop to 89°F in October and 75°F in November, following September's 99-degree average. Later-season temperatures support outdoor dining and a round at San Marcos Golf Course, an 18-hole, par-72 course located in Downtown Chandler.

October also adds Halloween celebrations to the agenda. The free Halloween Spooktacular features trunk-or-treat stations, carnival games and a costume parade. Explore our annual events and festivals to confirm dates as you plan your autumn visit.

What to Pack: Breathable daytime clothing suits warmer afternoons. Add a light layer for evenings and consider having a jacket or sweater handy, especially when your travel dates move closer to winter.

Winter

Winter’s daytime highs average 67°F in December and January and 71°F in February, supporting outdoor recreation in milder conditions. Morning and nighttime temperatures feel significantly cooler, with average lows hovering between 40°F and 45°F.

Take advantage of the milder afternoons with a guided ride at KOLI Equestrian Center, where you’ll follow desert trails on the Gila River Indian Community’s lands. The winter schedule includes 90-minute group rides. For a different view of the desert, take to the sky on a hot air balloon ride. Rainbow Ryders offers daily sunrise flights, weather permitting, with panoramic views of the Sonoran Desert, plus sunset flights November through March. After landing, passengers can celebrate the ride with a traditional toast and light refreshments.

What to Pack: Build your winter suitcase around light layers, a sweater or jacket for mornings and evenings, comfortable shoes and sun protection.

Spring

Afternoon highs average 77°F in March, 85°F in April and 94°F in May, so spring warms steadily.

Enjoy the seasonal weather by walking through wetland habitat and other areas of Veterans Oasis Park, which offers 4.5 miles of dirt trails and paths. A 0.4-mile paved path circles the lake, and the Solar System Walk uses monuments to represent the sun and planets at scaled distances. Compare hiking trails in and around the city to find other places to explore.

Chandler Jazz Festival puts outdoor live music on the spring calendar. April performances include local and national musicians. Check the current festival schedule to coordinate your visit and bring a blanket or lawn chair to get comfortable and watch the main stage.

What to Pack: Light layers, comfortable walking shoes, sunglasses and sun protection.

Summer

During June, July and August, average highs range from 104°F to 106°F. Schedule outdoor activities during cooler hours, reduce strenuous exercise in extreme heat and take regular breaks somewhere indoors and cool.

Summer evenings in Chandler generally cool down a bit, but heat can persist. Review evening temperatures when planning your time outside after dark, too.

When temperatures climb, an indoor stop can provide a welcome change of pace. Inside Chandler Museum, you'll find locally produced and nationally traveling exhibitions that examine history, art and culture. Admission is free, and regular hours run 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. Tuesday through Saturday and 1 to 5 p.m. Sunday. Other popular beat-the-heat activities include shopping and movie theaters.

Monsoon season runs June 15 through Sept. 30, bringing the potential for lightning, blowing dust and flash flooding. Keep an eye on weather alerts, seek shelter indoors when storms approach and never drive through a flooded roadway.

What to Pack: Keep lightweight clothing, sunscreen, a hat and sunglasses handy. Carry a reusable water bottle and drink water regularly, even when you don’t feel thirsty.

Plan Your Chandler Trip by Season

Match your interests to the season's weather, and use expected temperatures and patterns to guide reservations. Compare hotels by location and amenities so your accommodations suit the attractions you’ll visit and the things you want to do. Verify availability and current operating hours directly when booking activities, particularly those that depend on outdoor conditions.

Before your trip, review the Chandler, AZ, forecast to refine your packing list for possible weather changes. Daily highs, overnight lows and rain chances give you more specific information about your trip. Check again each morning during your stay to time that day’s plans around current temperatures and chances of rain.

Ready to experience Chandler in your favorite season? Start planning your visit and make the most of your Arizona getaway.

title: Visit Chandler Privacy Policy
metaDescription: The City of Chandler is committed to our visitors' privacy. Our privacy policy describes the information we collect and how we share and protect it.
bodyHtml:
Privacy Policy

The City of Chandler,Arizona, is committed to protecting the privacy of all visitors to our Website. This policy describes privacy practices of www.visitChandler.com and contains information about what data is collected and how it is used. We believe that the protection of personal privacy is of the utmost importance when visiting our site because it helps the City to deliver efficient and effective customer services, to ensure our users' confidence and to encourage online participation. Thank you for visiting our site.


Collection and Use of Online Information
Our Web server automatically collects your Internet Protocol address when you visit our site. Your IP address is your computer's unique address that lets other computers attached to the Internet know where to send data, but rarely can be used to identify you individually.

To help us provide better service and a more effective Web site, sections of this site may use cookies as part of its interaction with your browser. A cookie is a small text file that is placed on your hard drive to allow our server to identify your computer. Our use of cookies will not attempt to read any additional information on your hard drive, and we do not combine information collected through cookies with other personal information to determine your identity or your e-mail address.

In addition, we collect demographic data from Google's Internet-based advertising with Google Analytics. Visitors can opt-out of Google Analytics for Display Advertising and customize Google Display Network ads using the Add settings. The information that we collect is used to enhance the usability and improve the content of our website. It may be used to personalize information and for statistical purposes. Personal information will not be shared with third parties unless otherwise indicated or unless required to do so by law. www.visitchandler.com contains links to other sites. Please be aware that we are not responsible for the information collection processes on these sites and cannot control how the information is used.

Remarketing / Retargeting Policy 
Re-marketing or re-targeting allows advertisers to show ads to users who've previously visited the advertiser's website as they browse the Web. 
- Third party vendors, including Google, show http://www.visitchandler.com ads on sites on the Internet. 
- Third party vendors, including Google, use cookies to serve ads based on a user's prior visits to http://www.visitchandler.com.

Google provides info on opting out here: http://www.google.com/policies/technologies/ads/
If you would like to be able to opt out from vendors other than Google more info can be found here: http://www.networkadvertising.org/choices/

Protection of Personal Information
Your personal information will not be shared, sold or transferred to any third party without your prior consent, or unless it is required by law. To use certain services on our site, you may be asked to provide personal information, such as your name and address. If you are making a payment, we may ask for your credit card number and billing address. If you decline to provide the requested information, the ability to provide you the service via the Web may be limited.

Please be assured that the interactive services on our site are equipped with security measures to protect the information you provide us. We encrypt important data that must remain secure to meet legal requirements. Most Web browsers indicate a secure form by a ‘closed lock' icon at the bottom of the screen.

Links to Other Web sites
Chandler's privacy policy extends to www.visitChandler.com only. The City of Chandler Tourism Web site and its links  are provided as a community service. Many of the links listed on this site are not official sites of the City of Chandler. The City does not sponsor or endorse any of these sites. You should check the privacy policy of each of these sites if you have concerns about how they handle personally identifiable information.

Use of E-Mail and Other Correspondence
Please note that any correspondence, such as e-mail and letters, sent to City officials or staff becomes public record and is available for public/media review.

Correspondence to the City of Chandler via the Web site or e-mail shall in no way be deemed to constitute legal or official notice to the City, its agencies, officers, employees, representatives or agents with respect to any existing, pending or future claim or cause of action against the City of Chandler or for any other purpose.

City Records
All City records are subject to the State of Arizona public records law. Any and all information gathered by the City through its Web site shall be protected to the extent possible under the current law. Disclosure of public information may be required in response to an appropriate public records request or compelled by legal process. The City of Chandler will not release confidential information, such as Social Security Numbers and bank account information, without a court order. All other information is subject to release.

Protection of Minors
The City of Chandler believes that protecting children's privacy online is extremely important and respects national and international laws, including the Children's Online Privacy Protection Act ("COPPA"), which applies in the United States. The City does not knowingly collect personal information from children; however, the City does not verify the age of visitors to its site. Collection of personal information provided by minors is treated in the same way as adults and may be subject to public access laws. We hope parents monitor their children's Internet use and ask that minors get their parents' permission before providing any information online. If, at any time, you have a concern about children's use of the City's Web site or the Social Media sites  with City links, please contact us by clicking here, or call 480-782-2000.
 
In terms of photos of children on the City's Web site, the City's policy is to only use photos of children if they are taken in public spaces, with no identification, and are used only for editorial (not advertising) purposes. The City requires a photo release from a parent or guardian for pre-arranged photos taken in a protected environment such as a school and showing a highly defined  and recognizable image. If you have questions regarding this policy, believe there is a violation of such policy, or if a parent wants a photo of a child removed from the Web site, please contact the City by clicking here, or call 480-782-2000.

Terms of Use
The City of Chandler's Web site is governed and controlled by the statutes and ordinances of the State of Arizona and the City. Any use of the Web site shall conform with all City, State and federal laws, rules and regulations. By accessing www.chandleraz.gov, you agree that you will not use the site for any unlawful activity or use it in any way that would violate the law.

Disclaimer
Every effort has been made to ensure that the information provided on the City of Chandler's Web site is correct. However, the City makes no warranties or representations about the accuracy or completeness of any site's content and assumes no liability for any inaccuracies that the Web site may contain. The City of Chandler shall not be liable for any direct, incidental, consequential, indirect or punitive damages arising out of access to or use of any content on this site.

Questions about this Policy
If you have any questions about the City of Chandler's Privacy Statement and subsequent policies, you can contact the City of Chandler directly at:

City of Chandler
Communications & Public Affairs
Mail Stop 604
P.O. Box 4008
Chandler, AZ 85244-4008

You also can call us at480-782-2000.

bodyHtml:
Chandler’s Restaurants

Chandler's local restaurant scene is thriving and diverse, offering visitors plenty of choices that blend local ingredients and global flavors. From authentic Mexican dishes featuring local ingredients to fine-dining Indian cuisine, tempting Thai or uniquely local coffee shops and cafes to satisfy your sweet tooth - there's much to explore in Chandler.

Mexican food

Less than three hours north of the Mexican border, is it any wonder that Chandler has some of the best Mexican food restaurants in the country? We’ve got it all, from first-rate Sonoran hot dogs to chimichangas to street tacos to burritos so big you may need to dare yourself even to finish.

Local Bites

Dining out on vacation allows you to get a front-line feel for the community by visiting locally-owned spots that will make your taste buds do a happy dance. Some of the best restaurants in Chandler, AZ, are locally owned and offer exceptionally warm service. From award-winning eateries to local hot spots, whatever you're craving, we likely have an independent restaurant serving it with enthusiasm and expert care.

Breakfast & Brunch

Sure, vacation can be for sleeping in, but isn't it better to fuel up on a delicious Chandler breakfast before a day of exploring? Whether you're looking for an early breakfast or a later brunch, from healthy and delicious to bacon-driven delights to Bloody Marys after a long night on the town, we have something for everyone.

Thai

No matter where you travel, Thai food is always a main attraction for foodies. Thai restaurants in Chandler stand up to the best of them. The most tempting curry around, pad thai that you’ll want to write home about, and everything else you’d expect from glorious Thai food restaurants await your arrival.

Sports Bars

No matter where you are, if your team is playing, you’ll find a sense of home over pub grub, beer, and more flat screens than you can count at Chandler’s sports bars. We’ve got Irish Pubs, Chicago-themed joints, sports grills, and breweries, all with that familiar neighborhood sports bar decor every fan craves.

Beer Joints & Breweries

Chandler is a land of award-winning breweries and bars. Whatever your flavor, be it cozy pubs, craft breweries, or upscale restaurants with beer menus that’ll make your mouth water, our city has no shortage of prime beer-drinking establishments where you and your crew can relax, throw back a few, and swap stories from the glory days.

bodyHtml:
Asian Restaurants in Chandler 

Chandler’s Asian restaurants give diners a wide range of ways to work a meal into the day, whether it’s a quick lunch, a relaxed dinner, or a date night. The city’s lineup spans polished dining rooms and more casual neighborhood spots, with Chinese, Thai, Japanese, Korean, and Vietnamese cuisines all represented. Taiwanese specialties add even more depth, introducing desserts and tea‑focused menus that round out Chandler’s diverse Asian food offerings. 

Best Spots for a Business Lunch 

Our city has abundant options for lunch meetings and work breaks with fast service, quieter atmospheres, and dependable menus full of your favorite Asian dishes. Grace Thai in Downtown Chandler features a focused selection of Thai staples, including noodle dishes and curries, making it a practical stop during a workday.  

Pho Chandler has a streamlined menu centered on pho and rice plates, resulting in a smooth lunch. Don’t miss the lemon grass chicken.  

Need a trusted brand and a more energetic atmosphere? Pei Wei has counter-service ordering and a familiar menu structure. This one is great when time is limited, as their service is typically quick and efficient.  

Family‑Friendly Options 

Group dining calls for variety, and several area restaurants have the goods. Eastwind Sushi & Grill, located downtown, pairs conveyor-style sushi with a broader lineup that includes traditional Japanese bento boxes and cooked items.  

Jin Shabu, a Korean-style shabu-shabu eatery, introduces a more interactive format through its all-you-can-eat hot pot experience, where you can cook your ingredients in broth heated at your table. 

Chou’s Kitchen selections are rooted in northeastern Chinese cuisine, offering a mix of dumplings, noodles, and a range of traditional entrees that naturally lend themselves to groups. 

Near Chandler Fashion Center, P.F. Chang’s serves signature staples and has a table-service setting that makes group dining straightforward for families. 

Top Date Night Picks 

The best date nights start by selecting the right restaurant: somewhere that slows things down, sparks conversation, and gives you a reason to stay in each other’s company a little longer. Shimogamo offers an intimate feel, including a full sushi bar and traditional Japanese dining perfect for a night out with your person. Check out their exceptional Izakaya-style dishes. 

Head to Chon Thai Food and enjoy a stylish, sit-down vibe for Thai fare. Chon Thai is ideal for a more relaxed, conversation-focused date. Try the Tom Yum soup made with flavorful, fresh ingredients. 

Singing Pandas Asian Restaurant & Bar delivers a different element, offering nightly live performances while you dine, creating a built-in activity as part of the outing. Go with a classic Teriyaki Chicken or one of the curry chicken offerings.  

Chandler’s Asian food scene supports more than just a single meal. Each stop adds a fresh aspect to the visit, making it easy to shape a full day or night around where you choose to eat. Ready to see where your appetite takes you? Start planning your visit.

headings.text: Best Places to Grab a Beer in Chandler
Additional Craft Beer Destinations in Chandler

bodyHtml:
Best Places to Grab a Beer in Chandler

The craft beer community in Chandler continues to thrive as is seen with the expanding number of breweries popping up in Chandler.  There is no shortage of places to pop in for a local brew and with many showcasing the best of Arizona craft beer. Here is a guide to Chandler’s breweries, tap rooms and gastropubs for cold pints and bites.

 

One of the state’s best craft breweries is located in Downtown Chandler. SanTan Brewing Company specializes in Southwestern-style ales, which have slightly more carbonation, like its highly regarded pale ale, Devil’s Ale. Other year round beers include HopShock IPA, Mr. Pineapple, MoonJuice IPA, SunSpot Gold, Epicenter Amber, and Gordo Stout.

The brewery also has a seasonal lineup (watch for Sex Panther, a double chocolate porter available November through January) and limited releases that are aged a minimum of six to eight weeks. Several beers such as Hibiscus Pale Ale, Cherry Vanilla Stout, and Negro Nitron Black IPA are only available on tap at the brewery.

What's not to love - handcrafted pizza and beer are on tap at this neighborhood wood-fired pizzeria and brewery.  Featuring house-made mozzarella, breads and local ingredients along with 30 Arizona beers including eight of their own brews.  The Chandler eatery also offers a happy hour from 3-6 p.m. every day.

Also popular with beer lovers, The Perch Brewery & Pub has 40 craft beers on tap, many of which are brewed onsite. The ever-changing selection of Perch beers includes favorites like the Mas Macho Pilsner; Howler Back Girl, a hefeweizen; and the Why So Mad Bro, a rye beer.

Rotating selections from other Arizona craft breweries are also on tap, including suds from Huss and Sleepy Dog. Enjoy a 5-ounce sample or 16-ounce draft on the rooftop or on the brick patio surrounded by more than 50 rescue birds.

Chandler’s newest microbrewery features 20 beers on tap, eight of which are from Helluva: an American wheat, an IPA, pale ale, light lager, amber, red, Kölsch and two seasonal brews.  In addition, the brewpub features a variety of gastropub eats with an emphasis on smoked meats and vegetables.

Brews Taphouse - A Burger Joint is popular choice among beer lovers for more than just it's delicious burgers. While it doesn't brew its own beers, the joint offers 24 rotating taps dispensing craft brews from Arizona's favorite breweries, including Pedal Haus, Four Peaks Brewing Co., Fate Brewing, and Huss.

Other beers come from The Shop Beer Co., Wren House Brewing Co., AZ Loc Ale Beer Co., Mother Road Brewing Co., Dragoon and The Brewery at Tirrito Farm. Cider is also available from the Six Byrd Cider in Phoenix.

The similarly named Hop Social Grill doesn’t brew its own beers but boasts 52 local beers on tap including those from SanTan, Four Peaks, O.H.S.O., Oak Creek Brewing, Barrio Brewing, Mother Road Brewing, McFate, Huss, Papago, The Shop Beer Co., Prescott Brewing, and Sleepy Dog.

But, the list of Arizona breweries doesn’t end there. Look for selections from Arizona Wilderness, Barley Brothers, Thunder Canyon, Uncle Bear’s, Nimbus, Borderlands, Freak’n, Copper Mine, Tombstone Brewing, 8-Bit Aleworks, 12 West, and many, many others. Hop Social also has Chandler-made cider from Desert Cider House on tap.

Located southeast of Dr. A.J. Chandler Park in Downtown Chandler, QuartHaus offers more of a European-beer garden experience.  Offering a boutique selection of handcrafted brews - patrons may grab a bite from a visiting local food truck while enjoying the casual backyard-setting featuring a variety of lawn games and outdoor seating.

West Chandler Neighborhood

Dirty Blonde Tavern

A hot spot for live music, visitors to the Dirty Blonde Tavern, may sip Grand Canyon’s Sunset Amber, a bready American amber, or the Sonoran White Chocolate Ale, a light wheat with subtle chocolate flavor.

Good Time Charli’s Neighborhood Craft Pub

Another good option for Arizona beers is Good Time Charli’s Neighborhood Craft Pub. On tap, you’ll find College Street’s Big Blue Van; Four Peaks’ Kilt Lifter and Peach Ale; Lumberyard’s Humphrey’s Hefeweizen; and SanTan’s Devil’s Ale, Oktoberfest, and Sunspot Gold. Or, pop the top on canned beers from Barrio and Huss.

Good Time Charli’s also features Arizona wines on tap from Caduceus Cellars, Dos Cabezas, Fire Mountain, and Sand Reckoner as well as cocktails made using Arizona spirits from O.H.S.O., Del Bac, Arizona Distilling, and 3 Amigos.

South Chandler Neighborhood

The Casual Pint Craft Beer Market

The Casual Pint Craft Beer Market takes beer seriously, so much so it has “beer-tenders” manning its tap wall. Try Arizona beers from Borderlands, Wren House, Freak’n, and Wanderlust and mead from Superstition Meadery.  What’s not on tap is often available in cans or bottles in the cooler.

Looking for a particular Arizona craft beer to bring home? Fill a growler, order a keg, or create a mix-and-match six-pack of your favorites. In addition to Arizona beers, The Casual Pint has several California, Colorado, German, and other outstanding beers on tap or available for purchase in cans and bottles.

Downtown Chandler Neighborhood

Best Pizza & Brew

Sure, it has delicious hand-crafted pizza, but Best Pizza & Brew also has an impressive list of local craft beers on tap, too. Stop by on Wednesday evenings for the Wednesday Pint Nights special to try some of the rotating taps.

Pedal Haus Brewery

Offering a European flare, Pedal Haus Brewery is a top-notch taproom with a fantastic selection of handcrafted beer, cocktails and Bavarian-style eats.  Perfect for outdoor dining, the gastropub offers a large, back patio for outdoor dining with 80 seats and a smaller patio upfront with seats for 22.  

The Sleepy Whale

This casual beer bar and bottle shop features more than 30 Arizona beers on tap and has easy access to more than 40 Downtown Chandler restaurants. 

Central Chandler Neighborhood

Fibber Magee’s

Fibber Magee’s may be one of the few authentic, Irish-owned pubs in the Valley, but it’s also a great spot to try local beer. The line-up rotates frequently but features popular breweries like The Perch, Four Peaks, and Grand Canyon Brewing. Check the pub’s Facebook page to see what’s currently on tap.

The Hungry Monk

This neighborhood sports bar has 27 craft beers to choose from, and while most are not from Arizona breweries, the local beers on tap rank among the state’s best: Four Peaks’ Kilt Lifter and HopKnot IPA, SanTan’s Devil’s Ale, and Sleepy Dog’s Red Rover.

Patent 139 Brewing Company

This lakeside property currently holds 12 craft brews on tap, 10 of those being from well-known breweries like Huss Brewing, Helton Brewing Company, Wren House Brewing, and more, and two of those being their own, a raspberry blonde ale called Neon Nancer Blaster and a West Coast IPA called Willowood.

headings.text: More Ways to Explore Downtown Chandler
Downtown Chandler Murals That Will Inspire You

bodyHtml:
Dine in the Park

It's never been easier to enjoy a picnic in the park!  Grab your picnic blanket and lawn chairs and make your way to Downtown Chandler for Chandler's new pop-up beer garden. 

While many restaurant dining rooms are open, diners have a new way to support local restaurants.  Customers may place their to-go order from their fave downtown restaurant and enjoy a relaxing meal in the park complete with a cold, sealed beer or sealed glass of wine.  The pop-up beer garden in Dr. A.J. Chandler Park is family and dog friendly and a great way to experience the community.  The park is a short walk from any of the free garages and street-site parking available in Downtown Chandler.  

Signs are posted around the park that highlight rules and hours for Dine in the Park along with a QR code that will link you to Downtown Chandler restaurant menus as coordinated by the Downtown Chandler Community Partnership. 

Consumption of alcohol in the park is only permitted from 3 p.m. to 9 p.m. Monday-Thursday, and from noon to 9 p.m. on Friday-Sunday. Restaurants will check IDs for proper drinking ages and the sealed beer and wine may ONLY be opened once inside the park. 

Before or after your meal, consider a stroll through the historic square to see the many engaging murals that adorn Downtown Chandler.

Explore Chandler's Local Restaurants and Bars

bodyHtml:
Chandler's Local Bites

One of the best parts of travel is vacation dining - finding those unique gathering places at the heart of the community. Filled with iconic eats, awesome ethnic restaurants and local breweries, Chandler's thriving culinary scene is one to savor.

Singing Pandas Asian Restaurant & Bar

A family-run spot that expertly pairs authentic and Americanized Chinese food, the award-winning Singing Pandas Asian Restaurant & Bar offers a casual, contemporary vibe in its dining room and a fun lounge equipped with a bar and stage. In the lounge, catch live music and entertainment most nights of the week to add some sweet notes to your dining experience.

This Chandler restaurant’s menu bursts with tasty choices. You can’t miss the Teriyaki Chicken, Prawns with Lobster Sauce, or Eggplant & Tofu. Other dishes are Pork Lo Mein, Shrimp Lo Mein, and Beef Fried Rice. For dessert, treat yourself to a slice of New York Cheesecake, White Chocolate Triple Layer Mousse Cake, or Hot Chocolate Lava Molten Cake. Tuesday through Friday, take advantage of lunch specials from 11 a.m. to 3 p.m.

Hop Social Grill

Reward yourself after a long day of shopping at nearby Chandler Fashion Center with a trip to Hop Social Grill. The decor does a captivating job of presenting a modern industrial chic vibe that retains an inviting warmth. A breathtaking bar makes Hop Social a popular place to post up and have a few drinks. 

Seven days a week, happy hours occur from 3 p.m. to 6 p.m. and 9 p.m. to close. The menu reads “locally sourced, scratch-made” and features quality burgers, sandwiches, steaks, salads, and fish. Among the 52 craft beers on tap, you’ll find an emphasis on local and Arizona-based brews.

Feringhee Modern Indian Cuisine

Craving an Indian food restaurant in Chandler, AZ? Look no further than Feringhee Modern Indian Cuisine. Translating to “foreigner,” Feringhee combines the best traditions of Indian culture with current “gastronomy techniques, innovative culinary ideas and new flavours” to level up their offerings.

The restaurant's modern ambiance and splashes of Indian art and decor come together to create an enchanting atmosphere. There are several lunch specials, including the two-piece Kolkata-Style Chicken Kathi Roll and Feringhee's Special Vegetarian Lunch Thaali. For dinner, look to the Tandoori Chicken Kulcha, Kerala Fried Chicken, or Kashmiri Lamb Chops.  

The Stillery

Among the best restaurants in Chandler, located in our lively downtown, The Stillery has amplified the fun in the area. Straight out of Nashville, The Stillery serves up staples of Music City, like the Hot Chicken Two-Handed sandwich. A stage, dance floor, and consistent live music are some of the many finishing touches of this good-time spot.

Order your favorite cocktail in one of The Stillery’s signature mason jars while you peruse the menu. The house specials include Blackened Salmon and the Hot Chicken Plate. And don’t miss brunch served on weekends from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. 

With more than 40 locally owned and operated establishments, there’s always something exciting and delicious going down in Downtown Chandler. Explore these Downtown Chandler restaurants for your next outing of delicious Chandler dining.

bodyHtml:
Chandler Mexican Food

Chandler is home to many global cuisines, but spicy and flavorful Mexican and Southwestern foods are something of an Arizona specialty, with its neighbor to the south. From traditional taquerias to modern bistros and family-run restaurants that have operated for years in Chandler - here's looking at you Espo's Mexican Food (nearly 60 years) and Elmer's Tacos (a Chandler tradition since 1974) you'll find incredible dining spots in Chandler. Whether you are looking to meet colleagues for a business lunch at a Mexican restaurant in Chandler or hanging out with friends and sipping margaritas and munching on tacos all day, you'll find plenty of Chandler Mexican food restaurants to make you happy for days. 

When looking for the best Mexican food restaurant in Chandler, AZ, it can be hard to choose which one to try first as there is no doubt that you'll find incredible Mexican food options throughout Chandler's neighborhoods. From trendy birria tacos and birria ramen that will get you that delicious close-up shot for Instagram (check out The Taco Spot and CaliTacos) to more traditional fare including tacos, burritos and more - Chandler's got you covered for finding the best Mexican food in town.  And you may be pleasantly surprised to learn that several of Chandler's mainstay Mexican food restaurants are family-owned and pay tribute to their family history using recipes past down from generation to generation for authentic Mexican food.

Located in north Chandler, Los Taquitos was started by the Ochoa sisters and their food has been featured on the Food Network's "Diners, Drive-ins, and Dives" and "Guy's Big Bite. In Uptown Chandler, husband and wife team Armando Hernandez and Nadia Holguin share an authentic taste of Chihuahua, Mexico using their mothers and grandmothers recipes. Located near Chandler Fashion Center mall, Espo's Mexican Food initially launched in 1974 with an American-style menu but course-corrected soon after using family recipes which are still in use today.

Just north of Downtown Chandler, you'll find no frills and irresistible charm at Elmer's Tacos  which opened in 1974, directly across Chandler High School. The casual restaurant uses modified recipes from founder Elmer Cuen's mom and its tried and true red chile and the iconic strips, corn tortilla chips, served with freshly grated - not melted, cheese and sauce.

headings.text: Unique Patio Dining Experiences in Chandler, AZ

bodyHtml:
Outdoor Dining in Chandler, AZ

Chandler is known for its delicious food scene, ranging from authentic Mexican dishes to lively brunch go-tos. However, the city is also big on outdoor dining. There’s nothing like sitting on an inviting Chandler patio to improve any great dining experience. That's why "Let's sit outside" is so often overheard as one enters a restaurant. During the summer, we delight in misting systems and shade; in the winter, outdoor heaters keep things nice and cozy.

Let’s explore some of the best patio restaurants in Chandler.

Tryst Café

At the family-owned and operated Tryst Café, treat yourself to well-deserved self-care by ordering a mouthwatering healthy bite on their beautiful outdoor patio. For breakfast, look to the smoothies and protein shakes; eggs served your way, or an Asian Jackfruit Bowl. For lunch, you can’t miss the Seared Ahi Salad. Come dinnertime, check out the Thai Shrimp Lettuce Wraps.

The Brickyard Downtown

The Brickyard Downtown is a modern downtown Chandler restaurant with outdoor seating. The patio is stylish, with comfortable seating and a small fireplace that adds to the space’s intimate feel. The New American menu at this dinner-only spot has Spanish influences and shareable plates that you and your party will love over lively conversation and some of the best craft cocktails in town.

Crust Simply Italian

When visiting Crust Simply Italian, taking in the fresh air, the outdoor seating layout and the overall vibe are all part of the formula for an exceptional patio experience. With built-in heaters and a ton of room, you're sure to have a fabulous time when you dine on this Chandler patio. At Crust Simply Italian, authentic Italian ingredients and delicious wines combine so deliciously that you may even become a regular.

MVP Sports Bar and Grill

Looking for a modern sports bar that retains that sought-after neighborhood feel? Look no further than MVP Sports Bar and Grill. The welcoming and spacious climate-controlled patio has large picnic benches and games like pool, Jenga, and Connect Four. Outdoors and indoors, high-definition TVs are everywhere. Order a cold draft and phenomenal wings and kick back while you watch your favorite team secure the day's glory.

h1: The Best Sports Bars in Chandler

headings.text: The Best Sports Bars in Chandler

bodyHtml:
The Best Sports Bars in Chandler

You may be traveling, but you are still a fan. And we understand your need to watch your team or catch the big game while visiting our community. Chandler’s sports bars have you covered with plenty of screens to catch all the action. 

Hob Nob Sports Grill

Whether you’ve been waiting all day or all week to catch your team battling for another win, Hob Nob Sports Grill is the perfect place to post up and take in the action. This spot is Chicago-themed, with a welcoming Midwestern atmosphere and a ton of Chicago sports team decor. Don’t worry — no matter who you’re rooting for, you’ll have a blast at Hob Nob. 

A spacious place, there are flatscreens everywhere you look, weekly events like team trivia, tasty food, and a full bar. Choose from sports bar favorites like burgers, nachos, wings, and even a mighty Chicago Dog.

Brews Taphouse & Burger Joint

Another first-rate sports bar in Chandler is Brews Taphouse & Burger Joint. Offering two locations in Chandler, the restaurants are inviting and clean, and flat screens line the wall behind the bar with different games or events playing, so you won’t miss a second of the competition. Brews is a family-owned establishment serving incredibly fresh beef, craft beer, and creative and elevated bar food.

They make the burgers with Certified Hereford Beef, and the fresh brioche buns take the already heightened burgers to another level. An impressive beer menu, wings, sweet potato tots, and fried pickles only scratch the surface of the deliciousness offered. 

Murphy's Law Irish Pub 

Among the wide range of exciting Downtown Chandler bars is the always-fun Murphy’s Law Irish Pub. This lively Dublin-style pub provides great service, drink, and food. It has a familiar feel, especially for those who’ve made it a pastime to catch games at Irish bars. The decor is reminiscent of Irish bars from your past, making you feel right at home as your team dominates the other guys.

Murphy’s has a long list of daily specials and a fantastic happy hour food and drink menu. In addition to the main menu, there’s one for brunch, kids, and late night, all overflowing with pub favorites. 

MVP Sports Bar and Grill

Among the best sports bars in Chandler, AZ, MVP Sports Bar and Grill never fails to impress. Sports rule at MVP's, so whenever you pop in there's undoubtedly a good game playing. The sports bar menu has an all-star appetizer selection with wings, nachos, and other appetizers to start and main dishes include fresh salads, sandwiches, and burgers or their pitch-perfect pizza to fuel up for the big game.

Don’t miss the comfortable patio to enjoy fresh air and share stories of your favorite buzzer beaters or other clutch moments. If patios are your thing, check out these unique patio dining experiences in Chandler. 

Zipps Sports Grill

A delightful place to watch the game with the entire family, Zipps Sports Grill offers a spacious atmosphere with games playing everywhere you look. Family-owned and operated, Zipps has 14 locations across the Phoenix metropolitan area, so they’re definitely doing more than a few things right.

The drinks menu is excellent, including the signature Zipparita and specialty Zipparitas. The bar food never fails to impress with burgers, specialty burgers, hot wings, pizza, and fish tacos, to name a handful. Zip on over and have a ball.

title: Best Steakhouses in Chandler | Steak Restaurants Chandler, AZ
metaDescription: Browse steak restaurants in Chandler, AZ, from upscale dining rooms and patios to prime rib, seafood, and wine-focused menus.
ogTitle: Chandler American Restaurants | Restaurants in Chandler AZ
bodyHtml:
Steakhouses in Chandler

Chandler offers a great selection of steakhouses that are perfect for a special night out or a classic celebration. Full of ambiance, Chandler steakhouses are buzzing spots with lively cocktails, refreshing patios, and high-quality cuts of beef.

Whether you're looking for a traditional steakhouse or a more contemporary setting, we have a selection of can’t-miss essential steakhouses and fine-dining restaurants to try in Chandler.

Nestled in Downtown Chandler, the DC Steak House is a local gem known for its upscale dining experience. Whether you opt for the wonderfully old-school surf 'n' turf or a bone-in ribeye, you’ll find an elegant dining room with attentive service, or opt for the patio adorned with strands of string lights for a magical meal.

Also located in the downtown district, Elliott’s Steakhouse offers an upscale, fine-dining experience with a vibrant cocktail menu. Housed in the historic Rowena Theatre, the building was Chandler’s first brick grocery store when it opened in 1912 and eventually became Chandler’s first movie theater, but today offers diners an elegant backdrop to amazing seafood and steak.  

In south Chandler, find sophisticated ambiance and modern décor with a well-stocked bar at CHoP in Downtown Ocotillo. This Chandler-based restaurant has a passion for great food, serving up hand-cut steaks, seafood, and an extensive wine selection.  The restaurant provides an upscale yet inviting atmosphere in its modern dining room, on the patio, or in its private dining room.

Located near Chandler Fashion Center mall, The Keg + Steakhouse is celebrated nationally for its premium steaks, seafood, inviting atmosphere, and extensive wine list. The Keg's commitment to excellence in both food and service makes it a popular choice for steak enthusiasts.

In West Chandler, make your way to Fleming’s – an upscale steakhouse and wine bar for an elevated dining experience. Known for its impeccable service and ambiance, it specializes in USDA Prime steaks, fine wines, and gourmet cuisine. Fleming's offers a refined yet welcoming setting, perfect for special occasions or a luxurious night out.

So, indulge in Chandler’s steakhouse scene where flavor, quality, and ambiance come together to create unforgettable dining memories.

title: San Marcos Golf Course in Chandler | Historic Arizona Golf Course
metaDescription: Book a round at San Marcos Golf Course in Chandler, a par-72 layout with a driving range, golf instruction and Downtown Chandler nearby.
ogTitle: San Marcos Golf Course in Chandler | Historic Arizona Golf Course
bodyHtml:
San Marcos Golf Course

Originally opened in 1913, Arizona's first grass golf course was here at the San Marcos Golf Course in Chandler, Arizona. Today, it is an 18-hole PGA championship, par-72 course with lush fairways lined by mature Tamarisk and palm trees. The 6,640-yard course located at the Crowne Plaza San Marcos Golf Resort offers challenges with expanded lakes, reconstructed bunkers and new tee boxes for an enjoyable round of golf suitable for novice and experienced golfers.

The course easily accommodates tournaments of up to 144 people, a couple of foursomes, or just you and an associate with equal ease. Facilities include a driving range, putting green, complete golf-pro shop, golf instruction and the ability to grab a bite or drink on-site at Grill 60.  

Additional dining and entertainment options await you in Downtown Chandler, just steps away from the fairways where you'll discover a number of independent restaurants, craft cocktail lounges, boutique shops and more to round out your day.

headings.text: Welcome Sister Cities Visitors to Chandler, Arizona!

bodyHtml:
Welcome Sister Cities Visitors to Chandler, Arizona!

As a proud participant in the Sister Cities International program, Chandler, AZ extends a warm welcome to our global partners and friends. Whether you’re planning a cultural exchange, professional visit, or vacation, Chandler is ready to greet you with desert charm, innovation, and hospitality.

Why Visit Chandler?

Located in the heart of the Sonoran Desert and just minutes from the Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport, Chandler is a vibrant city known for its diverse community, innovative spirit, and rich cultural heritage. Here’s what you can expect to find in Chandler:

  • Authentic Southwestern Hospitality
    Enjoy friendly locals, welcoming accommodations, and community events that celebrate global cultures and local traditions.

  • Arts, Culture & History
    Explore the Chandler Museum, Vision Gallery, and downtown murals. Learn about Chandler’s origins as an agricultural town and its growth into a technology hub.

  • Year-Round Sunshine & Outdoor Fun
    From the scenic San Tan Mountains to relaxing golf resorts and family-friendly parks, Chandler offers outdoor experiences for every traveler.

Planning Your Visit

We’re here to help you make the most of your stay. Whether you’re organizing a group event or traveling independently, we can connect you with:

  • Local government and civic leaders
  • Cultural institutions and performance venues
  • Schools, business organizations, and innovation centers
  • Lodging options and group rates

Connect With Us

Let us know how we can assist with your visit. Our team is ready to assist you! We can provide visitor guides, transportation tips, and more.

Plan Your Winning Sports Tournament in Chandler, AZ

Bring Your Team to Chandler

Your partner in planning a winning tournament experience.

From first pitch to championship weekend, Chandler, Arizona, is ready to host. With championship-caliber sports facilities, team-friendly hotels, exciting local attractions, and personalized planning support, Chandler offers everything you need to create an exceptional youth sports tournament or sporting event.

Score Big with Complimentary Planning Assistance

Our sports sales team provides complimentary tournament planning assistance and local expertise to help make hosting your sporting event easier.

We can help you:

From early planning through tournament weekend, we're here to simplify the details, save you time, and create a positive experience for everyone involved.

You focus on delivering a great tournament. We'll help take care of the rest.

Simplify Communication with Custom Team Microsites

One link. Everything your teams need.

Less time answering questions. More time focusing on your event.

headings.text: Things to Do in Chandler, AZ

bodyHtml:
Things to Do in Chandler, AZ

Bursting with things to do, Chandler has developed a reputation as an inviting destination with its vibrant and diverse community and easy access to adventure and fun. Chandler offers visitors a wealth of activities and things to see and do.  From engaging art and cultural experiences to desert exploration, to enjoying a round of golf, a night on the town, or fun for the whole family, Chandler area attractions are sure to entertain.

Explore the Sonoran Desert

With easy access to the outdoors and more than 300 days of sunshine a year, there are many ways to explore the Arizona desert. Catch a sunrise view of the Sonoran skies via a hot air balloon ride or on foot with a desert hike or walk the desert trails at Veterans Oasis Park in east Chandler. The Chandler park is home to more than 150 species of birds, and the local Audubon Society provides free guided birdwalks the first Saturday of the month, November through April.

Have you always dreamed about the Old West? A popular experience is a private or group trail ride through the desert on horseback with KOLI Equestrian Center.

Arts & Culture

Chandler is filled with vibrant art and culture. From a stroll at the Vision Gallery in Downtown Chandler to a performance at the Chandler Center for the Arts, visitors are sure to view art in many different mediums. 

Art is not only found in the Chandler area attractions, but throughout the community. While out and about in the destination, keep an eye out for the amazing and vibrant Chandler murals dotting our community, painted by local and national artists that are an expression of the Chandler community.

Explore Chandler’s roots with an in-depth look at the history of Chandler alongside local and national exhibits at the Chandler Museum, located near Chandler Fashion Center mall, or pay a visit to regional attractions like the one-of-a-kind Musical Instrument Museum, located a short drive from Chandler hotels.

Fun for the Entire Family

Families have many options for kid-friendly attractions that will amuse the littlest of travelers. A must-see for train lovers of all ages, the Arizona Railway Museum is filled with information and vintage rail cars highlighting the trains of Arizona and the Southwest. Experience thrilling indoor kart races, laser tag, and more at Andretti Indoor Karting & Games for air-conditioned fun, or spend the day at the nearby Phoenix Zoo, one of the nation’s largest non-profit zoos and home to more than 3,000 animals.  For tweens and teens, an outing to Arizona's premier indoor adventure park, Rush Xtreme is next level with a large rock wall, bungee jumping, and much more!

Shopping in Chandler

Whether you are looking to treat yourself or shopping to find the perfect memento or gift to bring home, shopping in Chandler is a breeze. Chandler offers visitors a wide range of shopping experiences. Find a traditional, upscale shopping experience at Chandler Fashion Center mall featuring national retailers, local shops, and expansive food and entertainment options, and outlet shopping at the Phoenix Premium Outlets. For a more boutique experience, make your way to D'vine Gourmet in Downtown Chandler for a selection of made-in-Arizona gift basket items and handmade caramels.

Day trips from Chandler

Up for a drive? Chandler is conveniently located for exploring the best of Arizona, making it easy to enjoy a day trip to the red rocks of Sedona or head east for the recreational playground known as the White Mountains or simply take in the many metro Phoenix attractions that are within a short drive.

Browse our list of things to do in Chandler, AZ, and the surrounding area and start planning your Chandler trip today!

Stay in the know on what is happening in Chandler. Sign up for our free monthly e-newsletter, and we’ll keep you posted!

title: Days Out In Arizona | Things To Do In Downtown Chandler
metaDescription: Discover Downtown Chandler, packed with dining, entertainment, and fun. Plan your getaway with top things to do this weekend and exciting days out!
ogTitle: Days Out In Arizona | Things To Do In Downtown Chandler
bodyHtml:
Downtown Chandler

Ever walk in a city and felt like you were home? Downtown Chandler's vintage-style lanterns and trellis-covered walkways will charm you that way. That feeling is all by design. A.J. Chandler, who founded the town created it in the "City Beautiful" style, a movement popular in the late 1800s and early 1900s.  Anchoring the historic square, the San Marcos Hotel built in 1912 was quickly followed by the San Marcos Golf Course followed in 1913 and was seeded with Bermuda grass, establishing its rich history as the first grass links in course in Arizona. 

Today, Downtown Chandler is a vibrant, walkable destination brimming with activity. Here you'll discover Chandler's sustainably built City Hall,  a traditional Arizona resort, boutique shops, eclectic art galleries, entertainment options and the world-class Chandler Center for the Arts. Amidst it all are gathering spaces, engaging murals and public art that tie it all together in beauty and harmony.

In addition to all the unique shops and galleries, many residents and visitors enjoy the award-winning, local eateries with a global flair. Whether you are in the mood to grab a burger and brew at a micro-brewery, enjoy a romantic dinner for two under the stars on a lush patio with live music, or nosh the afternoon away at a craft cocktail lounge, this is one delicious destination!

Anchoring the historic square is the Crowne Plaza Phoenix Chandler Golf Resort, but the Chandler Arizona hotels are only a short drive away and many offer a courtesy shuttle, based on availability, that includes the Downtown Chandler.  Rest assured, if you are driving , the area is easily accessible with ample free parking in Downtown Chandler garages and surface parking. 

The Downtown Chandler area hosts a number of annual events ranging from running events to bar crawls and a weekly farmers market held on Saturdays.  In addition to fresh produce, visitors will find prepared foods, beverages and unique goods.  Start your Saturday off right by coming to the Downtown Chandler Farmers Market for the free yoga in the park class offered October - May, at 10 a.m.  Be sure to bring your mat, water and sunscreen.

bodyHtml:
Free (and FUN!) Things to Do in Chandler, AZ

Looking for fun that won’t stretch your budget? You’re in the right place. In Chandler, you can spend the morning wandering through colorful downtown alleys, the afternoon enjoying live music in the park, and the evening letting the kids splash to their hearts’ content—all without opening your wallet. The best part is how easy it is to stumble onto those little local moments that make a trip memorable. And when you’re ready to cool off, Chandler has plenty of indoor options too, from rainy day activities to free museums and budget‑friendly shopping spots that let you beat the heat while still exploring something new. Whether you’re here for a weekend or a week, you’ll find that some of Chandler’s greatest experiences come at little to no cost.

Quick tip: Some of the city’s most popular events are totally free, especially during festival season. From Downtown Chandler’s Third Thursdays, outdoor concerts, cultural shindigs—all the good stuff. Sign up for Visit Chandler’s newsletter before heading out. You’ll be surprised how much you can squeeze into one weekend.

Shop, Stroll & Explore

If browsing, people‑watching, and discovering new corners of the city is your idea of a good time, Chandler has plenty of ways to enjoy a day out without spending much at all. From indoor shopping escapes to outdoor markets and mural‑hunting adventures, here are a few fun (and mostly free) ways to explore.

Chandler Fashion Center

Beat the heat and wander through one of Arizona’s premier shopping destinations. The Chandler mall is fully indoor and wonderfully walkable, making it perfect for window shopping or simply stretching your legs in air‑conditioned comfort. Insider tip for practically free goodies - don’t miss SCHEELS, where you can ride the indoor Ferris wheel for just $1, a quick, quirky thrill that’s fun for all ages. And round out your visit with a stop at Round1 Bowling & Arcade for a $0.99 ice cream!

Downtown Chandler

Take a stroll through the historic square and keep an eye out for the colorful murals tucked along the downtown district's alleys and side streets. They make great photo ops and are a fun way to explore the area’s creative side.

Downtown Ocotillo

This charming neighborhood shopping and dining district offers a relaxed, lakeside vibe that’s perfect for an afternoon walk. Wander the paths around the water, browse boutique storefronts, or grab a seat on a patio and enjoy the view.

The Shoppes at Casa Paloma

A lovely spot for window shopping, this open‑air center features stylish storefronts and a relaxed, upscale atmosphere. It’s a great place to wander on a sunny morning or pair with lunch nearby.

Weekend Farmers Markets in Chandler

Downtown Chandler Farmers Market (Saturdays, year-round)

Enjoy live music, local produce, handmade goods, and donation‑based yoga at 9 a.m. The first Saturday of each month is Kids Day, with games and activities from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. Yoga and Kids Day are available seasonally, October through May.

Gilbert Farmers Market at Chandler‑Gilbert Community College (Saturdays, year‑round)

Just a short drive from your Chandler hotel, this lively market is packed with local vendors, fresh foods, and plenty of friendly community vibes.

All Culture, No Cover

Big fan of art, history, or cool cultural spots? Chandler is full of free museums and galleries perfect for whiling away an afternoon without taking a hit to your wallet.

Chandler Museum

Always free, always interesting. Here at the museum, local history meets modern design. Plus, it’s near Chandler Fashion Center so that you can make a day of it.

Vision Gallery

In the heart of Downtown Chandler, the gallery is a bright, welcoming space featuring rotating exhibits by local artists. Totally free and very chill.

Chandler Murals

Embark on the free Choose Chandler Mural Quest and discover community murals across Chandler to win a cool prize. Totally DIY and totally Insta-worthy.

Up for a quick drive? While participation is subject to change, check out these spots in and around Chandler, AZ that offer free days.

Arizona Railway Museum

Into vintage trains? You’ll love exploring old rail cars and cabooses at the Arizona Railway Museum, and tickets are free for active-duty military and children under two. Plan your visit in November, when the museum offers free admission for its Fall Rail Festival.

Huhugam Heritage Center

Learn about the culture and history of the Gila River Indian Community with rotating exhibits and outdoor trails. Open Tuesday to Friday, free admission.

Phoenix Art Museum

Explore one of the largest art collections in the Southwest for free every Wednesday evening and the first Friday of the month at the Phoenix Art Museum.

Desert Botanical Garden

Wander scenic trails lined with desert blooms and towering saguaros. The Garden offers a Community Day: Pay What You Can Day on the second Tuesday of the month (advance reservations required).

Arizona Capitol Museum

Step into Arizona’s political past with exhibits inside the historic Arizona State Capitol Museum. Always free and open to the public.

ASU Art Museum

Discover bold, modern works and experimental installations at this university-run gem. Admission is free.

Soak Up the Sun - Sports & Recreation

  • With 300-plus sunny days a year, Chandler practically dares you to stay indoors. So grab your hat, some sunscreen and go explore.
  • Hit the desert trails – Whether you’re hiking or biking, the views are unbeatable. Be sure to read up on these great desert safety tips.
  • Pack a picnic – Pick a shady spot at one of Chandler’s many beautiful parks. (Need ideas? Check out our best picnic spots blog!)
  • Veterans Oasis Park – Trails, a fishing lake, and even a scavenger hunt for little birdwatchers.
  • Desert Breeze Park – Kids love the low-cost mini train and carousel. Parents love the chill vibes.
  • Pickleball at Tumbleweed Park – 18 courts, totally free and open daily from 6 a.m. to 10:30 p.m. Courts are available on a first-come, first-served basis.
  • Third Thursdays in Downtown Chandler – From October to May, downtown turns into a big block party with artists, pop-ups, food, and music from 6 - 9 p.m.
  • Splash pads and pools – When it gets toasty, the kids can cool off at your hotel pool, free splash pads (seasonal), or low-cost-admission Chandler pools and aquatic centers.

Whether you’re browsing, strolling, or snapping photos, Chandler makes it easy to enjoy a day out and about in the community, and no big budget is required. Visit our planning page or and explore all things to do in Chandler to get a jump on planning your next visit to Chandler!
