headings.text: Indoor Family Adventures in Chandler, AZ

bodyHtml:
Indoor Family Adventures in Chandler, AZ

When the Arizona sun dials up the temperature, it’s time to take the fun inside. Chandler’s summer playbook is simple: seek shade, stay cool, and get creative. Luckily, there’s no shortage of ways to keep the whole crew engaged, active, and out of the sun. From color-splashed art spaces to adventure zones with built-in A/C, these inviting options make it easy to transition from the school year to summer break without missing a beat.

Creative Spaces for Curious Minds

If your child thrives on creativity and hands-on projects, Burst of Butterflies is a must-visit. The studio provides a variety of artistic activities, including pottery painting, canvas art, and clay wheel throwing. Whether you’re dropping in for a spontaneous session or participating in a structured class, there’s something to ignite every young artist’s imagination. The studio also hosts several enriching camps for kids—a refreshing way to beat the heat while nurturing your child’s curiosity. 

Families who love mixing inspiration with education will find discoveries packed into every corner of our museums. The Chandler Museum boasts a modern vibe, featuring rotating exhibits and family-friendly programming. The Vision Gallery showcases free, child-friendly art exhibitions filled with vibrant colors and wonder. Quiet, chilled, and full of spark, these are the kinds of places where curiosity thrives.

Don’t forget local libraries. With storytimes, summer reading programs, and STEAM-focused activities, they’re ideal for parents who want screen-free enrichment without leaving town. A little inventive spirit can make a big difference when the books are just steps away.

Action-Packed Adventures for All Ages

With kiddos, movement always beats mess, and indoor play delivers just that. Uptown Jungle Fun Park offers young explorers a chance to burn off energy on trampolines, climbing walls, a ninja course, and an obstacle course.

For puzzle-loving families, an escape room is an easy choice. Escape Chandler features themed rooms where groups work together to solve riddles, uncover clues, and beat the clock. It’s interactive, challenging, and a great way to unplug and think on your feet.

If you’re craving variety and speed all under one roof, Andretti Indoor Karting & Games is the ultimate playground for families with a competitive streak. Race electric Superkarts, dive into arcade games, conquer laser tag, and more. Refuel at the full-service restaurant, then get right back to the fun.

Another crowd-pleaser for families and groups, Round1 Bowling & Arcade is packed with bowling, arcade games, billiards, karaoke, and party packages. Visitors, young and old, can find something engaging here, where the buzzing of games meets the welcome blast of cool, conditioned air.

Cool Comforts & Family-Friendly Stops

We know shopping is a top activity to enjoy while visiting Chandler, but your kids need entertainment, and shopping at the right spots can check all the boxes. Chandler Fashion Center is more than a mall—it’s a hub for kid-friendly downtime. In addition to Round1 Bowling & Arcade, you’ll find a LEGO® store, kid zones, and plenty of spots to grab a snack and recharge. 

The layout is easy to navigate, and the options keep little ones from getting antsy while you run errands between their adventures. Movie magic is another summer staple. Harkins Theatres Chandler Fashion 20 offers an air-conditioned, quiet respite with stadium seating and parent-approved flicks.

No matter how high the temps climb, our indoor activities surround you with comfort, spark good times, and bring loved ones together. From art-filled experiences to action-packed afternoons, you don’t have to brave the sun to make summer memories. Bookmark this guide for your next summer outing, or share it with friends who are searching for ways to stay cool and entertained when the weather heats up. Discover all that our Arizona city has to offer, and start planning your visit today.

bodyHtml:
Movie Theaters in Chandler

Okay, this is sunny Arizona. But occasionally it does rain here and sometimes, your time away from home is the perfect chance to dash away for a movie.  

While it's certainly become easier to catch a movie - whether it's through an on-demand device or streaming a recent flick on your tablet, there are some great reasons to head to a Chandler, Arizona movie theater and catch a new release.  

Movie theaters offer exceptional, dark theaters showcasing sweeping views with complete surround sound that just can't be replicated on your tablet or in your hotel room.   Additionally, the food and beverage options have vastly improved with expanded snack bars, to dine-in theater options serving upscale bites and cocktails seat-side for dining and viewing enjoyment.  For your convenience, many Chandler, Arizona hotels offer a courtesy shuttle within a radius of their hotel making it easy to get to and from the hotel.

So whether you want to take a break from the weather with some indoor entertainment in a cool, dark movie theater or unwind from a busy day of meetings with a visit to a Chandler, Arizona movie theater, a trip to the cinema is a great outing.

ogTitle: Chandler Museums & Art Galleries | Performing Arts Center
bodyHtml:
Chandler Museums

Chandler is a hub for arts and culture activities offering a diverse array of activities.  The Chandler Center for the Arts plays host to a variety of performing arts, music performance in addition to museums, gallery exhibitions, public art, festivals, and more to fill your desire for learning more about the local arts and culture scene.

Across the street from Chandler Fashion Center mall lies the Chandler Museum.  The facility features rotating national and regional exhibits and serves as a research and archive center for Chandler's history and cultural heritage.  On Saturdays, the museum offers free family programming with hands-on activities for children. The museum also hosts a variety of events throughout the year that explore the region's agricultural roots at Tumbleweed Ranch which features a 1917 home, a historic grocery store and vintage farm equipment.

Train lovers of all ages will enjoy a visit to Chandler's very own Arizona Railway Museum which is home to vintage rail cars used in bygone eras for local and long distance rail travels. The museum acquires, preserves, and displays rail cars used during train travel's heydays. Among the displays are a Santa Fe caboose, an Alaska RR dining car, and Southern Railway Business Car along with information about Arizona's historic railways. The open-air museum is operated by volunteers and open Saturdays and Sundays from noon - 4 p.m. from September through May.  Admission for children ages 2-12 is $2.00, ages 13+ are $5.00 and family admission is $15.00.

Chandler art galleries showcasing local and regional artists and exhibits may be found at the Vision Gallery and the Gallery at CCA.  Both are located in Downtown Chandler, making it easy to spend part of the day with a meal, a visit to the galleries and a stroll through the historic square which is home to more than 60 pieces of public art.

Chandler has a dynamic public art program representing its rich, cultural diversity. While Downtown Chandler has a large collection of public art, Chandler's vast array of public art is showcased in City buildings, parks and public spaces throughout the community.

For performing arts, head to the Chandler Center for the Arts offers superb acoustics for viewing a variety of live performances within walking distance to Downtown Chandler's unique restaurants and nightlife.

Explore Arizona's Native American Culture

Located near Chandler, the Huhugam Heritage Center and situated on the Gila River Museum is a tribal facility for the preservation and display of important cultural artifacts and art.  The Huhugam Heritage Center is a climate-controlled repository for prehistoric and historic artifacts, cultural materials and vital records. The museum displays these materials to the public, and periodic traveling art and history shows.

In the fall, Chandler highlights its unique cultural heritage with key events.  At the Chandler Center for the Arts, is a local favorite, C.A.L.L.E. de Arizona's bright and colorful, Mariachi and Folklorico Festival.

Come November, discover the rich history of the original food truck as Chandler honors the history of the chuck wagon with a unique culinary competition that combines the tastes, smells, and sounds of the Old West. Teams work from authentic 1880s-style chuck wagons to cook five courses: bread, beans, meat, potatoes, and dessert. The Chandler Chuck Wagon Festival is a two-day event perfect for all ages.

title: Arizona Railway Museum | Step Into the Rail of Yesterday
metaDescription: At Arizona Railway Museum, travel back in time to discover jaw-dropping restorations of railroad history.
ogTitle: Arizona Railway Museum | Step Into the Rail of Yesterday

headings.text: What is the Arizona Railway Museum?

bodyHtml:
Arizona Railway Museum

Founded in 1983, the Arizona Railway Museum in Chandler, AZ, is a magical place with something for every age and family member. Among the many treasures featured at the museum are meticulously restored train cars from different periods of railroad history in the United States.

Thanks to the dedication of the organization's restoration team, the museum's train cars are among those featured in movies like 3:10 to Yuma, Stay Tuned, Terror Train, and There Will Be Blood.

What is the Arizona Railway Museum?

A nonprofit, educational, and historical organization, the Arizona Railway Museum is "dedicated to the railways of Arizona and the Southwest" and operated by volunteers. This paradise for rail enthusiasts works to acquire, renovate, and preserve rail cars, equipment, and other artifacts and keepsakes from former and current railway eras.

The museum's collection is impressive, with a primary focus on Arizona railroads and those of the Southwest.

If you are visiting with young kids in tow, consider extending your experience in the area and enjoy a picnic lunch at neighboring Tumbleweed Park filled with many tables and ramadas and a 2.5-acre playground, Playtopia.

What to Expect 

At the Arizona Railway Museum, visitors will delight in the extensive collection of rail cars in the rail yard, two of which are listed on the National Register of Historic Places. One is the breathtaking Southern Pacific Railroad Locomotive No. SP 2562, built in 1906. The other is the Railroad Steam Wrecking Crane and Tool Car, originally assembled in 1949.

On self-guided tours, visitors can explore the yard and view the equipment up close. Each piece has a nearby placard providing historical information. Visitors can also walk through several passenger cars and a caboose to check out the interior. Please note that the railcars are not accessible by wheelchair due to preserving the original widths of doors and hallways and requires visitors to climb stairs to enter and exit.

Group tours are available on a limited basis for a small fee. Please contact the museum for details. Passenger cars and cabooses are available for birthday parties. Meeting spaces are also available.

The museum's main building is a striking re-creation of the original Chandler Depot. Guests can view genuine rail company glass and china, railroad artifacts, and explore the gift shop. With more than 42,000 railroad-associated artifacts cataloged in the museum's archives, this unbelievable collection is available by appointment only for academic research. 

On select days, volunteers at this Chandler train museum bring history to life by operating model trains. The models traverse through detailed layouts of towns, industrial areas, and train stations. 

Good to Know

Closed for Summer
Historically, the museum is closed in June, July, and August.

Location
330 E. Ryan Rd., Chandler, AZ 85286

The outdoor train yard ground is crushed rock, so make sure to wear comfortable shoes and a hat.

Hours of Operation

  • Monday: Closed
  • Tuesday: Closed 
  • Wednesday: Closed  
  • Thursday: Closed
  • Friday: Closed
  • Saturday: 10:00 AM – 4:00 PM
  • Sunday: 10:00 AM – 4:00 PM

The museum is closed for Christmas Eve, Christmas Day, New Year’s Day, and Easter Sunday.

Admission Fees
Infant (Under 2 years): Free

Child (2-12 years): $10
Adult (12+ years): $15
Family (2 Adults, 3 Children): $40
Active Military: Free with ID (ARM is a Blue Star Museum)

The Arizona Railway Museum should be on the must-see list of any railroad lover, young or old. Even those without a passion for trains will appreciate visiting bygone eras and investigating all the fascinating artifacts and memorabilia. 

Visit the Arizona Railway Museum website to plan your visit today. While there, look into the membership options, which give you access to special events, member voting rights, and the museum’s quarterly newsletter. 

Please confirm operating hours, fees, and the most up-to-date information with the venue before your visit.

bodyHtml:
Chandler Art Galleries

Chandler art galleries are as varied as its residents, showcasing art from a variety of local, regional and national artists.  Admission to these Chandler art galleries is free of charge.

Downtown Chandler Art Galleries

The Gallery at CCA and The Vision Gallery are both located in the downtown area with easy access to free Downtown Chandler parking and within walking distance to the Crowne Plaza Phoenix Chandler Golf Resort and the Hilton Garden Inn.  Make a day of it and grab a bite or drink at one of the many restaurants and bars that call the historic square home.

Vision Gallery

Located in Downtown Chandler, this large, contemporary art gallery is perfect for art enthusiasts looking to connect and interact with local and regional artists.   Visitors to the gallery will find a varied palette of original artworks and exhibitions showcasing ceramics, oil and acrylic canvasses, printmaking, sculpture, multi-media art and more. 

The Vision Gallery is also home to an Art-O-Mat, one of two in Chandler. The Art-O-Mats are vending machines from which you can purchase miniature pieces of art - from jewelry to photos or paintings. A unique grab bag concept that's fun and whimsical!

The Gallery at CCA

Located inside the Chandler Center of the Arts, the Gallery at CCA hosts a variety of exhibitions throughout the year showcasing original art in a variety of media. Recent shows have celebrated mixed media, textiles, sculpture and more.

Visitors may commemorate their visit with the purchase of art for $5 cash at the Art-O-Mat machine located at the gallery. This "arts vending machine" makes art accessible and fun for all!

bodyHtml:
Chandler Center for the Arts

The awe-inspiring Chandler Center for the Arts, located in vibrant Downtown Chandler, showcases various performing and visual arts. With multiple spaces to enjoy, each offering something unique, this top Chandler attraction is a fantastic way to elevate your Chandler experience.

Round out your afternoon or evening with a meal and a show at the Chandler Center for the Arts. The performing arts venue is close to several Downtown Chandler restaurants, so you can easily enjoy a pre-show dinner and cocktails or treat yourself to dessert after the final act.

What is the Chandler Center for the Arts?

Since its grand opening in August 1989, the Chandler Center for the Arts has been a significant landmark of arts and culture in the city. In addition to serving over 210,000 guests annually and an impressive calendar of concerts and performances, the Center does big things for the community with its youth outreach programs.

The enchanting Steena Murray Mainstage Theatre, the Center’s largest space, has a maximum capacity of 1,508. At a more intimate 346 seats, the Hal Bogle Theatre provides a cozy atmosphere and ear-catching acoustics. The 246-seat Recital Hall Theatre is perfect for smaller showings like lectures, presentations, and paired-down recitals. Finally, the 2,000-square-foot Gallery at CCA, one of Chandler's art galleries featuring the work of local, regional and national artists.

What Type of Performances Will You See? 

From symphony orchestras to comedians to ballet, theater, and concerts, the Chandler Center for the Arts offers a wide array of artistic offerings. Notable past performers include Kansas, Joss Stone, Clint Black, Amy Grant, and Boz Scaggs.

Know Before You Go

Location
250 N Arizona Ave, Chandler, AZ 85225

Phone
(480) 782-2680

Chandler Center for the Arts Tickets

Patrons can purchase tickets online through Ticketmaster. Members or those who have registered a child for camp can buy tickets online through their Account Manager. 

Parking

Located on the northwest corner of Chandler Blvd. and Arizona Ave., the Chandler Center for the Arts offers FREE on-site parking on the west side of the building. Additional free parking is available at five parking garages and surface parking in the downtown area.

Tickets are available for purchase in person at the Chandler Center for the Arts:
Monday – Friday: 10 AM – 5 PM
Saturday: Noon – 5 PM

Purchase tickets by phone: (480) 782-2680

For showtimes and to purchase tickets online, visit the Chandler Center for the Arts website.

Box Office and Will Call windows open one hour before the start time of ticketed events.

Before your visit, please check with the venue for the most up-to-date information.

The Chandler Center for the Arts is a breathtaking venue with multiple ways to catch a memorable performance. Please take a look at their schedule of events. You’re sure to find several shows that speak to your interests.

bodyHtml:
Chandler Museum

The Chandler Museum comprises the historic McCullough-Price House (listed on the National Register of Historic Places) and a modern 10,000 sq ft facility serving as the primary museum space and an expansive courtyard. The museum is easily accessed from the 101 and 202 freeways across from Chandler Fashion Center mall in an area brimming with restaurants and entertainment - making it an easy outing.

Located a short drive from the museum, Tumbleweed Ranch features an up close and personal look at Chandler's agricultural origins with historic homes, 1900s grocery store, antique agricultural equipment and more. You’ll find Tumbleweed Ranch at the southwest corner of Tumbleweed Park. Currently, this location is closed for site improvements.

What to Expect

A trip to the Chandler Museum campus is a rewarding, enriching time for the entire family. The museum’s modern architecture—a work of art itself—is a striking complement to the historic Pueblo Revival style of McCullough-Price House, which today functions as a cutting-edge archive and research site.

Outdoors, the sculpture Infinite Shade, a shade structure, helps cool the courtyard by day while lending a touch of magic by night with its multicolored light.

Each year, the Chandler Museum’s exhibit hall features six to eight exhibitions. These include museum-produced exhibits exploring Chandler’s history and nationally traveling exhibits that examine art, culture, and history.

The museum’s mission states it is an “interdisciplinary learning environment where the community comes together to share its stories, preserve its cultural heritage, and experience Chandler as a people and place.”

This mission comes to life through the museum's many public programs. Through intriguing educational programs, 3 to 5 years olds, youth and adults benefit from demonstrations, lectures, and activities. Examples include Art Tots, where the little ones learn about and make age-appropriate art and History Bites: Lunchtime Talks, where adults discover Chandler's rich history during 30-minute talks given by local experts and museum curators. 

The museum hosts a book club, offers 45-minute docent-guided tours of the campus, a Stories Speakers Series for adults, and a play day for families where iconic games and toys are available. 

Time Commitment 

Depending on the speed at which you take in an exhibit, expect your Chandler Museum visit to last anywhere from one to several hours or more. Where one visitor may glance over an exhibit for 10 minutes, another could become absorbed for much longer.

If you are visiting the museum for a public program, please reference the official museum website so you can set aside the time needed. 

Know Before You Go

Chandler Museum Location
300 S. Chandler Village Drive
Chandler, AZ 85226

Phone
(480) 782-2717

Chandler Museum Admission Fees
Admission to the Chandler Museum is free.

Hours:
Tuesday through Saturday: 10 AM – 5 PM
Sunday: 1 PM – 5 PM

Before visiting, we encourage you to check with the museum for the most up-to-date information.

Whether you’re looking to visit the Chandler Museum or Tumbleweed Ranch, make a plan today by viewing their website for a full listing of current and upcoming exhibits and public programs.

title: Chandler Nightlife | Spots for Drinks, Music and Late Nights
metaDescription: Experience Chandler nightlife with lively patios, craft beer spots, and energetic bars offering music and chef‑driven menus.
ogTitle: Chandler Nightlife | Spots for Drinks, Music and Late Nights
bodyHtml:
Chandler Nightlife

Dining, dancing, meeting new people and having fun. Whether you want a casual night out with friends or an exciting escape, Chandler nightlife will help you find your groove with endless options. From the country-inspired, boot-stompin’ fun at Bourbon Jack's American Tavern, the live music and energy at a local gastropub, Good Time Charli’s or chillaxing on a fire pit-adorned patio – because grabbing a drink and enjoying it on a starlit patio is always more fun.

A post-work day with friends and colleagues may find you at any number of casual bars and restaurants with chef-driven menus, craft cocktails and casual bars with patios full of ambiance. Located in Downtown Chandler, the QuartHaus is a laid-back, beer garden-inspired wine bar featuring a rotating list of food trucks, live music and interactive games like cornhole and basketball. Or perhaps you’re looking for a high-energy bar patio for a quick drink and a few high fives before the weekend starts, you’ll find Hop Social Grill and Thirsty Lion Gastropub & Grill both within the Chandler Fashion Center mall area to be great options.

If a date night is on your mind or an evening out with dear friends – Brickyard Downtown in Downtown Chandler is a great option with its seasonal menu of globally inspired, creative New American plates and craft cocktails and modern-industrial setting. In south Chandler, neighborhood favorite, Stone & Vine Urban Italian is a contemporary Italian restaurant with a breezy patio and full bar.

The craft beer scene is alive and well in Chandler with a number of brewpubs and gastropubs serving up their own local pints or featuring the best of the best in craft beer. From easy-drinking lagers to dark stouts and feisty IPAs, you’re sure to find a brew that you will enjoy. 

Can’t decide on a specific brewery? Consider a visit to Craft 64 Chandler, a very local hot spot featuring 36 rotating taps featuring a large variety of styles of Arizona brews in addition to their own brews served alongside made-from-scratch wood-fired pizza. Or head over to The Hungry Monk – a lively hot spot that is home to 27 drafts and over 20 bottled selections and a menu that focuses on sourcing local ingredients. In west Chandler, craft beer and BBQ are the stars of the show at the neighborhood tap room, Helluva Brewing Company and in south Chandler you’ll want to make your way to The Casual Pint where their “beer-tenders” will help you find the best craft brew for you.

SanTan Brewing Company, located in Downtown Chandler not only has the prestige of being Chandler’s first microbrewery – but is now Arizona’s largest brewery. Located in a historic building, the brewery features a large patio and vibrant atmosphere and now a new distillery features a selection of year-round suds and seasonal brews to accompany their own distilled single malt whiskey, Kaffir Lime Vodka and SanTan Vodka. Follow up your visit with a tour at their Uptown Chandler to see Arizona's largest combined brewery and distillery.

A stone’s throw from the historic square of Downtown Chandler, The Perch Pub & Brewery features a rooftop bar and lush, courtyard patio which is home to more than 50 rescued tropical birds. The pub features over 40 craft beers in addition to their own, ever-changing selection of house brews. 

In central Chandler, H.O.P. Central Brewing Company and Tap Room is a locally-owned brewery and tap room featuring more than 36 craft beer and wine taps.

headings.text: Gila River Casinos - Lone Butte Casino
Gila River Casinos - Wild Horse Pass Casino

bodyHtml:
Chandler Casinos

Feeling lucky? Head to one of three Chandler, Arizona area casinos for some gaming fun - just minutes away from your Chandler hotel! Local casinos offer games like blackjack, poker, slot machines, and bingo for your gaming enjoyment. Try their on-site restaurants and lounges for entertainment too. 

Gila River Casinos - Lone Butte Casino

Visit Lone Butte Casino, just south of Chandler at the 202 Santan Freeway and Kyrene, for all your gaming entertainment. Lone Butte has a variety of games for all types of players including over 1,200 slots and a High Limit Slot Room and Electronic Table games area. The casino is also home to table games and poker. Dine at the Fullhouse Café or grab your favorite cocktail or beverage at The River Bar.

Table games feature Blackjack, 3 Card Poker Progressive or Ultimate Texas Hold’em Progressive. Lone Butte Casino has 20 tables with limits for all types of players ranging from $5 to $1,300.

Lone Butte’s 8,000 square feet Poker Room has 30 tables with a private entrance and convenient parking. Nine 90-inch screens are featured as well as a video wall.

Gila River Casinos - Wild Horse Pass Casino

The Wild Horse Pass Casino has exciting gaming action to suit everyone. The 100,000-square-foot, non-smoking casino located off the I-10 East and Wild Horse Pass Blvd, pops with over 1,100 slot machines and a High Limit Slot room featuring a great selection of games. Table games include Blackjack, Craps, Roulette, Baccarat and more. 

Dining and lounge options abound at Wild Horse Pass, with its rooftop lounge and restaurant, Prime, a Shula's Steak House and Asian-themed Ling & Louie's Asian Bar.

Gaming fans can also get their share of entertainment in The Showroom venue.

Casino Arizona

Just minutes north of Chandler on the 101 Freeway is a gaming experience on the Salt River Indian Reservation. Casino Arizona offers poker, slots, blackjack, keno, bingo and more.

Dining options include the fine-dining Cholla Steakhouse along with four other restaurants for casino-goers. Lounges include the Showroom, which is a 250-seat cabaret-style music and entertainment venue. Casino Arizona has featured some of the most popular performers from the world of jazz, country music, rock and popular music, as well as comedy, production reviews, dance and magic.

Things to Know 

  • In Arizona, the minimum age to gamble is 21.
  • Kids are welcome in the dining and entertainment areas, but not allowed on the casino floor. 
  • Many casinos permit smoking indoors as The Smoke-Free Arizona Act does not apply on tribal land.

bodyHtml:
Chandler Wildlife & Outdoor Recreation

With more than 300 days of sunshine and the beautiful Sonoran Desert terrain, Chandler is ideal for outdoor enthusiasts who like to hike, mountain bike, cycle, horseback ride, kayak, fishing, and hot air ballooning.

If you’re visiting in the warmer months, then you and the kids will love our waterparks and pools. You can even float down the Salt River!

Most regional parks and trails are open from sunrise to sunset, but no matter where you venture out to in the Sonoran Desert, don’t forget basic safety tips - let someone know where you’re going, apply your sunscreen, wear appropriate shoes and always drink plenty of water!

Birding

While Chandler is generally thought of as an urban destination, the community has been recognized as one of Arizona's premier birding sites, specifically Chandler's Veterans Oasis Park.

Perfect for experienced and novice bird enthusiasts, Veterans Oasis Park is home to over 150 species of birds - many of which may find their names on one's life list for active birders.  The area also is a habitat for burrowing owls. Early risers who walk the park's 4.5 miles of trails might just spot the owls or other birds such as Red-tailed Hawk, American Kestrel, herons, and egrets.

Before you head to the park, be sure to explore the City of Chandler birding information to see the various birding programs available.

Families will want to make plans for the FREE Family Bird Walks led by Desert Rivers Audubon Society the first Saturday of the month, November- April at Veterans Oasis Park. 

Birders with an interest in more information may find a helpful tool with the Desert Rivers Audubon's mobile app available on iTunes and Android, Guide to 101 Birding Sites which provides more than a birds-eye view of four sites, including the Veterans Oasis Park in Chandler. App users will discover current, aerial photos, seasonal bird lists, site overviews and specific site data.

After you've scoured the park and identified a number of birds on your list - consider a visit to The Perch Bar Pub & Brewery in Downtown Chandler.  The unique and creative brew pub is home to more than 60 rescue birds surrounding a lush courtyard serving upscale gastro-pub fare and 40 beers on tap, 20 of which are Perch beers.

headings.text: Tips for Navigating Chandler’s Bike Network
More Ways to Explore the Sonoran Desert

bodyHtml:
Chandler Bike Paths

Chandler is a bike-friendly city with a well-connected and growing network of trails, making it easy to explore on two wheels. With abundant sunshine and scenic desert surroundings, the city is great for cyclists of all experience levels. Whether riding with your family, training for distance, or seeking an off-road adventure, we have the bike trail for you. This guide offers an overview of the types of trails available, their difficulty levels, and tips for navigating Chandler’s cycling network.

Trail Types & Riding Levels

Cyclists will delight in several types of Chandler bike paths designed for different riding styles. For casual riders and families, mostly paved urban shared-use paths are a great fit. The Paseo Trail along the eastern side of the Consolidated Canal features a wide, mostly paved surface. It is fantastic for all skill levels.

Expanding on that route, the Consolidated Canal Path—which includes the Paseo Trail—is an 18-mile network of developed multi-use trails that links the community with neighboring cities like Gilbert and Mesa. With convenient access points, nearby parks, parking, and restrooms along the way, it’s a favorite among locals for its comfort, connectivity, and ease of use.

Riders seeking more scenic and natural experiences can explore multi-use trails through city parks and desert landscapes. Veterans Oasis Park offers paved and dirt trails, allowing cyclists to enjoy the region’s unique desert views and wildlife habitat. The area also includes mountain bike trails, delivering mild elevation changes and dirt paths ideal for beginner to intermediate off-road riders—a great way to experience rugged terrain and desert beauty without ever leaving the town.

Those craving to swap pavement for panoramic desert trails will find San Tan Mountain Regional Park just a short drive from Chandler. The park offers an unforgettable off-road biking experience. With over 8 miles of shared-use trails, the park welcomes mountain bikers to explore routes that range from easy loops to more strenuous climbs. Surrounded by stunning desert vistas, riders can enjoy a variety of trail lengths, making it a versatile destination for both casual and experienced mountain bikers.

The trail surfaces include paved, gravel, and natural dirt, providing options for every skill level. Riders can choose from smooth canal paths for a relaxed cruise or try out narrow, twisty dirt tracks for some technical fun. This variety makes this region ideal for recreational and performance-oriented cyclists. Looking for more route inspiration? Explore additional trail suggestions to keep your wheels spinning.

Tips for Navigating Chandler’s Bike Network

This vibrant desert community continues to invest in cycling infrastructure, including efforts to maintain and signpost its bike paths. This support makes it much easier to explore by bike. For route planning, riders can use the city’s online bicycle paths and trail maps or mobile apps to track distance, elevation, and access points.

During the warmer months, the best time to ride is in the cooler hours of the morning. It’s vital to stay hydrated, wear sun protection, and take breaks in shaded areas. Also, be mindful of trail etiquette—always exercise caution, pass with care, use hand signals, and share the path with pedestrians.

With a wide variety of trails, from flat family routes to exciting dirt loops, this cycling-friendly destination makes biking accessible and enjoyable year-round. Whether you’re visiting or a local, there’s always a new trail to explore. Ready to ride? Plan your visit and discover the best of Chandler on two wheels.

bodyHtml:
Hiking in Chandler, AZ

There are many ways to explore the great outdoors - and a favorite of visitors and residents alike is a walk or hike at one of the many popular hiking and walking trails in and around Chandler.  Before you head out, brush up on some hiking safety tips before you start that hike!

Located in east Chandler, Veterans Oasis Park is a combination of parkland, lake, and wetlands/groundwater recharge basins that are fun for all ages and abilities. It has 4.5 miles of trails where you can hike, ride a bike, or meander while bird-watching.  Science buffs will also enjoy the park's Solar System Walk, is a series of concrete monuments that represent the significant objects in our solar system. The walk is a scale representation of the solar system's major objects. It is set up along a 2,500-foot pathway around the lake. The concrete monuments are spaced at distances relative to their scale in the solar system.

Looking more for a leisurely stroll, check out the Paseo trail - part of the 315-mile Maricopa Trail that runs through metro Phoenix connecting parks is a great way to explore the area.  

To the west, you'll find South Mountain Park and Preserve with more than 50 miles of trails to explore.

Hiking in San Tan Mountain Regional Park and Preserve offers more than 8 miles of trails for hiking, mountain biking, and horseback riding. Trails range from 1.1 miles to more than 5 miles, and range in difficulty from easy to strenuous.

headings.text: KOLI Equestrian Center at Wild Horse Pass
More Ways to Explore the Desert

bodyHtml:
Chandler Horseback Riding

One of the best ways to enjoy the scenic landscape of the Arizonan desert is on horseback. Blazing the trails certainly captures the western spirit and many companies in and around Chandler, AZ offer guided horseback trail rides.

Most visitors experience horseback riding by booking a small group trail ride that depart at pre-determined times for 60 or 90 minute horseback trail rides. These guided horseback rides are well suited for new and novice riders as the terrain is easily crossed and the rides are leisurely paced allowing riders to enjoy the gorgeous Arizona desert and take photos along the way. For more experienced riders seeking a faster paced horseback riding experience, inquire about private guided trail rides that can generally be tailored to your schedule when booked in advance.

At check-in with the various horseback riding companies, horse wranglers will inquire about your riding experience and will select horses for riders based on riding ability.

Located a short drive from Chandler hotels is the KOLI Equestrian Center, offering horseback riding adventures, hay wagon rides and cattle drives. The facility is also able to host corporate events and social celebrations like reunions and birthday parties with fantastic desert views.

Arizona horseback riding companies offer seasonal hours and weather as well as holidays may adjust availability. Reservations are strongly encouraged for all rides.

For more experienced riders seeking a faster paced horseback riding experience, inquire about private guided trail rides that can generally be tailored to your schedule when booked in advance. At check-in with the various horseback riding companies, horse wranglers will inquire about your riding experience and will select horses for riders based on riding ability. title: Parks & Hiking Trails in Chandler | Outdoor Activities
metaDescription: Explore scenic parks, nature trails, and outdoor recreation. Embrace Arizona’s beauty and plan your next adventure today!
ogTitle: Chandler Parks & Trails | Hiking, Biking & Walking
bodyHtml:
Chandler Parks & Trails

Paseo Vista Trail is a 6.5-mile multi-use pathway and runs along the Consolidated Canal from Galveston Street south to Riggs Road. Here, you can walk, jog or bicycle the paved eastern side, or bicycle or horseback ride on the unimproved path on the western side of the canal. Parking is available at Tibshraeny Family Park and Tumbleweed Park.

South Mountain Park is the largest municipal park in the world and has a network of 58 miles of trails suitable for hiking, trail running, horseback riding and mountain bike riding. No wonder National Geographic named Phoenix one of the nation’s best hiking cities! Javelina Canyon Trail, which begins at Beverly Canyon parking lot at 46th Street, is the easiest trail. For a panoramic view of the entire Valley, hike (or drive) the 5.5 miles up to Summit Road at Dobbins Lookout.

The San Tan Regional Park is a little over a half hour drive from Downtown Chandler, making it extremely popular for hiking and mountain bikers who like to test themselves on the 5.1-mile San Tan Trail. Or you can hike to the three-mile Goldmine Trail for a bird’s eye view of Phoenix, Queen Creek and San Tan Valley. It’s also a great place for horseback riders and picnickers.

If you’re looking to stay closer to town, Tempe Town Lake is a two-mile-long, man-made lake adjacent to the Arizona State University campus and features a number of watersports. Papago Park is another great option and is perfect for a quick trail run.

title: Urban Fishing in Chandler, AZ | Lakes, Parks & Regulations
metaDescription: Take a day off for urban fishing in Chandler, AZ with locations that are seasonally stocked. Enjoy a day of outdoor recreation during your visit.
ogTitle: Urban Fishing in Chandler, AZ | Lakes, Parks & Regulations
bodyHtml:
Urban Fishing in Chandler, AZ

If you like to fish, why not cast your line in Chandler's urban fishing program? During fall, winter and spring, the Arizona Game and Fish Department stocks the Chandler lakes with Channel catfish, Rainbow trout, Largemouth bass and sunfish. Anglers can find fish in the lakes of two Chandler parks: Desert Breeze Park and Veterans Oasis Park.

Desert Breeze Lake is four acres with an average depth of eight feet and a maximum depth of 12 feet and also known as Chandler's first fishing lake. In addition to great fishing, the lake is an excellent choice for a fishing trip with the kids. Surrounded by an active park with a dedicated playing area featuring climbing structures, a spray pad and a vintage, open-top train and a charming antique carousel.  

Located in east Chandler, Veterans Oasis Park is five acres with an average depth of five feet and a maximum depth of 14 feet.  This lake has a more natural feel to it as it is designed as a more natural oasis, surrounded by desert shrubs.  In addition to great fishing, the park is an excellent place to see birds as one of the premiere birding spots in the area featuring desert walking trails and a self-guided Chandler Solar System Walk around the lake.

Stocking schedules are posted on the Arizona Game & Fish Department (AZGFD) website. Exact dates are not disclosed, but the week are listed. A valid fishing license is required and is available online at several Chandler retailers including Walmart, Sport Chalet and Big 5 Sporting Goods.

metaDescription: Plan your trip to a tee with a list of Chandler golf courses perfect for your Arizona golf vacation. Find info on course locations, prices and amenities.
ogTitle: Chandler AZ Golf Courses | Arizona Golf Vacations
bodyHtml:
Chandler Golf Courses

Arizona is a golfer's paradise. And nowhere is this more evident than in the beautiful city of Chandler, Arizona. With a total of seven golf courses totaling 153 holes and averaging 5,725 yards each, Chandler is known as one of the leading cities for golf in Arizona.

It was more than a century ago when the state's very first grass golf course, the San Marcos Golf Course opened  in Chandler, Arizona and began a great Arizona golf tradition.  Today, the San Marcos Golf Course, located adjacent to the Crowne Plaza Phoenix Chandler Golf Resort continues to be a popular spot for out-of-town visitors and guests visiting Downtown Chandler.

Chandler, Arizona golf is a perfect activity for both locals and visitors offering sweeping views of impeccably groomed greens, majestic water features and beautiful desert horticulture providing a memorable backdrop for an Arizona golf outing. Nestled in Phoenix's East Valley, Chandler is surrounded by beautiful mountain ranges in every direction that light up bright red at sunrise and sunset, adding to the drama of an intense round of golf. Every season has something to offer on a Chandler golf course, whether you are a casual or competitive player. You'll love the experience of playing on a Chandler golf course...it is one of the many reasons to love Chandler, Arizona!

Whether you are looking to get in a round of golf on your next business trip, plan a couple of foursomes or plan a golf tournament - take your pick form our list of Chandler golf courses including the historic San Marcos Golf Course, the stunning Ocotillo Golf Club designed by course architect Ted Robinson, Bear Creek Golf Complex, the Springfield Golf Resort, Sunbird Golf Club, Lone Tree Golf Club and Ironwood Golf Club.

Professional Sports

If you're a fan of professional sports, Arizona is the place to be to see one of Arizona's professional sports teams play.   With game facilities located minutes from Chandler, it's easy to take in a game during your Chandler trip as Arizona is home to three of the major professional sports leagues. Depending on the season, sports fans can catch the NFL's Arizona Cardinals, the NBA's Phoenix Suns, and the MLB's Arizona Diamondbacks.

In addition, fans of the WNBA can catch Phoenix Mercury and indoor football enthusiasts can catch the Arena Football League's Arizona Rattlers.  

Soccer fans can catch Arizona's highest-level soccer franchise and cheer for the USL's Phoenix Rising FC on the pitch, established in 2016, the team won the 2023 USL Championship.  

The Greater Phoenix metropolitan area also hosts several sporting events each year including the Fiesta Bowl, the PGA's Waste Management Phoenix Open, NASCAR events each spring and fall at Phoenix Raceway; and Cactus League Spring Training where baseball fans can get up close and personal to 15 teams that train and play each February and March.

title: Shopping in Chandler, Arizona | Shops, Stores & More
metaDescription: Treat yourself to a shopping spree in Chandler. Browse top stores and hidden gems in the city's best shops
ogTitle: Shopping in Chandler, Arizona | Shops, Stores & More
bodyHtml:
Shopping in Chandler, AZ

Are you looking for that perfect Chandler souvenir or a gift to bring home for family and friends? Chandler offers a diverse shopping scene that visitors have come to love. From spending the day at a traditional mall for a mix of favorite national and local retailers, a leisurely stroll at a Chandler farmers market perusing tasty treats and locally-made crafts, spending the afternoon in historic Downtown Chandler or visiting Chandler's best shopping boutiques - you're sure to find the best Chandler shopping experience to suit your mood.

 View our list below of popular shopping areas for the best shopping in Chandler, AZ!

Chandler Fashion Center Mall

A premier regional mall, Chandler Fashion Center is a popular, two-level shopping mall anchored by Dillard’s, Macy’s and the world’s largest destination sports store, SCHEELS. Shop some of your favorite Chandler Fashion Center stores including Apple, COACH, H&M, lululemon, Kendra Scott, MINISO, Bath & Body, LEGO, Sephora, Pottery Barn and more. The Chandler shopping mall boasts numerous entertainment options including Round1 Bowling & Arcade, Harkins 20-screen movie theatre, an escape room, a designated play area for the kids, comfortable seating areas throughout the mall, fun photo opp displays and murals for selfies and family photos, an outdoor splash pad and a variety of yard games. If you are looking for food options that could satisfy your most picky eater, there are a variety of Chandler Fashion Center restaurants in and around the mall including The Cheesecake Factory, Hop Social Grill, The Keg Steakhouse + Bar, PF Chang’s, and many fast-casual options.

The Shoppes at Casa Paloma

Located in West Chandler, at Ray Road and the I-10, The Shoppes at Casa Paloma is a premier outdoor shopping mall featuring boutique shops, national retailers, and a tasty selection of eateries for your dining pleasure. Grab a bite to eat at one of the restaurants including Grimaldi's Pizzeria or a light snack and refreshment with a visit to the Nekter Juice Bar.

Downtown Shopping & Souvenirs

Head to Downtown Chandler and pick up a unique Arizona souvenir at a Chandler boutique shop. d'Vine Gourmet features a variety of items from local artists and vendors, plus the best of Arizona-made fine foods, wine, and gift baskets. The historic downtown square is great for a stroll and a meal. Home to vibrant murals and more than forty restaurants and bars, from casual, healthy options at The Original ChopShop to modern fare at Jinya Ramen Bar or BlackSheep Wine Bar & Merchant, or southern comfort food with a Southwest twist at Bourbon Jack's American Tavern. After the shopping is done, enjoy an Arizona craft beer on the patio at SanTan Brewing Company, or an expertly mixed cocktail at SanTan Spirit House Coffee & Cocktails, Hidden House, Brickyard Downtown and The Ostrich and celebrate your shopping wins.

Phoenix Premium Outlets

Find the best Chandler outlet shopping experience with a visit to the Phoenix Premium Outlets featuring name-brand retailers offering discounted savings on designer goods. The outdoor shopping area is a popular, Phoenix outlet mall with more than 90 brands outlet shoppers love, including Coach Outlet, Michael Kors Outlet, Brooks Brothers Factory Store, Marc Jacobs and more.

Antiques

Antique enthusiasts and pickers will want to make sure a visit the Merchant Square is on the itinerary.  With more than 200 merchants selling collectibles, jewelry, furniture and more - this is a large, indoor antique marketplace you won't want to miss.  One weekend a month, Highland Yard Vintage makes an appearance behind Merchant Square for a four-day, indoor, air-conditioned  one-of-a-kind shopping extravaganza in Chandler, AZ.  The event features curated pieces from Arizona designers with unique items for the home and yard.  No visit to Merchant Square is complete without a meal at the American Way Smokehouse housed on the north side of the marketplace.  Whether you select one of their smokehouse favorites or fresh salad - you'll find yourself inspired by vintage American craftsmanship and antiques.  

Arizona's Largest Candy Store

For those with a sweet tooth, or a younger one in tow, will want to make their way to Arizona's largest candy store, Sweeties Candy of Arizona located in Uptown Chandler.  The candy emporium sells nostalgic and current sweet treats along with a large selection of bulk candies.  Located in the same plaza as Sweeties, pizza lovers will find authentic, Neapolitan-style pizza at Bella Gusto Urban Pizzeria.

It is no surprise that Chandler is often described as a shopper's paradise with all of these great options!

Chandler Fashion Center Mall

Shopping enthusiasts will enjoy a visit to Chandler Fashion Center, the second-largest mall in the metropolitan Phoenix area. This regional mall is the Southeast Valley’s premier shopping destination with an upscale collection of more than 200 stores, including Apple, Coach, Dillard’s, H&M, LEGO, lululemon, Macy’s, Sephora, Urban Outfitters, and Round1 Bowling & Arcade for boutique bowling, exciting claw machines, karaoke, pickleball fun , and more.

SCHEELS All Sports offers a variety of fun activities, plus a wide range of sporting goods and equipment, fan memorabilia, clothing, home decor, and indoor attractions like a Ferris wheel, Rollerball, video games, an aquarium, and more!

Additional entertainment options include a 20-screen Harkins movie theater and family-friendly attractions in the Chandler Fashion Center Outdoor Village, which features a seasonal splash pad with yard games like life-sized chess, Jenga, and cornhole. The Chandler mall splash pad is open in the warmer months, from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m., weather permitting.

Dining options located at the mall include The Cheesecake Factory, Firebirds Wood Fired Grill, Hop Social Grill, The Keg Steakhouse + Bar, Wildflower Bread Company, and more, or grab a more casual bite at the large food court featuring an array of fast-casual dining options. 

Out-of-town visitors are encouraged to text Chandler Fashion Center at (480) 526-9200 with questions and to receive complimentary Visitor Savings valued at more than $450 at participating restaurants and shops.

Spend the day or an afternoon at the mall with fun things to do at Chandler Fashion Center mall with activities for all ages - from boutique bowling and claw machines at Round1 Bowling & Arcade to testing your skills at an escape room, or catching a new release on one of 20 screens at Harkins Theatres Chandler Fashion 20.

Other Chandler mall amenities include complimentary wheelchair rentals, assistance with carrying out packages, free WiFi, weekend valet service, and a Text Concierge service where visitors are invited to text their questions directly for speedy assistance: (480) 526-9200.

Experience Chandler's art and cultural heritage with a visit to the Chandler Museum, located across the street from the south side of the mall. The museum offers engaging, world-class exhibits that highlight local and national culture, history, and art.

bodyHtml:
TOP 10 THINGS TO DO AT SCHEELS CHANDLER

Chandler, AZ is buzzing with excitement with the recent opening of the world’s largest destination sports store, SCHEELS All Sports located at Chandler Fashion Center mall. Fuel your passion for sports and outdoor recreation with a visit to Chandler's SCHEELS All Sports store for a one-stop shopping and entertainment experience.

You can reach the Chandler SCHEELS All Sports store via major roadways such as Loop 202 Santan Freeway, Loop 101, or Interstate 10, depending on your starting point. The store is easily accessible via West Chandler Boulevard or South Price Road.

SCHEELS is not your average sporting goods store. Spanning a colossal 250,000 square feet, this retail haven is a paradise for sports lovers and outdoor enthusiasts alike. Expect to find an extensive selection of sporting equipment, apparel, and gear for a wide range of activities, including hunting, fishing, camping, youth sports, golf, and more. The store is known for its exceptional customer service, knowledgeable staff, and top-notch brands, making it easy to find just what you need.

Beyond shopping, SCHEELS offers a wide range of entertainment attractions. Upon entry, shoppers are greeted by a 45-foot Ferris wheel that lifts them to a bird's-eye view of the 75 shops inside SCHEELS All Sports. Another favorite attraction is the awe-inspiring 16,000-gallon saltwater aquarium, featuring a variety of saltwater fish and coral for a colorful experience.

With more than a dozen hotels located near the Chandler SCHEELS All Sports, it is a must-visit for your next Chandler weekend shopping trip to enjoy all the SCHEELS All Sports attractions, explore Chandler Fashion Center mall, including Round1 Bowling & Arcade family-fun center, and enjoy local dining options for an unforgettable visit.

To help you plan your next visit, we’ve created a list of the top 10 things to see and do when visiting the Chandler SCHEELS All Sports store.

1. Explore the SCHEELS Chandler Store

SCHEELS All Sports store boasts more than 250,000 square feet of shopping space and has 75 specialty shops, including Fuzziwig’s Candy Factory. Find an extensive collection of sports and outdoor gear, apparel, toys, specialty foods, gifts, home décor and more!

2. Check Out the Ferris Wheel

The towering 1930s-style Ferris wheel is the first stop on everyone’s list when they visit the SCHEELS All Sports sporting goods store. Take a ride for panoramic views of the store and enjoy a memorable experience for visitors of all ages. Rides are offered for $1.

3. Wildlife Mountain

Experience the outdoors indoors at Wildlife Mountain. This stunning display features taxidermy mounts set against a mountain landscape, bringing the great outdoors inside. Use a smartphone to interact with the exhibit and learn fun facts about the animals on display.

4. Kid-Friendly Arcade Games

Don't miss the arcade area if you're traveling with children. It's filled with exciting arcade games and an indoor shooting gallery that will keep kids and adults entertained.

5. Rollerball!

SCHEELS All Sports brought rollerball to Arizona – perfect for all ages, this game is a miniature version of bowling for individual or group play.

6. Gaze at the Aquarium

Whether you opt to gaze and admire or walk under the 16,000-gallon saltwater aquarium, the colorful display is home to 600 different fish.

7. Enjoy a Bite to Eat at Ginna’s Café & Coffee Shop

After all the shopping and exploring, take a break at the SCHEELS restaurant to enjoy a cup of coffee, a meal or indulge your sweet tooth with delicious homemade fudge and sweet cravings from Fuzziwig’s Candy Factory to refuel for more adventure.

8. Attend In-Store Workshops and Events

SCHEELS All Sports is known for its passionate, knowledgeable staff, who offer expertise and recommendations on the best gear and equipment. Visitors can attend in-store workshops, events, and product demonstrations. Check their event calendar for the latest happenings during your visit.

9. Photo Opportunities

Add to your Instagram feed with several SCHEELS photo opps throughout the store, whether you choose Wildlife Mountain as your background or capture your view from atop the Ferris Wheel, you’ll find great photo opps for the gram.

10. Sports Fan Haven

For sports enthusiasts, SCHEELS All Sports offers a wide array of fan gear for your favorite teams. Find jerseys, hats, and memorabilia to support your team in style, and find everything you need to play your favorite sports or outfit your player.

bodyHtml:
Farmers Markets in Chandler

Perfect for a sunny Saturday stroll, farmers markets are a favorite for visitors and locals alike. The festive, open-air marketplaces feature local products, including locally grown, seasonal produce, grass-fed meats, local eggs, cheeses and butter, freshly baked breads, Arizona honey, jellies and salsas, assorted specialty foods and artisan crafts.

Visitors will find three Chandler AZ farmers markets open nearly, year-round on Saturdays providing a lively atmosphere for visitors to shop and enjoy various activities.

Downtown Chandler Farmers Market

Located in Downtown Chandler is a year-round market operated by the Downtown Chandler Community Partnership, a non-profit organization that programs activities and marketing for the downtown district. The year-round, farmers market offers locally grown and made products from 30-50 vendors. Downtown Chandler parking is plentiful, and most parking spots are free and easily accessible to the market, which takes place in Dr. A.J. Chandler Park-West on Saturdays, with seasonal hours:

October – May
Saturdays from 9 a.m. – 1 p.m.

Summer Farmers Market Hours June - September
Saturdays from 7 a.m. – 11:00 a.m.

 

Enjoy Yoga in the Park when visiting the Downtown Chandler Farmers Market, on Saturdays from November through April. This donation-based class is held seasonally on Saturdays, at 10:00 a.m. in conjunction with the market and the 45-minute class is perfect for all levels and great for an introduction to yoga. Bring a mat, sunscreen, and water to this outdoor class held on the turf lawn, next to the Crust Restaurant.

Starting in October, Kids Day at the Market is held the first Saturday of each month in conjunction with the Chandler Public Library at 9 a.m., children of all ages can enjoy activities and play life-size games in Dr. A.J. Chandler Park West from 9:00 a.m.-1:00 p.m.

Make the most of the great weather and complete your day with a stroll amongst the Chandler murals and a meal in the park with Downtown Chandler's Dine-in-the-Park option available by purchasing your meal to-go for an easy picnic.

Gilbert Farmers Market

Originating in Gilbert, this long-established farmers market earned its reputation as the East Valley's "Foodie Market". After 15 years, the market made its way into Chandler, AZ and has expanded to offer more than 160 local vendors. The Gilbert Farmers Market is now located at the Pecos Campus of Chandler Gilbert Community College, with seasonal hours:

October – April
Saturdays from 8 a.m. – 12 p.m.

Summer Farmers Market Hours May - September
Saturdays from 7 a.m. – 11 a.m.

 

Offering everything from farm-fresh produce such as cheese, meat, eggs, bread, sweets, coffee, tea, sauces, and seasonings to one-of-a-kind food experiences, visitors can expect a lively atmosphere full of locally made artisan products.

Greenhouse Gardens

Located in south Chandler, Greenhouse Gardens is a family-run, urban farm offering a seasonal selection of farm-fresh food every Saturday morning. Specializing in organic, seasonal vegetables, fruit, and herbs, the farm operates with no pesticides and is chemical-free. Visitors will enjoy the intimate setting of the working farm, chatting with the farmers themselves, and the occasional tour. 

In addition to the beautifully presented produce, visitors will find a handful of vendors ranging from fresh-baked breads, local Arizona honey, small-batch roasted coffee, farm fresh eggs, and arts and craft.  Follow this market on Instagram for seasonal updates and to fill your feed with beautiful, farm-fresh pics that celebrate urban farming in Arizona.

headings.text: Made in Chandler: Distinct Local Items to Bring Home

bodyHtml:
Made in Chandler: Distinct Local Items to Bring Home

Whether you are looking to welcome your conference guests with a uniquely Chandler business gift, create a welcome basket or take a piece of Chandler home with you, there are great options for items made in and around Chandler. Here’s a guide to finding the perfect gift that will remind you of your time in Chandler, Arizona.

Food and Drink

Opened in 2015, Peixoto Coffee Roasters is a local roaster specializing in small batch, house roasted beans from their family farm in Brazil.  Each batch offers a delectable flavor and aroma that is perfect for coffee lovers. In Uptown Chandler, coffee enthusiasts will find Sagebrush Coffee - a Chandler micro-roaster whose specialty is micro-batch roasted coffee made with a global assortment of coffee beans.

Urban Oven uses only the freshest and highest-quality ingredients in their oven-baked treats. Bring home lemon pistachio, cocoa, and pecan cookies, as well as savory rosemary parmesan, cheddar chive and three-seed crackers. Their cookies and crackers are widely available at specialty retailers and local grocery stores.

Bring home your new favorite craft beer!  Available from their Downtown Chandler taphouse, SanTan Brewing Company offers a 32-ounce aluminum can growler, the CanZilla “Crowler” while their six packs and individual cans are readily available at most local grocers. 

Located in Uptown Chandler, is SanTan Spirits Distillery.  In addition to tours, shoppers will find a selection of small batch, craft spirits featuring 21st century flavor twists. From their handcrafted limeleaf vodka to their award-winning, American single malt whiskey, Sacred Stave - this is a great option for cocktail enthusiasts.

Toys

Located in Uptown Chandler, YoYoFactory is the world’s premier manufacturer and designer of Yo-Yos and features an on-site store with a large selection of their coveted yo-yos.

Gift Baskets

From ‘speaker gifts’ to “welcome gifts’ or ‘thank you gifts’ a number of Chandler businesses offer great ways to "Gift Chandler" for your next business event including d’Vine Gourmet who specializes in homemade jellies, savory snacks and candies including their hand crafted, sea-salt caramels. d'Vine Gourmet offers a selection of premade baskets and boxes ready for gifting but will work with you customize the perfect Arizona gift.

More Ways to Experience Chandler

title: Things to Do with Kids in Chandler | Family Activity Guide
metaDescription: Discover family activities in Chandler, AZ including indoor play, amusement centers, parks, pools and museums, plus dining ideas for kids.
ogTitle: Things to Do with Kids in Chandler | Family Activity Guide
bodyHtml:
Find thrilling rides and games at Andretti Indoor Karting & Games, and if you are looking for competitive fun, pay a visit to an indoor sports-themed amusement park, Taroko Sports, complete with a high-energy mix of baseball simulators, or test your deduction skills at Escape Chandler, Chandler's original escape room.

Or splash into family fun at one of Chandler’s aquatic centers or splash pads for a quick cool-down!

With more than 330 days of sunshine, it’s easy to stay active and enjoy some quality family time at one of Chandler’s more than 60 parks, including several large, regional parks just waiting to be explored.  From Playtopia at Tumbleweed Park, one of the region’s largest playgrounds at 2.5 acres, it is an ideal place to play with slides, climbing structures, and bridges to explore, or take a more imaginative route and enjoy a stroll around the lake at Veterans Oasis Park for some urban birding, or take in the self-guided Chandler Solar System Walk.  

All ages are welcome to explore restored train cars from different periods in our country’s rail history at the Arizona Railway Museum. The attraction is staffed by volunteers and is open Saturdays and Sundays from Labor Day to Memorial Day. ⁣

The Chandler Center for the Arts features a variety of year-round entertainment from international, national, and regional entertainers and organizations, including musical performances, magic, ballet, dance, and annual events – all are a great avenue for exploring the arts as a family.

Explore the iconic Chandler Museum, which showcases local exhibits and hosts regional and national exhibits the whole family will enjoy.  Visitors will find a variety of family programming and a gift shop at this Arizona museum, located near Chandler Fashion Center mall.

Minutes from Chandler is a top Arizona activity for kids: the award-winning Phoenix Zoo – designed with the intent to connect kids of all ages to the natural world. This excursion is a must-see on any Arizona family trip. Complete your day at the zoo by getting up-close and personal, and book a giraffe encounter and feed them a treat for a memorable visit.

bodyHtml:
Chandler Aquatic Centers & Swimming

Water Parks & Splash Pads

Kids and water go hand in hand.  Whether you are looking to spend the day at the pool of your hotel or looking to venture out to one of Chandler’s spray pads, pools and aquatic centers - you're ready for great family fun.  Stay cool while enjoying a watery blast of fun during the warmer, summer months.  Whether you are looking to get totally drenched, dip the toes or mist the kids – Chandler pools and spray pads offer a number of free and inexpensive ways to cool down. 

Many of Chandler’s larger aquatic centers (Desert Oasis, Hamilton, Mesquite Groves and Nozomi)  are more like mini-water parks with a number of features to love including water slides, diving boards, zero-depth play pools, interactive water play features, the water vortex, and "current rivers" that mimic nature's waterways.  These aquatic facilities also include ramadas and family dressing rooms, making it a breeze for a family outing.

If you’re looking for more of a refreshing spray – consider a visit to one of Chandler’s splash pads to mist away the day.  From the fun flower-shaped sprays of Desert Breeze Park to the candy cane-shaped showers, ground sprays and spray rings at Chuparosa and Espee – you’re sure to have a cool afternoon.

An additional spray pad is also available at the Outdoor Village at Chandler Fashion Center mall, making it a snap to combine with a shopping or dining trip to the shopping mall. 

After spending the day in the sun, continue the cool-down with a sweet, frozen treat - the perfect ending to a summer afternoon!

bodyHtml:
Top 15 Things to Do with Kids in Chandler, AZ

If you are traveling with the family, you'll have lots of things to do with kids in and around Chandler. In Chandler, families can explore many family-friendly activities, see vintage rail cars at the Arizona Railway Museum, enjoy a desert walk with the family or visit one of Chandler's family attractions like the exciting Andretti Indoor Karting and Games or the unique baseball-themed indoor amusement park, Taroko Sports. Within a short drive of Chandler, families will find family fun exploring the desert, getting up close to see the wild animals at the Phoenix Zoo, interacting with sea creatures at aquariums, more than 300 engaging hands-on-activities at the Arizona Science Center and more!

1. Andretti Indoor Karting & Games 

Experience thrilling rides, laser tag, duckpin bowling, and more at this one-stop entertainment destination.

2. RUSH Xtreme

Rush Xtreme is an indoor adventure park offering extreme entertainment for the whole family. The amusement center features 12,000 sq. feet of trampolines for freestyle open jump, a dedicated kids trampoline for those 42" and under, Xtreme Basketball trampolines and Xtreme Dodgeball courts for kids and adults.

3. Phoenix Zoo

The Phoenix Zoo is Arizona’s largest collection of mammals, fish, invertebrates, birds and reptiles and one of the most successful zoos in the United States.

4. Arizona Museum of Natural History

Kids will enjoy the reenactments of a desert flash flood at Dinosaur Mountain as well as an exploration of Arizona and the Southwest region from creation until now at the Arizona Museum of Natural History. 

5. Arizona Science Center

With five galleries, an IMAX theater, the Dorrance Planetarium, and more than 300 hands-on exhibits – the Arizona Science Center is an excellent outing for your up-and-coming scientist.

6. Children's Museum of Phoenix

Kids can get creative in the art studio or travel through the Noodle Forest at this museum full of hands-on fun.

7. Hall of Flame Fire Museum

What kid doesn't fantasize about being a firefighter? This museum will give them a chance to dream those dreams – full of firefighting equipment, engines, and even a hands-on area where kids can learn valuable safety lessons.

8. i.d.e.a. Museum

A museum dedicated to art and children. Don't miss ArtVille, an experiential play place designed for young crawlers to curious toddlers who keep busy in a town built to cultivate awareness of color, line, shape and texture. 

9. SEA LIFE Aquarium 

Where ocean meets desert-- Check out SEA LIFE Aquarium! Visitors are transported into the amazing ocean world through close encounters with a vast array of sea creatures, including Sea Life's newest resident, Ziva, the sea turtle.

10. OdySea Aquarium

OdySea Aquarium is the largest aquarium in the Southwest, it features six attractions you won’t find anywhere else, including 12 tanks suspended from the lobby ceiling, an acrylic tube-enclosed escalator through a 2-story tank, and the Living Sea Carousel, a 20-minute show that rotates like a carousel.

11. Musical Instrument Museum

The world's first global musical instrument museum celebrates the world's cultures as expressed through music.  Families will enjoy the Experience Gallery where you can play unique instruments from all corners of the world.  

12. Desert Botanical Garden

Featuring five thematic trails, a seasonal Butterfly Pavilion each fall and spring, and flashlight tours in the summer – there are numerous activities and events that highlight native plants and unusual cacti in the Desert Botanical Garden in Chandler.

13. Arizona Railway Museum

The Arizona Railway Museum is a great place to explore the past. View antique rail cars from the days when rail transportation was in its heyday. Kids can climb in and ring the train's bell!

14. Goldfield Ghost Town

Walk down Main Street, explore the many shops and buildings, tour through the mine, visit the Goldfield Superstition Museum, pan for gold, take a narrow gauge train ride or witness an old west gun fight.

15. LEGOLAND DISCOVERY CENTER

The LEGOLAND Discovery Center is great for the whole family! The attraction features two LEGO rides, a 4-D cinema and large scale LEGO models featuring local landmarks including ASU Gammage and Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport.

bodyHtml:
Top 10 Attractions in Chandler, AZ

There is a lot to see and do in sunny Chandler, Arizona, where should you start?   We’ve put together a great list of must-see attractions, sites and all those great places you should not miss while in Chandler.  From enjoying the great outdoors, savoring a great local bite to taking in an inspiring performance – here are our picks for top 10 attractions in Chandler loved by locals and visitors.

Plan a great escape after a day of meetings and throw in a bit of entertainment and rejuvenation – its a snap at Chandler Fashion Center, the state’s second-largest mall.  With seasonal events, entertainment, engaging food court and dozens of full-service restaurants with a variety of national and local boutiques, this is a must-stop on your next trip!  Grab a great photo in front of world-renowned artist, Kelsey Montague’s original, interactive mural

Tip: Shop smart on your vacation and receive Visitor Savings with special offers by visitors by texting the word SAVINGS to (480) 526.9200 to sign up and receive your discounts.

Designed for all ages, the Andretti Indoor Karting & Games attraction features high-speed-indoor-kart racing, laser tag, virtual reality experiences and more making it a must visit when in Chandler.

Downtown Chandler is home to a densely packed array of eateries offering the best in local brew, wine and hand-crafted cocktails coupled with top notch eats. In addition to great sips and bites, visitors will find boutique shops, entertainment and more than 60 events each year with a cozy, neighborhood vibe.

Tip: Parking garages, lots and street parking offer more than 4,300 FREE parking spaces for visiting Chandler.

This 35,000-square-foot facility is home to SanTan Brewing Company's beer and spirits production, along with a spacious tasting room and patio. SanTan Gardens offers a guided behind the scenes tour of the production facility with tasting opportunities along the way.

Tip: Be sure to book your tour online in advance through the SanTan Gardens website. Tours are designed for groups of 10 or smaller and all attendees must be 21+ years old.

The Chandler Center for the Arts provides a robust arts season with performances that will delight and visual arts exhibits that will inspire.  With a diverse range of events and performances including Rock and Roll Hall of Fame inductees, GRAMMY® Award winners and emerging artists, you’re sure to find a great performance at this beautiful facility.

Tip: Plan to take in a meal before or after your performance – the arts center is located within a five-minute walk of more than 30 local eateries, cocktail bars and wine lounges located in Downtown Chandler.

With more than 100 acres of wetlands and desert habitats, hiking and biking trails, urban birding and fishing, picnic areas and more – this is a great outdoor recreation area.    The park is also home to the self-guided Chandler Solar System Walk and the Sonoran Sunset concert series, October through March.

Tip: Located in the eastern part of Chandler, this is a great park where all ages and all abilities can get out and explore the Sonoran desert – it’s truly where the city meets the desert.

The Chandler Museum campus features both locally produced and nationally traveling exhibits exploring culture, history, and art and serves as the East Valley History Center for researchers. The museum boosts a new 10,000 square foot facility adjacent to the historic McCullough-Price House. The modern building is the centerpiece of the new museum campus, designed to complement the historic house, preserving and honoring the past while representing Chandler’s progress as a community with a bright future.  On Saturdays, the museum offers family activities.

Tip:  The museum is located on the outer ring road of Chandler Fashion Center mall – which is brimming with more than a dozen, full –service restaurants in addition to their dynamic food court – making it a cinch to grab a bite to eat before or after your visit!

With more than 250 golf courses located in metro Phoenix, one might say it all started here at the San Marcos Golf Course.  While it wasn’t Arizona’s first golf course, the 18-hole course at the San Marcos Golf Course was the first to feature grass instead of sand. Test your skills where celebrities, politicians, and professional golfers have teed off since 1913.

Tip: Throughout the year, the course offers many specials including Golf & Lunch, Back 9 and Breakfast and Night Golf – keep an eye on their Facebook page for these events.

Recognized at one of the Top 5 Escape Rooms in the Western United States by the American Automobile Association (AAA) - this physical adventure game will delight!

Tip: The rooms are designed for small groups of 4-8, so grab your family, friends or co-workers and get ready to solve a series of puzzles and riddles.

Dedicated to showcasing the history and heritage of the railroads of Arizona and the Southwest, the outdoor, open-air museum features a re-creation of the Chandler train depot and a number of restored train cars from various time periods in addition to original rail company china and glass.  

Tip: The museum is open from Noon – 4:00 p.m., on Saturdays and Sundays from Labor Day to Memorial Day and has a nominal admittance fee for the volunteer staffed museum.

bodyHtml:
West Chandler

If you’re looking for easy access to everything, be sure to include a visit to West Chandler. Located a short drive from Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport with direct access from exits along Interstate 10 and the Loop 202 SanTan freeways, West Chandler is all about access.

When you visit West Chandler, you will find a variety of hotels, activities for the whole family, and some of the best shopping and dining in the community.

Whether you are searching for gifts or treating yourself, West Chandler offers many independent shops, name-brand retailers, and restaurants with a diverse selection of cuisines to satisfy every taste, from a quick and casual bite to a fine-dining occasion for that special celebration. Located along Ray Road and east of Interstate 10, you’ll find more than one million square feet of retail space at one of Chandler’s premier shopping districts, The Shoppes at Casa Paloma and Chandler Pavilions. The upscale Chandler shopping center boasts a mix of nationally recognized retailers and locally owned boutiques, providing a unique shopping experience. Notable retailers include Pottery Barn, Williams Sonoma, ULTA Beauty, and Chandler-based bakery and pet boutique, Bark & Luv. For dining, visitors can enjoy establishments like Flower Child, which offers a made-from-scratch menu catering to various dietary preferences, and Grimaldi’s Pizzeria.

In addition to great shopping and dining, visitors will find family fun centers, events, and seasonal pop-up stores in West Chandler.

And if you are extending your travels, staying in West Chandler gives you easy access to major sporting events, concerts, and regional attractions in Phoenix and beyond.

No matter what you're looking for, West Chandler places you at the crossroads of opportunity.

Visita Chandler

Chandler es una hermosa ciudad localizada en el área metropolitana de Phoenix, Arizona y a sólo 20 minutos del aeropuerto internacional Phoenix Sky Harbor. La céntrica ubicación de la ciudad de Chandler la hace perfecta para una estancia de fin de semana o para el inicio o final de unas vacaciones en Arizona. Los visitantes de Chandler disfrutarán de compras de clase mundial, reconocida gastronomía, arte y cultura, vida nocturna, diversión familiar y una gran variedad de hoteles y resorts. Chandler es reconocida por sus fabulosos campos de golf y cuando de deportes profesionales se trata, los aficionados podrán disfrutar de los partidos de su equipo favorito incluyendo fútbol americano, béisbol, hockey y hasta carreras de NASCAR.
